nodes.title: Model corner
nodes.section: Fourier conventions and the fractional multiplier
nodes.statement_html: The model corner is $W:\R\to\R$, $W(y)=y_-:=\max\{-y,0\}$.

nodes.title: Fourier transform
nodes.section: Fourier conventions and the fractional multiplier
nodes.statement_html: For $f\in L^1(\R;\C)$ the Fourier transform is \[ \widehat f(\xi)=\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} f(x)e^{-ix\xi}\,dx ,\qquad \xi\in\R, \] extended to tempered distributions $\mathcal S'(\R)$ by duality, $\langle \widehat u,\varphi\rangle=\langle u,\widehat\varphi\rangle$. The inverse transform is $\widecheck g(x)=\frac1{2\pi}\int_\R g(\xi)e^{ix\xi}\,d\xi$. With this convention $\widehat{\p_x f}(\xi)=i\xi\widehat f(\xi)$. A Fourier multiplier with symbol $m\in L^\infty_{\mathrm{loc}}(\R)$ of polynomial growth acts on $f\in\mathcal S(\R)$ by $m(D)f=(m\widehat f)^{\vee}$. (Mathlib's Real.fourierIntegral uses $e^{-2\pi i x\xi}$; the two conventions differ by the substitution $\xi\mapsto 2\pi\xi$.)

nodes.title: Secant
nodes.section: Fourier conventions and the fractional multiplier
nodes.statement_html: For $f:\R\to\R$ and $y\neq z$ put $S_f(y,z)=\dfrac{f(y)-f(z)}{y-z}$. If $f\in C^1$ we extend by $S_f(y,y)=f'(y)$; then $S_f(y,z)=\int_0^1 f'(z+s(y-z))\,ds$ for all $y,z$.

nodes.title: Admissible profile class
nodes.section: Fourier conventions and the fractional multiplier
nodes.statement_html: $\mathcal A$ denotes the set of $f\in C^1(\R)$ such that $f'\in L^\infty(\R)$ and $f'$ is locally Lipschitz. Equivalently $f\in W^{2,\infty}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\R)$ with $f'\in L^\infty(\R)$ (taking the $C^1$ representative). For $f\in\mathcal A$ and $R>0$ write $\mathrm{Lip}_R(f')$ for the Lipschitz constant of $f'$ on $[-R,R]$. Note that $\mathcal A$ contains functions with linear growth, e.g.\ any $f$ with $f'(y)\to-1$ as $y\to-\infty$; no decay of $f$ is required.

nodes.title: The fractional multiplier $|D|^{p}$ and $|D|^{p}\p_y$
nodes.section: Fourier conventions and the fractional multiplier
nodes.statement_html:
Let $0<p<1$, $\alpha=p+1$.
  • For $g\in L^\infty(\R)$ which is locally Lipschitz, define pointwise for every $y\in\R$ \[ |D|^{p}g(y):=c_\alpha\int_\R\frac{g(y)-g(z)}{|y-z|^{\alpha}}\,dz . \] (The integral is absolutely convergent by lem:c01_frac_well_defined; no principal value is needed because $\alpha<2$.)
  • For $f\in\mathcal A$ define $|D|^{p}\p_y f:=|D|^p(f')$, i.e. \[ |D|^{\alpha-1}\p_y f(y)=c_\alpha\int_\R\frac{f'(y)-f'(z)}{|y-z|^{\alpha}}\,dz . \] This is the meaning of $|D|^{\alpha-1}\p_y f$ for non-decaying $f$ (e.g.\ $f'\to-1$ at $-\infty$): only $f'$ enters, and $f'$ is bounded.
  • (Fourier side.) For $f\in\mathcal S(\R)$, $|D|^p f=(|\xi|^{p}\widehat f)^\vee$ and $|D|^{p}\p_y f=(i\xi|\xi|^{p}\widehat f)^\vee$; the two definitions agree on $\mathcal S(\R)$ by lem:c01_frac_singular_integral.

nodes.title: Absolute convergence of the singular integral
nodes.section: Fourier conventions and the fractional multiplier
nodes.statement_html: Let $0<p<1$, $\alpha=p+1$, and $g\in L^\infty(\R)$ be Lipschitz on $[y-1,y+1]$ with constant $\Lambda_y$. Then $z\mapsto (g(y)-g(z))|y-z|^{-\alpha}$ is in $L^1(\R)$ and \[ \bigl||D|^pg(y)\bigr|\le c_\alpha\Bigl(\frac{2\Lambda_y}{2-\alpha} +\frac{4\|g\|_{L^\infty}}{\alpha-1}\Bigr). \]
nodes.proof_html:
Split $\R=\{|z-y|\le1\}\cup\{|z-y|>1\}$.  On the first set
  $|g(y)-g(z)|\,|y-z|^{-\alpha}\le\Lambda_y|y-z|^{1-\alpha}$, and
  $\int_{|h|\le1}|h|^{1-\alpha}dh=2/(2-\alpha)$ since $1-\alpha>-1$.  On the second set the
  integrand is bounded by $2\|g\|_\infty|y-z|^{-\alpha}$ and
  $\int_{|h|>1}|h|^{-\alpha}dh=2/(\alpha-1)$ since $\alpha>1$.

nodes.title: Affine invariance
nodes.section: Fourier conventions and the fractional multiplier
nodes.statement_html: If $f_1,f_2\in\mathcal A$ and $f_1-f_2$ is affine, then $|D|^p\p_yf_1=|D|^p\p_yf_2$ pointwise. In particular $|D|^p\p_y f=|D|^p\p_y(f+y)$, so for $f$ with $f'(y)\to-1$ as $y\to-\infty$ one may compute $|D|^p\p_yf$ through the bounded function $f'+1$.
nodes.proof_html: $f_1'-f_2'$ is constant, so $f_1'(y)-f_1'(z)=f_2'(y)-f_2'(z)$ for all $y,z$.

nodes.title: Singular integral representation of $|\xi|^p$
nodes.section: Fourier conventions and the fractional multiplier
nodes.statement_html: Let $0<p<1$, $\alpha=p+1$. For every $g\in\mathcal S(\R)$ and $y\in\R$, \[ (|\xi|^p\widehat g)^\vee(y)=c_\alpha\int_\R\frac{g(y)-g(z)}{|y-z|^{\alpha}}\,dz, \qquad c_\alpha=\frac{\Gamma(1+p)\sin(\pi p/2)}{\pi}. \] Consequently, for $f\in\mathcal S(\R)$, $|D|^p\p_y f=(i\xi|\xi|^p\widehat f)^\vee$, and the linearization at $0$ of the gSQG nonlinearity is $|D|^{\alpha-1}\p_x$ (see lem:c01_linearization).
nodes.proof_html: Write $z=y+h$ and symmetrize ($h\mapsto-h$, allowed since the integral converges absolutely by lem:c01_frac_well_defined): \[ c_\alpha\int_\R\frac{g(y)-g(y+h)}{|h|^{\alpha}}dh =\frac{c_\alpha}2\int_\R\frac{2g(y)-g(y+h)-g(y-h)}{|h|^{\alpha}}dh . \] Insert $g(x)=\frac1{2\pi}\int\widehat g(\xi)e^{ix\xi}d\xi$: $2g(y)-g(y+h)-g(y-h)=\frac1{2\pi}\int\widehat g(\xi)e^{iy\xi}\,2(1-\cos h\xi)\,d\xi$. Fubini is justified since $|\widehat g(\xi)|\,(1-\cos h\xi)|h|^{-\alpha} \le|\widehat g(\xi)|\min(h^2\xi^2,2)|h|^{-\alpha}$, which is integrable on $\R^2$ ($\widehat g$ is Schwartz; $\int\min(h^2\xi^2,2)|h|^{-\alpha}dh=C|\xi|^{p}$). Substituting $s=|h\xi|$, \[ \int_\R\frac{1-\cos h\xi}{|h|^{1+p}}dh=2|\xi|^p\int_0^\infty\frac{1-\cos s}{s^{1+p}}ds =2|\xi|^p\,\frac{\Gamma(1-p)\cos(\pi p/2)}{p}. \] The last integral is classical (integrate by parts once to get $\frac1p\int_0^\infty s^{-p}\sin s\,ds=\frac1p\Gamma(1-p)\sin(\pi(1-p)/2)$). Hence the right side equals $c_\alpha\frac{2\Gamma(1-p)\cos(\pi p/2)}{p}(|\xi|^p\widehat g)^\vee(y)$, and by $\Gamma(p)\Gamma(1-p)=\pi/\sin(\pi p)$ and $\sin(\pi p)=2\sin(\pi p/2)\cos(\pi p/2)$, \[ \frac{p}{2\Gamma(1-p)\cos(\pi p/2)}=\frac{p\Gamma(p)\sin(\pi p)}{2\pi\cos(\pi p/2)} =\frac{\Gamma(1+p)\sin(\pi p/2)}{\pi}=c_\alpha . \] For the second claim apply the first to $g=f'$ and use $\widehat{f'}=i\xi\widehat f$.

nodes.title: Distributional meaning
nodes.section: Fourier conventions and the fractional multiplier
nodes.statement_html: Let $g\in L^\infty(\R)\cap W^{1,\infty}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\R)$ with $|g'(y)|\le C\ang{y}^N$ a.e.\ for some $C,N\ge0$. Then $|D|^pg$ (pointwise, def:frac_multiplier) is continuous, satisfies $\bigl||D|^pg(y)\bigr|\le C'\ang{y}^N$, and for every $\varphi\in\mathcal S(\R)$ \[ \int_\R |D|^pg(y)\,\varphi(y)\,dy=\int_\R g(y)\,|D|^p\varphi(y)\,dy , \] where $|D|^p\varphi=(|\xi|^p\widehat\varphi)^\vee$ satisfies $|\,|D|^p\varphi(y)|\le C_\varphi\ang{y}^{-\alpha}$. In particular the pointwise $|D|^pg$ coincides with the distribution $\varphi\mapsto\langle g,|D|^p\varphi\rangle$, so a pointwise identity $\mc E_\epsilon(f)=0$ on $\R$ (def:residual) for $f\in\mathcal A$ with $f''$ of polynomial growth implies $\mc E_\epsilon(f)=0$ in $\mathcal D'(\R)$.
nodes.proof_html: The pointwise bound follows from lem:c01_frac_well_defined with $\Lambda_y\le C\ang{|y|+1}^N\le C2^N\ang{y}^N$. Continuity: dominated convergence in the representation $c_\alpha\int(g(y)-g(y+h))|h|^{-\alpha}dh$, with dominating function $\Lambda|h|^{1-\alpha}\mathbf 1_{|h|\le1}+2\|g\|_\infty|h|^{-\alpha}\mathbf 1_{|h|>1}$ uniform for $y$ in compacts. The decay of $|D|^p\varphi$: by lem:c01_frac_singular_integral, $|D|^p\varphi(y)=c_\alpha\int(\varphi(y)-\varphi(z))|y-z|^{-\alpha}dz$; for $|y|\ge2$ split $|z-y|<|y|/2$ (use $|\varphi(y)-\varphi(z)|\le|y-z|\sup_{|w|\ge|y|/2}|\varphi'(w)|$, rapidly decaying) and $|z-y|\ge|y|/2$ (bounded by $\|\varphi\|_\infty\int_{|h|\ge|y|/2}|h|^{-\alpha}dh +(|y|/2)^{-\alpha}\|\varphi\|_{L^1}$). Duality: for $\delta>0$ put $K_\delta(y,z)=c_\alpha|y-z|^{-\alpha}\mathbf 1_{|y-z|>\delta}$. Then $\iint|g(y)-g(z)||\varphi(y)|K_\delta\,dz\,dy<\infty$ and likewise with $\varphi(z)$, so \[ \iint (g(y)-g(z))\varphi(y)K_\delta =\tfrac12\iint(g(y)-g(z))(\varphi(y)-\varphi(z))K_\delta =\iint g(y)(\varphi(y)-\varphi(z))K_\delta \] (swap $y\leftrightarrow z$, symmetry of $K_\delta$). Let $\delta\to0$: on the left the inner integral converges to $|D|^pg(y)$ and is dominated by $C'\ang{y}^N$, which is integrable against $|\varphi|$; on the right the inner integral converges to $|D|^p\varphi(y)$, dominated by $C_\varphi\ang{y}^{-\alpha}$, integrable against $|g|\le\|g\|_\infty$. For the last statement apply this with $g=f'$; the other terms of $\mc E_\epsilon(f)$ are continuous functions.

nodes.title: The coefficient $A_\epsilon$
nodes.statement_html: For $\epsilon\ge0$ and $u\in\R$ let $A_\epsilon(u)=(1+\epsilon u^2)^{-\alpha/2}$ and $B_\epsilon(u)=A_\epsilon(u)^{-1}=(1+\epsilon u^2)^{\alpha/2}$. Then $A_\epsilon$ is smooth, $0<A_\epsilon\le1$, $A_\epsilon(0)=1$, $A_\epsilon'(0)=0$, $A_0\equiv1$, and $|A_\epsilon'(u)|=\alpha\epsilon|u|(1+\epsilon u^2)^{-\alpha/2-1}\le\alpha\epsilon|u|$.

nodes.title: The nonlinearity $\mc J_\epsilon$
nodes.statement_html: For $\epsilon\ge0$ and $f\in\mathcal A$ define, for every $y\in\R$, \[ \mc J_\epsilon(f)(y)=c_\alpha\int_\R \frac{f'(y)-f'(z)}{\bigl((y-z)^2+\epsilon(f(y)-f(z))^2\bigr)^{\alpha/2}}\,dz =c_\alpha\int_\R\frac{f'(y)-f'(z)}{|y-z|^\alpha}A_\epsilon\bigl(S_f(y,z)\bigr)\,dz . \] (The two integrands agree for $z\ne y$ since $(y-z)^2+\epsilon(f(y)-f(z))^2=|y-z|^2(1+\epsilon S_f(y,z)^2)$.) We write $\mc J:=\mc J_1$. Note $\mc J_0(f)=|D|^p\p_yf$.

nodes.title: $\mc J_\epsilon$ is well defined
nodes.statement_html: For $\epsilon\ge0$, $f\in\mathcal A$ and $y\in\R$, the integrand defining $\mc J_\epsilon(f)(y)$ is absolutely integrable and $|\mc J_\epsilon(f)(y)|\le c_\alpha\bigl(\frac{2\Lambda_y}{2-\alpha}+\frac{4\|f'\|_\infty}{\alpha-1}\bigr)$, $\Lambda_y$ the Lipschitz constant of $f'$ on $[y-1,y+1]$.
nodes.proof_html: $0<A_\epsilon\le1$, so the integrand is bounded in absolute value by $|f'(y)-f'(z)||y-z|^{-\alpha}$; apply lem:c01_frac_well_defined to $g=f'$.

nodes.title: Front equation; classical solution
nodes.statement_html:
Let $I\subset\R$ be an open interval. A function $F:\R\times I\to\R$ is a classical solution of the gSQG front equation \begin{equation} \p_tF(x,t)=c_\alpha\int_\R\frac{\p_xF(x,t)-\p_xF(x',t)} {\bigl((x-x')^2+(F(x,t)-F(x',t))^2\bigr)^{\alpha/2}}\,dx' \end{equation} on $\R\times I$ if
  • $F\in C^1(\R\times I)$, $F(\cdot,t)\in C^2(\R)$ for every $t\in I$, and $\p_x^2F$ is continuous on $\R\times I$;
  • for every $t\in I$, $\p_xF(\cdot,t)\in L^\infty(\R)$ (hence $F(\cdot,t)\in\mathcal A$);
  • for every $(x,t)\in\R\times I$, $\p_tF(x,t)=\mc J(F(\cdot,t))(x)$, the right side being the absolutely convergent integral of lem:c01_J_well_defined.
This is the graph (front) formulation of the gSQG patch problem with $\Omega(t)=\{x_2<F(x_1,t)\}$; we take eqn:front_equation as the definition and do not formalize its derivation from the gSQG system.

nodes.title: Agreement with the geometric front equation in the paper
nodes.statement_html: Let $0<p<1$, $\epsilon\ge0$, and $f\in\mathcal A$. For every $y\in\R$ the integral \[ \mc J_\epsilon(f)(y)=c_\alpha\int_\R \frac{f'(y)-f'(z)}{((y-z)^2+\epsilon(f(y)-f(z))^2)^{(p+1)/2}}\,dz \] converges absolutely and equals the secant-factored operator used in Lean. Consequently every classical solution in def:gsqg_front_equation satisfies the literal equation eqn:front_equation, with an absolutely convergent right-hand side.
nodes.proof_html: For $y\ne z$ factor the denominator as $|y-z|^2(1+\epsilon S_f(y,z)^2)$; positivity permits the real-power product rule. The two integrands also agree at $y=z$ under Lean's total division convention, since the numerator vanishes. Transfer absolute convergence from lem:c01_J_well_defined. For a classical solution, each spatial slice is $C^2$ with bounded first derivative, hence belongs to $\mathcal A$; apply the identity with $\epsilon=1$.

nodes.title: Linearization at the flat interface
nodes.statement_html: Let $F\in\mathcal A$. Then $\mc J_0(F)=|D|^{p}\p_xF$, and for every $x$, $\lim_{s\to0}s^{-1}\mc J(sF)(x)=|D|^p\p_xF(x)$. More generally $\mc J(sF)=s\,\mc J_{s^2}(F)$ for $s\in\R$.
nodes.proof_html: Directly from def:c01_Jfull_eps: $(sF)'=sF'$ and $S_{sF}=sS_F$, and $A_1(sv)=A_{s^2}(v)$. The limit follows from dominated convergence, with the dominating function of lem:c01_J_well_defined, since $A_{s^2}(S_F(x,z))\to1$ pointwise.

nodes.title: Symmetries of the front equation
nodes.statement_html:
Let $F$ be a classical solution on $\R\times(a,b)$. Then the following are classical solutions:
  • $F(x-x_0,t-t_0)+h_0$ on $\R\times(a+t_0,b+t_0)$, for $x_0,t_0,h_0\in\R$;
  • $F_c(x,t)=c^{-1}F(cx,c^\alpha t)$ on $\R\times(c^{-\alpha}a,c^{-\alpha}b)$, for $c>0$;
  • $\sq F(x,t)=F(-x,-t)$ on $\R\times(-b,-a)$.
nodes.proof_html: Regularity conditions (1)--(2) of def:gsqg_front_equation are clearly preserved. (1): $\mc J$ only involves $F'$ and differences of $F$, and is translation covariant (substitute $x'\mapsto x'-x_0$). (2): $\p_tF_c=c^{\alpha-1}(\p_tF)(cx,c^\alpha t)$. In $\mc J(F_c(\cdot,t))(x)$ we have $\p_xF_c(x)=(\p_xF)(cx)$, $(x-x')^2+(F_c(x)-F_c(x'))^2=c^{-2}\bigl((cx-cx')^2+(F(cx)-F(cx'))^2\bigr)$; substituting $w=cx'$, $dx'=dw/c$ gives $\mc J(F_c(\cdot,t))(x)=c^{\alpha-1}\mc J(F(\cdot,c^\alpha t))(cx)$. (3): $\p_t\sq F(x,t)=-(\p_tF)(-x,-t)$ and $\p_x\sq F(x,t)=-(\p_xF)(-x,-t)$; substituting $x'\mapsto -x'$ gives $\mc J(\sq F(\cdot,t))(x)=-\mc J(F(\cdot,-t))(-x)$.

nodes.title: Self-similar ansatz
nodes.section: The self-similar ansatz and the profile equation
nodes.statement_html: For $T\in\R$ let $L_T(t)=(\alpha(T-t))^{1/\alpha}$ for $t<T$. For $\epsilon>0$ and $f:\R\to\R$ define $F=F_{\epsilon,T,f}:\R\times(-\infty,T)\to\R$ by \begin{equation} F(x,t)=\sqrt\epsilon\,L_T(t)\,f\Bigl(\frac{x}{L_T(t)}\Bigr). \end{equation} We call $y=x/L_T(t)$ the self-similar variable and $f$ the profile. The self-similar time is $\tau=-\log L_T(t)$.

nodes.title: Properties of $L$
nodes.section: The self-similar ansatz and the profile equation
nodes.statement_html: $L=L_T\in C^\infty((-\infty,T))$, $L>0$, $L(t)\to0$ as $t\uparrow T$, and $L'(t)=-L(t)^{1-\alpha}$.
nodes.proof_html: $L'=\frac1\alpha(\alpha(T-t))^{1/\alpha-1}\cdot(-\alpha)=-(\alpha(T-t))^{(1-\alpha)/\alpha}=-L^{1-\alpha}$.

nodes.title: Time derivative of the ansatz
nodes.section: The self-similar ansatz and the profile equation
nodes.statement_html: Let $\epsilon>0$, $T\in\R$, $f\in C^1(\R)$ and $F=F_{\epsilon,T,f}$. Then $F\in C^1(\R\times(-\infty,T))$ and, with $y=x/L(t)$, \[ \p_xF(x,t)=\sqrt\epsilon f'(y),\qquad \p_tF(x,t)=-\sqrt\epsilon\,L(t)^{1-\alpha}\bigl(f(y)-yf'(y)\bigr). \] If $f\in C^k(\R)$ then $\p_x^jF(x,t)=\sqrt\epsilon L(t)^{1-j}f^{(j)}(y)$ for $j\le k$, and $F\in C^k(\R\times(-\infty,T))$.
nodes.proof_html: Chain rule: $\p_t\bigl[L f(x/L)\bigr]=L'f(y)+Lf'(y)\cdot(-xL'/L^2)=L'(f(y)-yf'(y))$; use lem:c01_L_properties. Joint continuity of the derivatives follows from continuity of $f^{(j)}$, $L$, and $(x,t)\mapsto x/L(t)$.

nodes.title: Scaling of $\mc J$
nodes.section: The self-similar ansatz and the profile equation
nodes.statement_html: Let $\epsilon>0$, $\lambda>0$, $f\in\mathcal A$ and $G(x)=\sqrt\epsilon\,\lambda f(x/\lambda)$. Then $G\in\mathcal A$ and for every $x\in\R$ \[ \mc J(G)(x)=\sqrt\epsilon\,\lambda^{1-\alpha}\,\mc J_\epsilon(f)(x/\lambda). \]
nodes.proof_html: $G'(x)=\sqrt\epsilon f'(x/\lambda)$, bounded and locally Lipschitz. Put $y=x/\lambda$ and substitute $x'=\lambda z$, $dx'=\lambda dz$: $(x-x')^2+(G(x)-G(x'))^2=\lambda^2\bigl((y-z)^2+\epsilon(f(y)-f(z))^2\bigr)$, so the integrand becomes $\sqrt\epsilon(f'(y)-f'(z))\lambda^{-\alpha}(\dots)^{-\alpha/2}\cdot\lambda$. The change of variables is legitimate for absolutely integrable functions (lem:c01_J_well_defined).

nodes.title: Self-similar evolution
nodes.section: The self-similar ansatz and the profile equation
nodes.statement_html: Let $\epsilon>0$, $T\in\R$, and $f:\R\times\R\to\R$, $(y,\tau)\mapsto f(y,\tau)$, with $f,\p_yf,\p_y^2f,\p_\tau f$ continuous and $\p_yf(\cdot,\tau)$ bounded for each $\tau$. Let $F(x,t)=\sqrt\epsilon L(t)f(x/L(t),-\log L(t))$, $L=L_T$. Then $F$ is a classical solution on $\R\times(-\infty,T)$ iff for all $(y,\tau)$ \begin{equation} \p_\tau f=f-y\p_yf+\mc J_\epsilon(f(\cdot,\tau)). \end{equation}
nodes.proof_html: With $\tau(t)=-\log L(t)$ we have $\tau'(t)=-L'/L=L^{-\alpha}$ (lem:c01_L_properties). The chain rule gives $\p_tF=\sqrt\epsilon\bigl[L'(f-y\p_yf)+L^{1-\alpha}\p_\tau f\bigr] =\sqrt\epsilon L^{1-\alpha}\bigl[\p_\tau f-f+y\p_yf\bigr]$, and lem:c01_J_scaling with $\lambda=L(t)$ gives $\mc J(F(\cdot,t))(x)=\sqrt\epsilon L^{1-\alpha}\mc J_\epsilon(f(\cdot,\tau))(y)$. Divide by $\sqrt\epsilon L^{1-\alpha}>0$. Since $t\mapsto(\tau(t))$ is a bijection $(-\infty,T)\to\R$ and $(x,t)\mapsto(x/L,\tau)$ is a $C^\infty$ diffeomorphism of $\R\times(-\infty,T)$ onto $\R^2$, the identities are equivalent. Regularity: $\p_xF=\sqrt\epsilon\p_yf$ and $\p_x^2F=\sqrt\epsilon L^{-1}\p_y^2f$ are continuous, $\p_xF(\cdot,t)$ bounded.

nodes.title: The lower-order nonlinearity $\sq{\mc J}_\epsilon$
nodes.section: The self-similar ansatz and the profile equation
nodes.statement_html: For $\epsilon\ge0$, $f\in\mathcal A$ and $y\in\R$, \[ \sq{\mc J}_\epsilon(f)(y)=c_\alpha\int_\R\frac{f'(y)-f'(z)}{|y-z|^\alpha} \Bigl(A_\epsilon\bigl(S_f(y,z)\bigr)-A_\epsilon\bigl(f'(y)\bigr)\Bigr)\,dz . \]

nodes.title: The cubic remainder $\mc Q_\epsilon$
nodes.section: The self-similar ansatz and the profile equation
nodes.statement_html: For $\epsilon\ge0$, $f\in\mathcal A$ and $y\in\R$, \[ \mc Q_\epsilon(f)(y)=c_\alpha\int_\R\frac{f'(y)-f'(z)}{|y-z|^\alpha} \Bigl(A_\epsilon\bigl(S_f(y,z)\bigr)-1\Bigr)\,dz . \]

nodes.title: Decompositions of $\mc J_\epsilon$
nodes.section: The self-similar ansatz and the profile equation
nodes.statement_html: For $\epsilon\ge0$ and $f\in\mathcal A$ the integrals defining $\sq{\mc J}_\epsilon(f)(y)$ and $\mc Q_\epsilon(f)(y)$ converge absolutely for every $y$, and \[ \mc J_\epsilon(f)=|D|^{p}\p_yf+\mc Q_\epsilon(f) =A_\epsilon(f')\,|D|^p\p_yf+\sq{\mc J}_\epsilon(f)\qquad\text{pointwise on }\R . \]
nodes.proof_html: Since $|A_\epsilon(S)-1|\le1$ and $|A_\epsilon(S)-A_\epsilon(f'(y))|\le1$, both integrands are dominated by $|f'(y)-f'(z)||y-z|^{-\alpha}\in L^1(dz)$ (lem:c01_frac_well_defined). Write $A_\epsilon(S_f)=1+(A_\epsilon(S_f)-1)=A_\epsilon(f'(y))+(A_\epsilon(S_f)-A_\epsilon(f'(y)))$ in the second form of def:c01_Jfull_eps and split the absolutely convergent integral by linearity; $A_\epsilon(f'(y))$ does not depend on $z$.

nodes.title: $\sq{\mc J}_\epsilon$ is of lower order
nodes.section: The self-similar ansatz and the profile equation
nodes.statement_html: Let $\epsilon\ge0$, $f\in\mathcal A$, $y\in\R$, and $\Lambda$ the Lipschitz constant of $f'$ on $[y-1,y+1]$. Then for $|z-y|\le1$ the integrand of $\sq{\mc J}_\epsilon(f)(y)$ is bounded by $c_\alpha\,\alpha\epsilon\|f'\|_\infty\Lambda^2|y-z|^{2-\alpha}/2$.
nodes.proof_html: $|f'(y)-f'(z)|\le\Lambda|y-z|$. By the mean value theorem and def:A_eps, $|A_\epsilon(S_f(y,z))-A_\epsilon(f'(y))|\le\alpha\epsilon\|f'\|_\infty|S_f(y,z)-f'(y)|$ (note $|S_f|\le\|f'\|_\infty$), and $|S_f(y,z)-f'(y)|=|\int_0^1(f'(z+s(y-z))-f'(y))ds|\le\Lambda|y-z|/2$.

nodes.title: The semilinear residual $\mc E_\epsilon$
nodes.section: The self-similar ansatz and the profile equation
nodes.statement_html: For $\epsilon\ge0$ and $f\in\mathcal A$ define, pointwise for $y\in\R$, \[ \mc E_\epsilon(f)(y)=|D|^{\alpha-1}\p_yf(y)+\frac1{A_\epsilon(f'(y))} \Bigl(f(y)-yf'(y)+\sq{\mc J}_\epsilon(f)(y)\Bigr). \]

nodes.title: Quasilinear residual
nodes.section: The self-similar ansatz and the profile equation
nodes.statement_html: For $\epsilon\ge0$ and $f\in\mathcal A$ let $\sq{\mc E}_\epsilon(f)=|D|^{\alpha-1}\p_yf+f-yf'+\mc Q_\epsilon(f)$, i.e.\ $\sq{\mc E}_\epsilon(f)=\mc L_0(f)+\mc Q_\epsilon(f)$ with $\mc L_0(f)=|D|^{\alpha-1}f'+f-yf'$.

nodes.title: Residual identities
nodes.section: The self-similar ansatz and the profile equation
nodes.statement_html: For $\epsilon\ge0$ and $f\in\mathcal A$, pointwise on $\R$: \[ \sq{\mc E}_\epsilon(f)=f-yf'+\mc J_\epsilon(f)=A_\epsilon(f')\,\mc E_\epsilon(f). \] In particular, since $A_\epsilon>0$, for each $y$: $\mc E_\epsilon(f)(y)=0\iff f(y)-yf'(y)+\mc J_\epsilon(f)(y)=0$.
nodes.proof_html: First equality: lem:c01_J_decomposition, first form. Second: multiply def:residual by $A_\epsilon(f'(y))$ and use the second form of lem:c01_J_decomposition.

nodes.title: Profile equation
nodes.section: The self-similar ansatz and the profile equation
nodes.statement_html: Let $\epsilon\ge0$. A function $f\in\mathcal A$ solves the self-similar profile equation if \begin{equation} |D|^{\alpha-1}\p_yf+\frac{1}{A_\epsilon(\p_yf)}\Bigl(f-y\p_yf+\sq{\mc J}_\epsilon(f)\Bigr)=0 \quad\text{i.e. }\ \mc E_\epsilon(f)(y)=0\ \ \forall y\in\R, \end{equation} together with the boundary conditions $\lim_{y\to-\infty}f'(y)=-1$ and $\lim_{y\to+\infty}f(y)=0$. (The boundary conditions are not used in the reduction lem:self_similar_reduction; they encode that $F$ approaches the corner $\sqrt\epsilon\,x_-$.)

nodes.title: Self-similar reduction
nodes.section: The self-similar ansatz and the profile equation
nodes.statement_html: Let $\epsilon>0$, $T\in\R$ and $f\in C^2(\R)$ with $f'\in L^\infty(\R)$ (so $f\in\mathcal A$). Then $F=F_{\epsilon,T,f}$ is a classical solution of eqn:front_equation on $\R\times(-\infty,T)$ if and only if $\mc E_\epsilon(f)(y)=0$ for all $y\in\R$.
nodes.proof_html: Regularity: by lem:c01_ansatz_time_derivative with $k=2$, $F\in C^2(\R\times(-\infty,T))$, in particular $F,\p_xF\in C^1$, and $\|\p_xF(\cdot,t)\|_\infty=\sqrt\epsilon\|f'\|_\infty<\infty$. Fix $t<T$, $x\in\R$, $y=x/L(t)$. By lem:c01_ansatz_time_derivative, $\p_tF(x,t)=-\sqrt\epsilon L^{1-\alpha}(f(y)-yf'(y))$; by lem:c01_J_scaling with $\lambda=L(t)$, $\mc J(F(\cdot,t))(x)=\sqrt\epsilon L^{1-\alpha}\mc J_\epsilon(f)(y)$. Hence \[ \p_tF(x,t)-\mc J(F(\cdot,t))(x)=-\sqrt\epsilon L(t)^{1-\alpha}\bigl(f(y)-yf'(y)+\mc J_\epsilon(f)(y)\bigr) =-\sqrt\epsilon L(t)^{1-\alpha}A_\epsilon(f'(y))\,\mc E_\epsilon(f)(y) \] by lem:c01_residual_identity. The prefactor is nonzero. As $(x,t)$ ranges over $\R\times(-\infty,T)$ (with any fixed $t$), $y=x/L(t)$ ranges over all of $\R$, so the equation holds for all $(x,t)$ iff $\mc E_\epsilon(f)\equiv0$.

nodes.title: Self-similar corner formation
nodes.statement_html:
Let $\alpha\in(\frac74,2)$, $p=\alpha-1$, $\beta=\frac{\alpha}{2(\alpha-1)}$. There exist $\epsilon_0>0$ and $C>0$ (depending only on $\alpha$) such that for every $0<\epsilon<\epsilon_0$ there is a profile $f_\epsilon\in C^\infty(\R)$ with the following properties.
  • (Profile bounds.) For $y\le0$ and $0\le j\le2$: $|\p^j(f_\epsilon(y)+y)|\le C\ang{y}^{-p-j}$. For $y\ge0$: $|f_\epsilon(y)|\le C\ang{y}^{-p}$ and $|\p^{j+1}f_\epsilon(y)|\le C\ang{y}^{-\beta+j/p}$ for $j\in\{0,1\}$.
  • (Solution.) For every $T>0$, $F(x,t)=\sqrt\epsilon\,L(t)f_\epsilon(x/L(t))$, $L(t)=(\alpha(T-t))^{1/\alpha}$, is a classical solution of eqn:front_equation on $\R\times(-\infty,T)$ (def:gsqg_front_equation), and $F\in C^\infty(\R\times(-\infty,T))$.
  • (Corner convergence.) For all $T>0$ and $t<T$, \begin{equation} \|F(\cdot,t)-\sqrt\epsilon\,x_-\|_{L^\infty(\R)}\le C\sqrt\epsilon\,(T-t)^{1/\alpha}. \end{equation}
  • (Curvature blow-up.) There is $c=c(\epsilon)>0$ (independent of $T$ and $\delta$) such that for every $T>0$ and every $\delta>0$ there is $t_\delta<T$ with \begin{equation} \sup_{x\in(-\delta,\delta)}|\p_x^2F(x,t)|\ge c\,(T-t)^{-1/\alpha},\qquad t_\delta<t<T. \end{equation}
nodes.proof_html: Let $\epsilon_0$ be the minimum of the thresholds of lem:c01_profile_from_correction (inherited from thm:fixed_point_correction) and $1$, and for $0<\epsilon<\epsilon_0$ let $f_\epsilon=\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu_\epsilon}+r_\epsilon$ be the profile given there; it lies in $\mathcal A$ and $\mc E_\epsilon(f_\epsilon)\equiv0$. By lem:c01_profile_smooth, $f_\epsilon\in C^\infty(\R)$. (1) is lem:c01_profile_bounds. (2): by (1) $f_\epsilon'$ is bounded, so lem:self_similar_reduction applies; smoothness of $F$ follows from lem:c01_ansatz_time_derivative for all $k$. (3) is lem:c01_corner_convergence and (4) is lem:c01_curvature_blowup, both applied with the bounds (1).

nodes.title: The profile solves the profile equation
nodes.statement_html: Fix $\alpha\in(\frac74,2)$ and the parameters $p,\beta,\gamma_1,\gamma_2$ of def:parameters. There exists $\epsilon_1>0$ such that for every $0<\epsilon<\epsilon_1$, with $\mu_\epsilon$, $r_\epsilon\in X_{\gamma_2}$ given by thm:fixed_point_correction and $\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu_\epsilon}$ by thm:fixed_point_approximation, the function $f_\epsilon=\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu_\epsilon}+r_\epsilon$ belongs to $\mathcal A$, satisfies $\mc E_\epsilon(f_\epsilon)(y)=0$ for every $y\in\R$, and $|f_\epsilon''(y)|\le C\ang{y}^{1/p}$ for a.e.\ $y$, with $C$ independent of $\epsilon$. Moreover $\lim_{y\to-\infty}f_\epsilon'(y)=-1$ and $\lim_{y\to+\infty}f_\epsilon(y)=0$, so $f_\epsilon$ solves the profile equation (def:profile_equation).
nodes.proof_html: Take $\epsilon_1$ from thm:fixed_point_correction. Membership in $\mathcal A$: $\ov f=\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu_\epsilon}$ is $C^\infty$ with $|\ov f'|\le C$ on $\R$ (item 2 of thm:fixed_point_approximation: $|\ov f'|\lesssim\ang{y}^{-\beta}$ for $y\ge0$ and $|\ov f'+1|\lesssim\ang{y}^{-p-1}$ for $y\le0$), and $r=r_\epsilon\in X_{\gamma_2}\subset W^{2,\infty}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ with $|r'|\le\|r\|_{X_{\gamma_2}}\ang{y}^{-\gamma_2+1/p}$, $|r''|\le\|r\|_{X_{\gamma_2}}\ang{y}^{-\gamma_2+2/p}$ a.e.; since $\gamma_2>\beta+1/p>1/p$ these are bounded by $\|r\|_{X_{\gamma_2}}\ang{y}^{1/p}$, while $\ov f''$ has the stated polynomial growth and is bounded on every compact interval. So $f'$ is bounded and locally Lipschitz. The equation: by def:N_eps, $\mc N_{\epsilon,\ov f}(r)=\mc E_\epsilon(\ov f+r)-\mc E_\epsilon(\ov f)-\mc L_\epsilon(r)$ as functions on $\R$; inserting the correction equation $\mc L_\epsilon(r)=-\mc E_\epsilon(\ov f)-\mc N_{\epsilon,\ov f}(r)$ gives $\mc E_\epsilon(\ov f+r)=0$ pointwise. Limits: $|r(y)|\le\|r\|\ang{y}^{-\gamma_2}\to0$, $|r'(y)|\le\|r\|\ang{y}^{-\gamma_2-1}\to0$ as $y\to-\infty$, combined with item 1--2 of thm:fixed_point_approximation.

nodes.title: Smoothness of the profile
nodes.statement_html: The profile $f_\epsilon$ of lem:c01_profile_from_correction is in $C^\infty(\R)$; hence also $r_\epsilon=f_\epsilon-\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu_\epsilon}\in C^\infty(\R)$ and the a.e.\ bounds on $r_\epsilon''$ coming from $X_{\gamma_2}$ hold everywhere.
nodes.proof_html: $f_\epsilon\in W^{2,\infty}_{\mathrm{loc}}$, $f_\epsilon'\in L^\infty$ and $|f_\epsilon''|\le C\ang{y}^{1/p}$, so by lem:c01_frac_duality the pointwise identity $\mc E_\epsilon(f_\epsilon)\equiv0$ implies $\mc E_\epsilon(f_\epsilon)=0$ in $\mathcal D'(\R)$. Apply thm:fixed_point_smoothness. The bounds on $r_\epsilon''$ hold a.e.\ and $r_\epsilon''$ is continuous, hence they hold everywhere.

nodes.title: Profile bounds
nodes.statement_html: There exists $C>0$, independent of $\epsilon\in(0,\epsilon_1)$, such that the profile $f_\epsilon$ of lem:c01_profile_from_correction satisfies the bounds of item (1) of thm:main.
nodes.proof_html: Let $\ov f=\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu_\epsilon}$, $r=r_\epsilon$, $\rho=\|r\|_{X_{\gamma_2}}\le C_0\epsilon\le C_0$ (thm:fixed_point_correction). Recall $\beta+\frac1p<\gamma_2<2p+1$, so in particular $\gamma_2>p$ (because $\beta+1/p>1/p>1>p$) and $\gamma_2-\frac1p>\beta$. For $y\le0$ and $j\le2$: $|\p^j(\ov f+y)|\le C_j\ang{y}^{-p-j}$ by thm:fixed_point_approximation, and $|\p^jr|\le\rho\ang{y}^{-\gamma_2-j}\le\rho\ang{y}^{-p-j}$. For $y\ge0$: $|\ov f|\le C\ang{y}^{-p}$ and $|r|\le\rho\ang{y}^{-\gamma_2}\le\rho\ang{y}^{-p}$; $|\ov f'|\le C\ang{y}^{-\beta}$ and $|r'|\le\rho\ang{y}^{-\gamma_2+1/p}\le\rho\ang{y}^{-\beta}$; $|\ov f''|\le C\ang{y}^{-\beta+1/p}$ and $|r''|\le\rho\ang{y}^{-\gamma_2+2/p}\le\rho\ang{y}^{-\beta+1/p}$. Add; all constants are uniform in $\epsilon$ and $\mu\in\ov B$ by thm:fixed_point_approximation. (Pointwise validity of the $r''$ bound: lem:c01_profile_smooth.)

nodes.title: Bounded deviation from the corner
nodes.statement_html: Let $f:\R\to\R$ satisfy, for some $C>0$ and $p>0$, $|f(y)+y|\le C\ang{y}^{-p}$ for $y\le0$ and $|f(y)|\le C\ang{y}^{-p}$ for $y\ge0$. Then $\sup_{y\in\R}|f(y)-W(y)|\le C$, where $W(y)=\max\{-y,0\}$.
nodes.proof_html: $W(y)=-y$ for $y\le0$ and $W(y)=0$ for $y\ge0$; and $\ang{y}^{-p}\le1$.

nodes.title: Corner convergence
nodes.statement_html: Let $\epsilon>0$, $T\in\R$, and $f:\R\to\R$ with $M:=\sup_y|f(y)-W(y)|<\infty$. Then for all $t<T$, \[ \sup_{x\in\R}\bigl|F_{\epsilon,T,f}(x,t)-\sqrt\epsilon\,x_-\bigr|=\sqrt\epsilon\,\alpha^{1/\alpha}M\,(T-t)^{1/\alpha}. \] In particular, under the bounds of thm:main(1), eqn:intro_corner_convergence holds with constant $\alpha^{1/\alpha}C\le 2C$, and $F(\cdot,t)\to\sqrt\epsilon\,x_-$ uniformly as $t\uparrow T$.
nodes.proof_html: $W$ is positively homogeneous of degree one: $\lambda W(y)=W(\lambda y)$ for $\lambda>0$. Hence with $L=L_T(t)$ and $y=x/L$, $\sqrt\epsilon x_-=\sqrt\epsilon L\,W(y)$, so $F(x,t)-\sqrt\epsilon x_-=\sqrt\epsilon L\,(f(y)-W(y))$. Since $x\mapsto x/L$ is a bijection of $\R$, the supremum over $x$ equals $\sqrt\epsilon L M$, and $L=\alpha^{1/\alpha}(T-t)^{1/\alpha}$. Finally $\alpha^{1/\alpha}\le2$ for $\alpha\in(1,2)$, and use lem:c01_profile_minus_corner.

nodes.title: The profile is not affine
nodes.statement_html: Let $f\in C^2(\R)$ with $\lim_{y\to-\infty}f'(y)=-1$ and $f$ bounded on $[0,\infty)$. Then there exists $y_0\in\R$ with $f''(y_0)\ne0$.
nodes.proof_html:
If $f''\equiv0$ then $f'$ is constant, and the limit forces $f'\equiv-1$, so $f(y)=b-y$ for
  some $b$, which is unbounded on $[0,\infty)$; contradiction.

nodes.title: Curvature blow-up
nodes.statement_html: Let $\epsilon>0$ and $f\in C^2(\R)$ with $f''(y_0)\ne0$ for some $y_0\in\R$. Put $c=\sqrt\epsilon\,\alpha^{-1/\alpha}|f''(y_0)|>0$. Then for every $T\in\R$ and $\delta>0$, with \[ t_\delta=\begin{cases}T-\frac1\alpha\bigl(\delta/|y_0|\bigr)^\alpha,& y_0\ne0,\\ T-1,& y_0=0,\end{cases} \] we have $\sup_{|x|<\delta}|\p_x^2F_{\epsilon,T,f}(x,t)|\ge c\,(T-t)^{-1/\alpha}$ for all $t_\delta<t<T$. Moreover, if $f'$ is bounded, the geometric curvature $\kappa(x,t)=\p_x^2F/(1+(\p_xF)^2)^{3/2}$ satisfies $\sup_{|x|<\delta}|\kappa(x,t)|\ge c(1+\epsilon\|f'\|_\infty^2)^{-3/2}(T-t)^{-1/\alpha}$ for $t_\delta<t<T$.
nodes.proof_html: By lem:c01_ansatz_time_derivative, $\p_x^2F(x,t)=\sqrt\epsilon L(t)^{-1}f''(x/L(t))$. For $t_\delta<t<T$ we have $L(t)<\delta/|y_0|$ (if $y_0\ne0$), i.e.\ $x_0:=L(t)y_0$ satisfies $|x_0|<\delta$; if $y_0=0$ take $x_0=0$. Then $|\p_x^2F(x_0,t)|=\sqrt\epsilon L(t)^{-1}|f''(y_0)|=c(T-t)^{-1/\alpha}$ since $L(t)^{-1}=\alpha^{-1/\alpha}(T-t)^{-1/\alpha}$. For $\kappa$ use $|\p_xF|=\sqrt\epsilon|f'(x/L)|\le\sqrt\epsilon\|f'\|_\infty$.

nodes.title: Desingularization of a corner
nodes.statement_html: Let $\alpha\in(\frac74,2)$, $0<\epsilon<\epsilon_0$, and $F$ the solution of thm:main with $T=0$. Then $\sq F(x,t)=F(-x,-t)$ is a classical solution of eqn:front_equation on $\R\times(0,\infty)$, $\sq F\in C^\infty$, and $\|\sq F(\cdot,t)-\sqrt\epsilon\,x_+\|_{L^\infty}\le C\sqrt\epsilon\,t^{1/\alpha}\to0$ as $t\downarrow0$, where $x_+=\max\{x,0\}$.
nodes.proof_html: lem:c01_front_symmetries(3) with $(a,b)=(-\infty,0)$, and $(-x)_-=x_+$ in eqn:intro_corner_convergence.

nodes.title: Fixed parameters and cutoff
nodes.statement_html: Fix once and for all real numbers $p,\alpha,\beta,\gamma_1,\gamma_2$ with \[ \frac34 < p < 1,\qquad \alpha = p+1,\qquad \beta = \frac{p+1}{2p},\qquad \beta+\frac1p < \gamma_1 < \gamma_2 < 2p+1 . \] (Thus $\alpha\in(\tfrac74,2)$.) We call $\gamma$ admissible if $\beta+\frac1p<\gamma<2p+1$; both $\gamma_1$ and $\gamma_2$ are admissible. Fix also a cutoff $\chi_+\in C^\infty(\R;[0,1])$, nondecreasing, with $\chi_+(\xi)=0$ for $\xi\le 1$ and $\chi_+(\xi)=1$ for $\xi\ge2$; in particular $\chi_+'\in C^\infty_c(\R)$, $\operatorname{supp}\chi_+'\subset[1,2]$ and $\int_0^\infty\chi_+'(\xi)\,d\xi=1$. (The same function $\chi_+$ is used as a cutoff in the variable $y$ elsewhere.) Finally let $\Phi_0(\xi):=\frac1\alpha\,\xi|\xi|^{p}$ for $\xi\in\R$.

nodes.title: The admissible range is nonempty
nodes.statement_html: For every $p\in(\frac34,1)$ one has $\beta+\frac1p<2p+1$ with $\beta=\frac{p+1}{2p}$; hence there exist $\gamma_1<\gamma_2$ as in def:parameters. Moreover $\gamma-\frac1p>\beta>1$ for every admissible $\gamma$.
nodes.proof_html:
$\beta+\frac1p=\frac{p+3}{2p}$, and $\frac{p+3}{2p}<2p+1\iff p+3<4p^2+2p\iff
  (4p-3)(p+1)>0$, which holds since $p>\frac34$. Also $\beta=\frac12+\frac1{2p}>1$ since $p<1$.

nodes.title: Correction space $X_\gamma$
nodes.statement_html: Let $\gamma\in\R$. For $r\in W^{2,\infty}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\R;\R)$ (equivalently: $r\in C^1(\R)$ with $r'$ locally Lipschitz; then $r''$ exists a.e.\ and is in $L^\infty_{\mathrm{loc}}$) set \[ \|r\|_{X_\gamma}:=\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{y\ge0}\ang{y}^\gamma\bigl(|r(y)|+\ang{y}^{-1/p}|r'(y)|+\ang{y}^{-2/p}|r''(y)|\bigr) +\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{y\le0}\ang{y}^\gamma\bigl(|r(y)|+\ang{y}|r'(y)|+\ang{y}^{2}|r''(y)|\bigr)\in[0,\infty], \] and $X_\gamma:=\{r\in W^{2,\infty}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\R;\R):\|r\|_{X_\gamma}<\infty\}$, a real normed space.

nodes.title: Forcing space $Y_\gamma$
nodes.statement_html: Let $\gamma\in\R$. For $G\in W^{1,\infty}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\R;\R)$ (i.e.\ $G$ locally Lipschitz, $G'$ defined a.e.) set \[ \|G\|_{Y_\gamma}:=\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{y\ge0}\ang{y}^\gamma\bigl(|G(y)|+\ang{y}^{-1/p}|G'(y)|\bigr) +\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{y\le0}\ang{y}^\gamma\bigl(|G(y)|+\ang{y}|G'(y)|\bigr)\in[0,\infty], \] and $Y_\gamma:=\{G\in W^{1,\infty}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\R;\R):\|G\|_{Y_\gamma}<\infty\}$, a real normed space.

nodes.title: $X_\gamma$ is a Banach space
nodes.statement_html: For every $\gamma\in\R$, $(X_\gamma,\|\cdot\|_{X_\gamma})$ is a real Banach space.
nodes.proof_html: Norm axioms are immediate (definiteness: $\|r\|_{X_\gamma}=0$ forces $r=0$ a.e., hence everywhere by continuity). Put weights $w_0=\ang{y}^\gamma$, and $w_1=\ang{y}^{\gamma-1/p}$, $w_2=\ang{y}^{\gamma-2/p}$ on $y\ge0$, $w_1=\ang{y}^{\gamma+1}$, $w_2=\ang{y}^{\gamma+2}$ on $y<0$. Then $\frac12\max_k\|w_kr^{(k)}\|_{L^\infty}\le\|r\|_{X_\gamma}\le 6\max_k\|w_kr^{(k)}\|_{L^\infty}$, so it suffices to show completeness for the equivalent norm $\max_k\|w_kr^{(k)}\|_{L^\infty}$. Let $(r_n)$ be Cauchy. Then $w_kr_n^{(k)}\to h_k$ in $L^\infty(\R)$ for $k=0,1,2$. On each compact $[a,b]$ the weights are bounded above and below by positive constants, so $r_n\to g_0:=h_0/w_0$ and $r_n'\to g_1:=h_1/w_1$ uniformly on $[a,b]$ (these are uniform limits of continuous functions, so $g_0,g_1$ are continuous after modification on a null set; in fact the convergence is uniform on compacts for every point since $r_n,r_n'$ are continuous and Cauchy in sup on compacts), and $r_n''\to g_2:=h_2/w_2$ in $L^\infty([a,b])$. Passing to the limit in $r_n(y)-r_n(a)=\int_a^yr_n'$ and $r_n'(y)-r_n'(a)=\int_a^y r_n''$ (FTC for $C^1$ functions, resp.\ for Lipschitz functions) gives $g_0\in C^1$ with $g_0'=g_1$, and $g_1(y)-g_1(a)=\int_a^yg_2$; hence $g_1$ is locally Lipschitz with $g_1'=g_2$ a.e. Thus $r:=g_0\in W^{2,\infty}_{\mathrm{loc}}$, $w_kr^{(k)}=h_k$ a.e., so $r\in X_\gamma$ and $r_n\to r$ in $X_\gamma$.

nodes.title: $Y_\gamma$ is a Banach space
nodes.statement_html: For every $\gamma\in\R$, $(Y_\gamma,\|\cdot\|_{Y_\gamma})$ is a real Banach space.
nodes.proof_html: Identical to lem:c02_X_gamma_banach with only the two weights $w_0,w_1$ ($w_1=\ang{y}^{\gamma-1/p}$ on $y\ge0$, $\ang{y}^{\gamma+1}$ on $y<0$), using $G_n(y)-G_n(a)=\int_a^y G_n'$ for locally Lipschitz $G_n$.

nodes.title: Inclusion $X_{\gamma'}\subset X_\gamma$
nodes.statement_html: If $\gamma\le\gamma'$ then $X_{\gamma'}\subset X_\gamma$ and $\|r\|_{X_\gamma}\le\|r\|_{X_{\gamma'}}$ for all $r\in X_{\gamma'}$. In particular the inclusion $X_{\gamma_2}\hookrightarrow X_{\gamma_1}$ is a bounded linear map of norm $\le1$.
nodes.proof_html: $\ang{y}^{\gamma}\le\ang{y}^{\gamma'}$ pointwise since $\ang{y}\ge1$; all other factors are identical.

nodes.title: Inclusion $Y_{\gamma'}\subset Y_\gamma$
nodes.statement_html: If $\gamma\le\gamma'$ then $Y_{\gamma'}\subset Y_\gamma$ and $\|G\|_{Y_\gamma}\le\|G\|_{Y_{\gamma'}}$.
nodes.proof_html: As in lem:c02_X_inclusion.

nodes.title: Schwartz functions lie in every $Y_\gamma$
nodes.statement_html: If $G\in\mathcal S(\R;\R)$ then $G\in Y_\gamma$ for every $\gamma\in\R$, with $\|G\|_{Y_\gamma}\le 2\sup_{y}\ang{y}^{|\gamma|+2}(|G(y)|+|G'(y)|)<\infty$.
nodes.proof_html:
Since $p<1$, $\ang{y}^{\gamma-1/p}\le\ang{y}^{\gamma}$ and $\ang{y}^{\gamma+1}\le\ang{y}^{|\gamma|+2}$; bound each
  supremum by $\sup\ang{y}^{|\gamma|+2}(|G|+|G'|)$, which is finite for Schwartz $G$.

nodes.title: The obstruction functional $\ell$
nodes.section: The functional $\ell$, the functions $G_\pm$, $G_\mu$ and the projection $\Pi$
nodes.statement_html: Let $\gamma>1$ (so $Y_\gamma\subset L^1(\R)$ and $\widehat G$ is a bounded continuous function, with the Fourier transform of def:fourier_convention). For $G\in Y_\gamma$ define \[ \ell(G):=\lim_{R\to\infty}\int_0^R\xi\,e^{i\Phi_0(\xi)}\widehat G(\xi)\,d\xi\in\C \] whenever the limit exists. $\ell$ is $\R$-linear (not $\C$-linear: $Y_\gamma$ is a real space). For admissible $\gamma$ the limit exists for all $G\in Y_\gamma$ and $\ell:Y_\gamma\to\C$ is continuous: this is prop:linear_ell_continuity (where also the representation $\ell(G)=\int_\R G'(y)K(y)\,dy$, $K(y)=-i\int_0^\infty e^{i(\Phi_0(\xi)-y\xi)}d\xi$, is used; the normalising constants depend on def:fourier_convention). The value $\ell(G)$ does not depend on $\gamma$: if $G\in Y_{\gamma'}\subset Y_\gamma$ the defining expression is the same. For admissible $\gamma$ put $\sq Y_\gamma:=\{G\in Y_\gamma:\ell(G)=0\}$.

nodes.title: The functions $G_+$, $G_-$
nodes.section: The functional $\ell$, the functions $G_\pm$, $G_\mu$ and the projection $\Pi$
nodes.statement_html: Let $G_+,G_-:\R\to\C$ be the inverse Fourier transforms (def:fourier_convention) of \[ \widehat{G_+}(\xi)=\frac{\chi_+'(\xi)}{\xi}e^{-i\Phi_0(\xi)},\qquad \widehat{G_-}(\xi)=i\,\frac{\chi_+'(\xi)}{\xi}e^{-i\Phi_0(\xi)}\qquad(\xi\ge0), \] extended to $\xi<0$ by $\widehat{G_\pm}(\xi):=\overline{\widehat{G_\pm}(-\xi)}$.

nodes.title: Properties of $G_\pm$
nodes.section: The functional $\ell$, the functions $G_\pm$, $G_\mu$ and the projection $\Pi$
nodes.statement_html: $G_+$ and $G_-$ are real-valued Schwartz functions; $G_\pm\in Y_\gamma$ for every $\gamma$; and $\ell(G_+)=1$, $\ell(G_-)=i$.
nodes.proof_html: $\widehat{G_\pm}$ are $C^\infty$ with support in $\{1\le|\xi|\le2\}$ (the support of $\chi_+'$ and its reflection; division by $\xi$ and the factor $e^{-i\Phi_0}$ are smooth there), so $G_\pm$ are Schwartz. The Hermitian symmetry $\widehat{G_\pm}(-\xi)=\overline{\widehat{G_\pm}(\xi)}$ is equivalent to $G_\pm$ being real-valued. By lem:c02_schwartz_in_Y, $G_\pm\in Y_\gamma$. Finally, for $R\ge2$, $\int_0^R\xi e^{i\Phi_0}\widehat{G_+}\,d\xi=\int_0^R\chi_+'=\chi_+(R)-\chi_+(0)=1$, and similarly $\ell(G_-)=i$.

nodes.title: The functions $G_\mu$
nodes.section: The functional $\ell$, the functions $G_\pm$, $G_\mu$ and the projection $\Pi$
nodes.statement_html: Let $\mu_*\in\C\setminus\{0\}$ be as in def:mu_star (in the paper $\mu_*=-i/\sqrt{2\pi p}$). For $\mu\in\C$ let $G_\mu$ be the inverse Fourier transform of $\widehat{G_\mu}(\xi)=\bigl(1-\frac{\mu}{\mu_*}\bigr)\frac{\chi_+'(\xi)}{\xi}e^{-i\Phi_0(\xi)}$ for $\xi\ge0$, extended by $\widehat{G_\mu}(\xi)=\overline{\widehat{G_\mu}(-\xi)}$ for $\xi<0$.

nodes.title: Decomposition of $G_\mu$
nodes.section: The functional $\ell$, the functions $G_\pm$, $G_\mu$ and the projection $\Pi$
nodes.statement_html:
Write $z(\mu):=1-\mu/\mu_*$. Then for all $\mu\in\C$:
  • $G_\mu=\operatorname{Re}(z(\mu))\,G_++\operatorname{Im}(z(\mu))\,G_-$; in particular $G_\mu$ is a real Schwartz function and $G_{\mu_*}=0$;
  • $\ell(G_\mu)=z(\mu)$;
  • for every $\gamma$, $\mu\mapsto G_\mu$ is a continuous ($\R$-affine) map $\C\to Y_\gamma$, and $\sup_{|\mu-\mu_*|\le\delta}\|G_\mu\|_{Y_\gamma}\le\frac{\delta}{|\mu_*|}(\|G_+\|_{Y_\gamma}+\|G_-\|_{Y_\gamma})$ for any $\delta>0$.
nodes.proof_html: (1) Write $z=a+ib$. For $\xi\ge0$, $a\widehat{G_+}(\xi)+b\widehat{G_-}(\xi)=(a+ib)\frac{\chi_+'(\xi)}{\xi}e^{-i\Phi_0(\xi)}=\widehat{G_\mu}(\xi)$; for $\xi<0$, since $a,b\in\R$, $a\widehat{G_+}(\xi)+b\widehat{G_-}(\xi)=\overline{a\widehat{G_+}(-\xi)+b\widehat{G_-}(-\xi)}=\overline{\widehat{G_\mu}(-\xi)}=\widehat{G_\mu}(\xi)$. Injectivity of the Fourier transform gives (1). (The factor $i$ in $G_-$ is exactly what makes the imaginary part of $z$ pair with $G_-$.) $z(\mu_*)=0$. (2) $\R$-linearity of $\ell$ and lem:c02_G_pm_properties: $\ell(G_\mu)=a+ib$. (3) From (1), $\|G_\mu\|_{Y_\gamma}\le|z(\mu)|(\|G_+\|+\|G_-\|)$ and $|z(\mu)|=|\mu-\mu_*|/|\mu_*|$; affine maps $\C\cong\R^2\to Y_\gamma$ are continuous.

nodes.title: The projection $\Pi$
nodes.section: The functional $\ell$, the functions $G_\pm$, $G_\mu$ and the projection $\Pi$
nodes.statement_html: For admissible $\gamma$ and $G\in Y_\gamma$ define \[ \Pi G:=G-\operatorname{Re}(\ell(G))\,G_+-\operatorname{Im}(\ell(G))\,G_- . \] ($\Pi$ is given by the same formula for every $\gamma$, so $\Pi$ on $Y_{\gamma_2}$ is the restriction of $\Pi$ on $Y_{\gamma_1}$.)

nodes.title: $\Pi$ is a bounded projection onto $\sq Y_\gamma$
nodes.section: The functional $\ell$, the functions $G_\pm$, $G_\mu$ and the projection $\Pi$
nodes.statement_html:
Let $\gamma$ be admissible and let $C_\ell(\gamma)$ be a constant with $|\ell(G)|\le C_\ell(\gamma)\|G\|_{Y_\gamma}$ for $G\in Y_\gamma$ (which exists by prop:linear_ell_continuity). Then:
  • $\sq Y_\gamma$ is a closed $\R$-linear subspace of $Y_\gamma$ (hence a Banach space);
  • $\Pi:Y_\gamma\to Y_\gamma$ is $\R$-linear with $\|\Pi G\|_{Y_\gamma}\le\bigl(1+C_\ell(\gamma)(\|G_+\|_{Y_\gamma}+\|G_-\|_{Y_\gamma})\bigr)\|G\|_{Y_\gamma}$;
  • $\ell(\Pi G)=0$, i.e.\ $\Pi(Y_\gamma)\subset\sq Y_\gamma$; $\Pi G=G$ for $G\in\sq Y_\gamma$; hence $\Pi^2=\Pi$;
  • $\Pi G_\mu=0$ for all $\mu\in\C$, and $\Pi G=G-G_\mu$ whenever $\ell(G)=1-\mu/\mu_*$.
nodes.proof_html: (1) $\sq Y_\gamma=\ker\ell$ with $\ell$ continuous and $\R$-linear; closed subspaces of Banach spaces are complete. (2) $G\mapsto\operatorname{Re}\ell(G),\operatorname{Im}\ell(G)$ are $\R$-linear with norm $\le C_\ell(\gamma)$; triangle inequality. (3) $\ell(\Pi G)=\ell(G)-\operatorname{Re}\ell(G)\cdot1-\operatorname{Im}\ell(G)\cdot i=0$ by lem:c02_G_pm_properties; if $\ell(G)=0$ the correction terms vanish. (4) If $\ell(G)=z(\mu)$ then $\Pi G=G-\operatorname{Re}z(\mu)G_+-\operatorname{Im}z(\mu)G_-=G-G_\mu$ by lem:c02_G_mu_decomposition(1); with $G=G_\mu$ (using (2) of that lemma) this gives $\Pi G_\mu=0$.

nodes.title: Linear operators $\mc L_0$, $\mc L_\epsilon$
nodes.statement_html: For $r\in X_\gamma$ ($\gamma$ admissible) define the function $\mc L_0 r:\R\to\R$ by \[ \mc L_0r:=|D|^p\partial_yr+r-y\,\partial_yr, \] where $|D|^p\partial_y$ is as in def:frac_multiplier. For admissible $\gamma$, $r'$ is bounded, integrable and locally Lipschitz; its derivative need not be globally bounded. For $\epsilon\ge0$ let $b_\epsilon(y):=c_\epsilon\chi_+(y)y^{-p}$ with $c_\epsilon$ defined in def:c03_coefficient ($b_\epsilon:=0$ for $y\le1$), and define \[ \mc L_\epsilon r:=\mc L_0r+b_\epsilon\,\partial_yr+\mc R_\epsilon r, \] where $\mc R_\epsilon$ is the remainder operator of def:R_eps. In general $\mc L_\epsilon r\notin Y_\gamma$ (the term $y\,r'$ grows like $\ang{y}^{1+1/p-\gamma}$ relative to the $Y_\gamma$ weight); $\mc L_\epsilon$ is only a linear map from $X_\gamma$ into functions $\R\to\R$.

nodes.title: Nonlinear operator $\mc N_{\epsilon,\ov f}$
nodes.statement_html: For $\epsilon\ge0$, a profile $\ov f$ for which $\mc E_\epsilon(\ov f)$ is defined (def:residual), and $r\in X_\gamma$ such that $\mc E_\epsilon(\ov f+r)$ is defined, set \[ \mc N_{\epsilon,\ov f}(r):=\mc E_\epsilon(\ov f+r)-\mc E_\epsilon(\ov f)-\mc L_\epsilon(r), \] so that $\mc E_\epsilon(\ov f+r)=\mc E_\epsilon(\ov f)+\mc L_\epsilon(r)+\mc N_{\epsilon,\ov f}(r)$ identically.

nodes.title: Approximation properties for fixed parameters
nodes.statement_html:
For fixed $P$ as in def:parameters and real $R,\delta,\epsilon_0$, let $\mathsf A(P,R,\delta,\epsilon_0)$ denote the following conjunction. We use the explicit family $\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu}$ of def:approximate_solution_family at scale $R$ and $\ov B=\{\mu\in\C:|\mu-\mu_*|\le\delta\}$. First $\mu_*\ne0$, and every $\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu}$ is real and $C^\infty$ for $\epsilon\in[0,\epsilon_0]$, $\mu\in\ov B$. The remaining properties are:
  • $\lim_{y\to-\infty}[\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu}(y)+y]=0$ and $\lim_{y\to+\infty}\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu}(y)=0$.
  • For every $j\ge0$ there is $C_j>0$ such that for all $\epsilon\in[0,\epsilon_0]$, $\mu\in\ov B$: for $y\ge0$, $|\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu}(y)|\le C_j\ang{y}^{-p}$ and $|\partial_y^{j+1}\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu}(y)|\le C_j\ang{y}^{-\beta+j/p}$; for $y\le0$, $|\partial_y^j(\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu}(y)+y)|\le C_j\ang{y}^{-p-j}$.
  • For every admissible $\gamma$ there is $C_\gamma>0$ such that for all $\epsilon\in[0,\epsilon_0]$, $\mu\in\ov B$: $\mc E_\epsilon(\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu})\in Y_\gamma$ and \begin{equation} \|\mc E_\epsilon(\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu})-G_\mu\|_{Y_\gamma}\le C_\gamma\,\epsilon, \end{equation} where $G_\mu$ is the real Schwartz function of def:G_mu (independent of $\epsilon$, $G_{\mu_*}=0$).
  • For every $\epsilon\in[0,\epsilon_0]$: the map $\mu\mapsto\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu}$ is continuous from $\ov B$ into $C^2_{\mathrm{loc}}$, i.e.\ for every compact $K\subset\R$, $k\in\{0,1,2\}$ and $\mu_j\to\mu$ in $\ov B$, $\sup_K|\partial^k_y\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu_j}-\partial^k_y\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu}|\to0$; and for every admissible $\gamma$ the map $\mu\mapsto\mc E_\epsilon(\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu})$ is continuous from $\ov B$ into $Y_\gamma$ (norm topology).

nodes.title: Existence of approximate solutions
nodes.statement_html: For every parameter tuple $P$ there exist $R_0,\delta_0>0$ such that for every $R\ge R_0$ and $0<\delta\le\delta_0$ there exists $\epsilon_0>0$ for which $\mathsf A(P,R,\delta,\epsilon_0)$ of def:c02_approximation_statement holds. Thus the explicit family has all properties (1)--(4) there, with constants uniform in $\epsilon\in[0,\epsilon_0]$ and $\mu\in\ov B$.
nodes.proof_html: See lem:approx_assembly.

nodes.title: Linear inverse properties for fixed parameters
nodes.statement_html:
For fixed $P$ as in def:parameters and real $\delta,\epsilon_0$, let $\mathsf L(P,\delta,\epsilon_0)$ denote the following conjunction for the explicit operators of def:T_0, def:U_eps, def:V_eps and $\ov B=\{\mu:|\mu-\mu_*|\le\delta\}$. Every bound below has a positive constant, chosen before $\epsilon$, $\mu$ and the input functions. Well-definedness of $\ell(G)$ means convergence of its defining truncated integrals. Membership of $\mc T_0G$ includes the identity $\widehat{\mc T_0G}=m_G$ in $\mathcal S'$. The properties are:
  • For every admissible $\gamma$, $\ell:Y_\gamma\to\C$ is well defined and continuous: there is $C_\ell(\gamma)$ with $|\ell(G)|\le C_\ell(\gamma)\|G\|_{Y_\gamma}$.
  • There is an $\R$-linear map $\mc T_0$ (def:T_0), defined on $\bigcup_{\gamma\text{ adm.}}\sq Y_\gamma$ with values in functions $\R\to\R$ and given by a formula independent of $\gamma$, such that for every admissible $\gamma$: $\mc T_0(\sq Y_\gamma)\subset X_\gamma$, $\|\mc T_0G\|_{X_\gamma}\le C_T(\gamma)\|G\|_{Y_\gamma}$ for $G\in\sq Y_\gamma$, and \begin{equation} \mc L_0(\mc T_0G)=G\quad\text{pointwise on }\R,\qquad G\in\sq Y_\gamma . \end{equation}
  • For each $\epsilon\in[0,\epsilon_0]$ there are $\R$-linear bijections $\mc U_\epsilon,\mc V_\epsilon$ of the space of all functions $\R\to\R$ (def:U_eps, def:V_eps; independent of $\gamma$; in the paper $\mc U_\epsilon r=r\circ\phi_\epsilon^{-1}$, $\mc V_\epsilon u=(\phi_\epsilon')^{p+1}\,u\circ\phi_\epsilon$) such that for every admissible $\gamma$: $\mc U_\epsilon$ maps $X_\gamma$ bijectively onto $X_\gamma$, $\mc V_\epsilon$ maps $Y_\gamma$ bijectively onto $Y_\gamma$, and there is $C_{UV}(\gamma)$ with \[ \|\mc U_\epsilon\|_{X_\gamma\to X_\gamma},\ \|\mc U_\epsilon^{-1}\|_{X_\gamma\to X_\gamma},\ \|\mc V_\epsilon\|_{Y_\gamma\to Y_\gamma},\ \|\mc V_\epsilon^{-1}\|_{Y_\gamma\to Y_\gamma}\le C_{UV}(\gamma)\qquad(0\le\epsilon\le\epsilon_0); \] moreover $\mc L_\epsilon r=\mc V_\epsilon\bigl(\mc L_0(\mc U_\epsilon r)\bigr)$ for all $r\in X_\gamma$.
  • For every admissible $\gamma$ there is $C_G(\gamma)$ with \begin{equation} \sup_{\mu\in\ov B}\|(\mc V_\epsilon^{-1}-I)G_\mu\|_{Y_\gamma}\le C_G(\gamma)\,\epsilon,\qquad 0\le\epsilon\le\epsilon_0 . \end{equation}

nodes.title: Linear inverse
nodes.statement_html: For every parameter tuple $P$ there exists $\epsilon_0>0$, independent of $\delta$, such that $\mathsf L(P,\delta,\epsilon_0)$ of def:c02_linear_inverse_statement holds for every $\delta>0$. In the combined fixed-point argument one may take the minimum of this threshold and the approximation threshold. This gives all properties (1)--(4) of the definition.
nodes.proof_html: See lem:linear_inverse_assembly.

nodes.title: Nonlinear properties for fixed parameters
nodes.statement_html:
For fixed $P$ as in def:parameters and real $R,\delta,\epsilon_0$, let $\mathsf N(P,R,\delta,\epsilon_0)$ denote the following conjunction, using the explicit family of def:approximate_solution_family at scale $R$ and $\ov B=\{\mu:|\mu-\mu_*|\le\delta\}$. The quantitative constants below are positive and uniform in $\epsilon,\mu$:
  • (1)--(2) For every admissible $\gamma$ and every $N>0$ there is $C_{\mc N}(\gamma,N)$ such that for all $\epsilon\in[0,\epsilon_0]$, $\mu\in\ov B$ and $r,r_1,r_2\in X_\gamma$ with $\|r\|_{X_\gamma},\|r_1\|_{X_\gamma},\|r_2\|_{X_\gamma}\le N$, writing $\ov f=\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu}$: $\mc N_{\epsilon,\ov f}(r)$ belongs to $Y_\gamma$, and \begin{align} \|\mc N_{\epsilon,\ov f}(r)\|_{Y_\gamma}&\le C_{\mc N}(\gamma,N)\,\epsilon\,\|r\|_{X_\gamma},\\ \|\mc N_{\epsilon,\ov f}(r_1)-\mc N_{\epsilon,\ov f}(r_2)\|_{Y_\gamma}&\le C_{\mc N}(\gamma,N)\,\epsilon\,\|r_1-r_2\|_{X_\gamma}. \end{align}
  • (3) For each $\epsilon\in[0,\epsilon_0]$ and each fixed $r\in X_{\gamma_2}$, the map $\mu\mapsto\mc N_{\epsilon,\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu}}(r)$ is continuous from $\ov B$ into $Y_{\gamma_1}$.

nodes.title: Nonlinear estimates
nodes.statement_html: For every parameter tuple $P$ there exist $R_0,\delta_0>0$ such that for every $R\ge R_0$ and $0<\delta\le\delta_0$ there exists $\epsilon_0>0$ for which $\mathsf N(P,R,\delta,\epsilon_0)$ of def:c02_nonlinear_estimates_statement holds. The threshold is chosen before the admissible exponent $\gamma$ and the norm bound $N$; the constants in (1)--(2) may depend on $P,R,\delta,\epsilon_0,\gamma,N$.
nodes.proof_html: See lem:nonlinear_assembly.

nodes.title: Existence of the correction
nodes.statement_html: There exist $\epsilon_1\in(0,\epsilon_0]$ and $C>0$ such that for every $\epsilon\in[0,\epsilon_1]$ there exist $\mu_\epsilon\in\ov B$ and $r_\epsilon\in X_{\gamma_2}$ satisfying, as an identity of functions on $\R$, \begin{equation} \mc L_\epsilon(r_\epsilon)=-\mc E_\epsilon(\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu_\epsilon})-\mc N_{\epsilon,\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu_\epsilon}}(r_\epsilon), \end{equation} and \begin{equation} |\mu_\epsilon-\mu_*|+\|r_\epsilon\|_{X_{\gamma_2}}\le C\epsilon . \end{equation}
nodes.proof_html: Take $\epsilon_1$ and $C_*$ from lem:c02_K_self_map (which also ensures the hypotheses of lem:c02_w_exists). Fix $\epsilon\in[0,\epsilon_1]$. By lem:c02_K_continuity, lem:c02_K_self_map, $\mc K_\epsilon:\ov B\to\ov B$ is continuous; $\ov B$ is a closed disc in $\C$, so by lem:c02_brouwer_disc there is $\mu_\epsilon\in\ov B$ with $\mc K_\epsilon(\mu_\epsilon)=\mu_\epsilon$, i.e.\ $\mu_*[1-\ell(\mc G_{\epsilon,\mu_\epsilon}(w_{\epsilon,\mu_\epsilon}))]=\mu_\epsilon$, i.e.\ (dividing by $\mu_*\ne0$) $\ell(\mc G_{\epsilon,\mu_\epsilon}(w_{\epsilon,\mu_\epsilon}))=1-\mu_\epsilon/\mu_*$. Together with $w_{\epsilon,\mu_\epsilon}=\mc H_{\epsilon,\mu_\epsilon}(w_{\epsilon,\mu_\epsilon})$ (lem:c02_w_exists) the pair $(w_{\epsilon,\mu_\epsilon},\mu_\epsilon)$ solves the system of lem:c02_system_implies_correction, so $r_\epsilon:=\mc U_\epsilon^{-1}w_{\epsilon,\mu_\epsilon}\in X_{\gamma_2}$ solves eqn:fixed_point_correction. Bounds: $|\mu_\epsilon-\mu_*|=|\mc K_\epsilon(\mu_\epsilon)-\mu_*|\le C_*\epsilon$ by lem:c02_K_self_map, and $\|r_\epsilon\|_{X_{\gamma_2}}\le C_{UV}(\gamma_2)\|w_{\epsilon,\mu_\epsilon}\|_{X_{\gamma_2}}\le C_{UV}(\gamma_2)C_0\epsilon$ by thm:fixed_point_linear_inverse(3) and lem:c02_w_exists. Take $C:=C_*+C_{UV}(\gamma_2)C_0$.

nodes.title: The constructed profile solves the profile equation
nodes.statement_html: For $\epsilon\in[0,\epsilon_1]$ and $(\mu_\epsilon,r_\epsilon)$ as in thm:fixed_point_correction, $f_\epsilon:=\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu_\epsilon}+r_\epsilon$ satisfies $\mc E_\epsilon(f_\epsilon)=0$ on $\R$.
nodes.proof_html: By def:N_eps, $\mc E_\epsilon(f_\epsilon)=\mc E_\epsilon(\ov f)+\mc L_\epsilon(r_\epsilon)+\mc N_{\epsilon,\ov f}(r_\epsilon)$, which vanishes by eqn:fixed_point_correction.

nodes.title: Forcing map and fixed point map
nodes.statement_html: For $\epsilon\in[0,\epsilon_0]$, $\mu\in\ov B$, an admissible $\gamma$ and $w\in X_\gamma$ such that $\mc N_{\epsilon,\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu}}(\mc U_\epsilon^{-1}w)$ is defined and lies in $Y_\gamma$ (e.g.\ any $w\in X_\gamma$ by thm:fixed_point_nonlinear_estimates), define \begin{equation} \mc G_{\epsilon,\mu}(w):=-\bigl[\mc V_\epsilon^{-1}\mc E_\epsilon(\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu})-G_\mu\bigr]-\mc V_\epsilon^{-1}\mc N_{\epsilon,\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu}}(\mc U_\epsilon^{-1}w)\ \in Y_\gamma, \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \mc H_{\epsilon,\mu}(w):=\mc T_0\Pi\,\mc G_{\epsilon,\mu}(w)\ \in X_\gamma . \end{equation} Both are given by $\gamma$-independent formulas, so for $w\in X_{\gamma_2}$ the values computed in $\gamma_2$ and in $\gamma_1$ coincide.

nodes.title: The system implies the correction equation
nodes.statement_html: Let $\epsilon\in[0,\epsilon_0]$, $\mu\in\ov B$, $\gamma$ admissible, $w\in X_\gamma$, and suppose \begin{equation} \begin{cases} w=\mc T_0\Pi\,\mc G_{\epsilon,\mu}(w),\\ \ell(\mc G_{\epsilon,\mu}(w))=1-\frac{\mu}{\mu_*}.\end{cases} \end{equation} Then $r:=\mc U_\epsilon^{-1}w\in X_\gamma$ satisfies $\mc L_\epsilon(r)=-\mc E_\epsilon(\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu})-\mc N_{\epsilon,\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu}}(r)$ on $\R$.
nodes.proof_html: Since $\Pi\mc G_{\epsilon,\mu}(w)\in\sq Y_\gamma$ (lem:c02_Pi_bounded_projection(3)), eqn:fixed_point_free_inverse gives $\mc L_0w=\mc L_0\mc T_0\Pi\mc G_{\epsilon,\mu}(w)=\Pi\mc G_{\epsilon,\mu}(w)$. By the second equation and lem:c02_Pi_bounded_projection(4), $\Pi\mc G_{\epsilon,\mu}(w)=\mc G_{\epsilon,\mu}(w)-G_\mu$, and by eqn:fixed_point_forcing \[ \mc L_0 w=-\mc V_\epsilon^{-1}\mc E_\epsilon(\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu})-\mc V_\epsilon^{-1}\mc N_{\epsilon,\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu}}(r) \qquad(\text{the }G_\mu\text{ terms cancel}). \] Apply the linear map $\mc V_\epsilon$ (defined on all functions) and use $w=\mc U_\epsilon r$ and thm:fixed_point_linear_inverse(3): $\mc L_\epsilon r=\mc V_\epsilon\mc L_0\mc U_\epsilon r=-\mc E_\epsilon(\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu})-\mc N_{\epsilon,\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu}}(r)$. Also $r\in X_\gamma$ since $\mc U_\epsilon^{-1}$ preserves $X_\gamma$.

nodes.title: Conjugated residual bound
nodes.statement_html: For every admissible $\gamma$, with $C_R(\gamma):=C_{UV}(\gamma)C_\gamma+C_G(\gamma)$, \begin{equation} \|\mc V_\epsilon^{-1}\mc E_\epsilon(\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu})-G_\mu\|_{Y_\gamma}\le C_R(\gamma)\,\epsilon\qquad(\epsilon\in[0,\epsilon_0],\ \mu\in\ov B). \end{equation}
nodes.proof_html: Write $\mc V_\epsilon^{-1}\mc E_\epsilon(\ov f)-G_\mu=\mc V_\epsilon^{-1}(\mc E_\epsilon(\ov f)-G_\mu)+(\mc V_\epsilon^{-1}-I)G_\mu$ (both $\mc E_\epsilon(\ov f)$, $G_\mu\in Y_\gamma$) and use eqn:fixed_point_residual_bound, the bound on $\|\mc V_\epsilon^{-1}\|_{Y_\gamma\to Y_\gamma}$, and eqn:fixed_point_residual_transport.

nodes.title: Bounds for the forcing map
nodes.statement_html: Let $\gamma$ be admissible and $\epsilon\in[0,\epsilon_0]$, $\mu\in\ov B$. If $w,w_1,w_2\in X_\gamma$ satisfy $C_{UV}(\gamma)\|w\|_{X_\gamma}\le1$ and $C_{UV}(\gamma)\|w_i\|_{X_\gamma}\le1$, then with $C_{\mc N}:=C_{\mc N}(\gamma,1)$: \begin{align*} \|\mc G_{\epsilon,\mu}(w)\|_{Y_\gamma}&\le C_R(\gamma)\epsilon+C_{UV}(\gamma)^2C_{\mc N}\,\epsilon\|w\|_{X_\gamma},\\ \|\mc G_{\epsilon,\mu}(w_1)-\mc G_{\epsilon,\mu}(w_2)\|_{Y_\gamma}&\le C_{UV}(\gamma)^2C_{\mc N}\,\epsilon\|w_1-w_2\|_{X_\gamma}, \end{align*} and consequently, with $M(\gamma):=C_T(\gamma)\bigl(1+C_\ell(\gamma)(\|G_+\|_{Y_\gamma}+\|G_-\|_{Y_\gamma})\bigr)$, \begin{align} \|\mc H_{\epsilon,\mu}(w)\|_{X_\gamma}&\le M(\gamma)C_R(\gamma)\epsilon+M(\gamma)C_{UV}(\gamma)^2C_{\mc N}\epsilon\|w\|_{X_\gamma},\\ \|\mc H_{\epsilon,\mu}(w_1)-\mc H_{\epsilon,\mu}(w_2)\|_{X_\gamma}&\le M(\gamma)C_{UV}(\gamma)^2C_{\mc N}\epsilon\|w_1-w_2\|_{X_\gamma}. \end{align}
nodes.proof_html: $\|\mc U_\epsilon^{-1}w\|_{X_\gamma}\le C_{UV}(\gamma)\|w\|_{X_\gamma}\le1$, so eqn:fixed_point_nonlinear_bound with $N=1$ gives $\|\mc V_\epsilon^{-1}\mc N(\mc U_\epsilon^{-1}w)\|_{Y_\gamma}\le C_{UV}C_{\mc N}\epsilon\,C_{UV}\|w\|$; add lem:c02_conjugated_residual. The difference $\mc G(w_1)-\mc G(w_2)=-\mc V_\epsilon^{-1}[\mc N(\mc U_\epsilon^{-1}w_1)-\mc N(\mc U_\epsilon^{-1}w_2)]$ is bounded by eqn:fixed_point_nonlinear_lipschitz and linearity of $\mc U_\epsilon^{-1}$. Finally $\|\mc T_0\Pi G\|_{X_\gamma}\le M(\gamma)\|G\|_{Y_\gamma}$ by thm:fixed_point_linear_inverse(2) and lem:c02_Pi_bounded_projection(2),(3), and $\mc T_0\Pi$ is linear.

nodes.title: Choice of constants: $\mc H$ is a contraction in both norms
nodes.statement_html:
Put $C_0:=2M(\gamma_2)C_R(\gamma_2)$. There is $\epsilon_2\in(0,\epsilon_0]$ such that for all $\epsilon\in[0,\epsilon_2]$ and $\mu\in\ov B$, writing $\mc B_\epsilon:=\{w\in X_{\gamma_2}:\|w\|_{X_{\gamma_2}}\le C_0\epsilon\}$:
  • $\mc H_{\epsilon,\mu}(\mc B_\epsilon)\subset\mc B_\epsilon$;
  • $\|\mc H_{\epsilon,\mu}(w_1)-\mc H_{\epsilon,\mu}(w_2)\|_{X_{\gamma_2}}\le\frac12\|w_1-w_2\|_{X_{\gamma_2}}$ for $w_1,w_2\in\mc B_\epsilon$;
  • $\|\mc H_{\epsilon,\mu}(w_1)-\mc H_{\epsilon,\mu}(w_2)\|_{X_{\gamma_1}}\le\frac12\|w_1-w_2\|_{X_{\gamma_1}}$ for $w_1,w_2\in\mc B_\epsilon$;
  • $\|\mc G_{\epsilon,\mu}(w)\|_{Y_{\gamma_2}}\le 2C_R(\gamma_2)\epsilon$ for $w\in\mc B_\epsilon$.
nodes.proof_html: Choose $\epsilon_2$ so small that, for $\gamma\in\{\gamma_1,\gamma_2\}$ and $C_{\mc N}(\gamma):=C_{\mc N}(\gamma,1)$: (a) $C_{UV}(\gamma)C_0\epsilon_2\le1$; (b) $M(\gamma)C_{UV}(\gamma)^2C_{\mc N}(\gamma)\epsilon_2\le\frac12$; (c) $C_{UV}(\gamma_2)^2C_{\mc N}(\gamma_2)C_0\epsilon_2\le C_R(\gamma_2)$. Note that $N=1$ is fixed before choosing $\epsilon_2$, so there is no circularity. For $w\in\mc B_\epsilon$: $\|w\|_{X_{\gamma_1}}\le\|w\|_{X_{\gamma_2}}\le C_0\epsilon$ (lem:c02_X_inclusion), so by (a) the hypotheses of lem:c02_forcing_bounds hold for both $\gamma_1$ and $\gamma_2$. (1) By eqn:fixed_point_self_map_bound and (b): $\|\mc H(w)\|_{X_{\gamma_2}}\le\frac{C_0}2\epsilon+\frac12C_0\epsilon=C_0\epsilon$. (2) and (3): eqn:fixed_point_contraction_bound with $\gamma=\gamma_2$, resp.\ $\gamma=\gamma_1$, and (b). (4) By lem:c02_forcing_bounds and (c).

nodes.title: Banach fixed point theorem
nodes.statement_html: Let $(E,d)$ be a complete metric space (e.g.\ a closed subset of a Banach space), $T:E\to E$ with $d(Tx,Ty)\le K d(x,y)$ for some $K<1$. Then $T$ has a unique fixed point in $E$.

nodes.title: Selection of a fixed point when one exists
nodes.statement_html: For fixed parameters $P$, $R,\epsilon\in\R$, $\mu\in\C$ and radius $\rho\in\R$, select a function $w\in X_{\gamma_2}$ with $\|w\|_{X_{\gamma_2}}\le\rho$ and $\mc H_{\epsilon,\mu}(w)=w$ if such a function exists, and select $w=0$ otherwise. This total choice is denoted $w_{\epsilon,\mu}^{\rho}$. Existence and uniqueness on the contraction ball are a separate assertion; subsequently $w_{\epsilon,\mu}$ abbreviates $w_{\epsilon,\mu}^{C_0\epsilon}$.

nodes.title: Solution of the first equation
nodes.statement_html: For $\epsilon\in[0,\epsilon_2]$ and $\mu\in\ov B$ there is a unique $w_{\epsilon,\mu}\in\mc B_\epsilon$ with $w_{\epsilon,\mu}=\mc H_{\epsilon,\mu}(w_{\epsilon,\mu})$; in particular \begin{equation} \|w_{\epsilon,\mu}\|_{X_{\gamma_2}}\le C_0\epsilon . \end{equation}
nodes.proof_html: $\mc B_\epsilon$ is a closed ball in the Banach space $X_{\gamma_2}$ (lem:c02_X_gamma_banach), hence complete; by lem:c02_H_contraction(1),(2) $\mc H_{\epsilon,\mu}$ is a $\frac12$-contraction of $\mc B_\epsilon$ into itself. Apply lem:c02_banach_fixed_point. (For $\epsilon=0$, $\mc B_0=\{0\}$ and $w_{0,\mu}=0$.)

nodes.title: Continuity of $\mu\mapsto\mc G_{\epsilon,\mu}(w)$ for fixed $w$
nodes.statement_html: Fix $\epsilon\in[0,\epsilon_0]$ and $w\in X_{\gamma_2}$. Then $\mu\mapsto\mc G_{\epsilon,\mu}(w)$ is continuous from $\ov B$ into $Y_{\gamma_1}$, and $\mu\mapsto\mc H_{\epsilon,\mu}(w)$ is continuous from $\ov B$ into $X_{\gamma_1}$.
nodes.proof_html: Three terms: (i) $\mu\mapsto\mc E_\epsilon(\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu})\in Y_{\gamma_1}$ is continuous (thm:fixed_point_approximation(4) with $\gamma=\gamma_1$), and $\mc V_\epsilon^{-1}$ is a bounded linear operator on $Y_{\gamma_1}$ independent of $\mu$; (ii) $\mu\mapsto G_\mu\in Y_{\gamma_1}$ is continuous (lem:c02_G_mu_decomposition(3)); (iii) $r:=\mc U_\epsilon^{-1}w\in X_{\gamma_2}$ is independent of $\mu$, so $\mu\mapsto\mc N_{\epsilon,\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu}}(r)\in Y_{\gamma_1}$ is continuous by thm:fixed_point_nonlinear_estimates(3), and then so is its image under $\mc V_\epsilon^{-1}$. Finally $\mc T_0\Pi:Y_{\gamma_1}\to X_{\gamma_1}$ is bounded linear (thm:fixed_point_linear_inverse(2), lem:c02_Pi_bounded_projection).

nodes.title: Continuity of $\mu\mapsto w_{\epsilon,\mu}$ in $X_{\gamma_1}$
nodes.statement_html: For each $\epsilon\in[0,\epsilon_2]$ the map $\ov B\ni\mu\mapsto w_{\epsilon,\mu}\in X_{\gamma_1}$ is continuous.
nodes.proof_html: Let $\mu_j\to\mu$ in $\ov B$; write $w_j:=w_{\epsilon,\mu_j}$, $w:=w_{\epsilon,\mu}$, all in $\mc B_\epsilon$. Then \[ \|w_j-w\|_{X_{\gamma_1}}\le\|\mc H_{\epsilon,\mu_j}(w_j)-\mc H_{\epsilon,\mu_j}(w)\|_{X_{\gamma_1}}+\|\mc H_{\epsilon,\mu_j}(w)-\mc H_{\epsilon,\mu}(w)\|_{X_{\gamma_1}} \le\tfrac12\|w_j-w\|_{X_{\gamma_1}}+\|\mc H_{\epsilon,\mu_j}(w)-\mc H_{\epsilon,\mu}(w)\|_{X_{\gamma_1}}, \] using lem:c02_H_contraction(3) for the parameter $\mu_j$ (uniform in $\mu_j$). All norms are finite (lem:c02_X_inclusion), hence $\|w_j-w\|_{X_{\gamma_1}}\le2\|\mc H_{\epsilon,\mu_j}(w)-\mc H_{\epsilon,\mu}(w)\|_{X_{\gamma_1}}\to0$ by lem:c02_forcing_continuity (applied with the fixed $w\in X_{\gamma_2}$).

nodes.title: Obstruction map $\mc K_\epsilon$
nodes.statement_html: For any $R,\epsilon,\rho\in\R$ and $\mu\in\C$, use the selected $w_{\epsilon,\mu}^{\rho}$ of def:c02_fixed_point_selection and define \begin{equation} \mc K_\epsilon(\mu):=\mu_*\bigl[1-\ell(\mc G_{\epsilon,\mu}(w_{\epsilon,\mu}^{\rho}))\bigr]\in\C . \end{equation} The radius is subsequently $\rho=C_0\epsilon$.

nodes.title: Scalar fixed point identity
nodes.statement_html: For the parameters of def:c02_K_map, $\mc K_\epsilon(\mu)=\mu$ if and only if $\ell(\mc G_{\epsilon,\mu}(w_{\epsilon,\mu}^{\rho}))=1-\mu/\mu_*$.
nodes.proof_html: Since $p>0$, $\mu_*=-i/\sqrt{2\pi p}\ne0$. Divide the defining identity by $\mu_*$.

nodes.title: Continuity of $\mc K_\epsilon$
nodes.statement_html: For each $\epsilon\in[0,\epsilon_2]$, $\mu\mapsto\mc G_{\epsilon,\mu}(w_{\epsilon,\mu})$ is continuous $\ov B\to Y_{\gamma_1}$, and $\mc K_\epsilon:\ov B\to\C$ is continuous.
nodes.proof_html: With notation as in lem:c02_w_continuity, \[ \|\mc G_{\epsilon,\mu_j}(w_j)-\mc G_{\epsilon,\mu}(w)\|_{Y_{\gamma_1}}\le\|\mc G_{\epsilon,\mu_j}(w_j)-\mc G_{\epsilon,\mu_j}(w)\|_{Y_{\gamma_1}}+\|\mc G_{\epsilon,\mu_j}(w)-\mc G_{\epsilon,\mu}(w)\|_{Y_{\gamma_1}}. \] The first term is $\le C_{UV}(\gamma_1)^2C_{\mc N}(\gamma_1,1)\epsilon\|w_j-w\|_{X_{\gamma_1}}$ by lem:c02_forcing_bounds with $\gamma=\gamma_1$ (hypotheses verified in the proof of lem:c02_H_contraction; the constant is uniform in $\mu_j$), and tends to $0$ by lem:c02_w_continuity. The second tends to $0$ by lem:c02_forcing_continuity. Finally $\ell$ is continuous on $Y_{\gamma_1}$ (thm:fixed_point_linear_inverse(1)) and its value does not depend on whether $\mc G_{\epsilon,\mu}(w_{\epsilon,\mu})\in Y_{\gamma_2}$ is regarded in $Y_{\gamma_1}$ or $Y_{\gamma_2}$ (def:ell).

nodes.title: Smallness of $\mc K_\epsilon-\mu_*$; $\mc K_\epsilon$ maps $\ov B$ into itself
nodes.statement_html: Let $C_*:=2|\mu_*|C_\ell(\gamma_2)C_R(\gamma_2)$ and $\epsilon_1:=\min\{\epsilon_2,\delta/C_*\}$. For all $\epsilon\in[0,\epsilon_2]$ and $\mu\in\ov B$, \begin{equation} |\mc K_\epsilon(\mu)-\mu_*|=|\mu_*|\,|\ell(\mc G_{\epsilon,\mu}(w_{\epsilon,\mu}))|\le C_*\epsilon, \end{equation} and for $\epsilon\in[0,\epsilon_1]$, $\mc K_\epsilon(\ov B)\subset\ov B$.
nodes.proof_html: $|\ell(G)|\le C_\ell(\gamma_2)\|G\|_{Y_{\gamma_2}}$ and $\|\mc G_{\epsilon,\mu}(w_{\epsilon,\mu})\|_{Y_{\gamma_2}}\le2C_R(\gamma_2)\epsilon$ by lem:c02_H_contraction(4) since $w_{\epsilon,\mu}\in\mc B_\epsilon$. If $C_*\epsilon\le\delta$ then $|\mc K_\epsilon(\mu)-\mu_*|\le\delta$, i.e.\ $\mc K_\epsilon(\mu)\in\ov B$.

nodes.title: Brouwer fixed point theorem for a closed disc in $\C$
nodes.statement_html: Let $c\in\C$, $\delta>0$, $\ov B=\{\mu:|\mu-c|\le\delta\}$ and $g:\ov B\to\ov B$ continuous. Then $g$ has a fixed point.
nodes.proof_html: By the affine homeomorphism $\mu\mapsto(\mu-c)/\delta$ reduce to the closed unit disc $\ov{\mathbb D}$. If $g$ had no fixed point, the map $\rho(\mu):=$ the intersection of the ray from $g(\mu)$ through $\mu$ with $\partial\mathbb D$ (explicitly, $\rho(\mu)=\mu+t(\mu)(\mu-g(\mu))$ with $t(\mu)\ge0$ the nonnegative root of a quadratic depending continuously on $\mu$) would be a continuous retraction $\ov{\mathbb D}\to S^1$. No such retraction exists: composing with $\theta\mapsto e^{i\theta}$ and the homotopy $(s,\theta)\mapsto\rho(se^{i\theta})$ would show that the identity loop of $S^1$ (winding number $1$) is homotopic to a constant loop (winding number $0$), contradicting homotopy invariance of the winding number / $\pi_1(S^1)\cong\Z$. Reference: e.g.\ Milnor, Topology from the differentiable viewpoint, or any algebraic topology text.

nodes.title: Local H\"older spaces
nodes.statement_html: Let $s>0$ with $s\notin\N$, and write $s=k+\theta$ with $k\in\N_0$, $\theta\in(0,1)$. For a compact interval $I\subset\R$ and $g\in C^k(I;\C)$ put \[ \|g\|_{C^s(I)}:=\sum_{i=0}^k\sup_I|g^{(i)}| +\sup_{x\neq x'\in I}\frac{|g^{(k)}(x)-g^{(k)}(x')|}{|x-x'|^\theta}, \] and $C^s(I)=\{g\in C^k(I):\|g\|_{C^s(I)}<\infty\}$. For an open interval $U$, $C^s_{\textup{loc}}(U)$ is the set of $g\in C^k(U)$ with $g|_I\in C^s(I)$ for every compact interval $I\subset U$. We write $C^s_{\textup{loc}}=C^s_{\textup{loc}}(\R)$. For $0<s_0<1$ every locally Lipschitz function lies in $C^{s_0}_{\textup{loc}}$.

nodes.title: Secant
nodes.statement_html: For $f:\R\to\R$ and $y\neq z$ let $S_f(y,z)=\dfrac{f(y)-f(z)}{y-z}$. If $f\in C^1(\R)$ then $S_f(y,z)=\int_0^1f'(z+\tau(y-z))\,d\tau$, which extends continuously to $y=z$ by $S_f(y,y)=f'(y)$, and $|S_f(y,z)|\le\|f'\|_{L^\infty}$.

nodes.title: The coefficient $B_\epsilon$ and the kernel function $\Gamma_\epsilon$
nodes.statement_html: Let $\epsilon\ge0$, $A_\epsilon(u)=(1+\epsilon u^2)^{-\alpha/2}$ (def:A_eps) and $B_\epsilon(u):=A_\epsilon(u)^{-1}=(1+\epsilon u^2)^{\alpha/2}$. Let $c_\alpha=\Gamma(\alpha)\sin(\pi(\alpha-1)/2)/\pi$ be the constant of def:J_eps. Define $P_\epsilon,\Gamma_\epsilon:\R^2\to\R$ by \[ P_\epsilon(u,v):=\int_u^v\Bigl(1-\frac{A_\epsilon(s)}{A_\epsilon(u)}\Bigr)ds, \] \begin{equation} \Gamma_\epsilon(u,v):=c_\alpha\Bigl[p\int_u^v\Bigl(1-\frac{A_\epsilon(s)}{A_\epsilon(u)}\Bigr)ds+(v-u)\Bigl(1-\frac{A_\epsilon(v)}{A_\epsilon(u)}\Bigr)\Bigr] =c_\alpha\Bigl[p\,P_\epsilon(u,v)+(v-u)\Bigl(1-\frac{A_\epsilon(v)}{A_\epsilon(u)}\Bigr)\Bigr], \end{equation} and \[ \sq\Gamma_\epsilon(u,v):=-\frac{c_\alpha}{A_\epsilon(u)}\int_0^1\bigl[1+p(1-t)\bigr]A_\epsilon'\bigl(u+t(v-u)\bigr)\,dt . \] Since $A_\epsilon\in C^\infty(\R)$ and $A_\epsilon>0$, the functions $B_\epsilon,P_\epsilon,\Gamma_\epsilon,\sq\Gamma_\epsilon$ are $C^\infty$ on their domains.

nodes.title: The nonlocal operator $\mc I_\epsilon$
nodes.statement_html: For $f\in W^{2,\infty}_{\textup{loc}}(\R)$ with $f'\in L^\infty(\R)$ and $y\in\R$ set \[ \mc I_\epsilon(f)(y):=\int_\R\frac{\Gamma_\epsilon\bigl(f'(y),S_f(y,z)\bigr)}{|y-z|^\alpha}\,dz =\int_\R\frac{\Gamma_\epsilon\bigl(f'(y),S_f(y,y-t)\bigr)}{|t|^\alpha}\,dt . \] (Absolute convergence is part of lem:c03_I_well_defined.)

nodes.title: Bounds on $A_\epsilon$
nodes.statement_html: Let $1<\alpha<2$, $0\le\epsilon\le1$ and $R\ge1$. Then $0<A_\epsilon\le1$, $A_\epsilon(0)=1$, $A_\epsilon'(0)=0$, $A_\epsilon'(s)=-\alpha\epsilon s(1+\epsilon s^2)^{-\alpha/2-1}$, so $|A_\epsilon'(s)|\le\alpha\epsilon|s|$ and $|1-A_\epsilon(s)|\le\frac\alpha2\epsilon s^2$ for all $s\in\R$. Moreover for each $k\ge0$ there is $C=C(k,R,\alpha)$ with $|\partial_s^kA_\epsilon'(s)|\le C\epsilon$, $|\partial_s^k(A_\epsilon(s)-1)|\le C\epsilon$ and $|\partial_s^kB_\epsilon(s)|\le C$ for all $|s|\le R$ and all $0\le\epsilon\le1$.
nodes.proof_html:
Direct differentiation. $1-(1+x)^{-\alpha/2}\le\frac\alpha2x$ for $x\ge0$ by concavity/mean value theorem.
  For the uniform bounds: $A_\epsilon'(s)=\epsilon\cdot g(\epsilon,s)$ with
  $g(\epsilon,s)=-\alpha s(1+\epsilon s^2)^{-\alpha/2-1}$ smooth on $[0,1]\times[-R,R]$, so every $s$-derivative of $g$ is bounded on this compact set;
  similarly $A_\epsilon(s)-1=\int_0^sA_\epsilon'$ and $B_\epsilon(s)=(1+\epsilon s^2)^{\alpha/2}$ is jointly smooth in $(\epsilon,s)$.

nodes.title: Quadratic factorisation of $\Gamma_\epsilon$
nodes.statement_html: For all $\epsilon\ge0$ and $(u,v)\in\R^2$: \begin{equation} \Gamma_\epsilon(u,v)=(u-v)^2\sq\Gamma_\epsilon(u,v),\qquad \sq\Gamma_\epsilon(u,v)=-\frac{c_\alpha}{A_\epsilon(u)}\int_0^1\bigl[1+p(1-t)\bigr]A_\epsilon'\bigl(u+t(v-u)\bigr)\,dt . \end{equation} Moreover $|P_\epsilon(u,v)|\le\frac12(v-u)^2B_\epsilon(u)\sup_{[u,v]}|A_\epsilon'|$.
nodes.proof_html:
Put $g(s)=1-A_\epsilon(s)/A_\epsilon(u)$, so $g(u)=0$, $g'(s)=-A_\epsilon'(s)/A_\epsilon(u)$.
  Substituting $s=u+t(v-u)$ and using $g(u+t(v-u))=(v-u)\int_0^tg'(u+\tau(v-u))d\tau$ and Fubini,
  \[
    P_\epsilon(u,v)=(v-u)\int_0^1g(u+t(v-u))dt=(v-u)^2\int_0^1(1-\tau)g'(u+\tau(v-u))d\tau,
  \]
  \[
    (v-u)g(v)=(v-u)^2\int_0^1g'(u+\tau(v-u))d\tau .
  \]
  Hence $\Gamma_\epsilon/c_\alpha=(v-u)^2\int_0^1[1+p(1-\tau)]g'(u+\tau(v-u))d\tau$, which is the claim.
  The bound on $P_\epsilon$ follows from the first display.

nodes.title: Kernel bounds; Remark ``vanishing diagonal''
nodes.statement_html:
Let $1<\alpha<2$ and $R\ge1$. There are constants $C_j=C(j,R,\alpha)$ such that for all $0\le\epsilon\le1$ and all $|u|,|v|\le R$:
  • $|\sq\Gamma_\epsilon(u,v)|\le C_0\epsilon(|u|+|v|)$ and $|\nabla^j\sq\Gamma_\epsilon(u,v)|\le C_j\epsilon$ for all $j\ge0$;
  • for every $j\ge0$, \begin{equation} |\nabla\Gamma_\epsilon(u,v)|\le C_1\epsilon|u-v|(|u|+|v|),\quad |\nabla^2\Gamma_\epsilon(u,v)|\le C_2\epsilon(|u|+|v|),\quad |\nabla^j\Gamma_\epsilon(u,v)|\le C_j\epsilon; \end{equation}
  • for every $j\ge0$, \begin{equation} |(\partial_1+\partial_2)^j\Gamma_\epsilon(u,v)|\le C_j\epsilon|u-v|^2,\qquad |(\partial_1+\partial_2)\nabla\Gamma_\epsilon(u,v)|\le C_1\epsilon|u-v|. \end{equation}
Consequently, if $f\in W^{2,\infty}_{\textup{loc}}$, $f'\in L^\infty$, then for $|y|\le R$, $0<|y-z|\le 2$, $|\Gamma_\epsilon(f'(y),S_f(y,z))|\,|y-z|^{-\alpha}\le C\epsilon|y-z|^{2-\alpha}$ with $C$ depending on $R,\|f'\|_{L^\infty},\|f''\|_{L^\infty(-R-2,R+2)}$.
nodes.proof_html: (1) By lem:c03_A_eps_bounds, $|A_\epsilon'(w)|\le\alpha\epsilon|w|\le\alpha\epsilon(|u|+|v|)$ for $w$ between $u,v$, and $B_\epsilon(u)\le(1+R^2)^{\alpha/2}$; this gives the first bound with $C_0=c_\alpha(1+p)\alpha(1+R^2)^{\alpha/2}$. For derivatives, differentiate under the $t$-integral; every derivative falls on $B_\epsilon(u)$ or on $A_\epsilon'$, and both are bounded with the factor $\epsilon$ coming from $A_\epsilon'$ (lem:c03_A_eps_bounds, applied on $[-R,R]$; note $u+t(v-u)\in[-R,R]$). (2) Write $\Gamma_\epsilon=(u-v)^2\sq\Gamma_\epsilon$ (lem:c03_Gamma_quadratic_factor). Then $\nabla\Gamma_\epsilon=2(u-v)(1,-1)\sq\Gamma_\epsilon+(u-v)^2\nabla\sq\Gamma_\epsilon$; use (1) and $|u-v|\le|u|+|v|$. $\nabla^2\Gamma_\epsilon=2(1,-1)^{\otimes2}\sq\Gamma_\epsilon+4(u-v)(1,-1)\otimes_s\nabla\sq\Gamma_\epsilon+(u-v)^2\nabla^2\sq\Gamma_\epsilon$; use (1) and $|u-v|^2\le2R(|u|+|v|)$. For $j\ge3$ use Leibniz and (1). (3) $(\partial_1+\partial_2)(u-v)^2=0$, hence $(\partial_1+\partial_2)^j\Gamma_\epsilon=(u-v)^2(\partial_1+\partial_2)^j\sq\Gamma_\epsilon$, bounded by (1). Also $(\partial_1+\partial_2)\nabla\Gamma_\epsilon=\nabla[(u-v)^2(\partial_1+\partial_2)\sq\Gamma_\epsilon]=2(u-v)(1,-1)(\partial_1+\partial_2)\sq\Gamma_\epsilon+(u-v)^2\nabla(\partial_1+\partial_2)\sq\Gamma_\epsilon$. Consequence: $|f'(y)-S_f(y,z)|=|\int_0^1(f'(y)-f'(z+\tau(y-z)))d\tau|\le\frac12\|f''\|_{L^\infty(-R-2,R+2)}|y-z|$, and $|f'(y)|,|S_f|\le\|f'\|_\infty$; apply (1) with $R$ replaced by $\max(R,\|f'\|_\infty)$.

nodes.title: Well-posedness and continuity of the terms of $\mc E_\epsilon$
nodes.statement_html:
Let $\epsilon\ge0$, $f\in W^{2,\infty}_{\textup{loc}}(\R)$ with $f'\in L^\infty(\R)$. Then:
  • $|D|^pf'(y)=c_p\int_\R\frac{f'(y)-f'(y+z)}{|z|^{1+p}}dz$ (def:frac_multiplier, lem:c03_frac_kernel_formula) converges absolutely for every $y$ and defines a continuous function;
  • the integral defining $\sq{\mc J}_\epsilon(f)(y)$ (def:J_eps) and the integrals $\int\frac{|f'(y)-f'(z)|}{|y-z|^\alpha}\bigl|\frac{A_\epsilon(S_f(y,z))}{A_\epsilon(f'(y))}-1\bigr|dz$ and $\int\frac{|\Gamma_\epsilon(f'(y),S_f(y,z))|}{|y-z|^\alpha}dz$ converge, locally uniformly in $y$, and $\sq{\mc J}_\epsilon(f)$ and $\mc I_\epsilon(f)$ are continuous;
  • consequently $\mc E_\epsilon(f)$ (def:residual) is a continuous function on $\R$, and $\mc E_\epsilon(f)=0$ in $\mc D'(\R)$ if and only if $\mc E_\epsilon(f)(y)=0$ for every $y\in\R$.
nodes.proof_html: Fix $R\ge1$, $|y|\le R$; let $L=\|f''\|_{L^\infty(-R-2,R+2)}$, $K=\|f'\|_\infty$. (1) For $|z|\le1$ the integrand is bounded by $L|z|^{-p}$, for $|z|\ge1$ by $2K|z|^{-1-p}$; both integrable as $0<p<1$. Continuity in $y$ follows from dominated convergence (the dominating function is uniform for $|y|\le R$). (2) For $|y-z|\le2$: $|f'(y)-f'(z)|\le L|y-z|$ and, by the mean value theorem and $|A'_\epsilon|\le\alpha\epsilon\max(K,1)$ on $[-K,K]$, $|A_\epsilon(S_f)-A_\epsilon(f'(y))|\le C|S_f-f'(y)|\le CL|y-z|$; so the integrand is $\le C|y-z|^{2-\alpha}$, integrable since $\alpha<3$. For $|y-z|\ge2$ the integrands are $\le C|y-z|^{-\alpha}$, integrable as $\alpha>1$ ($A_\epsilon\le1$, $B_\epsilon(f'(y))\le(1+\epsilon K^2)^{\alpha/2}$, $\Gamma_\epsilon$ bounded on $[-K,K]^2$). For $\Gamma_\epsilon$ near the diagonal use the consequence in rmk:analysis_vanishing_diagonal (the $\epsilon\le 1$ restriction there is only for uniformity; for fixed $\epsilon$ the same argument applies with $\epsilon$-dependent constants). The integrands are continuous in $y$ for $z\ne y$ ($f\in C^1$), so continuity follows by dominated convergence after the change of variables $z=y-t$. (3) $\mc E_\epsilon(f)=|D|^pf'+B_\epsilon(f')(f-yf'+\sq{\mc J}_\epsilon(f))$ is a sum of products of continuous functions. A continuous function vanishing as a distribution vanishes identically.

nodes.title: Secant integration by parts identity
nodes.statement_html: Let $f\in C^1(\R)$, $y\in\R$, $u=f'(y)$. For $z\ne y$, $z\mapsto S_f(y,z)$ is $C^1$ with $\partial_zS_f(y,z)=\frac{S_f(y,z)-f'(z)}{y-z}$, hence \begin{equation} (y-z)\partial_zP_\epsilon(u,S_f(y,z))=(S_f-u)\Bigl(1-\tfrac{A_\epsilon(S_f)}{A_\epsilon(u)}\Bigr)+(u-f'(z))\Bigl(1-\tfrac{A_\epsilon(S_f)}{A_\epsilon(u)}\Bigr), \end{equation} with $S_f=S_f(y,z)$. Moreover $\partial_z\bigl((y-z)|y-z|^{-\alpha}\bigr)=p|y-z|^{-\alpha}$ for $z\ne y$.
nodes.proof_html:
Quotient rule; $\partial_vP_\epsilon(u,v)=1-A_\epsilon(v)/A_\epsilon(u)$ by the fundamental theorem of calculus; chain rule; and
  split $S_f-f'(z)=(S_f-u)+(u-f'(z))$. For the last identity write $w=y-z$: $\operatorname{sgn}(w)|w|^{1-\alpha}$ has $w$-derivative $(1-\alpha)|w|^{-\alpha}$ and $dw/dz=-1$.

nodes.title: Semilinear kernel form
nodes.statement_html: Let $1<\alpha<2$, $p=\alpha-1$, $\epsilon\ge0$, $f\in W^{2,\infty}_{\textup{loc}}(\R)$ with $f'\in L^\infty(\R)$. Then for every $y\in\R$ \[ \frac{\sq{\mc J}_\epsilon(f)(y)}{A_\epsilon(f'(y))}=\mc I_\epsilon(f)(y), \qquad\text{hence}\qquad \mc E_\epsilon(f)=|D|^pf'+B_\epsilon(f')(f-yf')+\mc I_\epsilon(f). \]
nodes.proof_html: Fix $y$, $u=f'(y)$, $S=S_f(y,z)$, $K=\|f'\|_\infty$, $L=\|f''\|_{L^\infty(y-1,y+1)}$. Step 1. Dividing the absolutely convergent integral (lem:c03_I_well_defined) by $A_\epsilon(u)>0$: \begin{equation} \frac{\sq{\mc J}_\epsilon(f)(y)}{A_\epsilon(u)}=c_\alpha\int_\R\frac{u-f'(z)}{|y-z|^\alpha}\Bigl(\frac{A_\epsilon(S)}{A_\epsilon(u)}-1\Bigr)dz . \end{equation} Step 2. By lem:c03_secant_ibp, for $z\ne y$ the integrand equals $c_\alpha|y-z|^{-\alpha}(S-u)(1-\frac{A_\epsilon(S)}{A_\epsilon(u)})-c_\alpha(y-z)|y-z|^{-\alpha}\partial_zP_\epsilon(u,S)$. The first term is absolutely integrable: $O(|y-z|^{2-\alpha})$ for $|y-z|\le1$ (as $|S-u|\le L|y-z|/2$ and $|1-A_\epsilon(S)/A_\epsilon(u)|\le C|S-u|$) and $O(|y-z|^{-\alpha})$ at infinity. Hence so is the second. Step 3 (integration by parts on $\{\delta\le|y-z|\le M\}$). On each of $[y-M,y-\delta]$ and $[y+\delta,y+M]$, both factors are $C^1$; by lem:c03_secant_ibp \[ -\int_{\delta\le|y-z|\le M}\frac{y-z}{|y-z|^\alpha}\partial_zP_\epsilon(u,S)dz =p\int_{\delta\le|y-z|\le M}\frac{P_\epsilon(u,S)}{|y-z|^\alpha}dz-\Bigl[\frac{y-z}{|y-z|^\alpha}P_\epsilon(u,S)\Bigr]_{\text{4 endpoints}} . \] Boundary terms: by lem:c03_Gamma_quadratic_factor, $|P_\epsilon(u,S)|\le C(S-u)^2\le CL^2|y-z|^2$, so the terms at $|y-z|=\delta$ are $O(\delta^{3-\alpha})\to0$; $|P_\epsilon(u,S)|\le|S-u|(1+B_\epsilon(u))\le 2K(1+B_\epsilon(u))$, so the terms at $|y-z|=M$ are $O(M^{1-\alpha})=O(M^{-p})\to0$. Step 4. Letting $\delta\to0$, $M\to\infty$ (dominated convergence for the absolutely integrable pieces; $P_\epsilon(u,S)|y-z|^{-\alpha}$ is absolutely integrable by the same two bounds) gives $\sq{\mc J}_\epsilon(f)(y)/A_\epsilon(u)=\int|y-z|^{-\alpha}\Gamma_\epsilon(u,S)dz=\mc I_\epsilon(f)(y)$ by the definition of $\Gamma_\epsilon$. Step 5. Substitute into $\mc E_\epsilon(f)=|D|^pf'+B_\epsilon(f')(f-yf'+\sq{\mc J}_\epsilon(f))$ (def:residual).

nodes.title: Nonperturbative coefficient
nodes.statement_html: For real $p,\epsilon$ define \[ c_\epsilon=c_\alpha\int_0^1\bigl[A_\epsilon(t)-1\bigr](1-t)^{p-1}\,dt, \qquad \alpha=p+1. \] The integral is understood as the total Bochner integral in Lean; its role in the kernel and its quantitative bound for $0<p<1$, $0\le\epsilon\le1$ are proved separately below.

nodes.title: The nonperturbative coefficient
nodes.statement_html: Let $1<\alpha<2$, $0\le\epsilon\le1$, $W(y)=\max\{-y,0\}$ and let $\chi_+\in C^\infty(\R)$ with $\chi_+=1$ on $[2,\infty)$, $\chi_+=0$ on $(-\infty,1]$. For $y>1$ the integral $\int_\R\frac{\partial_1\Gamma_\epsilon(W'(y),S_W(y,z))}{|y-z|^\alpha}dz$ converges absolutely; define $b_\epsilon(y)$ as $\chi_+(y)$ times this integral for $y>1$, and $b_\epsilon(y)=0$ for $y\le1$.
