nodes.statement_html: For every $j\ge0$ there is an admissible $C_j$ such that for $\epsilon\in[0,\epsilon_0]$, $\mu\in\ov B$, $R\ge R_0$ and $y\ge R$, eqn:approx_phase_difference, eqn:approx_lambda_difference, eqn:approx_Z_difference hold, and \begin{equation} |\p^j_yf_{\textup{osc}}(y)|\le C_j\min\bigl\{\epsilon\ang y^{-p-\beta+\frac jp},\ \ang y^{-\beta+\frac{j-1}p}\bigr\}. \end{equation} ($f_{\textup{osc}}=0$ on $(-\infty,R]$.) Consequently \begin{equation} \|f_{\textup{osc}}\|_{L^1(\R)}\le C\epsilon R^{1-p-\beta}\le C\epsilon . \end{equation}
nodes.proof_html: The first three are lem:c04_lambda_psi_difference, lem:c04_Z_difference. For $y\ge R\ge2$, $y\le\ang y\le\sqrt2y$, so it suffices to prove the bounds with $y$. $j=0$: $|f_{\textup{osc}}|\le2|\int_y^\infty(Z-\frac\mu{\mu_*}Z_0)|+2|c_{\textup{cubic}}\int_y^\infty Z^3|\le C\epsilon y^{-p-\beta}$ by lem:c04_Z_primitive(b),(c); and $|f_{\textup{osc}}|\le2|\int Z|+2|\frac\mu{\mu_*}||\int Z_0|+2|c_{\textup{cubic}}\int Z^3|\le Cy^{-\beta-1/p}$ by (a) (also for $Z_0$), (c). $j\ge1$: by Leibniz, $\p^jf_{\textup{osc}}=-2\sum_{k}\binom jk\p^{j-k}\chi_R\,\p^k\operatorname{Re}F$ with $F(y)=\int_y^\infty(Z+c_{\textup{cubic}}Z^3-\frac\mu{\mu_*}Z_0)$ and $\p^kF=-\p^{k-1}(Z+c_{\textup{cubic}}Z^3-\frac\mu{\mu_*}Z_0)$ for $k\ge1$. By eqn:approx_Z_difference and lem:c04_Z_bounds, $|\p^{k-1}(Z-\frac\mu{\mu_*}Z_0)|\le C\epsilon y^{-p-\beta+k/p}$, $|c_{\textup{cubic}}\p^{k-1}Z^3|\le C\epsilon y^{-3\beta+(k-1)/p}\le C\epsilon y^{-p-\beta+k/p}$ (as $2\beta+1/p\ge p$), and also $|\p^{k-1}(\cdots)|\le Cy^{-\beta+(k-1)/p}$. The factors $\p^{j-k}\chi_R$, $j-k\ge1$, are supported in $[R,2R]$ where $R^{-(j-k)}\le2^{j-k}y^{-(j-k)}\le2^{j-k}y^{(j-k)/p}$; combine with the $k$-th term bounds (the $k=0$ term uses the $j=0$ bounds). Finally $\int_R^\infty C\epsilon y^{-p-\beta}dy=\frac{C\epsilon}{p+\beta-1}R^{1-p-\beta}$, and $p+\beta>1$, $R\ge1$.

nodes.title: Profile bounds
nodes.statement_html: For every $j\ge0$ there is an admissible $C_j$ such that for all $\epsilon\in[0,\epsilon_0]$, $\mu\in\ov B$, $R\ge R_0$: \[ |\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu}(y)|\le C_0\ang y^{-p},\qquad|\p^{j+1}\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu}(y)|\le C_j\ang y^{-\beta+\frac jp}\qquad(y\ge0), \] \[ |\p^j(\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu}(y)+y)|\le C_j\ang y^{-p-j}\qquad(y\le0). \] Moreover, for each $\epsilon$ and $k\ge0$, $\mu\mapsto\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu}$ is continuous from $\ov B$ into $C^k(K)$ for every compact $K\subset\R$ (in particular into $C^2_{\textup{loc}}$). $\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu}$ is real-valued and $C^\infty$.
nodes.proof_html: Smoothness/reality: lem:c04_family_regions. Bounds for $f_{\textup{slow}}$ (all $y$): since $\chi_R(\pm y)$ is supported in $|y|\ge R\ge2$, and $|\p^l\chi_R|\le CR^{-l}\le C2^ly^{-l}$ on its support (where $|y|\le2R$ when $l\ge1$), $|\p^jf_{\textup{slow}}|\le C_j\epsilon\ang y^{-p-j}$. Case $y\ge0$. Using $f_0=f_{0,\textup{low}}+2\operatorname{Re}f_{0,+}$: $\ov f=f_{0,\textup{low}}+2\operatorname{Re}[\frac\mu{\mu_*}f_{0,+}]+f_{\textup{slow}}+f_{\textup{osc}}$. Here $W=0$ so $|\p^jf_{0,\textup{low}}|\le C\ang y^{-p-j}$ (lem:approx_linear_seed(2) for $y\ge1$, continuity on $[0,1]$), and $\ang y^{-p-1-j}\le\ang y^{-\beta+j/p}$ ($\beta\le p+1$). For $y\ge R_0$: $f_{0,+}(y)=-\int_y^\infty Z_0$, so $|f_{0,+}|\le Cy^{-\beta-1/p}\le Cy^{-p}$ (lem:c04_Z_primitive(a) at $\epsilon=0$ with $R=R_0$; $Z_0$ does not depend on $R$), and $|\p^{j+1}f_{0,+}|\le Cy^{-\beta+j/p}$ (lem:c04_seed_amplitude); on $[0,R_0]$ use continuity. $|\mu/\mu_*|\le2$. $f_{\textup{osc}}$: eqn:approx_fosc_bounds, second entry ($j=0$: $\ang y^{-\beta-1/p}\le\ang y^{-p}$). Case $y\le0$. $f_{\textup{osc}}=0$ and $\ov f+y=(f_0+y)+2\operatorname{Re}[(\frac\mu{\mu_*}-1)f_{0,+}]+f_{\textup{slow}}$; use lem:approx_linear_seed(2) for $y\le-1$ and smoothness on $[-1,0]$, lem:c04_f0plus_negative (with $N=p+j$) and continuity on $[-1,0]$, and the $f_{\textup{slow}}$ bound. Constants: none depends on $\epsilon,\mu,R$. Continuity in $\mu$. $f_{0,\mu}$ is $\R$-affine in $\mu$ with fixed smooth coefficients; $f_{\textup{slow}}$ is independent of $\mu$. In $f_{\textup{osc}}$, $\mu$ enters through $\mu$, $\mu/\mu_*$ and $c_{\textup{log}}(\mu)$, so $(\mu,t)\mapsto Z_{\epsilon,\mu}(t)$ and all its $t$-derivatives are jointly continuous on $\ov B\times(R/2,\infty)$. On a compact $K$, $\p^kf_{\textup{osc}}$ is a finite combination of $\p^l\chi_R$ times either $\int_y^\infty(\cdots)$ (continuous in $\mu$ uniformly in $y\in K$ by dominated convergence, majorant $Ct^{-\beta}$, lem:c04_Z_bounds) or $t$-derivatives of the integrand (uniformly continuous on $\ov B\times K$).

nodes.title: $\mc Q_\epsilon$ at the corner
nodes.statement_html: For $\epsilon\ge0$ and $y>0$, the integral $\mc Q_\epsilon(W)(y):=c_\alpha\int_\R\frac{W'(y)-W'(z)}{|y-z|^\alpha}\bigl(A_\epsilon(S_W(y,z))-1\bigr)dz$ converges absolutely and equals $c_\epsilon y^{-p}$.
nodes.proof_html: For $z\ge0$, $W'(y)=W'(z)=0$. For $z<0$, $W'(y)-W'(z)=1$ and $S_W(y,z)=\frac{0-(-z)}{y-z}=\frac z{y-z}\in(-1,0)$, so the integrand is bounded by $(y-z)^{-\alpha}$, integrable on $(-\infty,0)$. Substituting $t=-z/(y-z)$ ($y-z=y/(1-t)$, $dz=-y(1-t)^{-2}dt$) gives $c_\alpha y^{-p}\int_0^1[A_\epsilon(-t)-1](1-t)^{p-1}dt=c_\epsilon y^{-p}$, as in the proof of lem:analysis_coefficient.

nodes.title: Residual decomposition
nodes.statement_html: Fix $\chi\in C_c^\infty((\frac14,4);[0,1])$ with $\chi=1$ on $[\frac12,3]$. For $Y\ge8R$ let $\chi_Y(z):=\chi(z/Y)$ (so $|\p^j\chi_Y|\le\|\chi^{(j)}\|_\infty Y^{-j}$) and \begin{equation} v_Y(z)=-2\chi_Y(z)\operatorname{Re}\int_z^\infty\bigl(Z(t)+c_{\textup{cubic}}Z(t)^3\bigr)dt\quad(z>R),\qquad v_Y(z)=0\ (z\le R). \end{equation} $\mc Q_\epsilon$ is def:c01_Q_eps and $\mc Q_{\epsilon,3}$ is eqn:approx_cubic_operator. For $h\in\mathcal A$ and $y>0$ define (the Gateaux derivative of $\mc Q_\epsilon$ at the corner $W$, written with $W'(y)-W'(z)=\mathbf 1_{z<0}$, $A_\epsilon(S_W)-1=0$ for $z\ge0$) \[ D\mc Q_\epsilon(W)[h](y):=c_\alpha\int_{-\infty}^0\Bigl[(h'(y)-h'(z))\Bigl(A_\epsilon\Bigl(\frac z{y-z}\Bigr)-1\Bigr)+A_\epsilon'\Bigl(\frac z{y-z}\Bigr)S_h(y,z)\Bigr]\frac{dz}{(y-z)^\alpha}, \] absolutely convergent ($|h'|,|S_h|\le\|h'\|_\infty$, $(y-z)^{-\alpha}\in L^1(-\infty,0)$). With $f=\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu}$, for $y>R$ set \begin{align} \mc E_1&=\mc L_0(f_{\textup{slow}})+\mc Q_\epsilon(W),\\ \mc E_2&=2\Bigl(\lambda^p-y-p\lambda_0^{p-1}\frac{c_{\textup{log}}(\mu)}y+c_\epsilon y^{-p}\Bigr)\operatorname{Re}Z,\\ \mc E_3&=2\Bigl(p\lambda_0^{p-1}\frac{c_{\textup{log}}(\mu)}y+n_\epsilon\lambda^p|Z|^2\Bigr)\operatorname{Re}Z,\\ \mc E_4&=2c_{\textup{cubic}}\bigl(\lambda^p-y+c_\epsilon y^{-p}\bigr)\operatorname{Re}(Z^3),\\ \mc E_5^{Y}&=\mc L_0(f_{\textup{osc}})+\mc Q_{\epsilon,3}(v_Y)-2\bigl(\lambda^p-y+n_\epsilon\lambda^p|Z|^2\bigr)\operatorname{Re}Z-2c_{\textup{cubic}}(\lambda^p-y)\operatorname{Re}(Z^3),\\ \mc E_6&=D\mc Q_\epsilon(W)[f-W]-2c_\epsilon y^{-p}\operatorname{Re}\bigl(Z+c_{\textup{cubic}}Z^3\bigr),\\ \mc E_7^{Y}&=\mc Q_{\epsilon,3}(\chi_Yf)-\mc Q_{\epsilon,3}(v_Y),\\ \mc E_8^{Y}&=\mc Q_\epsilon(\chi_Yf)-\mc Q_{\epsilon,3}(\chi_Yf),\\ \mc E_9^{Y}&=\mc Q_\epsilon(f)-\mc Q_\epsilon(W)-D\mc Q_\epsilon(W)[f-W]-\mc Q_\epsilon(\chi_Yf). \end{align} (Here $f-W$ is used only through $(f-W)'$ and $S_{f-W}$, which are bounded since $f'$ is bounded; $f-W\notin C^1$ at $0$ but $D\mc Q_\epsilon(W)[f-W](y)$ only involves $z<0<y$, where the formula makes sense with $(f-W)'(y)=f'(y)$, $(f-W)'(z)=f'(z)+1$.) We write $\mc E_k$ for $\mc E_k^Y$ when $Y$ is fixed.

nodes.title: Convergence needed for the residual decomposition
nodes.statement_html:
Fix $\frac34<p<1$ and $0<\delta\le |\mu_*|/2$. There are $\epsilon_0\in(0,1]$ and $R_0\ge2$ such that, for every $R\ge R_0$, $\epsilon\in[0,\epsilon_0]$, $\mu\in\ov B(\mu_*,\delta)$, $Y\ge8R$, and $y>R$, $f_{\textup{slow}}$ and $f_{\textup{osc}}$ are differentiable on $\R$ and the following kernels are in $L^1(dz)$ (write $f=\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu}$):
  • $\dfrac{u'(y)-u'(z)}{|y-z|^{p+1}}$ for $u\in\{f_{0,\mu},f_{\textup{slow}},f_{\textup{osc}}\}$;
  • $\dfrac{u'(y)-u'(z)}{|y-z|^{p+1}}[A_\epsilon(S_u(y,z))-1]$ for $u\in\{f,\chi_Y f,W\}$;
  • $\dfrac{v'(y)-v'(z)}{|y-z|^{p+1}}S_v(y,z)^2$ for $v\in\{v_Y,\chi_Y f\}$;
  • on $(-\infty,0)$, with $h=f-W$, \[ \frac{(h'(y)-h'(z))[A_\epsilon(z/(y-z))-1] +A_\epsilon'(z/(y-z))S_h(y,z)}{(y-z)^{p+1}}. \]
The choices of $\epsilon_0,R_0$ are made before $R,\epsilon,\mu,Y,y$.
nodes.proof_html: The seed and family have bounded first derivatives and locally Lipschitz first derivatives; the same is true for the slow and oscillatory pieces. The functions $\chi_Y f,v_Y$ are smooth with compact support. For each such profile the difference of first derivatives is $O(|y-z|)$ locally, and the secant is bounded. Thus the first three kernel types are dominated near $z=y$ by $C|y-z|^{-p}$ and at infinity by $C|y-z|^{-p-1}$. For $W$, use lem:c04_QW. The last kernel only involves $z<0<y$: $h'$ and $S_h$ are bounded, and $(y-z)^{-p-1}$ is integrable on $(-\infty,0)$. The family lemmas supply common thresholds after taking a minimum in $\epsilon_0$ and a maximum in $R_0$. This node records the analytic convergence obligations explicitly.

nodes.title: Linear reduction of the residual
nodes.statement_html: Let $p,R,\epsilon,y\in\R$ and $\mu\in\C$. Suppose that $f_{0,\mu},f_{\textup{slow}},f_{\textup{osc}}$ are differentiable on $\R$, that $z\mapsto(u'(y)-u'(z))|y-z|^{-p-1}$ is integrable for each of these three functions, and that $\mc L_0f_{0,\mu}(y)=G_\mu(y)$. Then, with $f=f_{0,\mu}+f_{\textup{slow}}+f_{\textup{osc}}$, \[ \sq{\mc E}_\epsilon(f)(y)-G_\mu(y) =\mc L_0f_{\textup{slow}}(y)+\mc L_0f_{\textup{osc}}(y)+\mc Q_\epsilon(f)(y). \]
nodes.proof_html:
Differentiate the sum. Absolute convergence permits addition of the three fractional
  derivative integrals. Expand $\mc L_0$ and
  $\sq{\mc E}_\epsilon(f)=\mc L_0f+\mc Q_\epsilon(f)$, then cancel $\mc L_0f_{0,\mu}=G_\mu$.

nodes.title: Algebraic cancellation of the nine residual pieces
nodes.statement_html: For all $p,R,\epsilon,Y,y\in\R$ and $\mu\in\C$, the expressions in def:residual_decomposition satisfy the algebraic identity \[ \mc L_0f_{\textup{slow}}(y)+\mc L_0f_{\textup{osc}}(y)+\mc Q_\epsilon(f)(y) =\sum_{k=1}^9\mc E_k^Y(y). \] Here the expressions are the total Lean definitions; convergence in the analytic parameter range is supplied separately by lem:c04_residual_integrability.
nodes.proof_html:
Expand the nine definitions and use
  $\operatorname{Re}(Z+c_{\textup{cubic}}Z^3)
   =\operatorname{Re}Z+c_{\textup{cubic}}\operatorname{Re}(Z^3)$.
  The $\lambda^p$, $y$, $c_{\textup{log}}$, $n_\epsilon$, and $c_\epsilon$ terms cancel.
  The remaining terms $\mc Q_\epsilon(W)$, $D\mc Q_\epsilon(W)[f-W]$,
  $\mc Q_{\epsilon,3}(v_Y)$, and $\mc Q_{\epsilon,3}(\chi_Y f)$ cancel pairwise.
  This is a polynomial identity in the values of the named expressions.

nodes.title: Residual identity
nodes.statement_html: For $\epsilon\in[0,\epsilon_0]$, $\mu\in\ov B$, $Y\ge8R$ and every $y>R$, all terms in def:residual_decomposition are finite and \begin{equation} \sq{\mc E}_\epsilon(f)(y)-G_\mu(y)=\mc L_0(f_{\textup{slow}})(y)+\mc L_0(f_{\textup{osc}})(y)+\mc Q_\epsilon(f)(y)=\sum_{k=1}^9\mc E_k^{Y}(y). \end{equation}
nodes.proof_html: Choose the common thresholds from lem:c04_residual_integrability; all integral expressions then converge absolutely. The seed is smooth and $\mc L_0f_{0,\mu}=G_\mu$ by lem:approx_linear_seed(3), so the first equality is lem:c04_residual_linear_identity. The second equality is exactly lem:c04_residual_sum_algebra. No additional parameter threshold is needed.

nodes.title: $C^1$ regularity of the residual terms near the window $Y\le y\le2Y$
nodes.statement_html:
Let $\frac34<p<1$. For every $\delta\in(0,|\mu_*|/2]$ there are $\epsilon_0\in(0,1]$ and $R_0\ge2$ such that for all $R\ge R_0$, $\epsilon\in[0,\epsilon_0]$ and $\mu\in\ov B$:
  • $\mc E_2$, $\mc E_3$, $\mc E_4$ are $C^1$ on $(R,\infty)$;
  • for every $Y\ge8R$: $\mc E_5^Y$ is $C^1$ at every $y\in[Y,2Y]$, and $\mc E_7^Y$, $\mc E_8^Y$, $\mc E_9^Y$ are $C^1$ on $J_Y=(3Y/4,5Y/2)$;
  • consequently, for every $Y\ge8R$, $\mc E_2,\mc E_3,\mc E_4,\mc E_7^Y,\mc E_8^Y,\mc E_9^Y$ are $C^1$ on $J_Y$ and $\mc E_5^Y$ is $C^1$ at every point of $[Y,2Y]$.
nodes.proof_html: (1) $\mc E_2,\mc E_3,\mc E_4$ are explicit expressions in $y$, $\lambda$, $\lambda_0$, $|Z|^2$ and $Z$, all $C^\infty$ on $(R,\infty)$ with $\lambda>0$ there (lem:c04_phase_basic). (2) Take $\epsilon_0$ below the thresholds of lem:c07_E5_C1 and $\min\{1,\epsilon_0^*(\delta)\}$ of the chapter on $\mc E_6$--$\mc E_9$, and $R_0$ above all thresholds. $\mc Q_{\epsilon,3}(v_Y)$ is $C^1$ on $\R$ (lem:c06_cubic_vY_C1), so lem:c07_E5_C1 applies at each $y\in[Y,2Y]$; $\mc E_7^Y$, $\mc E_8^Y$ are $C^1$ on $\R$ (lem:c06_E7_C1, lem:c06_E8_C1) and $\mc E_9^Y$ on $J_Y$ (lem:c06_E9_C1). (3) $J_Y\subset(R,\infty)$ since $3Y/4\ge6R$.

nodes.title: Residual bound for $y\ge8R$
nodes.statement_html: There is an admissible constant $C$ (it may also depend on $R$ through the constants of prop:approx_E6, lem:approx_E7, lem:approx_E8, lem:approx_E9, prop:approx_E5_linear, prop:approx_E5_cubic) such that for all $\epsilon\in[0,\epsilon_0]$, $\mu\in\ov B$, the function $\sq{\mc E}_\epsilon(\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu})-G_\mu$ is $C^1$ on $(8R,\infty)$ and \[ |\p^j(\sq{\mc E}_\epsilon(\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu})-G_\mu)(y)|\le C\epsilon\ang y^{-2p-1+\frac jp},\qquad y\ge8R,\ j=0,1 . \] In particular, for every $\gamma\le2p+1$ (hence every admissible $\gamma$), $|\p^j(\sq{\mc E}_\epsilon(\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu})-G_\mu)(y)|\le C\epsilon\ang y^{-\gamma+j/p}$ for $y\ge8R$, $j=0,1$.
nodes.proof_html: Fix $y_1\ge8R$ and take $Y=y_1$. By lem:c04_residual_identity the identity eqn:approx_residual_decomposition holds on $(R,\infty)$ for this $Y$; each $\mc E_k^Y$ is $C^1$ near $[Y,2Y]$ (lem:c04_residual_terms_C1 for $k=2,3,4,5,7,8,9$; prop:approx_E1 and prop:approx_E6 for $k=1,6$) and satisfies at $y=y_1\in[Y,2Y]$ (with $\epsilon^2\le\epsilon$): $\mc E_1$: $C\epsilon y^{-2p-1-j}$ (prop:approx_E1); $\mc E_2$: $C\epsilon y^{-2p-1-\beta+j/p}$ (prop:approx_E2); $\mc E_3$: $C\epsilon(y^{-p-3\beta+j/p}+y^{1-5\beta+j/p})$ (prop:approx_E3); $\mc E_4$: $C\epsilon y^{1-5\beta+j/p}$ (prop:approx_E4); $\mc E_5$: $C\epsilon y^{-2p-1+j/p}$ (prop:approx_E5_cubic, which combines prop:approx_E5_linear); $\mc E_6$: $C\epsilon y^{-2p-1+j/p}$ (prop:approx_E6); $\mc E_7$: $C\epsilon y^{-2p-1+j/p}$ (lem:approx_E7); $\mc E_8$: $C\epsilon y^{-2p-1+j/p}$ (lem:approx_E8); $\mc E_9$: $C\epsilon y^{-p-2+j/p}$ (lem:approx_E9). Each exponent is $\le-2p-1+j/p$: $-2p-1-j\le-2p-1+j/p$; $p+3\beta-(2p+1)=(p+1)(\frac3{2p}-1)>0$; $5\beta-1-(2p+1)=\frac{5+p-4p^2}{2p}>0$ for $p<1$; $p+2>2p+1$. Since $y\ge8R\ge16$, $y^{-a}\le2^{a/2}\ang y^{-a}$ for $a\ge0$ and all exponents $-2p-1+j/p$ are negative ($1/p<2p+1$). Sum the nine bounds. The last claim: $\ang y^{-2p-1}\le\ang y^{-\gamma}$ for $\gamma\le2p+1$.

nodes.title: $\mc E_1$ is a fractional derivative of $f_{\textup{slow}}$
nodes.statement_html: For $y\ge2R$: $\mc E_1(y)=|D|^pf_{\textup{slow}}'(y)$, and the same holds for the first derivatives (both sides are $C^1$ on $(R,\infty)$ and their derivatives agree on $[2R,\infty)$). Moreover $|\p^kf_{\textup{slow}}(y)|\le C_k\epsilon\ang y^{-p-k}$ for all $y\in\R$, $k\ge0$.
nodes.proof_html: By lem:c04_QW, $\mc Q_\epsilon(W)=c_\epsilon y^{-p}$. On $[2R,\infty)$, $f_{\textup{slow}}=c_+y^{-p}$ together with all derivatives ($\chi_R-1$ vanishes on $[2R,\infty)$), so $f_{\textup{slow}}-yf_{\textup{slow}}'=(1+p)c_+y^{-p}=-c_\epsilon y^{-p}$ there, also after one differentiation. $C^1$: lem:c04_frac_derivative with $g=f_{\textup{slow}}'$. The bound on $f_{\textup{slow}}$ is as in the proof of prop:approx_profile_bounds.

nodes.title: Near-diagonal part of $|D|^p$ on decaying functions
nodes.statement_html: Fix $\chi^\flat\in C_c^\infty((-\frac12,\frac12);[0,1])$ with $\chi^\flat=1$ on $[-\frac14,\frac14]$. Let $k\in\{0,1\}$, $K>0$, $h\in C^{3}(\R)$ with $|\p^lh(z)|\le K\ang z^{-p-l}$ for $0\le l\le3$, $z\in\R$. Then for $y\ge2$, \[\Bigl|c_\alpha\int_\R\chi^\flat\Bigl(\frac{y-z}y\Bigr)\frac{h^{(k+1)}(y)-h^{(k+1)}(z)}{|y-z|^{1+p}}dz\Bigr|\le C(p)Ky^{-2p-1-k}.\]

nodes.title: Far part of $|D|^p$ on decaying functions
nodes.statement_html: With $\chi^\flat,k,K,h$ as in lem:c04_frac_decay_near and $y\ge2$, \[\Bigl|c_\alpha\int_\R\Bigl(1-\chi^\flat\Bigl(\frac{y-z}y\Bigr)\Bigr)\frac{h^{(k+1)}(y)-h^{(k+1)}(z)}{|y-z|^{1+p}}dz\Bigr|\le C(p,\chi^\flat)Ky^{-2p-1-k}.\]
nodes.proof_html: Let $\kappa_y(z):=(1-\chi^\flat(\frac{y-z}y))|y-z|^{-1-p}$, smooth (it vanishes for $|y-z|\le y/4$). The $h^{(k+1)}(y)$ term: $|h^{(k+1)}(y)|\int_{|y-z|\ge y/4}|y-z|^{-1-p}\le CKy^{-p-1-k}y^{-p}$. The $h^{(k+1)}(z)$ term: integrate by parts $k+1$ times in $z$ (boundary terms at $\pm\infty$ vanish since $h^{(l)}$ is bounded and $\kappa_y^{(l)}$ decays); $|\p_z^l\kappa_y(z)|\le C_l|y-z|^{-1-p-l}\mathbf 1_{|y-z|\ge y/4}$, because the derivatives falling on $\chi^\flat$ produce factors $y^{-1}\le\frac12|y-z|^{-1}$ on $\operatorname{supp}(\chi^\flat)'(\frac{y-\cdot}y)$. Thus the term is $\le CK\int_{|y-z|\ge y/4}\ang z^{-p}|y-z|^{-2-p-k}dz$. Split: $|z|\le2y$ gives $\le(y/4)^{-2-p-k}\int_{|z|\le2y}\ang z^{-p}\le Cy^{-2-p-k}y^{1-p}$; $|z|>2y$ gives $|y-z|\ge|z|/2$ and $\le C\int_{|z|>2y}|z|^{-2-2p-k}\le Cy^{-1-2p-k}$.

nodes.title: Control of $\mc E_1$
nodes.statement_html: There is an admissible $C$ with, for $\epsilon\in[0,\epsilon_0]$, $\mu\in\ov B$, $y\ge2R$, $j=0,1$: \begin{equation} |\p^j\mc E_1(y)|\le C\epsilon\ang y^{-2p-1-j}, \end{equation} hence $|\p^j\mc E_1(y)|\le C\epsilon\ang y^{-\gamma+j/p}$ for every $\gamma\le2p+1$.
nodes.proof_html: By lem:c04_E1_formula, $\p^j\mc E_1=\p^j|D|^pf_{\textup{slow}}'=|D|^pf_{\textup{slow}}^{(j+1)}$ on $[2R,\infty)$ (lem:c04_frac_derivative), and $h=f_{\textup{slow}}$ satisfies the hypotheses of lem:c04_frac_decay_near with $K=C\epsilon$. Split $|D|^ph^{(j+1)}$ with $\chi^\flat+(1-\chi^\flat)$ and apply lem:c04_frac_decay_near, lem:c04_frac_decay_far with $k=j$; $y\ge2R\ge4$, $y\approx\ang y$. Finally $-2p-1-j\le-\gamma+j/p$.

nodes.title: Second-order Taylor remainder of $\lambda^p$
nodes.statement_html: Let $g(x)=(1+x)^p-1-px$. For $y\ge R$: $\lambda^p-y-p\lambda_0^{p-1}\frac{c_{\textup{log}}(\mu)}y+c_\epsilon y^{-p}=y\,g(\sq\lambda)$, and $\lambda^p-y+c_\epsilon y^{-p}=pc_{\textup{log}}(\mu)y^{-1/p}+y\,g(\sq\lambda)$, with $|y\,g(\sq\lambda)|\le C\epsilon^2y^{-2p-1}$, $|\p_y(y\,g(\sq\lambda))|\le C\epsilon^2y^{-2p-2}$, and $|\p_y^k(\lambda^p-y+c_\epsilon y^{-p})|\le C\epsilon y^{-1/p-k}$ ($k=0,1$).
nodes.proof_html: $\lambda^p=\lambda_0^p(1+\sq\lambda)^p=y(1+\sq\lambda)^p$ and $py\sq\lambda=-c_\epsilon y^{-p}+pc_{\textup{log}}y^{-1/p}$, while $p\lambda_0^{p-1}c_{\textup{log}}/y=pc_{\textup{log}}y^{(p-1)/p-1}=pc_{\textup{log}}y^{-1/p}$. Taylor: for $|x|\le\frac12$, $g(x)=p(p-1)x^2\int_0^1(1-t)(1+tx)^{p-2}dt$, so $|g(x)|\le Cx^2$, $|g'(x)|=p|(1+x)^{p-1}-1|\le C|x|$. With $|\sq\lambda|\le C\epsilon y^{-p-1}$, $|\sq\lambda'|\le C\epsilon y^{-p-2}$: $|yg|\le C\epsilon^2y^{-2p-1}$, $|(yg)'|\le|g|+y|g'||\sq\lambda'|\le C\epsilon^2y^{-2p-2}$. The last claim uses $|c_{\textup{log}}|\le C\epsilon$ and $2p+1>1/p$ (as $p>\frac12$), $\epsilon\le1$.

nodes.title: Control of $\mc E_2$
nodes.statement_html: There is an admissible $C$ with $|\p^j\mc E_2(y)|\le C\epsilon^2\ang y^{-2p-1-\beta+j/p}$ for $y\ge2R$, $j=0,1$.
nodes.proof_html: $\mc E_2=2yg(\sq\lambda)\operatorname{Re}Z$ (lem:c04_lambda_taylor); Leibniz with $|\p^jZ|\le Cy^{-\beta+j/p}$ (lem:c04_Z_bounds): $j=1$ gives $C\epsilon^2(y^{-2p-2-\beta}+y^{-2p-1-\beta+1/p})$.

nodes.title: Cancellation in $\mc E_3$
nodes.statement_html: For $y\ge R$, \begin{equation} \mc E_3=2n_\epsilon|\mu|^2\Bigl(\frac{|a_*|^2}\lambda-\frac1{\lambda_0}\Bigr)\operatorname{Re}Z, \end{equation} and for $k=0,1$ \begin{equation} \Bigl|\p^k_y\Bigl(\frac{|a_*|^2}\lambda-\frac1{\lambda_0}\Bigr)\Bigr|\le Cy^{-1/p-k}\bigl(y^{-2\beta}+\epsilon y^{-p-1}\bigr). \end{equation}
nodes.proof_html: $p\lambda_0^{p-1}c_{\textup{log}}/y=-n_\epsilon|\mu|^2\lambda_0^{p-1}y^{-1}=-n_\epsilon|\mu|^2/\lambda_0$ (as $\lambda_0^p=y$), and $\lambda^p|Z|^2=|\mu|^2|a_*|^2\lambda^{-1}$ from eqn:approx_Z_definition. Next $\frac{|a_*|^2}\lambda-\frac1{\lambda_0}=\frac1{\lambda_0}\cdot\frac{|a_*|^2-1-\sq\lambda}{1+\sq\lambda}$, with $|\p^k(|a_*|^2-1)|\le Cy^{-2\beta-k}$ (lem:c04_seed_amplitude, $|a_*|^2-1=2\operatorname{Re}(a_*-1)+|a_*-1|^2$), $|\p^k\sq\lambda|\le C\epsilon y^{-p-1-k}$, $1+\sq\lambda\ge\frac12$, $|\p^k\lambda_0^{-1}|\le Cy^{-1/p-k}$. Leibniz.

nodes.title: Control of $\mc E_3$
nodes.statement_html: There is an admissible $C$ with, for $y\ge2R$, $j=0,1$, \begin{equation} |\p^j\mc E_3(y)|\le C\epsilon^2\ang y^{-p-3\beta+\frac jp}+C\epsilon\ang y^{1-5\beta+\frac jp}. \end{equation}
nodes.proof_html: By eqn:approx_E3_cancellation, eqn:approx_E3_coefficient_bounds, $|n_\epsilon|\le C\epsilon$, $|\mu|\le2|\mu_*|$ and $|\p^jZ|\le Cy^{-\beta+j/p}$: $|\p^j\mc E_3|\le C\epsilon y^{-3\beta-1/p+j/p}+C\epsilon^2y^{-\beta-1/p-p-1+j/p}$ (the derivative of the coefficient costs $y^{-1}\le y^{1/p}$). Now $3\beta+\frac1p=5\beta-1$ and $\beta+\frac1p+p+1=p+3\beta$ (as $\frac1p=2\beta-1$).

nodes.title: Control of $\mc E_4$
nodes.statement_html: There is an admissible $C$ with, for $y\ge2R$, $j=0,1$, \begin{equation} |\p^j\mc E_4(y)|\le C\epsilon^2\ang y^{1-5\beta+\frac jp}. \end{equation}
nodes.proof_html: $|c_{\textup{cubic}}|\le C\epsilon$, $|\p^k(\lambda^p-y+c_\epsilon y^{-p})|\le C\epsilon y^{-1/p-k}$ (lem:c04_lambda_taylor), $|\p^j(Z^3)|\le Cy^{-3\beta+j/p}$; Leibniz gives $C\epsilon^2y^{-1/p-3\beta+j/p}$ and $\frac1p+3\beta=5\beta-1$.

nodes.title: Standing hypotheses and notation for this chapter
nodes.statement_html:
Fix $p\in(3/4,1)$, $\alpha=1+p$, $\beta=\frac{p+1}{2p}$ (so $2\beta=1+\frac1p$). Let $c_\alpha>0$ be the constant with $|D|^ph(y)=c_\alpha\int_\R\frac{h(y)-h(z)}{|y-z|^{1+p}}\,dz$ for bounded $C^1$ functions $h$ (def:frac_multiplier); for complex-valued $h$ the same formula is used, so that $|D|^p(\operatorname{Re}h)=\operatorname{Re}|D|^ph$. For $g$ with $g'$ bounded and $C^1$ put $\mc{L}_0g:=|D|^pg'+g-yg'$ (this is $\mc{L}_\epsilon$ of def:L_eps at $\epsilon=0$).

Fix $\delta\in(0,|\mu_*|/2]$, $\mu_*=-i/\sqrt{2\pi p}$ (def:mu_star), and $\epsilon_0\in(0,\epsilon_0^*(\delta)]$, where $\epsilon_0^*(\delta)\in(0,1]$ is the minimum of the smallness thresholds for $\epsilon$ provided (for this $\delta$) by lem:c04_lambda_psi_difference, lem:c04_Z_bounds, lem:c04_Z_difference_products, lem:c04_Z_difference, lem:c04_lambda_taylor, lem:c04_Z_primitive, lem:c04_phase_exponential_difference and lem:approx_phase_differences (Lean: c05\_eps0\_star); put $\ov{B}=\ov{B}(\mu_*,\delta)$, the cutoff $\chi_+$ and the profile of $\chi_R$ as in def:approximate_solution_family. For every $Y>0$ let $\chi_Y\in C^\infty(\R;[0,1])$ be the cutoff of def:residual_decomposition: $\operatorname{supp}\chi_Y\subset(Y/4,4Y)$, $\chi_Y\equiv1$ on $[Y/2,3Y]$. We assume constants $K_j$ ($j\ge0$), independent of $R,Y$, with $|\partial^j\chi_R|\le K_jR^{-j}$ and $|\partial^j\chi_Y|\le K_jY^{-j}$.

A parameter tuple is $(\epsilon,\mu,R,Y)$ with $\epsilon\in[0,\epsilon_0]$, $\mu\in\ov{B}$, $R\ge R_0$, $Y\ge8R$, where $R_0\ge1$ depends only on $(p,\epsilon_0,\delta,\chi_+)$ and is so large that for all $y\ge R_0$: (R1) the bounds of lem:approx_linear_seed(1) hold and $|a_*(y)-1|\le\frac12$; (R2) writing $\lambda=\lambda_{\epsilon,\mu}=y^{1/p}(1+\sq{\lambda})$ with $\sq{\lambda}(y)=-\frac{c_\epsilon}{p}y^{-p-1}+c_{\textup{log}}(\mu)y^{-1-1/p}$ one has $|\sq{\lambda}(y)|\le\frac12$; (R3) the estimates of lem:approx_phase_differences hold on $[R,\infty)$.

Notation (all for $y\ge R$): $Z=Z_{\epsilon,\mu}$, $\lambda=\lambda_{\epsilon,\mu}$, $\Psi=\Psi_{\epsilon,\mu}$, $\Phi:=\Psi-\pi/4$, $A:=\mu a_*\lambda^{-(p+1)/2}$, so $Z=Ae^{i\Phi}$; $\lambda_0=y^{1/p}$, $\Psi_0$, $\Phi_0:=\Psi_0-\pi/4$, $A_0:=\mu a_*\lambda_0^{-(p+1)/2}$, so $\frac{\mu}{\mu_*}Z_0=A_0e^{i\Phi_0}$. The constants $c_\epsilon,n_\epsilon,c_{\textup{cubic}},c_{\textup{log}}(\mu)$, the cubic operator $\mc{Q}_{\epsilon,3}$, the function $f_{\textup{osc}}$, the local front $v_Y$ and $\mc{E}_5$ are those of def:approximate_solution_family, def:residual_decomposition; in particular $\mc{Q}_{\epsilon,3}(2\sin)(x)=2n_\epsilon\cos x-2(3^p-1)c_{\textup{cubic}}\cos(3x)$ and $v_Y(z)=-2\chi_Y(z)\operatorname{Re}\int_z^\infty(Z+c_{\textup{cubic}}Z^3)\,dt$.

An admissible constant is a number $C\in(0,\infty)$ depending only on $p,c_\alpha,\epsilon_0,\delta,\chi_+,(K_j)_j$ (and, where indicated, on an integer $k$), but not on the tuple $(\epsilon,\mu,R,Y)$ nor on the points $y,s,t,z$.

nodes.title: Smallness of the correction constants
nodes.statement_html: There is an admissible $C_0$ such that for all $\epsilon\in[0,\epsilon_0]$, $\mu\in\ov{B}$: $|c_\epsilon|+|n_\epsilon|+|c_{\textup{cubic}}|+|c_{\textup{log}}(\mu)|\le C_0\epsilon$.
nodes.proof_html: $|c_\epsilon|\lesssim\epsilon$ is lem:analysis_coefficient. By the lemma following the definition of $\mc{Q}_{\epsilon,3}$ in Chapter 4, $\mc{Q}_{\epsilon,3}(\sin)=c_1\cos+c_2\cos(3\cdot)$ with $|c_1|,|c_2|\lesssim\epsilon$. Cubic homogeneity gives $\mc{Q}_{\epsilon,3}(2\sin)=8\mc{Q}_{\epsilon,3}(\sin)$, so $n_\epsilon=4c_1$ and $c_{\textup{cubic}}=-4c_2/(3^p-1)$ (note $3^p-1>0$). Finally $|c_{\textup{log}}(\mu)|=|n_\epsilon||\mu|^2/p\le|n_\epsilon|(|\mu_*|+\delta)^2/p$.

nodes.title: Components of $\mc{E}_5$
nodes.statement_html: For a parameter tuple define the fundamental and third-harmonic parts of $f_{\textup{osc}}$, \begin{equation} f_{\textup{osc},1}(y)=-2\chi_R(y)\operatorname{Re}\int_y^\infty\Bigl(Z-\tfrac{\mu}{\mu_*}Z_0\Bigr)dt,\qquad f_{\textup{osc},3}(y)=-2c_{\textup{cubic}}\chi_R(y)\operatorname{Re}\int_y^\infty Z^3\,dt \end{equation} (both $:=0$ for $y\le R$; the improper integrals converge by lem:c05_primitive). For $y>2R$ define \begin{align} \mc{R}_{\textup{lin}}&:=\mc{L}_0(f_{\textup{osc}})-2(\lambda^p-y)\operatorname{Re}Z -2c_{\textup{cubic}}(3^p\lambda^p-y)\operatorname{Re}(Z^3),\\ \mc{R}_{\textup{cub}}&:=\mc{Q}_{\epsilon,3}(v_Y)-2n_\epsilon\lambda^p|Z|^2\operatorname{Re}Z +2c_{\textup{cubic}}(3^p-1)\lambda^p\operatorname{Re}(Z^3), \end{align} and \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} \mc{R}_{\textup{lin},1}&:=|D|^pf_{\textup{osc},1}'+f_{\textup{osc},1}-2\lambda^p\operatorname{Re}Z +2y\operatorname{Re}\Bigl(\tfrac{\mu}{\mu_*}Z_0\Bigr),\\ \mc{R}_{\textup{lin},3}&:=|D|^pf_{\textup{osc},3}'+f_{\textup{osc},3} -2c_{\textup{cubic}}3^p\lambda^p\operatorname{Re}(Z^3). \end{aligned} \end{equation} ($\mc{R}_{\textup{cub}}$ depends on $Y$ through $v_Y$; $\mc{R}_{\textup{lin}}$ does not.)

nodes.title: Localization, multiplier and primitive remainders
nodes.statement_html: For a parameter tuple, a function $g:\R\to\R$ and $y\in(Y/2,3Y)$ put \begin{equation} \mc{R}_{\textup{far},Y}[g](y):=c_\alpha\int_\R g(z)\,\partial_z\Bigl[\frac{1-\chi_Y(z)}{|y-z|^{1+p}}\Bigr]dz. \end{equation} Regard $\chi_YZ$, $\chi_Y\frac{\mu}{\mu_*}Z_0$, $\chi_YZ^3$ as functions in $C_c^\infty((Y/4,4Y))$ (extended by $0$). For $y\in(Y/2,3Y)$ define \begin{align*} \mc{E}_{\textup{mult}}&:=|D|^p(\chi_YZ)-\Bigl[\lambda^pZ+i\frac{(\lambda^p)'}{\lambda}Z-ip\mu a_*'\lambda^{(p-3)/2}e^{i\Phi}\Bigr],\\ \mc{E}_{\textup{mult},0}&:=|D|^p\Bigl(\chi_Y\tfrac{\mu}{\mu_*}Z_0\Bigr)-\Bigl[y\tfrac{\mu}{\mu_*}Z_0+\frac{i}{\lambda_0}\tfrac{\mu}{\mu_*}Z_0-ip\mu a_*'\lambda_0^{(p-3)/2}e^{i\Phi_0}\Bigr], \end{align*} and, for $y\ge R$, \begin{equation} \mc{R}_{\textup{prim}}(y):=2\operatorname{Re}\int_y^\infty\Bigl[e^{i\Phi(s)}\partial_s\Bigl(\frac{A(s)}{i\lambda(s)}\Bigr) -e^{i\Phi_0(s)}\partial_s\Bigl(\frac{A_0(s)}{i\lambda_0(s)}\Bigr)\Bigr]ds . \end{equation} (Note $A/(i\lambda)=\mu a_*/(i\lambda^{(p+3)/2})$, matching the paper.)

nodes.title: Frozen plane wave and cubic integrands
nodes.statement_html: For a parameter tuple and $y\ge R$ write $\lambda=\lambda(y)$ and define $P_y(z):=2\operatorname{Re}\bigl[\frac{Z(y)}{i\lambda}e^{i\lambda(z-y)}\bigr]$, $z\in\R$. For a function $h$ set $\Delta h(y,s):=h(y)-h(y-s)$; for $P_y$ the increment is always taken at the same base point $y$ that freezes $P_y$. Put $K_\epsilon:=-\frac{(p+1)\epsilon c_\alpha}{2}$ and \begin{align*} N_0(y,s)&:=\Delta v_Y'(\Delta v_Y)^2-\Delta P_y'(\Delta P_y)^2,\\ N_1(y,s)&:=\bigl[\Delta v_Y''(\Delta v_Y)^2-\Delta P_y''(\Delta P_y)^2\bigr] +2\bigl[(\Delta v_Y')^2\Delta v_Y-(\Delta P_y')^2\Delta P_y\bigr]. \end{align*} Finally $G(y):=2n_\epsilon\lambda^p|Z|^2\operatorname{Re}Z-2c_{\textup{cubic}}(3^p-1)\lambda^p\operatorname{Re}(Z^3)$ and $T_P(y):=\partial_z\bigl[\mc{Q}_{\epsilon,3}(P_y)(z)\bigr]_{z=y}$ ($y$ held fixed inside $P_y$).

nodes.title: Algebraic splitting of $\mc{E}_5$
nodes.statement_html: For every parameter tuple and $y>2R$: $\mc{E}_5(y)=\mc{R}_{\textup{lin}}(y)+\mc{R}_{\textup{cub}}(y)$ and $\mc{R}_{\textup{lin}}(y)=\mc{R}_{\textup{lin},1}(y)+\mc{R}_{\textup{lin},3}(y)$ (the latter is the splitting (eqn:approx\_E5\_linear\_split) of the paper).
nodes.proof_html: Adding eqn:approx_E5_linear_response and eqn:approx_E5_cubic_response, the $\operatorname{Re}(Z^3)$ coefficients combine to $-2c_{\textup{cubic}}(3^p\lambda^p-y)+2c_{\textup{cubic}}(3^p-1)\lambda^p =-2c_{\textup{cubic}}(\lambda^p-y)$, and the $\operatorname{Re}Z$ coefficients to $-2(\lambda^p-y+n_\epsilon\lambda^p|Z|^2)$, which is the definition of $\mc{E}_5$ (eqn:approx\_E5). For the second identity: $f_{\textup{osc}}=f_{\textup{osc},1}+f_{\textup{osc},3}$ by def:approximate_solution_family; for $y>2R$, $\chi_R\equiv1$ near $y$, so $f_{\textup{osc}}'(y)=2\operatorname{Re}(Z+c_{\textup{cubic}}Z^3-\frac{\mu}{\mu_*}Z_0)$ (fundamental theorem of calculus). Hence $-yf'_{\textup{osc}}+2y\operatorname{Re}Z+2c_{\textup{cubic}}y\operatorname{Re}Z^3=2y\operatorname{Re}(\frac{\mu}{\mu_*}Z_0)$, and $\mc{R}_{\textup{lin}}=|D|^pf'_{\textup{osc}}+f_{\textup{osc}}-2\lambda^p\operatorname{Re}Z-2c_{\textup{cubic}}3^p\lambda^p\operatorname{Re}Z^3+2y\operatorname{Re}(\frac{\mu}{\mu_*}Z_0)$; linearity of $|D|^p$ gives the split.

nodes.title: Symbol bounds for $Z$, $\lambda$, $A$
nodes.statement_html:
For every integer $k\ge0$ there is an admissible $C_k$ such that for every parameter tuple and every $y\ge R$:
  • $\frac12y^{1/p}\le\lambda(y)\le2y^{1/p}$, $|\partial^k\lambda(y)|\le C_ky^{1/p-k}$, $|\partial^k(\lambda-\lambda_0)(y)|\le C_k\epsilon y^{1/p-p-1-k}$, $|\partial^k(\Psi-\Psi_0)(y)|\le C_k\epsilon y^{1/p-p-k}$;
  • $|\partial^kA(y)|+|\partial^kA_0(y)|\le C_ky^{-\beta-k}$, $|\partial^k(A-A_0)(y)|\le C_k\epsilon y^{-\beta-p-1-k}$, $|\partial^ka_*'(y)|\le C_ky^{-2\beta-1-k}$;
  • $|\partial^kZ(y)|+|\partial^k(\tfrac{\mu}{\mu_*}Z_0)(y)|\le C_ky^{-\beta+k/p}$, $|\partial^k(Z^3)(y)|\le C_ky^{-3\beta+k/p}$; moreover $Z'-i\lambda Z=A'e^{i\Phi}$, hence $|Z'(y)-i\lambda(y)Z(y)|\le C_0y^{-\beta-1}$;
  • for $k\in\{0,1\}$: $|\partial^k((\lambda^p)'-1)(y)|\le C\epsilon y^{-p-1-k}$;
  • $|e^{i(\Psi-\Psi_0)(y)}-1|\le C\epsilon y^{1/p-p}$;
  • if $t\ge R$ and $|t-y|\le y/2$, then $\frac14\lambda(y)\le\lambda(t)\le4\lambda(y)$ and $|\lambda(t)-\lambda(y)|\le C\lambda(y)|t-y|/y$.
nodes.proof_html: (1) From (eqn:approx\_modified\_frequency) and $c_{\textup{power}}\frac{1-p^2}{p}=-\frac{c_\epsilon}{p}$ we get $\lambda=y^{1/p}(1+\sq\lambda)$ with $\sq\lambda$ as in (R2). Since $1+\frac1p>p+1$ and by lem:c05_small_constants, $|\partial^k\sq\lambda|\le C_k\epsilon y^{-p-1-k}$, and $|\sq\lambda|\le\frac12$ by (R2); the bounds on $\lambda$ and $\lambda-\lambda_0=y^{1/p}\sq\lambda$ follow by Leibniz; the $\Psi$ bound is (eqn:approx\_phase\_difference). (2) $a_*$: lem:approx_linear_seed(1) with $|a_*|\le\frac32$ (R1). $\lambda^{-(p+1)/2}=y^{-\beta}(1+\sq\lambda)^{-(p+1)/2}$ and $(1+x)^{-(p+1)/2}$ is smooth on $|x|\le\frac12$ (Fa\`a di Bruno); $|\mu|\le|\mu_*|+\delta$. For the difference, $A-A_0=\mu a_*y^{-\beta}[(1+\sq\lambda)^{-(p+1)/2}-1]$ and $|\partial^k[(1+\sq\lambda)^{-(p+1)/2}-1]|\le C_k\epsilon y^{-p-1-k}$. (3) $Z=Ae^{i\Phi}$, $\Phi'=\lambda$; $\partial^ke^{i\Phi}$ is $e^{i\Phi}$ times a polynomial in $\lambda,\dots,\lambda^{(k-1)}$ of weighted degree $k$, bounded by $C_ky^{k/p}$ (as $y^{1/p-1}\le y^{1/p}$); Leibniz. $Z^3=A^3e^{3i\Phi}$ likewise. $Z'=(A'+i\lambda A)e^{i\Phi}$. (4) $\lambda^p=y(1+\sq\lambda)^p$, so $(\lambda^p)'-1=[(1+\sq\lambda)^p-1]+py(1+\sq\lambda)^{p-1}\sq\lambda'$; use (1). (5) $|e^{ix}-1|\le|x|$ and (1). (6) $\lambda(t)/\lambda(y)=(t/y)^{1/p}(1+\sq\lambda(t))/(1+\sq\lambda(y))$ with $t/y\in[\frac12,\frac32]$, giving the two-sided bound; the mean value theorem with $|\lambda'|\le C_1\tau^{1/p-1}$, $\tau\in[y/2,3y/2]$, gives the last bound.

nodes.title: Primitives of $Z$ and $Z^3$
nodes.statement_html: For every parameter tuple and $z\ge R$ the improper integrals $\int_z^\infty Z$, $\int_z^\infty Z^3$ converge, \[ \int_z^\infty Z(t)\,dt=-\frac{Z(z)}{i\lambda(z)}-\int_z^\infty e^{i\Phi(t)}\partial_t\Bigl(\frac{A(t)}{i\lambda(t)}\Bigr)dt,\qquad \int_z^\infty Z(t)^3dt=-\frac{Z(z)^3}{3i\lambda(z)}-\int_z^\infty e^{3i\Phi}\partial_t\Bigl(\frac{A^3}{3i\lambda}\Bigr)dt, \] and there is an admissible $C$ with $|\int_z^\infty Z|\le Cz^{-\beta-1/p}$, $|\int_z^\infty Z^3|\le Cz^{-3\beta-1/p}$. The same holds with $(Z,A,\Phi,\lambda)$ replaced by $(\frac{\mu}{\mu_*}Z_0,A_0,\Phi_0,\lambda_0)$.
nodes.proof_html: On $[z,M]$ write $Z=\frac{A}{i\lambda}\partial_te^{i\Phi}$ and integrate by parts: $\int_z^MZ=[\frac{A}{i\lambda}e^{i\Phi}]_z^M-\int_z^Me^{i\Phi}\partial_t(\frac{A}{i\lambda})$. By lem:c05_symbol_bounds, $|A/\lambda|\le Ct^{-\beta-1/p}\to0$ and $|\partial_t(A/\lambda)|\le Ct^{-\beta-1/p-1}$, which is integrable; let $M\to\infty$. The bound follows: $Cz^{-\beta-1/p}+C\int_z^\infty t^{-\beta-1/p-1}dt$. For $Z^3=\frac{A^3}{3i\lambda}\partial_te^{3i\Phi}$ the same argument with $|A^3/\lambda|\le Ct^{-3\beta-1/p}$ and $|\partial_t(A^3/\lambda)|\le Ct^{-3\beta-1/p-1}$. Identical for the $0$-quantities.

nodes.title: Bounds on the two parts of $f_{\textup{osc}}$
nodes.statement_html: For every parameter tuple: $f_{\textup{osc},1},f_{\textup{osc},3}\in C^\infty(\R)$ vanish on $(-\infty,R]$, are bounded with bounded first derivative, $f_{\textup{osc}}=f_{\textup{osc},1}+f_{\textup{osc},3}$, and for $y\ge2R$, $f_{\textup{osc},1}'(y)=2\operatorname{Re}(Z-\frac{\mu}{\mu_*}Z_0)(y)$, $f_{\textup{osc},3}'(y)=2c_{\textup{cubic}}\operatorname{Re}(Z^3)(y)$. There is an admissible $C$ such that for all $y\ge R$ \[ |f_{\textup{osc},3}(y)|\le C\epsilon y^{-3\beta-1/p},\qquad |f_{\textup{osc},1}(y)|\le C\epsilon y^{-p-\beta},\qquad \|f_{\textup{osc},1}\|_{L^1(\R)}+\|f_{\textup{osc},3}\|_{L^1(\R)}\le C\epsilon . \]
nodes.proof_html: Smoothness: $\int_y^\infty Z=\int_y^{y_1}Z+\int_{y_1}^\infty Z$ is smooth in $y$; $\chi_R$ vanishes on $(-\infty,R]$. The sum identity is eqn:approx_oscillatory_correction. Derivatives: product rule, with $\chi_R'=0$ on $[2R,\infty)$. Boundedness of $f'$: $|\chi_R'|\le K_1R^{-1}$ times the primitive bounds, plus $|Z|+|Z_0|+|Z|^3$. The bound on $f_{\textup{osc},3}$ is lem:c05_primitive with $|c_{\textup{cubic}}|\le C_0\epsilon$. Then $|f_{\textup{osc},1}|\le|f_{\textup{osc}}|+|f_{\textup{osc},3}|\le C\epsilon\ang{y}^{-p-\beta}+C\epsilon y^{-3\beta-1/p}$ by (eqn:approx\_fosc\_bounds) with $j=0$; and $3\beta+\frac1p\ge p+\beta$ because $2\beta+\frac1p=1+\frac2p>p$. The $L^1$ bounds follow by integrating over $(R,\infty)$, since $p+\beta>1$ and $3\beta+\frac1p>1$.

nodes.title: Localization of $|D|^p$ away from {$[Y/2,3Y]$}
nodes.statement_html: Let $(\epsilon,\mu,R,Y)$ be a parameter tuple and $g\in C^\infty(\R;\R)$ with $g,g'$ bounded, $g\in L^1(\R)$, $g=0$ on $(-\infty,R]$. Then for every $y\in(Y/2,3Y)$, \begin{equation} |D|^pg'(y)=|D|^p(\chi_Yg')(y)+\mc{R}_{\textup{far},Y}[g](y), \end{equation} both terms are $C^1$ on $(Y/2,3Y)$, and there is an admissible $C$ with $|\partial_y^j\mc{R}_{\textup{far},Y}[g](y)|\le CY^{-p-2-j}\|g\|_{L^1}$ for $y\in[Y,2Y]$, $j=0,1$.
nodes.proof_html: By linearity $|D|^pg'=|D|^p(\chi_Yg')+|D|^p((1-\chi_Y)g')$. Fix $y\in(Y/2,3Y)$; $(1-\chi_Y)g'$ vanishes on a neighbourhood of $y$, so $|D|^p((1-\chi_Y)g')(y)=-c_\alpha\int(1-\chi_Y(z))g'(z)|y-z|^{-1-p}dz$, absolutely convergent ($g'$ bounded, the integrand vanishes near $z=y$). Integrate by parts on $[-M,M]$: the kernel $k_y(z)=(1-\chi_Y(z))|y-z|^{-1-p}$ is smooth, the boundary terms $g(\pm M)k_y(\pm M)\to0$ ($g$ bounded, $k_y(z)=O(|z|^{-1-p})$), giving eqn:approx_E5_far_remainder. For $y\in[Y,2Y]$ and $z\in\operatorname{supp}(1-\chi_Y)$ one has $|y-z|\ge Y/2$, so $|\partial_z k_y|\le K_1Y^{-1}(Y/2)^{-1-p}+(1+p)(Y/2)^{-2-p}\le CY^{-p-2}$, and $|\partial_y\partial_zk_y|\le CY^{-p-3}$; differentiation under the integral is justified by these uniform bounds and $g\in L^1$. Regularity of $|D|^p(\chi_Yg')$: $\chi_Yg'\in C^\infty_c$, so $|D|^p(\chi_Yg')$ is $C^1$ with derivative $|D|^p((\chi_Yg')')$; it equals $|D|^pg'-\mc{R}_{\textup{far},Y}[g]$ on $(Y/2,3Y)$.

nodes.title: Hypotheses of the oscillatory multiplier lemma
nodes.statement_html:
Let $(\epsilon,\mu,R,Y)$ be a parameter tuple, $I_Y=(Y/4,4Y)$, $\Lambda=Y^{1/p}$, $\delta_Y=\epsilon Y^{1/p-p}$. Put $a_1=\chi_YA$, $a_0=\chi_YA_0$, $a_3=\chi_YA^3$ (in $C_c^\infty(I_Y)$). Then, with constants $c_*,C_k$ admissible:
  • $(a_1,\Phi)$ and $(a_0,\Phi_0)$ satisfy the hypotheses of lem:appendix_oscillatory_multiplier on $I_Y$ with amplitude size $Y^{-\beta}$ and frequency size $\Lambda$: $c_*\Lambda\le\Phi'\le c_*^{-1}\Lambda$, $|\partial^k\Phi'|\le C_k\Lambda Y^{-k}$, $|\partial^ka_\nu|\le C_kY^{-\beta-k}$ (same for $\Phi_0$);
  • the difference hypotheses hold with $\delta=\delta_Y$: $|\partial^k(a_1-a_0)|\le C_k\delta_YY^{-\beta}Y^{-k}$, $|\partial^k(\Phi-\Phi_0)|\le C_k\delta_YY^{-k}$ on $I_Y$;
  • $(a_3,3\Phi)$ satisfies the hypotheses with amplitude size $Y^{-3\beta}$ and frequency size $\Lambda$.
nodes.proof_html: On $I_Y$ one has $y\ge Y/4\ge2R\ge R$ and $y\in(Y/4,4Y)$, so $y^{\theta}\le C_\theta Y^\theta$ for every real $\theta$ (with $C_\theta=\max(4^\theta,4^{-\theta})$). Apply lem:c05_symbol_bounds(1)--(2) and Leibniz with $|\partial^k\chi_Y|\le K_kY^{-k}$. For (2): $\epsilon Y^{-\beta-p-1-k}\le\delta_YY^{-\beta-k}$ since $-1\le\frac1p$. For (3): $|\partial^kA^3|\le C_kY^{-3\beta-k}$, $(3\Phi)'=3\lambda$.

nodes.title: Multiplier expansion for the fundamental harmonic
nodes.statement_html: For every parameter tuple and $y\in(Y/2,3Y)$ (with the notation of def:c05_auxiliary_remainders), \begin{equation} \mc{E}_{\textup{mult}}=e^{i\Phi}\sq{\mc{R}}_{\textup{mult},2}[a_1,\Phi],\qquad \mc{E}_{\textup{mult},0}=e^{i\Phi_0}\sq{\mc{R}}_{\textup{mult},2}[a_0,\Phi_0], \end{equation} where $\sq{\mc{R}}_{\textup{mult},2}[a,\Phi]$ is the remainder of (eqn:appendix\_oscillatory\_multiplier\_two\_term\_expansion). Moreover there is an admissible $C$ such that for $y\in[Y,2Y]$ and $j=0,1$ \begin{equation} |\partial_y^j(\mc{E}_{\textup{mult}}-\mc{E}_{\textup{mult},0})(y)|\le C\epsilon Y^{-p-3\beta+j/p}. \end{equation}
nodes.proof_html:
Identity. By lem:c05_multiplier_hypotheses(1) the two-term expansion applies: $|D|^p(a_1e^{i\Phi})=e^{i\Phi}[\lambda^pa_1-ip\lambda^{p-1}a_1'-\frac{ip(p-1)}2\lambda^{p-2}\lambda'a_1+\sq{\mc{R}}]$. For $y\in(Y/2,3Y)$, $\chi_Y\equiv1$ near $y$, so $a_1=A$ near $y$, and $A'=\mu a_*'\lambda^{-(p+1)/2}-\frac{p+1}2A\lambda'/\lambda$. Hence $-ip\lambda^{p-1}A'-\frac{ip(p-1)}2\lambda^{p-2}\lambda'A=-ip\mu a_*'\lambda^{(p-3)/2}+ip\lambda^{p-2}\lambda'A$ and $ip\lambda^{p-2}\lambda'=i(\lambda^p)'/\lambda$. Multiplying by $e^{i\Phi}$ gives the claimed form. For $\nu=0$ use $\lambda_0^p=y$, $(\lambda_0^p)'=1$.

Difference. Write $\sq{\mc{R}}_\nu=\mc{R}_{\textup{mult},2,\nu}-\frac{p(p-1)}2\lambda_\nu^{p-2}a_\nu''$ ($\lambda_1:=\lambda$) and \[ \mc{E}_{\textup{mult}}-\mc{E}_{\textup{mult},0}=e^{i\Phi}(\sq{\mc{R}}_1-\sq{\mc{R}}_0)+(e^{i\Phi}-e^{i\Phi_0})\sq{\mc{R}}_0 . \] By (eqn:appendix\_oscillatory\_multiplier\_amplitude\_difference) with $N=2$ and lem:c05_multiplier_hypotheses(2), $|\partial^j(\mc{R}_{\textup{mult},2,1}-\mc{R}_{\textup{mult},2,0})|\le C\min\{1,\delta_Y\}Y^{-\beta-2-j}\Lambda^{p-2}$. By lem:c05_symbol_bounds, $|\partial^j(\lambda^{p-2}a_1''-\lambda_0^{p-2}a_0'')|\le C\delta_YY^{-\beta-2-j}\Lambda^{p-2}$. Also $|\partial^j\sq{\mc{R}}_0|\le CY^{-\beta-2-j}\Lambda^{p-2}$ (appendix lemma), $|e^{i\Phi}-e^{i\Phi_0}|\le|\Psi-\Psi_0|\le C\delta_Y$ and $|\partial_y(e^{i\Phi}-e^{i\Phi_0})|\le\lambda|e^{i\Phi}-e^{i\Phi_0}|+|\lambda-\lambda_0|\le C\Lambda\delta_Y$, $|\partial_ye^{i\Phi}|\le C\Lambda$. Leibniz (with $Y^{-1}\le\Lambda$) gives $|\partial^j(\cdots)|\le C\delta_YY^{-\beta-2}\Lambda^{p-2+j}$, and $\delta_YY^{-\beta-2}\Lambda^{p-2+j}=\epsilon Y^{\frac1p-p-\beta-2+1-\frac2p+\frac jp}=\epsilon Y^{-p-3\beta+j/p}$ using $3\beta=\beta+1+\frac1p$.

nodes.title: Integration by parts in $f_{\textup{osc},1}$
nodes.statement_html: For every parameter tuple and $y\ge2R$, \begin{equation} f_{\textup{osc},1}(y)=-2\operatorname{Re}\Bigl[i\Bigl(\frac{Z}{\lambda}-\frac{\mu}{\mu_*}\frac{Z_0}{\lambda_0}\Bigr)\Bigr](y)+\mc{R}_{\textup{prim}}(y). \end{equation} $\mc{R}_{\textup{prim}}\in C^1([R,\infty))$ with $\mc{R}_{\textup{prim}}'=-2\operatorname{Re}[e^{i\Phi}\partial(\frac{A}{i\lambda})-e^{i\Phi_0}\partial(\frac{A_0}{i\lambda_0})]$, and there is an admissible $C$ with, for $y\ge R$, $|\mc{R}_{\textup{prim}}(y)|\le C\epsilon y^{-p-3\beta}$ and $|\mc{R}_{\textup{prim}}'(y)|\le C\epsilon y^{-p-3\beta+1/p}$.
nodes.proof_html:
Identity. For $y\ge2R$, $\chi_R(y)=1$; insert lem:c05_primitive for $Z$ and $\frac{\mu}{\mu_*}Z_0$ into eqn:approx_E5_oscillatory_split, using $-\frac{Z}{i\lambda}=\frac{iZ}{\lambda}$.

Derivative. The integrand $F(s)=e^{i\Phi}g-e^{i\Phi_0}g_0$, $g:=\partial_s(A/(i\lambda))$, $g_0:=\partial_s(A_0/(i\lambda_0))$, is continuous and absolutely integrable; fundamental theorem of calculus. By lem:c05_symbol_bounds, $|g|+|g_0|\le Cs^{-\beta-1/p-1}$, $|g-g_0|\le C\epsilon s^{-\beta-1/p-p-2}$ (from $|\partial^k(A-A_0)|$ and $|\partial^k(\lambda^{-1}-\lambda_0^{-1})|\le C\epsilon s^{-1/p-p-1-k}$). Hence $|F(y)|\le|g-g_0|+|g_0||e^{i(\Psi-\Psi_0)}-1|\le C\epsilon y^{-\beta-1/p-p-2}+C\epsilon y^{-\beta-1-p}\le C\epsilon y^{-p-\beta-1}$, and $-p-\beta-1=-p-3\beta+\frac1p$.

Value. Set $b=g/(i\lambda)$, $b_0=g_0/(i\lambda_0)$, so $e^{i\Phi}g=b\,\partial_se^{i\Phi}$. Then $|\partial^kb|+|\partial^kb_0|\le Cs^{-\beta-1-2/p-k}$ and $|\partial^k(b-b_0)|\le C\epsilon s^{-p-\beta-2-2/p-k}$ ($k=0,1$). Integrating by parts on $[y,M]$ and letting $M\to\infty$ ($b(M)\to0$): $\int_y^\infty F=-(be^{i\Phi}-b_0e^{i\Phi_0})(y)-\int_y^\infty(b'e^{i\Phi}-b_0'e^{i\Phi_0})$. As in the derivative step, $|be^{i\Phi}-b_0e^{i\Phi_0}|\le|b-b_0|+|b_0||e^{i(\Psi-\Psi_0)}-1|\le C\epsilon y^{-p-\beta-1-1/p}=C\epsilon y^{-p-3\beta}$, and $|b'e^{i\Phi}-b_0'e^{i\Phi_0}|\le C\epsilon s^{-p-3\beta-1}$, whose integral over $[y,\infty)$ is $\le C\epsilon y^{-p-3\beta}$.

nodes.title: Cancellation identity for $\mc{R}_{\textup{lin},1}$
nodes.statement_html: For every parameter tuple and $y\in(Y/2,3Y)$, \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} \mc{R}_{\textup{lin},1}={}&2\operatorname{Re}\Bigl[i\bigl((\lambda^p)'-1\bigr)\frac{Z}{\lambda} -ip\mu a_*'\bigl(\lambda^{(p-3)/2}e^{i\Phi}-\lambda_0^{(p-3)/2}e^{i\Phi_0}\bigr)\Bigr]\\ &+2\operatorname{Re}(\mc{E}_{\textup{mult}}-\mc{E}_{\textup{mult},0})+\mc{R}_{\textup{prim}}+\mc{R}_{\textup{far},Y}[f_{\textup{osc},1}]. \end{aligned} \end{equation}
nodes.proof_html: By lem:c05_osc_split_bounds $g=f_{\textup{osc},1}$ satisfies the hypotheses of lem:c05_far_localization, and on $\operatorname{supp}\chi_Y\subset(Y/4,4Y)\subset(2R,\infty)$, $\chi_Yf'_{\textup{osc},1}=2\operatorname{Re}[\chi_YZ-\chi_Y\frac{\mu}{\mu_*}Z_0]$. Thus $|D|^pf'_{\textup{osc},1}=2\operatorname{Re}[|D|^p(\chi_YZ)-|D|^p(\chi_Y\frac{\mu}{\mu_*}Z_0)]+\mc{R}_{\textup{far},Y}[f_{\textup{osc},1}]$. Substitute the definitions of $\mc{E}_{\textup{mult}},\mc{E}_{\textup{mult},0}$ and eqn:approx_E5_fundamental_primitive into eqn:approx_E5_linear_components: the terms $\pm2\lambda^p\operatorname{Re}Z$ and $\pm2y\operatorname{Re}(\frac{\mu}{\mu_*}Z_0)$ cancel, $2\operatorname{Re}[i\frac{(\lambda^p)'}{\lambda}Z]-2\operatorname{Re}[i\frac{Z}{\lambda}]=2\operatorname{Re}[i((\lambda^p)'-1)\frac Z\lambda]$, and $-2\operatorname{Re}[\frac{i}{\lambda_0}\frac{\mu}{\mu_*}Z_0]+2\operatorname{Re}[i\frac{\mu}{\mu_*}\frac{Z_0}{\lambda_0}]=0$.

nodes.title: Explicit terms in $\mc{R}_{\textup{lin},1}$
nodes.statement_html: Let $T_1=i((\lambda^p)'-1)Z/\lambda$ and $T_2=-ip\mu a_*'(\lambda^{(p-3)/2}e^{i\Phi}-\lambda_0^{(p-3)/2}e^{i\Phi_0})$. There is an admissible $C$ such that for every parameter tuple, $y\ge R$, $j=0,1$: $|\partial^jT_1(y)|+|\partial^jT_2(y)|\le C\epsilon y^{-p-3\beta+j/p}$.
nodes.proof_html: $T_1$: $|(\lambda^p)'-1|\le C\epsilon y^{-p-1}$, $|\partial((\lambda^p)'-1)|\le C\epsilon y^{-p-2}$, $|Z/\lambda|\le Cy^{-\beta-1/p}$, $|\partial(Z/\lambda)|\le Cy^{-\beta}$; and $p+1+\beta+\frac1p=p+3\beta$. $T_2$: split $\lambda^{(p-3)/2}e^{i\Phi}-\lambda_0^{(p-3)/2}e^{i\Phi_0}=(\lambda^{(p-3)/2}-\lambda_0^{(p-3)/2})e^{i\Phi}+\lambda_0^{(p-3)/2}(e^{i\Phi}-e^{i\Phi_0})$. The first is $\le C\epsilon y^{(p-3)/(2p)-p-1}$, the second $\le C\epsilon y^{(p-3)/(2p)+1/p-p}$; with $|a_*'|\le Cy^{-2\beta-1}$ and $-2\beta-1+\frac{p-3}{2p}+\frac1p-p=-p-3\beta$ the claim for $j=0$ follows. For $j=1$ each derivative costs at most $Cy^{1/p}$: $\partial_y(e^{i\Phi}-e^{i\Phi_0})=i\lambda(e^{i\Phi}-e^{i\Phi_0})+i(\lambda-\lambda_0)e^{i\Phi_0}$, and derivatives of the amplitudes cost $Cy^{-1}\le Cy^{1/p}$.

nodes.title: Bound on $\mc{R}_{\textup{lin},1}$
nodes.statement_html: There is an admissible $C$ such that for every parameter tuple, $y\in[Y,2Y]$, $j=0,1$, \begin{equation} |\partial_y^j\mc{R}_{\textup{lin},1}(y)|\le C\epsilon\bigl(Y^{-p-3\beta+j/p}+Y^{-p-2-j}\bigr)\le C\epsilon Y^{-2p-1+j/p}. \end{equation}
nodes.proof_html: Differentiate eqn:approx_E5_fundamental_error_identity term by term (all terms are $C^1$ on $(Y/2,3Y)$): lem:c05_fundamental_explicit, eqn:approx_E5_multiplier_difference_bound, lem:c05_fundamental_primitive (with $y\approx Y$), and lem:c05_far_localization with $\|f_{\textup{osc},1}\|_{L^1}\le C\epsilon$. The last inequality: $p+3\beta\ge2p+1$ iff $3\beta\ge p+1$ iff $\frac3{2p}\ge1$; and $p+2+j\ge2p+1-\frac jp$ as $p<1$; and $Y\ge1$.

nodes.title: Third-harmonic multiplier bound
nodes.statement_html: There is an admissible $C$ such that for every parameter tuple, $y\in[Y,2Y]$, $j=0,1$, $\bigl|\partial_y^j\bigl[|D|^p(\chi_YZ^3)-3^p\lambda^pZ^3\bigr](y)\bigr|\le CY^{1-5\beta+j/p}$.
nodes.proof_html: Apply (eqn:appendix\_oscillatory\_multiplier\_two\_term\_expansion) to $(a_3,3\Phi)$ (lem:c05_multiplier_hypotheses(3)), frequency $3\lambda$. On $[Y,2Y]$, $(3\lambda)^pa_3e^{3i\Phi}=3^p\lambda^pZ^3$; the difference equals $e^{3i\Phi}[B+\sq{\mc{R}}]$ where $B=-ip(3\lambda)^{p-1}a_3'-\frac{ip(p-1)}2(3\lambda)^{p-2}3\lambda'a_3$ satisfies $|\partial^jB|\le CY^{-3\beta-1-j}\Lambda^{p-1}$ and $|\partial^j\sq{\mc{R}}|\le CY^{-3\beta-2-j}\Lambda^{p-2}$. Since $|\partial_ye^{3i\Phi}|=3\lambda\le C\Lambda$, $|\partial^j(\cdot)|\le CY^{-3\beta-1}\Lambda^{p-1+j}$, and $-3\beta-1+\frac{p-1}p=-3\beta-\frac1p=1-5\beta$.

nodes.title: Bound on $\mc{R}_{\textup{lin},3}$
nodes.statement_html: There is an admissible $C$ such that for every parameter tuple, $y\in[Y,2Y]$, $j=0,1$, \begin{equation} |\partial_y^j\mc{R}_{\textup{lin},3}(y)|\le C\epsilon\bigl(Y^{1-5\beta+j/p}+Y^{-p-2-j}\bigr)\le C\epsilon Y^{-2p-1+j/p}. \end{equation}
nodes.proof_html: By lem:c05_far_localization with $g=f_{\textup{osc},3}$ and $\chi_Yf_{\textup{osc},3}'=2c_{\textup{cubic}}\operatorname{Re}(\chi_YZ^3)$, \[ \mc{R}_{\textup{lin},3}=2c_{\textup{cubic}}\operatorname{Re}\bigl[|D|^p(\chi_YZ^3)-3^p\lambda^pZ^3\bigr]+f_{\textup{osc},3}+\mc{R}_{\textup{far},Y}[f_{\textup{osc},3}] \] on $[Y,2Y]$. First term: $|c_{\textup{cubic}}|\le C_0\epsilon$ and lem:c05_multiplier_third. Second: $|f_{\textup{osc},3}|\le C\epsilon Y^{-3\beta-1/p}=C\epsilon Y^{1-5\beta}$ and $|f'_{\textup{osc},3}|=2|c_{\textup{cubic}}||\operatorname{Re}Z^3|\le C\epsilon Y^{-3\beta}=C\epsilon Y^{1-5\beta+1/p}$. Third: $CY^{-p-2-j}\|f_{\textup{osc},3}\|_{L^1}\le C\epsilon Y^{-p-2-j}$. Finally $5\beta-1\ge2p+1$ iff $\frac{5}{2p}\ge2$, true for $p<1$.

nodes.title: Linear remainder of $\mc{E}_5$
nodes.statement_html: There is an admissible constant $C$ such that for every parameter tuple $(\epsilon,\mu,R,Y)$ (so $Y\ge8R$), every $y\in[Y,2Y]$ and $j\in\{0,1\}$, $\mc{R}_{\textup{lin}}$ is $C^1$ near $y$ and \begin{equation} |\partial_y^j\mc{R}_{\textup{lin}}(y)|\le C\epsilon\ang{y}^{-2p-1+\frac jp}. \end{equation}
nodes.proof_html: $\mc{R}_{\textup{lin}}=\mc{R}_{\textup{lin},1}+\mc{R}_{\textup{lin},3}$ (lem:c05_E5_split); add eqn:approx_E5_fundamental_bound and eqn:approx_E5_third_harmonic_bound. Since $Y\ge8$ and $y\in[Y,2Y]$, $Y\le\ang{y}\le3Y$, so $Y^{\theta}\le3^{|\theta|}\ang{y}^\theta$ for $\theta=-2p-1+j/p$.

nodes.title: Basic properties of $\mc{Q}_{\epsilon,3}$
nodes.statement_html: Let $v\in C^2(\R;\R)$ with $v,v',v''$ bounded. Then for every $y$ the integral defining $\mc{Q}_{\epsilon,3}(v)(y)$ converges absolutely and \begin{equation} \mc{Q}_{\epsilon,3}(v)(y)=K_\epsilon\int_\R|s|^{-p-3}\,\Delta v'(y,s)\,\bigl(\Delta v(y,s)\bigr)^2ds . \end{equation} If moreover $v\in C^3$ with $v'''$ bounded, then $\mc{Q}_{\epsilon,3}(v)\in C^1(\R)$ and $\partial_y\mc{Q}_{\epsilon,3}(v)(y)=K_\epsilon\int|s|^{-p-3}[\Delta v''(\Delta v)^2+2(\Delta v')^2\Delta v](y,s)\,ds$. Finally, for $c\in\R$, $\kappa>0$, $x_0\in\R$ and $g\in C^2_b$, the function $v(z)=c\,g(\kappa z+x_0)$ satisfies $\mc{Q}_{\epsilon,3}(v)(z)=c^3\kappa^{p+3}\mc{Q}_{\epsilon,3}(g)(\kappa z+x_0)$.
nodes.proof_html:
Substitute $z=y-s$ in (eqn:approx\_cubic\_operator); $|y-z|^{-\alpha}(y-z)^{-2}=|s|^{-p-3}$. Domination:
  $|\Delta v'|\le\min\{\|v''\|_\infty|s|,2\|v'\|_\infty\}$, $|\Delta v|\le\min\{\|v'\|_\infty|s|,2\|v\|_\infty\}$, so the integrand is
  $\le\|v''\|\|v'\|^2|s|^{-p}$ for $|s|\le1$ and $\le8\|v'\|\|v\|^2|s|^{-p-3}$ for $|s|\ge1$, both integrable since $p<1$.
  The $y$-derivative of the integrand is $[\Delta v''(\Delta v)^2+2(\Delta v')^2\Delta v]|s|^{-p-3}$, dominated (uniformly in $y$) by
  the same type of bound with $\|v'''\|$; differentiate under the integral (dominated convergence) and continuity follows likewise.
  Scaling: substitute $w=\kappa z+x_0$ in the original integral: $v(y)-v(z)=c(g(x)-g(w))$, $v'=c\kappa g'$, $y-z=(x-w)/\kappa$,
  $dz=dw/\kappa$, giving the factor $c^3\kappa^{1+\alpha+2-1}=c^3\kappa^{p+3}$.

nodes.title: Response to the frozen plane wave
nodes.statement_html: For every parameter tuple, $y\ge R$, $\lambda=\lambda(y)$ and all $z\in\R$: \begin{equation} \mc{Q}_{\epsilon,3}(P_y)(z)=2n_\epsilon\lambda^p|Z(y)|^2\operatorname{Re}\bigl(Z(y)e^{i\lambda(z-y)}\bigr) -2(3^p-1)c_{\textup{cubic}}\lambda^p\operatorname{Re}\bigl(Z(y)^3e^{3i\lambda(z-y)}\bigr). \end{equation} In particular \begin{equation} \mc{Q}_{\epsilon,3}(P_y)(y)=G(y),\qquad T_P(y)=-2n_\epsilon\lambda^{p+1}|Z|^2\operatorname{Im}Z+6(3^p-1)c_{\textup{cubic}}\lambda^{p+1}\operatorname{Im}(Z^3). \end{equation}
nodes.proof_html: If $Z(y)=0$ then $P_y=0$ and both sides vanish. Otherwise write $Z(y)=|Z|e^{i\theta}$; then $P_y(z)=\frac{|Z|}{\lambda}\,2\sin(\lambda z+\theta-\lambda y)$. By the scaling law of lem:c05_Q3_basic with $c=|Z|/\lambda$, $\kappa=\lambda$, $g=2\sin$ and the normalization (eqn:approx\_cubic\_normalization), $\mc{Q}_{\epsilon,3}(P_y)(z)=|Z|^3\lambda^p[2n_\epsilon\cos\vartheta-2(3^p-1)c_{\textup{cubic}}\cos3\vartheta]$ with $\vartheta=\lambda(z-y)+\theta$. Use $|Z|^3\cos\vartheta=|Z|^2\operatorname{Re}(Ze^{i\lambda(z-y)})$ and $|Z|^3\cos3\vartheta=\operatorname{Re}(Z^3e^{3i\lambda(z-y)})$. For $T_P$ differentiate in $z$ at $z=y$: $\operatorname{Re}(i\lambda Z)=-\lambda\operatorname{Im}Z$, $\operatorname{Re}(3i\lambda Z^3)=-3\lambda\operatorname{Im}Z^3$.

nodes.title: Dependence of the frozen response on the base point
nodes.statement_html: $G\in C^1([R,\infty))$ and there is an admissible $C$ such that for every parameter tuple and $y\in[Y,2Y]$, $|T_P(y)-G'(y)|\le C\epsilon Y^{-3\beta}=C\epsilon Y^{1-5\beta+1/p}$.
nodes.proof_html: Writing $T_P=2n_\epsilon\lambda^p|Z|^2\operatorname{Re}(i\lambda Z)-2(3^p-1)c_{\textup{cubic}}\lambda^p\operatorname{Re}(3i\lambda Z^3)$ and differentiating $G$, \[ T_P-G'=-2n_\epsilon(\lambda^p|Z|^2)'\operatorname{Re}Z-2n_\epsilon\lambda^p|Z|^2\operatorname{Re}(Z'-i\lambda Z) +2(3^p-1)c_{\textup{cubic}}\bigl[(\lambda^p)'\operatorname{Re}Z^3+3\lambda^p\operatorname{Re}(Z^2(Z'-i\lambda Z))\bigr]. \] Now $\lambda^p|Z|^2=|\mu|^2|a_*|^2/\lambda$, so $|(\lambda^p|Z|^2)'|\le Cy^{-1/p-1}$; $|Z|\le Cy^{-\beta}$; $|Z'-i\lambda Z|\le Cy^{-\beta-1}$; $|(\lambda^p)'|\le C$; $\lambda^p\le Cy$. Each term is $\le C\epsilon y^{-3\beta}$ (using $\beta+1+\frac1p=3\beta$), and $-3\beta=1-5\beta+\frac1p$ because $2\beta=1+\frac1p$.

nodes.title: Integral representation of $\mc{R}_{\textup{cub}}$ and of its derivative
nodes.statement_html: For every parameter tuple, $\mc{R}_{\textup{cub}}\in C^1((R,\infty))$ and for $y\in[Y,2Y]$ \begin{equation} \mc{R}_{\textup{cub}}(y)=\mc{Q}_{\epsilon,3}(v_Y)(y)-\mc{Q}_{\epsilon,3}(P_y)(y)=K_\epsilon\int_\R|s|^{-p-3}N_0(y,s)\,ds, \end{equation} \[ \mc{R}_{\textup{cub}}'(y)=K_\epsilon\int_\R|s|^{-p-3}N_1(y,s)\,ds+\bigl(T_P(y)-G'(y)\bigr). \]
nodes.proof_html: $v_Y\in C_c^\infty$ and $P_y$ is a trigonometric function, so lem:c05_Q3_basic applies to both. By definition and eqn:approx_cubic_plane_wave_frozen, $\mc{R}_{\textup{cub}}=\mc{Q}_{\epsilon,3}(v_Y)-G$; apply eqn:approx_cubic_remainder_translated to $v_Y$ at $y$ and to $P_y$ at $z=y$ and subtract. Derivative: $\mc{R}_{\textup{cub}}'=\partial_y\mc{Q}_{\epsilon,3}(v_Y)-T_P+(T_P-G')$, with both $\partial_y\mc{Q}_{\epsilon,3}(v_Y)(y)$ and $T_P(y)$ given by the derivative formula of lem:c05_Q3_basic.

nodes.title: Size of $v_Y$, $P_y$ and their increments
nodes.statement_html:
There is an admissible $C$ such that for every parameter tuple, $y\in[Y,2Y]$, $\lambda=\lambda(y)$:
  • on $[Y/2,3Y]$: $v_Y'=2\operatorname{Re}(Z+c_{\textup{cubic}}Z^3)$ and $v_Y''=2\operatorname{Re}(Z'+3c_{\textup{cubic}}Z^2Z')$;
  • $\|v_Y\|_\infty\le CY^{-\beta}\lambda^{-1}$, $\|v_Y'\|_\infty\le CY^{-\beta}$, $\|v_Y''\|_\infty\le CY^{-\beta}\lambda$; and $\|P_y^{(k)}\|_\infty\le2|Z(y)|\lambda^{k-1}\le CY^{-\beta}\lambda^{k-1}$, $k=0,1,2$;
  • for $h\in\{v_Y,P_y\}$ and all $s\in\R$: $|\Delta h(y,s)|\le CY^{-\beta}\min\{|s|,\lambda^{-1}\}$, $|\Delta h'(y,s)|\le CY^{-\beta}\min\{1,\lambda|s|\}$, $|\Delta h''(y,s)|\le CY^{-\beta}\lambda\min\{1,\lambda|s|\}$.
nodes.proof_html: (1) $\chi_Y\equiv1$ there. (2) On $\operatorname{supp}\chi_Y$, $z\in(Y/4,4Y)$, $z\ge R$, and by lem:c05_primitive and $|c_{\textup{cubic}}|\le C_0\epsilon\le C_0$, $|\int_z^\infty(Z+c_{\textup{cubic}}Z^3)|\le CY^{-\beta-1/p}$; $\lambda\le2(2Y)^{1/p}$ gives $Y^{-1/p}\le C\lambda^{-1}$. Then $v_Y'=-2\chi_Y'\operatorname{Re}\int+2\chi_Y\operatorname{Re}(Z+c_{\textup{cubic}}Z^3)$ and $v_Y''=-2\chi_Y''\operatorname{Re}\int+4\chi_Y'\operatorname{Re}(Z+c_{\textup{cubic}}Z^3)+2\chi_Y\operatorname{Re}(Z'+3c_{\textup{cubic}}Z^2Z')$; use $|\partial^k\chi_Y|\le K_kY^{-k}$, lem:c05_symbol_bounds(3) and $Y^{-1}\le Y^{1/p}\le C\lambda$. $P_y$: direct. (3) $|\Delta h|\le\min\{|s|\|h'\|_\infty,2\|h\|_\infty\}$ and similarly for $h',h''$; note $\min\{1,\lambda|s|\}=\lambda\min\{|s|,\lambda^{-1}\}$.

nodes.title: Frozen-frequency comparison for $Z$
nodes.statement_html:
Let a parameter tuple, $y\in[Y,2Y]$, $\lambda=\lambda(y)$ and $w(t):=Z'(t)-i\lambda Z(t)$ ($t\ge R$) be given. There is an admissible $C$ such that for $|s|\le Y/4$ and $t$ between $y-s$ and $y$:
  • $Z(y)e^{-i\lambda s}-Z(y-s)=\int_{y-s}^ye^{-i\lambda(t-y+s)}w(t)\,dt$;
  • $|w(t)|\le CY^{-\beta-1}(1+\lambda|t-y|)$ and $|w'(t)|\le CY^{-\beta-1}\lambda(1+\lambda|t-y|)$;
  • $|Z(y)e^{-i\lambda s}-Z(y-s)|\le CY^{-\beta-1}(|s|+\lambda s^2)$ and $|w(y)-w(y-s)|\le CY^{-\beta-1}\lambda(|s|+\lambda s^2)$;
  • $|Z(y)^3-Z(y-s)^3|\le CY^{-3\beta}\min\{1,\lambda|s|\}$ and $|(Z^2Z')(y)-(Z^2Z')(y-s)|\le CY^{-3\beta}\lambda\min\{1,\lambda|s|\}$.
nodes.proof_html: $t\in[3Y/4,9Y/4]$, so $t\ge R$ and $|t-y|\le Y/4\le y/2$. (1) $\partial_t[Z(t)e^{-i\lambda(t-y+s)}]=e^{-i\lambda(t-y+s)}w(t)$; integrate over $[y-s,y]$. (2) $w=A'e^{i\Phi}+i(\lambda(t)-\lambda)Z(t)$; use lem:c05_symbol_bounds(2),(3),(6). Also $w'=[A''+i(2\lambda(t)-\lambda)A'+i\lambda'(t)A+\lambda(t)(\lambda-\lambda(t))A]e^{i\Phi}$, each term $\le CY^{-\beta-1}\lambda(1+\lambda|t-y|)$ (using $Y^{-1}\le C\lambda$, $|\lambda'|\le C\lambda/Y$). (3) Integrate (2): $\int_0^{|s|}(1+\lambda\tau)d\tau\le|s|+\lambda s^2$; for $w$ use the mean value inequality. (4) Mean value inequality with $|(Z^3)'|\le CY^{-3\beta}\lambda$, $|(Z^2Z')'|\le CY^{-3\beta}\lambda^2$, combined with the sup bounds $CY^{-3\beta}$, $CY^{-3\beta}\lambda$.

nodes.title: Comparison of $v_Y$ with the frozen plane wave
nodes.statement_html: There is an admissible $C$ such that for every parameter tuple, $y\in[Y,2Y]$, $\lambda=\lambda(y)$ and $|s|\le Y/4$, with $m_0=\min\{|s|,\lambda^{-1}\}$, $m_1=\min\{1,\lambda|s|\}$: \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} |\Delta v_Y-\Delta P_y|&\le C\bigl[Y^{-\beta-1}s^2+\epsilon Y^{-3\beta}m_0\bigr],\\ |\Delta v_Y'-\Delta P_y'|&\le C\bigl[Y^{-\beta-1}(|s|+\lambda s^2)+\epsilon Y^{-3\beta}m_1\bigr],\\ |\Delta v_Y''-\Delta P_y''|&\le C\lambda\bigl[Y^{-\beta-1}(|s|+\lambda s^2)+\epsilon Y^{-3\beta}m_1\bigr]. \end{aligned} \end{equation}
nodes.proof_html: The segment between $y-s$ and $y$ lies in $[Y/2,3Y]$, where lem:c05_vY_bounds(1) holds; also $P_y'(z)=2\operatorname{Re}(Z(y)e^{i\lambda(z-y)})$, $P_y''(z)=2\operatorname{Re}(i\lambda Z(y)e^{i\lambda(z-y)})$. Hence the identities \begin{align} \Delta v_Y'-\Delta P_y'&=2\operatorname{Re}\bigl[Z(y)e^{-i\lambda s}-Z(y-s)+c_{\textup{cubic}}(Z(y)^3-Z(y-s)^3)\bigr],\\ \Delta v_Y-\Delta P_y&=2\operatorname{Re}\int_{y-s}^y\bigl[Z(t)-Z(y)e^{i\lambda(t-y)}+c_{\textup{cubic}}Z(t)^3\bigr]dt,\\ \Delta v_Y''-\Delta P_y''&=2\operatorname{Re}\bigl[w(y)-w(y-s)+i\lambda(Z(y)e^{-i\lambda s}-Z(y-s))+3c_{\textup{cubic}}((Z^2Z')(y)-(Z^2Z')(y-s))\bigr].\notag \end{align} The second and third bounds follow from lem:c05_frozen_frequency(3),(4) and $|c_{\textup{cubic}}|\le C_0\epsilon$. For the first: since $\int_{y-s}^yZ=\frac1{i\lambda}[Z(y)-Z(y-s)-\int_{y-s}^yw]$ and $\int_{y-s}^yZ(y)e^{i\lambda(t-y)}=\frac{Z(y)(1-e^{-i\lambda s})}{i\lambda}$, lem:c05_frozen_frequency(1) gives $\int_{y-s}^y[Z(t)-Z(y)e^{i\lambda(t-y)}]dt=\frac1{i\lambda}\int_{y-s}^y[e^{-i\lambda(t-y+s)}-1]w(t)dt$. With $|e^{-i\lambda(t-y+s)}-1|/\lambda\le2m_0$ and lem:c05_frozen_frequency(2) this is $\le CY^{-\beta-1}m_0(|s|+\lambda s^2)\le CY^{-\beta-1}s^2$ (cases $\lambda|s|\le1$, $\lambda|s|\ge1$). The cubic part: $|\int_{y-s}^yZ^3|\le CY^{-3\beta}|s|$ and, by lem:c05_primitive, $\le|\int_{y-s}^\infty Z^3|+|\int_y^\infty Z^3|\le CY^{-3\beta-1/p}\le CY^{-3\beta}\lambda^{-1}$.

nodes.title: Elementary kernel integrals
nodes.statement_html: For $p\in(0,1)$, $\lambda>0$, $L>0$, with $m_0,m_1$ as above: $\int_\R(|s|+\lambda s^2)m_0^2|s|^{-p-3}ds\le(\frac4{1-p}+\frac4p)\lambda^{p-1}$, $\int_\R m_1m_0^2|s|^{-p-3}ds\le(\frac2{1-p}+\frac2{p+2})\lambda^p$, and $\int_{|s|\ge L}|s|^{-p-3}ds=\frac{2}{p+2}L^{-p-2}$.
nodes.proof_html:
Split at $|s|=\lambda^{-1}$. First: for $|s|\le\lambda^{-1}$ the integrand is $\le2|s|^{-p}$; for $|s|\ge\lambda^{-1}$ it is
  $\le2\lambda^{-1}|s|^{-p-1}$. Second: $\lambda|s|^{-p}$ resp.\ $\lambda^{-2}|s|^{-p-3}$. Integrate explicitly.

nodes.title: Near region
nodes.statement_html: There is an admissible $C$ such that for every parameter tuple, $y\in[Y,2Y]$, $j\in\{0,1\}$, \begin{equation} |K_\epsilon|\int_{|s|\le Y/4}|s|^{-p-3}|N_j(y,s)|\,ds\le C\epsilon Y^{1-5\beta+j/p}. \end{equation}
nodes.proof_html: Write $X_0=Y^{-\beta-1}s^2+\epsilon Y^{-3\beta}m_0$, $X_1=Y^{-\beta-1}(|s|+\lambda s^2)+\epsilon Y^{-3\beta}m_1$ and recall $m_1=\lambda m_0$. Using $a_1b_1^2-a_2b_2^2=(a_1-a_2)b_1^2+a_2(b_1-b_2)(b_1+b_2)$, \begin{align*} N_0&=(\Delta v'-\Delta P')(\Delta v)^2+\Delta P'(\Delta v-\Delta P)(\Delta v+\Delta P),\\ N_1&=(\Delta v''-\Delta P'')(\Delta v)^2+\Delta P''(\Delta v-\Delta P)(\Delta v+\Delta P) +2(\Delta v'-\Delta P')(\Delta v'+\Delta P')\Delta v+2(\Delta P')^2(\Delta v-\Delta P) \end{align*} ($v=v_Y$, $P=P_y$). By lem:c05_vY_bounds(3) and lem:c05_plane_wave_comparison, every term is bounded by $C\lambda^jY^{-2\beta}m_0^2(X_1+\lambda X_0)$, and $Y^{-2\beta}m_0^2(X_1+\lambda X_0)\le C[Y^{-3\beta-1}(|s|+\lambda s^2)m_0^2+\epsilon Y^{-5\beta}m_1m_0^2]$ (as $\lambda s^2\le|s|+\lambda s^2$ and $\lambda m_0=m_1$). By lem:c05_cubic_kernel_integrals and $|K_\epsilon|\le C\epsilon$, the left side is $\le C\epsilon\lambda^j(Y^{-3\beta-1}\lambda^{p-1}+\epsilon Y^{-5\beta}\lambda^p)$. With $\frac12Y^{1/p}\le\lambda\le2^{1+1/p}Y^{1/p}$: $Y^{-3\beta-1}\lambda^{p-1}\le CY^{-3\beta-1/p}=CY^{1-5\beta}$, $Y^{-5\beta}\lambda^p\le CY^{1-5\beta}$, $\lambda^j\le CY^{j/p}$, $\epsilon\le1$.

nodes.title: Far region
nodes.statement_html: There is an admissible $C$ such that for every parameter tuple, $y\in[Y,2Y]$, $j\in\{0,1\}$, $|K_\epsilon|\int_{|s|\ge Y/4}|s|^{-p-3}|N_j(y,s)|\,ds\le C\epsilon Y^{1-5\beta+j/p}$.
nodes.proof_html: Triangle inequality and the sup bounds of lem:c05_vY_bounds(2): $|\Delta h|\le CY^{-\beta}\lambda^{-1}$, $|\Delta h'|\le CY^{-\beta}$, $|\Delta h''|\le CY^{-\beta}\lambda$, so $|N_j|\le CY^{-3\beta}\lambda^{j-2}$. With lem:c05_cubic_kernel_integrals ($L=Y/4$) the left side is $\le C\epsilon Y^{-3\beta-p-2}Y^{(j-2)/p}$, and $-3\beta-p-2+\frac{j-2}p\le-3\beta-\frac1p+\frac jp=1-5\beta+\frac jp$ since $p+2+\frac1p\ge0$.

nodes.title: Cubic remainder of $\mc{E}_5$; bound on $\mc{E}_5$
nodes.statement_html: There is an admissible constant $C$ such that for every parameter tuple $(\epsilon,\mu,R,Y)$, every $y\in[Y,2Y]$ and $j\in\{0,1\}$, \begin{equation} |\partial_y^j\mc{R}_{\textup{cub}}(y)|\le C\epsilon\ang{y}^{1-5\beta+\frac jp}, \end{equation} and consequently \begin{equation} |\partial_y^j\mc{E}_5(y)|\le C\epsilon\ang{y}^{-2p-1+\frac jp}. \end{equation}
nodes.proof_html: By lem:c05_cubic_remainder_representation, $|\partial^j\mc{R}_{\textup{cub}}(y)|\le|K_\epsilon|\int_\R|s|^{-p-3}|N_j|\,ds+j|T_P-G'|(y)$; split the integral at $|s|=Y/4$ and use lem:c05_cubic_near, lem:c05_cubic_far, lem:c05_plane_wave_parameter; convert $Y$ to $\ang{y}$ as in prop:approx_E5_linear. For eqn:approx_E5_bound: $y\ge Y\ge8R>2R$, so $\mc{E}_5=\mc{R}_{\textup{lin}}+\mc{R}_{\textup{cub}}$ (lem:c05_E5_split); add eqn:approx_E5_linear_remainder, using $1-5\beta\le-2p-1$ ($\Leftrightarrow\frac5{2p}\ge2$) and $\ang{y}\ge1$.

nodes.title: Bounds for the coefficient $A_\epsilon$
nodes.statement_html:
Let $0<p<1$, $\alpha=1+p$, $0\leq\epsilon\leq1$, and define the quintic remainder \[\sq A_\epsilon(u):=c_\alpha\Bigl[A_\epsilon(u)-1+\tfrac{\alpha}{2}\epsilon u^2\Bigr].\] There is a constant $C_A$ depending only on $p$ such that for all $u\in\R$:
  • $0\leq 1-A_\epsilon(u)\leq \frac\alpha2\epsilon u^2$;
  • $|A_\epsilon'(u)|\leq\alpha\epsilon|u|$;
  • $|A_\epsilon''(u)|+|A_\epsilon'''(u)|\leq C_A\epsilon$;
  • $|\sq A_\epsilon(u)|\leq C_A\epsilon^2u^4$ and $|\sq A_\epsilon'(u)|\leq C_A\epsilon^2|u|^3$.
In particular $A_\epsilon(0)=1$, $A_\epsilon'(0)=0$.
nodes.proof_html:
Write $A_\epsilon(u)=g(\epsilon u^2)$ with $g(\sigma)=(1+\sigma)^{-\alpha/2}$, $\sigma\geq0$; then
  $g^{(k)}(\sigma)=(-1)^k\frac{\alpha}{2}(\frac\alpha2+1)\cdots(\frac\alpha2+k-1)(1+\sigma)^{-\alpha/2-k}$,
  so $|g^{(k)}(\sigma)|\leq c_k(1+\sigma)^{-\alpha/2-k}$ with $c_1=\alpha/2$.
  (1) is $|g(\sigma)-g(0)|\leq\sup|g'|\,\sigma$ and $g$ decreasing.
  (2): $A_\epsilon'(u)=2\epsilon u\,g'(\epsilon u^2)$ and $|g'|\leq\alpha/2$.
  (3): $A_\epsilon''=2\epsilon g'+4\epsilon^2u^2g''$ and
  $A_\epsilon'''=12\epsilon^2u\,g''+8\epsilon^3u^3g'''$, all evaluated at $\epsilon u^2$. Put $x=\sqrt\epsilon\,u$;
  then $\epsilon^2u^2|g''|=\epsilon\,x^2(1+x^2)^{-\alpha/2-2}c_2\leq c_2\epsilon$,
  $\epsilon^2|u||g''|=\epsilon^{3/2}|x|(1+x^2)^{-\alpha/2-2}c_2\leq c_2\epsilon$ and
  $\epsilon^3|u|^3|g'''|\leq c_3\epsilon^{3/2}\leq c_3\epsilon$ (using $\epsilon\le1$).
  (4): $\sq A_\epsilon(u)=c_\alpha[g(\sigma)-g(0)-g'(0)\sigma]$ with $\sigma=\epsilon u^2$ (note $g'(0)=-\alpha/2$),
  so Taylor's formula gives $|\sq A_\epsilon(u)|\leq \frac{c_\alpha c_2}{2}\epsilon^2u^4$. Also
  $\sq A_\epsilon'(u)=2c_\alpha\epsilon u\,[g'(\epsilon u^2)-g'(0)]$ and $|g'(\sigma)-g'(0)|\leq c_2\sigma$.

nodes.title: Secant calculus
nodes.statement_html:
Let $w\in C^1(\R)$ with $\sup|w'|<\infty$. Then:
  • $|S_w(y,z)|\leq\sup_{\R}|w'|$ for all $y\neq z$; more precisely $|S_w(y,z)|\le\sup_{I}|w'|$ where $I$ is the segment between $y$ and $z$;
  • if moreover $w\in C^2(\R)$ with $\sup|w''|<\infty$, then for every $s\in\R$ the map $y\mapsto S_w(y,y-s)$ is $C^1$ with $\partial_yS_w(y,y-s)=S_{w'}(y,y-s)$, and $|S_{w'}(y,y-s)|\leq\sup|w''|$;
  • for fixed $z$ and $y\neq z$, $\partial_yS_w(y,z)=\dfrac{w'(y)-S_w(y,z)}{y-z}$;
  • $S_{w_1+w_2}=S_{w_1}+S_{w_2}$ and $S_{cw}=cS_w$ for $c\in\R$.
nodes.proof_html:
(1) mean value theorem. (2) differentiate $S_w(y,y-s)=\int_0^1w'(y-\theta s)\,d\theta$ under the
  integral (the integrand's $y$-derivative $w''(y-\theta s)$ is bounded), obtaining
  $\int_0^1w''(y-\theta s)\,d\theta=S_{w'}(y,y-s)$. (3) quotient rule. (4) linearity.

nodes.title: Fractional difference integral
nodes.statement_html: Let $0<p<1$, $A,B>0$, and let $w:\R\to\R$ satisfy $|w|\leq A$ and $|w(a)-w(b)|\leq B|a-b|$ for all $a,b$. Then for every $y\in\R$ \[\int_\R\frac{|w(y)-w(y-s)|}{|s|^{1+p}}\,ds\leq C_pA^{1-p}B^p,\qquad C_p=2^{2-p}\Bigl(\frac1{1-p}+\frac1p\Bigr).\]
nodes.proof_html:
$|w(y)-w(y-s)|\leq\min\{2A,B|s|\}$. Put $r=2A/B$. Then
  $\int_{|s|<r}B|s|^{-p}\,ds=\frac{2B r^{1-p}}{1-p}=\frac{2^{2-p}}{1-p}A^{1-p}B^p$ and
  $\int_{|s|\geq r}2A|s|^{-1-p}\,ds=\frac{4Ar^{-p}}{p}=\frac{2^{2-p}}{p}A^{1-p}B^p$.

nodes.title: Differentiating translated fractional integrals
nodes.statement_html: Let $0<p<1$ and $w\in C^3(\R)$ with $\sup|w^{(k)}|\leq B_k<\infty$, $k=1,2,3$ ($B_k>0$). Let $\Phi:\R\times\R\to\R$ be measurable, such that for every $s$ the map $y\mapsto\Phi(y,s)$ is differentiable, $y\mapsto \partial_y\Phi(y,s)$ is measurable in $(y,s)$, and $|\Phi|\leq M_0$, $|\partial_y\Phi|\leq M_1$ on $\R\times\R$. Set \[I(y)=\int_\R\frac{w'(y)-w'(y-s)}{|s|^{1+p}}\Phi(y,s)\,ds .\] Then the integral converges absolutely for every $y$, $I$ is differentiable on $\R$, \[I'(y)=\int_\R\frac{(w''(y)-w''(y-s))\Phi(y,s)+(w'(y)-w'(y-s))\partial_y\Phi(y,s)}{|s|^{1+p}}\,ds,\] and, with $C_p$ as in lem:c06_difference_integral, \[|I(y)|\leq C_pM_0B_1^{1-p}B_2^p,\qquad |I'(y)|\leq C_p\bigl(M_0B_2^{1-p}B_3^p+M_1B_1^{1-p}B_2^p\bigr).\]
nodes.proof_html: Absolute convergence and the bound for $I$: apply lem:c06_difference_integral to $w'$ ($A=B_1$, $B=B_2$). For differentiability use the dominated differentiation theorem (Mathlib: hasDerivAt\_integral\_of\_dominated\_loc\_of\_deriv\_le): the $y$-derivative of the integrand is bounded, uniformly in $y$, by $\bigl(M_0\min\{2B_2,B_3|s|\}+M_1\min\{2B_1,B_2|s|\}\bigr)|s|^{-1-p}$, which is integrable in $s$ by the computation in lem:c06_difference_integral; the integrand at a base point is integrable likewise. The bound for $I'$ follows by applying lem:c06_difference_integral to $w''$ ($A=B_2$, $B=B_3$) and to $w'$.

nodes.title: Continuity of the derivative of translated fractional integrals
nodes.statement_html: Under the hypotheses of lem:c06_translated_derivative ($0<p<1$, $w\in C^3(\R)$ with $\sup|w^{(k)}|\le B_k$, $k=1,2,3$; $\Phi$, $\partial_y\Phi$ jointly measurable and bounded by $M_0$, $M_1$, $y\mapsto\Phi(y,s)$ differentiable), assume in addition that $y\mapsto\partial_y\Phi(y,s)$ is continuous for every $s\in\R$. Then $I(y)=\int_\R\frac{w'(y)-w'(y-s)}{|s|^{1+p}}\Phi(y,s)\,ds$ is $C^1$ on $\R$.
nodes.proof_html: By lem:c06_translated_derivative, $I$ is differentiable with $I'(y)$ given by the integral of $\bigl[(w''(y)-w''(y-s))\Phi(y,s)+(w'(y)-w'(y-s))\partial_y\Phi(y,s)\bigr]|s|^{-1-p}$. For each $s\ne0$ this integrand is continuous in $y$ ($w',w''$ continuous, $\Phi(\cdot,s)$ differentiable, $\partial_y\Phi(\cdot,s)$ continuous) and it is dominated, uniformly in $y$, by $\bigl(M_0\min\{2B_2,B_3|s|\}+M_1\min\{2B_1,B_2|s|\}\bigr)|s|^{-1-p}\in L^1$ (lem:c06_difference_integral). Dominated convergence gives continuity of $I'$.

nodes.title: Elementary tail integrals
nodes.statement_html:
Let $0<p<1$.
  • For $a>1$ and $y>0$: $\int_{-\infty}^0(y-z)^{-a}\,dz=\frac{y^{1-a}}{a-1}$.
  • For $a>1$, $r>0$ and $y\in\R$: $\int_{|y-z|\geq r}|y-z|^{-a}\,dz=\frac{2r^{1-a}}{a-1}$.
  • For $a>0$ and $y>0$: $\int_{-\infty}^0\ang z^{-1-p}(y-z)^{-a}\,dz\leq(1+\frac1p)\,y^{-a}$.
  • For $a>1-p$ and $y>0$: $\int_0^\infty\ang t^{-p}(y+t)^{-a}\,dt\leq\bigl(\frac1{1-p}+\frac1{a+p-1}\bigr)y^{1-p-a}$.
nodes.proof_html:
(1),(2) direct integration. (3) $(y-z)^{-a}\leq y^{-a}$ for $z\leq0$ and
  $\int_{-\infty}^0\ang z^{-1-p}\,dz\leq1+\int_1^\infty z^{-1-p}\,dz=1+\frac1p$.
  (4) On $[0,y]$ use $(y+t)^{-a}\leq y^{-a}$ and $\ang t^{-p}\leq t^{-p}$, giving
  $y^{-a}\frac{y^{1-p}}{1-p}$; on $[y,\infty)$ use $\ang t^{-p}(y+t)^{-a}\leq t^{-p-a}$, giving
  $\frac{y^{1-p-a}}{a+p-1}$.

nodes.title: Consequences of the profile bounds
nodes.statement_html:
Let $\epsilon_0\le\epsilon_0^*(\delta)$ (standing assumptions). There is an admissible constant $C_0\geq1$ such that for all $\epsilon\in[0,\epsilon_0]$, $\mu\in\ov B$, $f=\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu}$ is a real $C^\infty$ function and
  • $|f'(z)|\leq C_0$ and $|f(z)-W(z)|\leq C_0\ang z^{-p}$ for all $z\in\R$;
  • $|f(z)|\leq C_0\ang z^{-p}$ and $|f'(z)|\le C_0\ang z^{-\beta}$ for $z\geq0$, and $|f'(z)+1|\leq C_0\ang z^{-p-1}$ for $z\leq0$;
  • for $z\geq1$ and $k=0,1,2$: $|f(z)|\le C_0z^{-p}$ and $|f^{(k+1)}(z)|\leq C_0z^{-\beta+k/p}$.
nodes.proof_html: Smoothness and the bounds for $y\geq0$ (with $j\le2$) and $y\le0$ (with $j\le1$) are prop:approx_profile_bounds; its constants are uniform in $\epsilon,\mu$. For $z\le0$, $W(z)=-z$, so $f-W=f+z$ and $|f'|\le1+|f'+1|$; for $z\ge0$, $W=0$ and $\ang z^{-\beta}\le1$. For (3): for $z\geq1$, $z\leq\ang z\leq\sqrt2 z$, so $\ang z^{b}\le 2^{|b|/2}z^{b}$ for every real $b$.

nodes.title: Representation of $f$ on the positive side
nodes.statement_html:
Let $P(y)=-2\operatorname{Re}\int_y^\infty\bigl(Z(t)+c_{\textup{cubic}}Z(t)^3\bigr)\,dt$ for $y\geq R$ (absolutely convergent). There is an admissible constant $C_1$ such that for all $\epsilon\in[0,\epsilon_0]$, $\mu\in\ov B$:
  • $|c_\epsilon|+|c_+|\leq C_1\epsilon$;
  • for $y\geq2R$: $f(y)=f_{0,\textup{low}}(y)+c_+y^{-p}+P(y)$ and \[f'(y)-2\operatorname{Re}\bigl(Z(y)+c_{\textup{cubic}}Z(y)^3\bigr)=f_{0,\textup{low}}'(y)-pc_+y^{-p-1};\]
  • for $y\geq2R$ and $0\le k\le3$: $|\partial_y^k(f_{0,\textup{low}}+c_+y^{-p})(y)|\leq C_1y^{-p-k}$;
  • for $y\geq2R$ and $j=0,1$: $\bigl|\partial_y^j\bigl[f'-2\operatorname{Re}(Z+c_{\textup{cubic}}Z^3)\bigr](y)\bigr|\leq C_1y^{-p-1-j}$.
nodes.proof_html: (1) $|c_\epsilon|\lesssim\epsilon$ is lem:analysis_coefficient and $c_+=-c_\epsilon/(p+1)$ (eqn:approx\_correction\_constants). Absolute convergence of $P$: $|Z(t)|\le C t^{-\beta}$ for $t\geq R$ (from lem:approx_phase_differences with $j=0$ and $|Z_0|=|f_{0,+}'|\lesssim t^{-\beta}$, $\mu/\mu_*$ bounded on $\ov B$) and $\beta>1$. (2) is eqn:approx\_family\_positive of def:approximate_solution_family; differentiating (fundamental theorem of calculus for the absolutely convergent tail integral) gives the second identity. (3) For $y\geq2R\geq R_0$, $W(y)=0$ and lem:approx_linear_seed(2) gives $|\partial^k f_{0,\textup{low}}(y)|\lesssim y^{-p-k}$; also $|\partial^k y^{-p}|\le C_k y^{-p-k}$ and (1). (4) follows from (2), (3) with $k=j+1$.

nodes.title: Wedge kernel
nodes.statement_html: For $\epsilon\ge0$, $y>0$, $t\ge0$ set \[K_\epsilon(y,t)=\frac{A_\epsilon\bigl(-t/(y+t)\bigr)-1}{(y+t)^{1+p}} .\]

nodes.title: Wedge kernel bounds and identities
nodes.statement_html:
There is a constant $C_K$ depending only on $p$ such that for $0\le\epsilon\le1$, $y>0$, $t\ge0$:
  • $K_\epsilon(y,0)=0$ and $K_\epsilon$ is $C^\infty$ on $(0,\infty)\times[0,\infty)$;
  • $|\partial_y^kK_\epsilon(y,t)|\leq C_K\epsilon(y+t)^{-1-p-k}$ for $k=0,1,2$;
  • $\partial_yK_\epsilon(y,t)-\partial_tK_\epsilon(y,t)=\dfrac{A_\epsilon'(-t/(y+t))}{(y+t)^{p+2}}$.
nodes.proof_html: Write $\sigma=t/(y+t)\in[0,1)$, $G(\sigma)=A_\epsilon(-\sigma)-1$, so $K=G(\sigma)(y+t)^{-1-p}$. By lem:c06_A_eps_bounds (with $|\sigma|\le1$): $|G|\le\frac\alpha2\epsilon$, $|G'|\le\alpha\epsilon$, $|G''|\le C_A\epsilon$ on $[0,1]$. (1): $G(0)=0$. (2): $\partial_y\sigma=-\sigma/(y+t)$, so $\partial_yK=-(y+t)^{-2-p}\bigl[\sigma G'(\sigma)+(1+p)G(\sigma)\bigr]$ and $\partial_y^2K=(y+t)^{-3-p}\bigl[\sigma^2G''+(2p+4)\sigma G'+(1+p)(2+p)G\bigr]$ (using $\partial_y(\sigma G'(\sigma))=-(\sigma G'+\sigma^2G'')/(y+t)$); bound each bracket using $0\le\sigma\le1$. (3): $\partial_y\sigma-\partial_t\sigma=-\frac{t}{(y+t)^2}-\frac{y}{(y+t)^2}=-\frac1{y+t}$ and the factor $(y+t)^{-1-p}$ has equal $y$- and $t$-derivatives, so $\partial_yK-\partial_tK=-G'(\sigma)(y+t)^{-2-p}=A_\epsilon'(-\sigma)(y+t)^{-2-p}$.

nodes.title: Mass of the wedge kernel
nodes.statement_html: For $\epsilon\ge0$ and $y>0$: $c_\alpha\int_0^\infty K_\epsilon(y,t)\,dt=c_\epsilon y^{-p}$, where $c_\epsilon=c_\alpha\int_0^1[(1+\epsilon\sigma^2)^{-\alpha/2}-1](1-\sigma)^{p-1}\,d\sigma$ is the constant of lem:analysis_coefficient.
nodes.proof_html: Substitute $t=y\sigma/(1-\sigma)$, $\sigma\in[0,1)$: $y+t=y/(1-\sigma)$, $dt=y(1-\sigma)^{-2}d\sigma$, so $\int_0^\infty K\,dt=y^{-p}\int_0^1[A_\epsilon(-\sigma)-1](1-\sigma)^{p-1}\,d\sigma$, and $A_\epsilon$ is even. This is the computation in the proof of lem:analysis_coefficient. The integral converges since $p-1>-1$.

nodes.title: First variation of $\mc Q_\epsilon$ at the wedge
nodes.statement_html: Let $0\le\epsilon\le1$ and let $h:\R\to\R$ be bounded and Lipschitz, with $h\in C^2((0,\infty))$. Fix $y>0$. Then $s\mapsto\mc Q_\epsilon(W+sh)(y)$ is differentiable at $s=0$, and its derivative $D\mc Q_\epsilon(W)[h](y)$ equals \begin{equation} c_\alpha\Bigl(\int_0^\infty K_\epsilon(y,t)\bigl(h'(y)-h'(-t)\bigr)\,dt\Bigr) +c_\alpha\Bigl(\int_0^\infty\frac{A_\epsilon'(-t/(y+t))}{(y+t)^{p+2}}\bigl(h(y)-h(-t)\bigr)\,dt\Bigr) \end{equation} (here $h'(-t)$ is the a.e.\ derivative), equivalently, in the $z$ variable, $c_\alpha\int_{-\infty}^0\frac{h'(y)-h'(z)}{(y-z)^{1+p}}[A_\epsilon(S_W(y,z))-1]\,dz +c_\alpha\int_{-\infty}^0\frac{A_\epsilon'(S_W(y,z))S_h(y,z)}{(y-z)^{1+p}}\,dz$, with $S_W(y,z)=z/(y-z)$. Moreover the function $y\mapsto\int_0^\infty K_\epsilon(y,t)(h(y)-h(-t))\,dt$ is differentiable on $(0,\infty)$ and \begin{equation} D\mc Q_\epsilon(W)[h](y)=c_\alpha\int_0^\infty\bigl[K_\epsilon(y,t)h'(y)+\partial_yK_\epsilon(y,t)(h(y)-h(-t))\bigr]dt =c_\alpha\,\partial_y\!\int_0^\infty K_\epsilon(y,t)\bigl(h(y)-h(-t)\bigr)\,dt . \end{equation}
nodes.proof_html:
Step 1 (Gâteaux derivative). For $y>0$: $W'(y)=0$; for $z>0$, $S_W(y,z)=0$; for $z<0$, $W'(z)=-1$ and $S_W(y,z)=z/(y-z)\in(-1,0)$. Let $L$ be the Lipschitz constant of $h$. The $z>0$ part of $\mc Q_\epsilon(W+sh)(y)$ is $c_\alpha s\int_0^\infty\frac{h'(y)-h'(z)}{|y-z|^{1+p}}[A_\epsilon(sS_h(y,z))-1]\,dz$, whose modulus is $\le c_\alpha\frac\alpha2\epsilon L^2|s|^3\int_0^\infty|h'(y)-h'(z)||y-z|^{-1-p}dz=O(|s|^3)$ (the last integral is finite: near $z=y$ use $h\in C^2$ near $y$, elsewhere $|h'|\le L$); hence it contributes $0$ to the derivative. The $z<0$ part is $c_\alpha\int_{-\infty}^0\bigl(1+s(h'(y)-h'(z))\bigr)[A_\epsilon(S_W+sS_h)-1](y-z)^{-1-p}\,dz$; for $|s|\le1$ the $s$-derivative of the integrand is bounded by $C(L)\epsilon(y-z)^{-1-p}$ (using $|A_\epsilon-1|\le\frac\alpha2\epsilon u^2$, $|A_\epsilon'(u)|\le\alpha\epsilon|u|$ with $|u|\le 1+L$, $|S_h|\le L$), which is integrable on $(-\infty,0)$ since $y-z\ge y>0$. Differentiating under the integral at $s=0$ and substituting $z=-t$ gives eq:c06_first_variation_F1.

Step 2 (integration by parts). By lem:c06_wedge_kernel_bounds(3) the second integral in eq:c06_first_variation_F1 is $c_\alpha\int_0^\infty(\partial_yK-\partial_tK)(h(y)-h(-t))\,dt$, each part absolutely convergent ($|\partial_yK|,|\partial_tK|\lesssim\epsilon(y+t)^{-2-p}$, $h$ bounded; for $\partial_tK$ use (3) and lem:c06_A_eps_bounds(2)). On $[0,T]$, $t\mapsto h(y)-h(-t)$ is Lipschitz with a.e.\ derivative $h'(-t)$, so $-\int_0^T\partial_tK\,(h(y)-h(-t))\,dt=-K(y,T)(h(y)-h(-T))+K(y,0)(h(y)-h(0))+\int_0^TK\,h'(-t)\,dt$. The boundary terms vanish: $K(y,0)=0$ and $|K(y,T)|\,2\sup|h|\le 2C_K\epsilon\sup|h|\,(y+T)^{-1-p}\to0$. Adding to the first integral of eq:c06_first_variation_F1 the terms $\pm K h'(-t)$ cancel, giving the first equality in eq:c06_first_variation_F2 (all integrals absolutely convergent since $\int_0^\infty|K|\,dt<\infty$).

Step 3 (divergence form). For $y$ in a compact $J\subset(0,\infty)$ with $\min J=y_1$, $|\partial_y[K(y,t)(h(y)-h(-t))]|\le C_K\epsilon\bigl[(y_1+t)^{-2-p}2\sup|h|+(y_1+t)^{-1-p}L\bigr]$, integrable in $t$; dominated differentiation gives the second equality.

nodes.title: Exact decomposition of $\mc E_6$
nodes.statement_html: For $\epsilon\in[0,\epsilon_0]$, $\mu\in\ov B$ and $y\ge2R$, \[\mc E_6(y)=c_\epsilon y^{-p}\bigl[f_{0,\textup{low}}'(y)-pc_+y^{-p-1}\bigr]-pc_\epsilon y^{-p-1}f(y) -c_\alpha\int_0^\infty\partial_yK_\epsilon(y,t)\bigl(f(-t)-t\bigr)\,dt,\] and the last integral converges absolutely.
nodes.proof_html: $h=f-W$ is bounded and Lipschitz (lem:c06_profile_consequences(1); $W$ is $1$-Lipschitz) and $h=f$ is smooth on $(0,\infty)$. For $y>0$, $h(y)=f(y)$ and $h(-t)=f(-t)-t$. By eq:c06_first_variation_F2 and lem:c06_wedge_kernel_mass, \[D\mc Q_\epsilon(W)[f-W](y)=\partial_y\bigl(c_\epsilon y^{-p}f(y)\bigr)-c_\alpha\,\partial_y\!\int_0^\infty K_\epsilon(y,t)(f(-t)-t)\,dt,\] and the last derivative may be taken under the integral (dominated by $C_K\epsilon(y_1+t)^{-2-p}C_0$ on compacts, using $|f(-t)-t|\le C_0$). Hence $D\mc Q_\epsilon(W)[f-W]=c_\epsilon y^{-p}f'-pc_\epsilon y^{-p-1}f-c_\alpha\int_0^\infty\partial_yK(f(-t)-t)\,dt$. Subtract $2c_\epsilon y^{-p}\operatorname{Re}(Z+c_{\textup{cubic}}Z^3)$ and use lem:c06_positive_representation(2).

nodes.title: Remote wedge interaction
nodes.statement_html: Let $\mc R_6(y)=c_\alpha\int_0^\infty\partial_yK_\epsilon(y,t)(f(-t)-t)\,dt$ for $y>0$. Then $\mc R_6\in C^1((0,\infty))$, $\mc R_6'(y)=c_\alpha\int_0^\infty\partial_y^2K_\epsilon(y,t)(f(-t)-t)\,dt$, and there is an admissible $C$ with \[|\partial_y^j\mc R_6(y)|\le C\epsilon\,y^{-2p-1-j},\qquad y>0,\ j=0,1,\] for all $\epsilon\in[0,\epsilon_0]$, $\mu\in\ov B$.
nodes.proof_html: By lem:c06_profile_consequences(1) with $z=-t$: $|f(-t)-t|=|f(-t)-W(-t)|\le C_0\ang t^{-p}$. By lem:c06_wedge_kernel_bounds(2), $|\partial_y^{1+j}K|\le C_K\epsilon(y+t)^{-2-p-j}$; on compact subsets of $(0,\infty)$ this gives an integrable dominating function, justifying differentiation under the integral. Then $|\partial^j_y\mc R_6(y)|\le c_\alpha C_KC_0\,\epsilon\int_0^\infty\ang t^{-p}(y+t)^{-p-2-j}dt$ and lem:c06_tail_integrals(4) with $a=p+2+j$ gives the bound $\lesssim\epsilon y^{1-p-(p+2+j)}=\epsilon y^{-2p-1-j}$.

nodes.title: Control of $\mc E_6$
nodes.statement_html: There is an admissible constant $C$ such that for all $\epsilon\in[0,\epsilon_0]$, $\mu\in\ov B$, $\mc E_6$ is $C^1$ on $(2R,\infty)$ and \[|\partial_y^j\mc E_6(y)|\le C\epsilon\ang y^{-2p-1+\frac jp},\qquad y\geq 8R,\quad j=0,1.\] In fact $|\mc E_6(y)|\le C\epsilon y^{-2p-1}$ and $|\partial_y\mc E_6(y)|\le C\epsilon(y^{-2p-2}+y^{-p-1-\beta})$.
nodes.proof_html: Use lem:c06_E6_exact_decomposition: $\mc E_6=T_1-T_2-\mc R_6$ with $T_1=c_\epsilon y^{-p}g$, $g=f_{0,\textup{low}}'-pc_+y^{-p-1}$, and $T_2=pc_\epsilon y^{-p-1}f$.
