By lem:c06_positive_representation(1),(4): $|c_\epsilon|\le C_1\epsilon$ and $|g|\le C_1y^{-p-1}$, $|g'|\le C_1y^{-p-2}$; so $|T_1|\le C\epsilon y^{-2p-1}$, $|T_1'|\le C\epsilon(py^{-2p-2}+y^{-2p-2})$. By lem:c06_profile_consequences(3) ($y\ge2R\ge1$): $|f|\le C_0y^{-p}$, $|f'|\le C_0y^{-\beta}$, so $|T_2|\le C\epsilon y^{-2p-1}$ and $|T_2'|\le C\epsilon(y^{-2p-2}+y^{-p-1-\beta})$. lem:c06_E6_remote_term bounds $\mc R_6$. This proves the "in fact" bounds. Conversion: $y^{-2p-2}\le y^{-2p-1+1/p}$ and $y^{-p-1-\beta}\le y^{-2p-1+1/p}$, the latter because $p-\beta<1/p$ (as $p<1<1/p$). Finally, for $y\ge1$ and $b>0$, $y^{-b}\le 2^{b/2}\ang y^{-b}$, and $b=2p+1-j/p>0$ for $j=0,1$ (since $1/p<4/3<2p+1$).

nodes.title: Bounds for the localized pieces
nodes.statement_html:
Let $Y\ge8R$, $\epsilon\in[0,\epsilon_0]$, $\mu\in\ov B$, and $h_Y:=\chi_Yf-v_Y$. Then:
  • $\chi_Yf$, $v_Y$, $h_Y$ are $C^\infty$ with support in $(Y/4,4Y)\subset(2R,\infty)$, and $h_Y=\chi_Y\,(f_{0,\textup{low}}+c_+z^{-p})$;
  • there is an admissible constant $C_2$ such that for all $z\in\R$: \begin{align*} |\partial^jh_Y(z)|&\le C_2Y^{-p-j}\quad(0\le j\le3),\\ |\chi_Yf(z)|\le C_2Y^{-p},\qquad |\partial^{j+1}(\chi_Yf)(z)|&\le C_2Y^{-\beta+j/p}\quad(0\le j\le2),\\ |\partial^{j+1}v_Y(z)|&\le C_2Y^{-\beta+j/p}\quad(0\le j\le2). \end{align*}
nodes.proof_html: (1) $\operatorname{supp}\chi_Y\subset(Y/4,4Y)$ and $Y/4\ge2R$. By definition $v_Y=\chi_YP$ with $P$ as in lem:c06_positive_representation, so lem:c06_positive_representation(2) gives $h_Y=\chi_Y(f-P)=\chi_Y(f_{0,\textup{low}}+c_+z^{-p})$. Smoothness of $P$ on $(R,\infty)$ follows from $P'=2\operatorname{Re}(Z+c_{\textup{cubic}}Z^3)$ and smoothness of $Z$. (2) Leibniz rule with $|\partial^k\chi_Y|\le C_kY^{-k}$ and, on $[Y/4,4Y]$ (where $z\simeq Y$ up to factor $4$): for $h_Y$, lem:c06_positive_representation(3) gives $|\partial^k(f_{0,\textup{low}}+c_+z^{-p})|\le C_14^{p+k}Y^{-p-k}$; each Leibniz term is $\lesssim Y^{-m}Y^{-p-(j-m)}=Y^{-p-j}$. For $\chi_Yf$, lem:c06_profile_consequences(3): the term with $m$ derivatives on $\chi_Y$ is $\lesssim Y^{-m}Y^{-\beta+(j-m)/p}\le Y^{-\beta+j/p}$ for $m\le j$, and for $m=j+1$ it is $\lesssim Y^{-j-1}Y^{-p}\le Y^{-\beta+j/p}$ because $\beta<1+p$ and $Y\ge1$. For $v_Y=\chi_Yf-h_Y$ combine the two, using $Y^{-p-1-j}\le Y^{-\beta+j/p}$.

nodes.title: Algebraic form of $\mc E_7$
nodes.statement_html: With $h=h_Y$, $v=v_Y$ and $\kappa:=-\frac{(p+1)\epsilon c_\alpha}2$, for every $y\in\R$ \[\mc E_7(y)=\kappa\,(T_{7,1}(y)+T_{7,2}(y)),\] \[T_{7,1}(y)=\int_\R\frac{h'(y)-h'(y-s)}{|s|^{1+p}}S_{v+h}(y,y-s)^2\,ds,\quad T_{7,2}(y)=\int_\R\frac{v'(y)-v'(y-s)}{|s|^{1+p}}S_h(y,y-s)\,S_{2v+h}(y,y-s)\,ds,\] all integrals (including those defining $\mc Q_{\epsilon,3}(\chi_Yf)$ and $\mc Q_{\epsilon,3}(v_Y)$) converging absolutely.
nodes.proof_html: Absolute convergence: for $w\in\{v,\chi_Yf\}$, $|S_w|\le\sup|w'|$ and lem:c06_difference_integral applies to $w'$. Substitute $z=y-s$ (so $|y-z|^\alpha=|s|^{1+p}$). With $a_1=(v+h)'(y)-(v+h)'(z)$, $b_1=S_{v+h}$, $a_2=v'(y)-v'(z)$, $b_2=S_v$ use $a_1b_1^2-a_2b_2^2=(a_1-a_2)b_1^2+a_2(b_1-b_2)(b_1+b_2)$ together with $v+h=\chi_Yf$, $a_1-a_2=h'(y)-h'(z)$, $b_1-b_2=S_h$, $b_1+b_2=S_{2v+h}$ (lem:c06_secant_calculus(4)).

nodes.title: Size of $\mc E_7$
nodes.statement_html: There is an admissible $C$ such that for $Y\ge8R$, all $y\in\R$, $\epsilon\in[0,\epsilon_0]$, $\mu\in\ov B$: $|T_{7,1}(y)|\le CY^{-2p-1-2\beta}$, $|T_{7,2}(y)|\le CY^{-p-2\beta}$, hence $|\mc E_7(y)|\le C\epsilon Y^{-p-2\beta}$.
nodes.proof_html: By lem:c06_localized_bounds and lem:c06_secant_calculus(1): $|S_{v+h}|=|S_{\chi_Yf}|\le C_2Y^{-\beta}$, $|S_h|\le C_2Y^{-p-1}$, $|S_{2v+h}|\le3C_2Y^{-\beta}$. lem:c06_difference_integral with $w=h'$ ($A=C_2Y^{-p-1}$, $B=C_2Y^{-p-2}$) gives $\int|h'(y)-h'(y-s)||s|^{-1-p}ds\le C_pC_2Y^{-(p+1)(1-p)-(p+2)p}=C_pC_2Y^{-2p-1}$; with $w=v'$ ($A=C_2Y^{-\beta}$, $B=C_2Y^{-\beta+1/p}$) it gives $C_pC_2Y^{1-\beta}$. Hence $|T_{7,1}|\lesssim Y^{-2\beta}Y^{-2p-1}$ and $|T_{7,2}|\lesssim Y^{-p-1}Y^{-\beta}Y^{1-\beta}$. Since $2p+1+2\beta\ge p+2\beta$ and $Y\ge1$, and $|\kappa|\le C\epsilon$, the claim follows.

nodes.title: Derivative of $\mc E_7$
nodes.statement_html: For $Y\ge8R$, $\mc E_7$ is differentiable on $\R$ and there is an admissible $C$ with $|\partial_y\mc E_7(y)|\le C\epsilon Y^{-p-2\beta+1/p}$ for all $y\in\R$, $\epsilon\in[0,\epsilon_0]$, $\mu\in\ov B$.
nodes.proof_html: Apply lem:c06_translated_derivative to $T_{7,1}$ with $w=h$, $\Phi(y,s)=S_{\chi_Yf}(y,y-s)^2$: by lem:c06_secant_calculus(2), $\partial_y\Phi=2S_{\chi_Yf}S_{(\chi_Yf)'}$, so $M_0=C_2^2Y^{-2\beta}$, $M_1=2C_2^2Y^{-2\beta+1/p}$, and $B_k=C_2Y^{-p-k}$ ($k=1,2,3$). Thus $|T_{7,1}'|\lesssim Y^{-2\beta}Y^{-(p+2)(1-p)-(p+3)p}+Y^{-2\beta+1/p}Y^{-2p-1}=Y^{-2\beta-2p-2}+Y^{-2\beta-2p-1+1/p}$. Apply it to $T_{7,2}$ with $w=v$, $\Phi=S_hS_{2v+h}$, $\partial_y\Phi=S_{h'}S_{2v+h}+S_hS_{2v'+h'}$: $M_0=3C_2^2Y^{-p-1-\beta}$, $M_1\lesssim Y^{-p-2-\beta}+Y^{-p-1-\beta+1/p}$, and $B_k=C_2Y^{-\beta+(k-1)/p}$. Since $B_2^{1-p}B_3^p\lesssim Y^{1-\beta+1/p}$ and $B_1^{1-p}B_2^p\lesssim Y^{1-\beta}$: $|T_{7,2}'|\lesssim Y^{-p-2\beta+1/p}+Y^{-p-1-2\beta}$. All four exponents are $\le -p-2\beta+1/p$ (using $p\le 1/p$, $Y\ge1$). Multiply by $|\kappa|\le C\epsilon$.

nodes.title: Control of $\mc E_7$
nodes.statement_html: There is an admissible $C$ such that for all $Y\ge8R$, $\epsilon\in[0,\epsilon_0]$, $\mu\in\ov B$, \[|\partial_y^j\mc E_7(y)|\le C\epsilon\ang y^{-p-2\beta+\frac jp}\le C\epsilon\ang y^{-2p-1+\frac jp},\qquad Y\le y\le2Y,\ j=0,1.\]
nodes.proof_html: By lem:c06_E7_value, lem:c06_E7_derivative, $|\partial^j\mc E_7|\le C\epsilon Y^{-p-2\beta+j/p}$. The exponent $-p-2\beta+j/p=-p-1-(1-j)/p$ is negative, and for $1\le Y\le y\le2Y$ we have $\ang y\le\sqrt2y\le2\sqrt2Y$, so $Y^{-b}\le(2\sqrt2)^b\ang y^{-b}$ for $b\geq0$. The second inequality is $p+2\beta\ge2p+1$, i.e.\ $1/p\ge p$.

nodes.title: $\mc E_7$ is $C^1$
nodes.statement_html: Under the standing assumptions of this chapter (in particular $\delta\in(0,|\mu_*|/2]$ and $\epsilon_0\in(0,\epsilon_0^*(\delta)]$) there is $R_0\ge1$ such that for all $R\ge R_0$, $Y\ge8R$, $\epsilon\in[0,\epsilon_0]$ and $\mu\in\ov B$, with $f=\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu}$: $\mc E_7^Y$ is $C^1$ on $\R$.
nodes.proof_html: By lem:c06_E7_decomposition, $\mc E_7^Y=\kappa(T_{7,1}+T_{7,2})$. Each $T_{7,i}$ has the form of lem:c06_translated_C1 with $w=h_Y$, $\Phi=S_{v+h}(y,y-s)^2$, resp.\ $w=v_Y$, $\Phi=S_h(y,y-s)S_{2v+h}(y,y-s)$; the bounds on $w^{(k)}$, $\Phi$, $\partial_y\Phi$ come from lem:c06_localized_bounds and lem:c06_secant_calculus, and $\partial_y\Phi$ is continuous in $y$ because the secants of the $C^\infty$ functions $v_Y$, $h_Y$ have continuous $y$-derivatives $\partial_yS_w(y,y-s)=\int_0^1w''(y-\theta s)\,d\theta$.

nodes.title: Quintic remainder representation
nodes.statement_html: Let $0\le\epsilon\le1$ and $w\in C^2(\R)$ with $w',w''$ bounded. Then for every $y\in\R$ \[\mc Q_\epsilon(w)(y)-\mc Q_{\epsilon,3}(w)(y)=\int_\R\frac{w'(y)-w'(y-s)}{|s|^{1+p}}\,\sq A_\epsilon\bigl(S_w(y,y-s)\bigr)\,ds,\] with $\sq A_\epsilon$ as in lem:c06_A_eps_bounds, all three integrals converging absolutely.
nodes.proof_html: The integrands of $\mc Q_\epsilon(w)$ and $\mc Q_{\epsilon,3}(w)$ are $c_\alpha\frac{w'(y)-w'(z)}{|y-z|^{1+p}}[A_\epsilon(S_w)-1]$ and $c_\alpha\frac{w'(y)-w'(z)}{|y-z|^{1+p}}[-\frac\alpha2\epsilon S_w^2]$ (note $\frac{p+1}2=\frac\alpha2$); each is bounded by a constant times $|w'(y)-w'(z)||y-z|^{-1-p}$ since $S_w$ is bounded, which is integrable by lem:c06_difference_integral. Subtract and substitute $z=y-s$.

nodes.title: Control of $\mc E_8$
nodes.statement_html: There is an admissible $C$ such that for all $Y\ge8R$, $\epsilon\in[0,\epsilon_0]$, $\mu\in\ov B$, $\mc E_8$ is differentiable, $|\mc E_8(y)|\le C\epsilon^2Y^{1-5\beta}$, $|\partial_y\mc E_8(y)|\le C\epsilon^2Y^{1-5\beta+1/p}$ for all $y\in\R$, and \[|\partial_y^j\mc E_8(y)|\le C\epsilon^2\ang y^{-2p-1+\frac jp},\qquad Y\le y\le2Y,\ j=0,1.\]
nodes.proof_html: Apply lem:c06_quintic_representation with $w=\chi_Yf$ and then lem:c06_translated_derivative with $\Phi(y,s)=\sq A_\epsilon(S_w(y,y-s))$, $\partial_y\Phi=\sq A_\epsilon'(S_w)S_{w'}$ (lem:c06_secant_calculus(2)). By lem:c06_localized_bounds, $|S_w|\le C_2Y^{-\beta}$, $|S_{w'}|\le C_2Y^{-\beta+1/p}$, and $B_k=C_2Y^{-\beta+(k-1)/p}$; by lem:c06_A_eps_bounds(4), $M_0=C_AC_2^4\epsilon^2Y^{-4\beta}$, $M_1=C_AC_2^4\epsilon^2Y^{-4\beta+1/p}$. Hence $|\mc E_8|\lesssim\epsilon^2Y^{-4\beta}Y^{1-\beta}$ and $|\mc E_8'|\lesssim\epsilon^2(Y^{-4\beta}Y^{1-\beta+1/p}+Y^{-4\beta+1/p}Y^{1-\beta})$. Finally $5\beta>2p+2$ (equivalently $5/p+1>4p$, true as $p<1$), so $Y^{1-5\beta+j/p}\le Y^{-2p-1+j/p}$, and the conversion to $\ang y$ is as in the proof of lem:approx_E7 ($2p+1-j/p>0$).

nodes.title: $\mc E_8$ is $C^1$
nodes.statement_html: Under the standing assumptions of this chapter (in particular $\delta\in(0,|\mu_*|/2]$ and $\epsilon_0\in(0,\epsilon_0^*(\delta)]$) there is $R_0\ge1$ such that for all $R\ge R_0$, $Y\ge8R$, $\epsilon\in[0,\epsilon_0]$ and $\mu\in\ov B$, with $f=\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu}$: $\mc E_8^Y$ is $C^1$ on $\R$.
nodes.proof_html: By lem:c06_quintic_representation with $w=\chi_Yf$, $\mc E_8^Y$ is the integral of lem:c06_translated_C1 with $\Phi(y,s)=\sq A_\epsilon(S_w(y,y-s))$, whose $y$-derivative $\sq A_\epsilon'(S_w)\partial_yS_w$ is continuous ($\sq A_\epsilon$ smooth, $w\in C^\infty$) and bounded (lem:c06_A_eps_bounds, lem:c06_localized_bounds), with the constants computed in the proof of the bound for $\mc E_8$.

nodes.title: The cubic term of the local front is $C^1$
nodes.statement_html: Under the standing assumptions of this chapter (in particular $\delta\in(0,|\mu_*|/2]$ and $\epsilon_0\in(0,\epsilon_0^*(\delta)]$) there is $R_0\ge1$ such that for all $R\ge R_0$, $Y\ge8R$, $\epsilon\in[0,\epsilon_0]$ and $\mu\in\ov B$, with $f=\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu}$: $\mc Q_{\epsilon,3}(v_Y)$ is $C^1$ on $\R$.
nodes.proof_html: After the substitution $z=y-s$, $\mc Q_{\epsilon,3}(v_Y)(y)=\kappa\int_\R\frac{v_Y'(y)-v_Y'(y-s)}{|s|^{1+p}}S_{v_Y}(y,y-s)^2\,ds$ with $\kappa=-\frac{(p+1)\epsilon c_\alpha}2$; apply lem:c06_translated_C1 with $w=v_Y$ and $\Phi=S_{v_Y}^2$ (bounds from lem:c06_localized_bounds and lem:c06_secant_calculus); $\partial_y\Phi=2S_{v_Y}\partial_yS_{v_Y}$ is continuous in $y$ since $\partial_yS_{v_Y}(y,y-s)=\int_0^1v_Y''(y-\theta s)\,d\theta$.

nodes.title: Splitting of $\mc E_9$
nodes.statement_html: For $y\in J_Y$ (write $S_\bullet=S_\bullet(y,z)$), $\mc E_9(y)=\mc E_{9,+}(y)+\mc I_1(y)+\mc I_2(y)+\mc I_3(y)$, where \begin{align*} \mc E_{9,+}(y)&=c_\alpha\int_{(0,\infty)\setminus[Y/2,3Y]}\frac{(f'(y)-f'(z))[A_\epsilon(S_f)-1]-(f'(y)-(\chi_Yf)'(z))[A_\epsilon(S_{\chi_Yf})-1]}{|y-z|^{1+p}}\,dz,\\ \mc I_1(y)&=c_\alpha\int_{-\infty}^0\frac{A_\epsilon(S_f)-A_\epsilon(S_W)-A_\epsilon'(S_W)S_{f-W}}{(y-z)^{1+p}}\,dz,\\ \mc I_2(y)&=c_\alpha\int_{-\infty}^0\frac{(f'(y)-f'(z)-1)[A_\epsilon(S_f)-A_\epsilon(S_W)]}{(y-z)^{1+p}}\,dz,\\ \mc I_3(y)&=-c_\alpha\int_{-\infty}^0\frac{f'(y)}{(y-z)^{1+p}}\Bigl[A_\epsilon\Bigl(\frac{f(y)}{y-z}\Bigr)-1\Bigr]dz, \end{align*} with all integrals absolutely convergent.
nodes.proof_html: Split each of $\mc Q_\epsilon(f)(y)$, $\mc Q_\epsilon(\chi_Yf)(y)$ into $z>0$ and $z<0$. For $y>0$: $\mc Q_\epsilon(W)(y)=c_\alpha\int_{-\infty}^0[A_\epsilon(S_W)-1](y-z)^{-1-p}dz$ (since $W'(y)-W'(z)=1$ for $z<0$ and $S_W=0$ for $z>0$), and by lem:c06_wedge_first_variation (z-form, $h=f-W$, $h'(y)-h'(z)=f'(y)-f'(z)-1$ for $z<0$) $D\mc Q_\epsilon(W)[f-W](y)=c_\alpha\int_{-\infty}^0\frac{(f'(y)-f'(z)-1)[A_\epsilon(S_W)-1]+A_\epsilon'(S_W)S_{f-W}}{(y-z)^{1+p}}dz$. Writing $f'(y)-f'(z)=1+(f'(y)-f'(z)-1)$ in the $z<0$ part of $\mc Q_\epsilon(f)$ and using $S_f-S_W=S_{f-W}$, the $z<0$ parts of $\mc Q_\epsilon(f)-\mc Q_\epsilon(W)-D\mc Q_\epsilon(W)[f-W]$ combine to $\mc I_1+\mc I_2$. For $z<0$, $\chi_Y(z)=0$ and $\chi_Y=1$ near $y$, so the $z<0$ part of $-\mc Q_\epsilon(\chi_Yf)(y)$ is $\mc I_3$. For $z\in[Y/2,3Y]$ and $y\in J_Y$, $(\chi_Yf)(z)=f(z)$, $(\chi_Yf)'(z)=f'(z)$, $(\chi_Y f)(y)=f(y)$, so the two $z>0$ integrands cancel there, leaving $\mc E_{9,+}$. Absolute convergence: the $z<0$ integrands are $O(\epsilon(y-z)^{-2-p})$ by lem:c06_profile_consequences(1) and lem:c06_A_eps_bounds(1),(2) (all secants are bounded, $|S_{f-W}|\le 2C_0/(y-z)$); the integrand of $\mc E_{9,+}$ is $O(\epsilon|y-z|^{-3-p})$ on $|y-z|\ge Y/4$; and $\mc Q_\epsilon(f)(y)$, $\mc Q_\epsilon(\chi_Yf)(y)$ converge near $z=y$ since $|f'(y)-f'(z)|\le C_y|y-z|$ there and $|A_\epsilon-1|\le1$, and at infinity since $f'$ is bounded and $|A_\epsilon-1|\le1$.

nodes.title: Far positive contribution
nodes.statement_html: $\mc E_{9,+}$ is differentiable on $J_Y$ (derivative under the integral sign) and there is an admissible $C$ with $|\partial_y^j\mc E_{9,+}(y)|\le C\epsilon Y^{-p-2+j/p}$ for $y\in[Y,2Y]$, $j=0,1$, all $\epsilon\in[0,\epsilon_0]$, $\mu\in\ov B$.
nodes.proof_html: Let $g\in\{f,\chi_Yf\}$. On $[0,\infty)$: $|g|\le C_0$ and $|g'|\le C_0+\sup|\chi_Y'|C_0\le C$ (lem:c06_profile_consequences(2)); at $y\in J_Y$, $g(y)=f(y)$, $g'(y)=f'(y)$, $g''(y)=f''(y)$ with $|f'(y)|\le C Y^{-\beta}$, $|f''(y)|\le CY^{-\beta+1/p}$ (lem:c06_profile_consequences(3)). For $z>0$ with $|y-z|\ge Y/4\geq1$: $|S_g(y,z)|\le2C_0|y-z|^{-1}$ and, by lem:c06_secant_calculus(3), $|\partial_yS_g(y,z)|\le(|f'(y)|+|S_g|)|y-z|^{-1}\le C|y-z|^{-1}$; by lem:c06_A_eps_bounds(1),(2), $|A_\epsilon(S_g)-1|\le C\epsilon|y-z|^{-2}$ and $|A_\epsilon'(S_g)|\le C\epsilon|y-z|^{-1}$. With $F_g(y,z)=(f'(y)-g'(z))[A_\epsilon(S_g)-1]|y-z|^{-1-p}$ we get $|F_g|\le C\epsilon|y-z|^{-3-p}$ and \[|\partial_yF_g|\le |f''(y)||A_\epsilon(S_g)-1||y-z|^{-1-p}+C|A_\epsilon'(S_g)||\partial_yS_g||y-z|^{-1-p}+(1+p)C|A_\epsilon(S_g)-1||y-z|^{-2-p}\] $\le C\epsilon(Y^{-\beta+1/p}+1)|y-z|^{-3-p}$, uniformly for $y\in J_Y$ (this also justifies differentiating under the integral). By lem:c06_tail_integrals(2) with $r=Y/4$, $a=3+p$: $|\partial^j\mc E_{9,+}|\le C\epsilon(1+Y^{-\beta+1/p})^jY^{-2-p}$, and $1+Y^{-\beta+1/p}\le2Y^{1/p}$.

nodes.title: Second-order Taylor term $\mc I_1$
nodes.statement_html: $\mc I_1$ is differentiable on $J_Y$ and there is an admissible $C$ with $|\mc I_1(y)|\le C\epsilon Y^{-p-2}$, $|\partial_y\mc I_1(y)|\le C\epsilon Y^{-p-3}$ for $y\in[Y,2Y]$.
nodes.proof_html: For $y\in J_Y$, $z<0$: $S_W=z/(y-z)\in(-1,0)$, $\partial_yS_W=-S_W/(y-z)$ so $|\partial_yS_W|\le(y-z)^{-1}$; $|S_{f-W}|\le2C_0(y-z)^{-1}$ (lem:c06_profile_consequences(1)); and since $W'(y)=0$, $\partial_yS_{f-W}=(f'(y)-S_{f-W})/(y-z)$, so $|\partial_yS_{f-W}|\le CY^{-\beta}(y-z)^{-1}+C(y-z)^{-2}$. Let $T=A_\epsilon(S_f)-A_\epsilon(S_W)-A_\epsilon'(S_W)S_{f-W}$. Taylor (eqn:approx\_E9\_I1\_taylor): $T=S_{f-W}^2\int_0^1(1-\theta)A_\epsilon''(S_W+\theta S_{f-W})d\theta$, so $|T|\le\frac{C_A}2\epsilon S_{f-W}^2\le C\epsilon(y-z)^{-2}$. Using $S_f=S_W+S_{f-W}$, $\partial_yT=[A_\epsilon'(S_f)-A_\epsilon'(S_W)-A_\epsilon''(S_W)S_{f-W}]\partial_yS_W+[A_\epsilon'(S_f)-A_\epsilon'(S_W)]\partial_yS_{f-W}$, and by Taylor with $|A_\epsilon''|+|A_\epsilon'''|\le C_A\epsilon$: $|\partial_yT|\le C\epsilon[(y-z)^{-3}+Y^{-\beta}(y-z)^{-2}]$. Hence $|\partial_y(T(y-z)^{-1-p})|\le C\epsilon[(y-z)^{-4-p}+Y^{-\beta}(y-z)^{-3-p}]$ (uniformly on $J_Y$, justifying differentiation), and lem:c06_tail_integrals(1) gives $|\mc I_1|\le C\epsilon y^{-2-p}$, $|\mc I_1'|\le C\epsilon(y^{-3-p}+Y^{-\beta}y^{-2-p})\le C\epsilon Y^{-p-3}$ ($\beta>1$, $y\ge Y$).

nodes.title: Mixed term $\mc I_2$
nodes.statement_html: $\mc I_2$ is differentiable on $J_Y$ and there is an admissible $C$ with $|\partial^j_y\mc I_2(y)|\le C\epsilon Y^{-p-2+j/p}$ for $y\in[Y,2Y]$, $j=0,1$.
nodes.proof_html: With the secant bounds from the proof of lem:c06_E9_I1: all arguments $S_W+\theta S_{f-W}$ lie in $[-1-2C_0,2C_0]$, so $|A_\epsilon'|\le\alpha(1+2C_0)\epsilon$ there and (eqn:approx\_E9\_I2\_taylor) $|A_\epsilon(S_f)-A_\epsilon(S_W)|\le C\epsilon(y-z)^{-1}$. Also $|f'(y)-f'(z)-1|\le|f'(y)|+|f'(z)+1|\le C(Y^{-\beta}+\ang z^{-p-1})$ (lem:c06_profile_consequences(2),(3)). $j=0$: lem:c06_tail_integrals(1),(3) with $a=2+p$ give $|\mc I_2|\le C\epsilon(Y^{-\beta-1-p}+Y^{-2-p})\le C\epsilon Y^{-p-2}$. $j=1$: $\partial_y[A_\epsilon(S_f)-A_\epsilon(S_W)]=[A_\epsilon'(S_f)-A_\epsilon'(S_W)]\partial_yS_W+A_\epsilon'(S_f)\partial_yS_{f-W}$ (eqn:approx\_E9\_I2\_coefficient\_derivative), bounded by $C\epsilon[(y-z)^{-2}+Y^{-\beta}(y-z)^{-1}]$. Differentiating the integrand (three terms: $f''(y)$; the coefficient; the kernel, giving $(1+p)(y-z)^{-2-p}$) and using $|f''(y)|\le CY^{-\beta+1/p}$, lem:c06_tail_integrals(1),(3) give $|\mc I_2'|\le C\epsilon(Y^{-p-1-\beta+1/p}+Y^{-p-2-\beta}+Y^{-p-3}+Y^{-p-1-2\beta})\le C\epsilon Y^{-p-2+1/p}$, using $\beta>1$. The same pointwise bounds, uniform on $J_Y$, justify differentiation under the integral.

nodes.title: Truncation term $\mc I_3$
nodes.statement_html: $\mc I_3$ is differentiable on $J_Y$ and there is an admissible $C$ with $|\partial^j_y\mc I_3(y)|\le C\epsilon Y^{-p-2+j/p}$ for $y\in[Y,2Y]$, $j=0,1$.
nodes.proof_html: By lem:c06_A_eps_bounds(1),(2) (eqn:approx\_E9\_I3\_coefficient\_bounds) with $u=f(y)/(y-z)$ and $|f(y)|\le CY^{-p}$, $|f'(y)|\le CY^{-\beta}$, $|f''(y)|\le CY^{-\beta+1/p}$: $|\mc I_3|\le C\epsilon|f'(y)||f(y)|^2\int_{-\infty}^0(y-z)^{-3-p}dz\le C\epsilon Y^{-\beta-2p}Y^{-2-p}$. Using $\partial_y\frac{f(y)}{y-z}=\frac{f'(y)}{y-z}-\frac{f(y)}{(y-z)^2}$, $|\mc I_3'|\le C\epsilon\bigl[(|f''||f|^2+|f'|^2|f|)\int_{-\infty}^0(y-z)^{-3-p}dz+|f'||f|^2\int_{-\infty}^0(y-z)^{-4-p}dz\bigr]$ $\le C\epsilon[(Y^{-\beta-2p+1/p}+Y^{-2\beta-p})Y^{-p-2}+Y^{-\beta-2p}Y^{-p-3}]\le C\epsilon Y^{-p-2+1/p}$.

nodes.title: Control of $\mc E_9$
nodes.statement_html: There is an admissible $C$ such that for all $Y\ge8R$, $\epsilon\in[0,\epsilon_0]$, $\mu\in\ov B$, $\mc E_9$ is differentiable on $[Y,2Y]$ and \[|\partial_y^j\mc E_9(y)|\le C\epsilon\ang y^{-p-2+\frac jp},\qquad Y\le y\le2Y,\ j=0,1.\]
nodes.proof_html: Sum the four bounds (the identity of lem:c06_E9_split holds on the open set $J_Y\supset[Y,2Y]$, so derivatives add); $Y^{-p-3}\le Y^{-p-2+1/p}$. Convert to $\ang y$ as in lem:approx_E7, since $p+2-j/p>0$.

nodes.title: $C^1$ regularity of the pieces of $\mc E_9$
nodes.statement_html: Under the standing assumptions of this chapter (in particular $\delta\in(0,|\mu_*|/2]$ and $\epsilon_0\in(0,\epsilon_0^*(\delta)]$) there is $R_0\ge1$ such that for all $R\ge R_0$, $Y\ge8R$, $\epsilon\in[0,\epsilon_0]$ and $\mu\in\ov B$, with $f=\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu}$: each of the four functions $\mc E_{9,+}$, $\mc I_1$, $\mc I_2$, $\mc I_3$ of lem:c06_E9_split is $C^1$ on $J_Y=(3Y/4,5Y/2)$.
nodes.proof_html: The proofs of lem:c06_E9_positive, lem:c06_E9_I1, lem:c06_E9_I2 and lem:c06_E9_I3 differentiate under the integral sign with majorants uniform for $y\in J_Y$. The differentiated integrands are continuous in $y\in J_Y$ for each fixed $z$ ($f\in C^\infty$, $A_\epsilon$ smooth, secants $S_g(y,z)$ with $z$ off the diagonal), and are dominated by the same integrable majorants; dominated convergence gives continuity of the derivatives on $J_Y$.

nodes.title: $\mc E_9$ is $C^1$ on $J_Y$
nodes.statement_html: Under the standing assumptions of this chapter (in particular $\delta\in(0,|\mu_*|/2]$ and $\epsilon_0\in(0,\epsilon_0^*(\delta)]$) there is $R_0\ge1$ such that for all $R\ge R_0$, $Y\ge8R$, $\epsilon\in[0,\epsilon_0]$ and $\mu\in\ov B$, with $f=\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu}$: $\mc E_9^Y$ is $C^1$ on $J_Y=(3Y/4,5Y/2)\supset[Y,2Y]$.
nodes.proof_html: On the open set $J_Y$, $\mc E_9^Y=\mc E_{9,+}+\mc I_1+\mc I_2+\mc I_3$ (lem:c06_E9_split); each summand is $C^1$ on $J_Y$ by lem:c06_E9_parts_C1.

nodes.title: Free operator, cubic remainder, divided residual
nodes.statement_html:
Let $f\in C^2(\R;\R)$ with $f'\in L^\infty(\R)$ and $0\le\epsilon\le1$.
  • The secant is $S_f(y,z):=\frac{f(y)-f(z)}{y-z}$ for $y\neq z$.
  • The free operator is $\mc L_0(f):=|D|^pf'+f-yf'$ (this is $\mc L_\epsilon$ of def:L_eps at $\epsilon=0$).
  • The nonlinear remainder is $\mc Q_\epsilon(f)(y):=c_\alpha\int_\R\frac{f'(y)-f'(z)}{|y-z|^\alpha}\bigl[A_\epsilon(S_f(y,z))-1\bigr]\,dz$.
  • The divided residual is $\sq{\mc E}_\epsilon(f):=A_\epsilon(f')\,\mc E_\epsilon(f)$, where $\mc E_\epsilon$ is the residual of def:residual.
  • The corner profile is $W(y):=\max\{-y,0\}$.

nodes.title: Secant kernel operator
nodes.statement_html: For $f\in C^2(\R;\R)$ with $f'$ bounded and $\Gamma\in C^1(\R;\R)$, set \[ \mc T_\Gamma(f)(y):=c_\alpha\int_\R\frac{f'(y)-f'(y-s)}{|s|^\alpha}\,\Gamma\bigl(S_f(y,y-s)\bigr)\,ds, \qquad S_f(y,y-s)=\frac{f(y)-f(y-s)}{s}. \] Thus $\mc T_1(f)=|D|^pf'$, $\mc T_{A_\epsilon-1}(f)=\mc Q_\epsilon(f)$ and, by linearity in $\Gamma$, $\mc T_{A_\epsilon}(f)=|D|^pf'+\mc Q_\epsilon(f)$ (whenever the integrals converge absolutely, see lem:c07_kernel_C1). For $K>0$ write $\|\Gamma\|_{K}:=\sup_{|u|\le K}(|\Gamma(u)|+|\Gamma'(u)|)$.

nodes.title: Admissible profile class
nodes.statement_html:
For $K\geq1$, $\mc P(K)$ is the set of $f\in C^3(\R;\R)$ such that for all $y\in\R$:
  • $|f'(y)|\le K$;
  • $|f''(y)|\le K\ang{y}^{\theta}$ if $y\geq0$, and $|f''(y)|\le K\ang{y}^{-1}$ if $y\le 0$ (recall $\theta=\tfrac1p-\beta$);
  • $|f'''(y)|\le K\ang{y}^{2/p}$.

nodes.title: Elementary bounds on $A_\epsilon$, $B_\epsilon$
nodes.statement_html: There is $C=C(p)$ such that for all $0\le\epsilon\le1$ and $u\in\R$: \[ |A_\epsilon(u)-1|\le \tfrac\alpha2\epsilon u^2,\quad |A_\epsilon'(u)|\le\alpha\epsilon|u|,\quad |A_\epsilon''(u)|\le C\epsilon,\quad 0\le B_\epsilon(u)-1\le\tfrac\alpha2\epsilon u^2,\quad |B_\epsilon'(u)|\le\alpha\epsilon|u|. \] In particular, for $K\ge1$, $\|A_\epsilon-1\|_K+\|A_\epsilon'\|_K\le C K^2\epsilon$ and $\|A_\epsilon\|_K\le 1+CK^2$.
nodes.proof_html:
Put $x=\epsilon u^2\ge0$. Since $x\mapsto(1+x)^{-\alpha/2}$ is convex with derivative $-\alpha/2$ at
  $0$, $0\le1-(1+x)^{-\alpha/2}\le\frac\alpha2x$. Since $\alpha/2<1$, $x\mapsto(1+x)^{\alpha/2}$
  is concave, so $0\le(1+x)^{\alpha/2}-1\le\frac\alpha2x$. Directly,
  $A_\epsilon'(u)=-\alpha\epsilon u(1+\epsilon u^2)^{-\alpha/2-1}$,
  $B_\epsilon'(u)=\alpha\epsilon u(1+\epsilon u^2)^{\alpha/2-1}$, and both factors
  $(1+x)^{-\alpha/2-1},(1+x)^{\alpha/2-1}$ are $\le1$. Finally
  $A_\epsilon''(u)=-\alpha\epsilon(1+x)^{-\alpha/2-1}+\alpha(\alpha+2)\epsilon\frac{x}{1+x}(1+x)^{-\alpha/2-1}$,
  so $|A_\epsilon''|\le\alpha(\alpha+3)\epsilon$.

nodes.title: Secant calculus
nodes.statement_html: Let $f\in C^1(\R)$ with $f'$ bounded. For $y\ne z$: $|S_f(y,z)|\le\|f'\|_{L^\infty}$, and \[ \p_yS_f=\frac{f'(y)-S_f}{y-z},\qquad \p_zS_f=\frac{S_f-f'(z)}{y-z},\qquad \p_y\p_zS_f=\frac{f'(y)+f'(z)-2S_f}{(y-z)^2}. \] Moreover $S_f(y,y-s)=\int_0^1f'(y-ts)\,dt$, $\p_y[S_f(y,y-s)]=\frac{f'(y)-f'(y-s)}{s}$, and $S_f-S_g=S_{f-g}$ (linearity). If $f$ is only continuous and piecewise $C^1$ with bounded derivative (e.g.\ $f=W$) the same holds wherever the derivatives exist.
nodes.proof_html:
Mean value theorem / fundamental theorem of calculus for the first claims, quotient rule for the
  derivatives: e.g.\ $\p_zS_f=\frac{-f'(z)(y-z)+(f(y)-f(z))}{(y-z)^2}$; then
  $\p_y\p_zS_f=\frac{\p_yS_f}{y-z}-\frac{S_f-f'(z)}{(y-z)^2}$ and insert $\p_yS_f$.

nodes.title: Divided residual identity
nodes.statement_html: Let $0\le\epsilon\le1$ and $f\in C^2(\R;\R)$ with $f'$ bounded. Then for every $y\in\R$ the integrals defining $|D|^pf'(y)$, $\mc Q_\epsilon(f)(y)$, $\sq{\mc J}_\epsilon(f)(y)$ and $\mc T_{A_\epsilon}(f)(y)$ converge absolutely, and \[ \sq{\mc E}_\epsilon(f)=\mc L_0(f)+\mc Q_\epsilon(f)=f-yf'+\mc T_{A_\epsilon}(f), \qquad \mc E_\epsilon(f)=B_\epsilon(f')\,\sq{\mc E}_\epsilon(f). \]
nodes.proof_html: Fix $y$. For $|y-z|\le1$, $|f'(y)-f'(z)|\le|y-z|\sup_{[y-1,y+1]}|f''|$, so each integrand is $O(|y-z|^{1-\alpha})=O(|y-z|^{-p})$, integrable; for $|y-z|>1$ each integrand is $\le 2\|f'\|_\infty(1+\sup|A_\epsilon|)|y-z|^{-\alpha}$, integrable since $\alpha>1$ (and $0<A_\epsilon\le1$). By def:J_eps, $\sq{\mc J}_\epsilon(f)(y)=c_\alpha\int\frac{f'(y)-f'(z)}{|y-z|^\alpha}A_\epsilon(S_f)\,dz-A_\epsilon(f'(y))|D|^pf'(y)$, splitting an absolutely convergent integral. Hence by def:residual $A_\epsilon(f')\mc E_\epsilon(f)=A_\epsilon(f')|D|^pf'+f-yf'+\sq{\mc J}_\epsilon(f)=f-yf'+\mc T_{A_\epsilon}(f)$. Writing $A_\epsilon(S)=1+(A_\epsilon(S)-1)$ gives $\mc T_{A_\epsilon}(f)=|D|^pf'+\mc Q_\epsilon(f)$, hence $\sq{\mc E}_\epsilon(f)=\mc L_0(f)+\mc Q_\epsilon(f)$. Dividing by $A_\epsilon(f')>0$ gives the last identity.

nodes.title: $C^1$ regularity and local bounds for $\mc T_\Gamma$
nodes.statement_html: Let $K\ge1$, $f\in\mc P(K)$ and $\Gamma\in C^1(\R;\R)$. Then for every $y$ the integral defining $\mc T_\Gamma(f)(y)$ converges absolutely, $\mc T_\Gamma(f)\in C^1(\R)$, and \[ \p_y\mc T_\Gamma(f)(y)=c_\alpha\int_\R\Bigl[\frac{f''(y)-f''(y-s)}{|s|^\alpha}\Gamma(S) +\frac{(f'(y)-f'(y-s))^2}{s|s|^\alpha}\Gamma'(S)\Bigr]ds,\qquad S=S_f(y,y-s), \] again absolutely convergent. Moreover, for every $M\ge1$ there is $C=C(p,K,M)$ with $\|\mc T_\Gamma(f)\|_{C^1([-M,M])}\le C\|\Gamma\|_K$.
nodes.proof_html: Write $k(y,s)$ for the integrand of $\mc T_\Gamma(f)$ and $k_1(y,s)$ for the integrand above. By lem:c07_secant_calculus, $|S|\le K$ and $\p_yk=k_1$ for $s\neq0$ (chain rule, using $\p_y S_f(y,y-s)=(f'(y)-f'(y-s))/s$). Fix $M\ge1$ and let $|y|\le M+1$. Set $K_2:=K\ang{M+2}^{1/p}\ge\sup_{|x|\le M+2}|f''(x)|$ and $K_3:=K\ang{M+2}^{2/p}\ge\sup_{|x|\le M+2}|f'''(x)|$. Near region $|s|\le1$: by the mean value theorem $|f'(y)-f'(y-s)|\le K_2|s|$ and $|f''(y)-f''(y-s)|\le K_3|s|$, hence $|k|\le c_\alpha K_2\|\Gamma\|_K|s|^{-p}$ and $|k_1|\le c_\alpha(K_3+K_2^2)\|\Gamma\|_K|s|^{-p}$. Far region $|s|>1$: $|f'(y)-f'(y-s)|\le2K$, so $|k|\le 2c_\alpha K\|\Gamma\|_K|s|^{-1-p}$; and by def:c07_profile_class(2), $|f''(x)|\le K\ang{x}^\theta$ for all $x$, and $\ang{y-s}\le\sqrt2\ang{y}\ang{s}$, so $|f''(y)|+|f''(y-s)|\le 4K\ang{M+1}^\theta|s|^\theta$; hence $|k_1|\le c_\alpha(4K\ang{M+1}^\theta|s|^{\theta}+4K^2|s|^{-1})\|\Gamma\|_K|s|^{-1-p}$. Let $D_M(s)$ be the resulting majorant (independent of $y\in[-M-1,M+1]$). Since $p<1$ and $\theta<p$ (here $p>\tfrac12$ is used), $D_M\in L^1(\R)$ with $\|D_M\|_{L^1}\le C(p,K,M)\|\Gamma\|_K$. Absolute convergence and the bound $|\mc T_\Gamma(f)(y)|\le\|D_M\|_{L^1}$ follow. For each $s\ne0$, $y\mapsto k(y,s)$ is $C^1$ with derivative $k_1$ and $|k_1(y,s)|\le D_M(s)$ for $|y|<M+1$; the theorem on differentiation under the integral sign (dominated derivative; Mathlib hasDerivAt\_integral\_of\_dominated\_loc\_of\_deriv\_le) gives differentiability with the stated formula. Continuity of $y\mapsto\int k_1(y,s)ds$ follows from continuity of $k_1(\cdot,s)$ for $s\ne0$ and dominated convergence with $D_M$. The $C^1([-M,M])$ bound is $2\|D_M\|_{L^1}$.

nodes.title: Continuity of $\mc T_\Gamma$ under $C^2_{\textup{loc}}$ convergence
nodes.statement_html: Let $K\geq1$, $\Gamma\in C^1(\R;\R)$, and $f_n,f\in\mc P(K)$ with $f_n\to f$ in $C^2_{\textup{loc}}$. Then $\mc T_\Gamma(f_n)\to\mc T_\Gamma(f)$ in $C^1_{\textup{loc}}$.
nodes.proof_html: Fix $M\ge1$; let $k_n,k_{1,n}$ (resp.\ $k,k_1$) be the integrands of lem:c07_kernel_C1 for $f_n$ (resp.\ $f$). Since all functions lie in $\mc P(K)$, the majorant $D_M$ of that proof serves for all $n$ simultaneously. Define $e_n(s):=\sup_{|y|\le M}\bigl(|k_n(y,s)-k(y,s)|+|k_{1,n}(y,s)-k_1(y,s)|\bigr)$, which is continuous in $s\ne0$ (supremum over a compact set of a jointly continuous function), hence measurable, and $e_n\le 2D_M$. Claim: $e_n(s)\to0$ for each fixed $s\ne0$. Indeed on the compact interval $I_s=[-M-|s|,M+|s|]$ we have $f_n^{(i)}\to f^{(i)}$ uniformly for $i\le2$; hence $S_{f_n}(y,y-s)\to S_f(y,y-s)$ uniformly in $|y|\le M$ (it is $(f_n(y)-f_n(y-s))/s$ with $s$ fixed), all secants lie in $[-K,K]$, and $\Gamma,\Gamma'$ are uniformly continuous on $[-K,K]$; the integrands are finite sums of products of these uniformly convergent bounded quantities and the fixed factor $|s|^{-\alpha}$ or $s^{-1}|s|^{-\alpha}$. By dominated convergence $\int e_n\to0$, and $\|\mc T_\Gamma(f_n)-\mc T_\Gamma(f)\|_{C^1([-M,M])}\le 2c_\alpha\int e_n(s)\,ds\to0$, using the derivative formula of lem:c07_kernel_C1. Lean route: dominated convergence along the filter $n\to\infty$ jointly with $y\to x$ within $[-M,M]$, plus the compact local-uniform convergence criterion; this avoids the measurability of the supremum $e_n$.

nodes.title: Elementary weighted integrals
nodes.statement_html:
Let $0<p<1$ and $q>1$. There is $C=C(p,q)$ such that for all $|y|\geq1$:
  • $\int_{|y-z|\ge|y|/4}\ang{z}^{-p}|y-z|^{-q}\,dz\le C|y|^{1-p-q}$;
  • $\int_{|y-z|\ge|y|/4}|y-z|^{-q}\,dz\le C|y|^{1-q}$ and $\int_{|s|\le|y|/2}|s|^{-p}\,ds\le C|y|^{1-p}$;
  • if $y<0$: $\int_0^\infty\bigl(|y|^{-p}+\ang{z}^{-p}\bigr)(|y|+z)^{-q}\,dz\le C|y|^{1-p-q}$.
nodes.proof_html:
(2) is explicit integration. (1): on $\{|z|\le2|y|\}$ bound $|y-z|^{-q}\le4^q|y|^{-q}$ and
  $\int_{|z|\le2|y|}\ang{z}^{-p}dz\le\int_{|z|\le2|y|}|z|^{-p}dz=\frac{2(2|y|)^{1-p}}{1-p}$; on
  $\{|z|>2|y|\}$, $|y-z|\ge|z|/2$ and $\ang z^{-p}\le|z|^{-p}$, so the integral is
  $\le2^q\int_{|z|>2|y|}|z|^{-p-q}dz=C|y|^{1-p-q}$ since $p+q>1$. (3): the first part is
  $|y|^{-p}\frac{|y|^{1-q}}{q-1}$; for the second split at $z=|y|$ as in (1).

nodes.title: Decay of $|D|^ph'$ for decaying $h$
nodes.statement_html: Let $0<p<1$, $K\ge0$, and $h\in C^3(\R;\R)$ with $|h^{(i)}(y)|\le K\ang{y}^{-p-i}$ for $i=0,1,2,3$ and all $y\in\R$. Then $|D|^ph'\in C^1(\R)$, $\p_y|D|^ph'=|D|^ph''$, and there is $C=C(p)$ such that for all $|y|\ge1$ and $j\in\{0,1\}$, \[|\p_y^j|D|^ph'(y)|\le CK\ang{y}^{-2p-1-j}.\]
nodes.proof_html: Differentiation under the integral in $|D|^ph'(y)=c_\alpha\int(h'(y)-h'(y-s))|s|^{-1-p}ds$ is justified by the majorant $\|h'''\|_\infty|s|^{-p}\mathbf 1_{|s|\le1}+2\|h''\|_\infty|s|^{-1-p}\mathbf 1_{|s|>1}$, giving $\p_y|D|^ph'=|D|^ph''$, continuous by dominated convergence. Fix $|y|\ge1$ (so $\ang y\le\sqrt2|y|$), let $g\in\{h',h''\}$, i.e.\ $g=h^{(1+j)}$, and split with $\chi_y(z):=\chi((y-z)/|y|)$: \[ |D|^pg(y)=\underbrace{c_\alpha\!\int\!\chi_y\frac{g(y)-g(z)}{|y-z|^{1+p}}dz}_{I_{\rm near}} +\underbrace{c_\alpha g(y)\!\int\!\frac{1-\chi_y}{|y-z|^{1+p}}dz}_{I_{\rm far,1}} \underbrace{-c_\alpha\!\int\!\frac{(1-\chi_y)\,g(z)}{|y-z|^{1+p}}dz}_{I_{\rm far,2}}. \] Near: on $\operatorname{supp}\chi_y$, $|y-z|\le|y|/2$, so $|z|\geq|y|/2$ and the segment $[y,z]$ stays in $\{|x|\ge|y|/2\}$; thus $|g(y)-g(z)|\le CK\ang{y}^{-p-2-j}|y-z|$ and, by lem:c07_tail_integrals(2), $|I_{\rm near}|\le CK\ang{y}^{-p-2-j}|y|^{1-p}$. Far 1: $1-\chi_y$ is supported in $|y-z|\ge|y|/4$, so $|I_{\rm far,1}|\le CK\ang{y}^{-p-1-j}|y|^{-p}$. Far 2: integrate by parts $1+j$ times in $z$ to move all derivatives from $g=h^{(1+j)}$ onto $\kappa(z):=(1-\chi_y(z))|y-z|^{-1-p}$; boundary terms vanish since $\kappa$ vanishes near $z=y$ and $h^{(i)}(z)\kappa^{(l)}(z)\to0$ as $|z|\to\infty$. Since $\p_z\chi_y=-\chi'(\cdot)/|y|$ and $|y|^{-1}\le(2|y-z|)^{-1}$ on $\operatorname{supp}\chi'_y$, we get $|\p_z^{1+j}\kappa(z)|\le C\mathbf 1_{|y-z|\ge|y|/4}|y-z|^{-2-p-j}$. Then $|I_{\rm far,2}|\le CK\int_{|y-z|\ge|y|/4}\ang{z}^{-p}|y-z|^{-2-p-j}dz\le CK|y|^{-1-2p-j}$ by lem:c07_tail_integrals(1) with $q=2+p+j$. Summing, $|D|^pg(y)=O(K\ang{y}^{-2p-1-j})$.

nodes.title: Local estimate for $|D|^pu'$ and $\mc L_0u$
nodes.statement_html: Let $0<p<1$, $M\ge1$, and $u\in C^3(\R;\R)$ with $u,u'$ bounded on $\R$. Then $|D|^pu'\in C^1(\R)$ and there is $C=C(p)$ with \[ \bigl\||D|^pu'\bigr\|_{C^1([-M,M])}\le C\bigl(\|u\|_{C^3([-M-1,M+1])}+\|u\|_{L^\infty(\R)}\bigr), \qquad \|\mc L_0u\|_{C^1([-M,M])}\le C(1+M)\bigl(\|u\|_{C^3([-M-1,M+1])}+\|u\|_{L^\infty(\R)}\bigr). \] (The finiteness of $\|u'\|_{L^\infty(\R)}$ is only used to make the integrals absolutely convergent; it does not enter the constant.)
nodes.proof_html:
For $|y|\le M$ write $|D|^pu'(y)=c_\alpha\int_{|s|\le1}\frac{u'(y)-u'(y-s)}{|s|^{1+p}}ds+\frac{2c_\alpha}{p}u'(y)-c_\alpha\int_{|s|>1}\frac{u'(y-s)}{|s|^{1+p}}ds$.
  The first term is $\le C\|u''\|_{L^\infty[-M-1,M+1]}$. In the last, integrate by parts on
  $s>1$ and $s<-1$ separately ($\p_s[u(y-s)]=-u'(y-s)$):
  $\int_{|s|>1}\frac{u'(y-s)}{|s|^{1+p}}ds=u(y-1)-u(y+1)-(1+p)\int_{|s|>1}\frac{\operatorname{sgn}(s)\,u(y-s)}{|s|^{2+p}}ds$,
  bounded by $C(\|u\|_{L^\infty[-M-1,M+1]}+\|u\|_{L^\infty(\R)})$. For the derivative (differentiation
  under the integral is justified by the bounded $u',u''$ on compacts and $u'\in L^\infty$), differentiate
  this representation in $y$: the near term becomes $\int_{|s|\le1}\frac{u''(y)-u''(y-s)}{|s|^{1+p}}ds$,
  bounded by $C\|u'''\|_{L^\infty[-M-1,M+1]}$; the local terms give $u''(y),u'(y\pm1)$; and
  $\p_y\int_{|s|>1}\operatorname{sgn}(s)u(y-s)|s|^{-2-p}ds=\int_{|s|>1}\operatorname{sgn}(s)u'(y-s)|s|^{-2-p}ds$,
  which after one more integration by parts is bounded by $C(\|u\|_{L^\infty[-M-1,M+1]}+\|u\|_{L^\infty(\R)})$.
  Finally $u-yu'$ and $(u-yu')'=-yu''$ are bounded on $[-M,M]$ by $(1+2M)\|u\|_{C^2([-M,M])}$.

nodes.title: Smoothness of $f_{0,+}$
nodes.section: Uniform properties of the approximate family
nodes.statement_html: The function $f_{0,+}(y)=-\frac1{2\pi}\int_0^\infty\frac{\chi_+(\xi)}{\xi^2}e^{i(y\xi-\Phi_0(\xi))}d\xi$ (absolutely convergent) belongs to $C^\infty(\R;\C)$.
nodes.proof_html:
Fix $M\ge1$, $k\ge0$, and $\Xi:=(2M)^{1/p}+2$; let $\eta\in C_c^\infty([0,2\Xi))$ with $\eta=1$ on
  $[0,\Xi]$. The part with amplitude $\eta\chi_+\xi^{-2}$ is an integral over a compact
  $\xi$-interval of a smooth function of $(y,\xi)$, hence smooth in $y$. For the part with amplitude
  $a(\xi)=(1-\eta)\chi_+\xi^{-2}$ (supported in $[\Xi,\infty)$) and phase $\varphi=y\xi-\Phi_0(\xi)$,
  for $|y|<M$ we have $|\p_\xi\varphi|=|y-\xi^p|\ge\xi^p/2$ on $\operatorname{supp}a$. Integrating by parts
  $N$ times with $e^{i\varphi}=\frac{\p_\xi e^{i\varphi}}{i(y-\xi^p)}$ (no boundary terms: $a$ vanishes near
  $\Xi$, decay at $\infty$) gives $\int a e^{i\varphi}=\int (\mathcal D^t)^Na\,e^{i\varphi}$ with
  $\mathcal D^tg=-\p_\xi\bigl(g/(i(y-\xi^p))\bigr)$, and $|\p_y^l(\mathcal D^t)^Na|\le C_{N,l,M}\xi^{-2-Np}$.
  Therefore the $y$-derivatives up to order $k$ of $(\mathcal D^t)^Na\,e^{i\varphi}$ are bounded by
  $C\xi^{k-2-Np}$, integrable on $[\Xi,\infty)$ once $Np>k$; differentiation under the integral sign
  gives $C^k$ on $(-M,M)$. As $M,k$ are arbitrary, $f_{0,+}\in C^\infty$.

nodes.title: The family is real and smooth
nodes.section: Uniform properties of the approximate family
nodes.statement_html: For all $0\le\epsilon\le\epsilon_0$ and $\mu\in\ov B$, $\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu}\in C^\infty(\R;\R)$, and the pieces $f_{0,\mu}$, $f_{\textup{slow}}$, $f_{\textup{osc}}$ of eqn:approx_family_definition are real-valued and $C^\infty$. Moreover $f_{\textup{osc}}=0$ on $(-\infty,R]$ and $f_{\textup{slow}}=0$ on $[-R,R]$.
nodes.proof_html: $f_0$ is real and smooth by lem:approx_linear_seed (its formula is real); $f_{0,+}$ is smooth by lem:c07_f0plus_smooth, so $f_{0,\mu}=f_0+2\operatorname{Re}[(\mu/\mu_*-1)f_{0,+}]$ is real and smooth. $\chi_R$ is smooth with closed support in $(R,\infty)$, so it vanishes on a neighbourhood of $(-\infty,R]$; hence $y^{-p}\chi_R(y)$ and $|y|^{-p}\chi_R(-y)$ are smooth on $\R$ and vanish for $|y|\le R$. For $t\ge R$, $\lambda_{\epsilon,\mu}(t)\geq\frac12t^{1/p}>0$ (standing assumption), so $Z_{\epsilon,\mu}$ in eqn:approx_Z_definition is smooth on $[R,\infty)$ and $|Z_{\epsilon,\mu}(t)|\le Ct^{-\beta}$ (using that $a_*$ is bounded on $[R,\infty)$ by lem:approx_linear_seed(1) and continuity). As $\beta>1$, $H_\mu:=Z_{\epsilon,\mu}+c_{\textup{cubic}}Z_{\epsilon,\mu}^3-\frac{\mu}{\mu_*}Z_0\in L^1([R,\infty))$, so $F_\mu(y):=\int_y^\infty H_\mu$ is $C^\infty$ on $[R,\infty)$ with $F_\mu'=-H_\mu$, and $f_{\textup{osc}}=-2\chi_R\operatorname{Re}F_\mu$ (extended by $0$) is real and $C^\infty$ on $\R$.

nodes.title: Uniform bounds for the family
nodes.section: Uniform properties of the approximate family
nodes.statement_html:
There is an admissible $K_0\ge1$ such that for all $0\le\epsilon\le\epsilon_0$ and $\mu\in\ov B$, with $f=\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu}$ and $g:=f-W$:
  • $f\in\mc P(K_0)$;
  • $|g(y)|\le K_0\ang{y}^{-p}$ for all $y\in\R$;
  • $|g^{(i)}(y)|\le K_0\ang{y}^{-p-i}$ for $y\le0$ and $i=0,1,2,3$ (note $g=f+y$ on $(-\infty,0]$).
nodes.proof_html: By lem:c07_family_smooth, $f\in C^\infty$. By prop:approx_profile_bounds (whose constants are uniform in $\epsilon,\mu$) with $j=0,1,2$: for $y\ge0$, $|f|\lesssim\ang y^{-p}$, $|f'|\lesssim\ang y^{-\beta}\le1$, $|f''|\lesssim\ang y^{-\beta+1/p}=\ang y^\theta$, $|f'''|\lesssim\ang y^{-\beta+2/p}\le\ang y^{2/p}$; for $y\le0$, $|\p^i(f+y)|\lesssim\ang y^{-p-i}$, so $|f'|\le1+C$, $|f''|\lesssim\ang y^{-p-2}\le\ang y^{-1}$, $|f'''|\lesssim\ang{y}^{-p-3}$. Since $W=0$ on $[0,\infty)$ and $W=-y$ on $(-\infty,0]$, (2)--(3) follow. Take $K_0$ the maximum of the constants.

nodes.title: Continuity of the family in $\mu$
nodes.section: Uniform properties of the approximate family
nodes.statement_html: Fix $0\le\epsilon\le\epsilon_0$ and $k\ge0$. The map $\mu\mapsto\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu}$ is continuous from $\ov B$ into $C^k_{\textup{loc}}$. In particular (case $k=2$) it is continuous into $C^2_{\textup{loc}}$.
nodes.proof_html: Let $\mu_n\to\mu$ in $\ov B$. (i) $f_{0,\mu}=f_0+2\operatorname{Re}[(\mu/\mu_*-1)f_{0,+}]$ is affine in $\mu$ with smooth coefficient $f_{0,+}$, so $\|f_{0,\mu_n}-f_{0,\mu}\|_{C^k([-M,M])}\le\frac{2|\mu_n-\mu|}{|\mu_*|}\|f_{0,+}\|_{C^k([-M,M])}\to0$. (ii) $f_{\textup{slow}}$ does not depend on $\mu$ ($c_\pm$ depend only on $\epsilon$, by eqn:approx_correction_constants). (iii) For $f_{\textup{osc}}$: by eqn:approx_correction_constants, $c_{\textup{log}}(\mu)=-n_\epsilon|\mu|^2/p$ is continuous in $\mu$; by eqn:approx_modified_frequency, $\lambda_{\epsilon,\mu}(t)$ and $\Psi_{\epsilon,\mu}(t)=\Psi_0(R)+\int_R^t\lambda_{\epsilon,\mu}$ (explicitly a combination of powers of $t$ and $c_{\textup{log}}(\mu)\log(t/R)$) and all their $t$-derivatives are jointly continuous in $(\mu,t)\in\ov B\times[R,\infty)$; since $\lambda_{\epsilon,\mu}\ge\frac12t^{1/p}>0$, the same holds for $Z_{\epsilon,\mu}(t)$ in eqn:approx_Z_definition and for $H_\mu=Z_{\epsilon,\mu}+c_{\textup{cubic}}Z_{\epsilon,\mu}^3-\frac\mu{\mu_*}Z_0$. By uniform continuity on compacts $\ov B\times[R,T]$, $\p_t^lH_{\mu_n}\to\p_t^lH_\mu$ uniformly on $[R,T]$ for each $l,T$. Moreover $|H_\nu(t)|\le Ct^{-\beta}$ uniformly in $\nu\in\ov B$ (as in lem:c07_family_smooth), and $\beta>1$; by dominated convergence, $\sup_{y\ge R}|F_{\mu_n}(y)-F_\mu(y)|\le\int_R^\infty|H_{\mu_n}-H_\mu|\,dt\to0$. Since $\p_y^lF_\nu=-\p_y^{l-1}H_\nu$ for $l\ge1$, the Leibniz rule applied to $f_{\textup{osc}}=-2\chi_R\operatorname{Re}F_\nu$ gives $f_{\textup{osc}}^{(\mu_n)}\to f_{\textup{osc}}^{(\mu)}$ in $C^k_{\textup{loc}}$. Summing (i)--(iii) via eqn:approx_family_definition proves the claim.

nodes.title: Bounds on the slow correction
nodes.section: Uniform properties of the approximate family
nodes.statement_html: There is an admissible $C$ such that for all $0\le\epsilon\le\epsilon_0$: $|c_+|+|c_-|\le C\epsilon$, and $|f_{\textup{slow}}^{(i)}(y)|\le C\epsilon\ang{y}^{-p-i}$ for all $y\in\R$ and $i=0,1,2,3$. Moreover $f_{\textup{slow}}(y)=c_-|y|^{-p}$ for $y\le-2R$.
nodes.proof_html: $c_+=-c_\epsilon/(p+1)$ and $|c_\epsilon|\lesssim\epsilon$ by lem:analysis_coefficient (directly: $|(1+\epsilon t^2)^{-\alpha/2}-1|\le\frac\alpha2\epsilon t^2$ and $\int_0^1t^2(1-t)^{p-1}dt<\infty$). $|c_-|\le\frac{c_\alpha}{p+1}\int_0^1\frac\alpha2\epsilon t^{2}t^{p-1}dt\le C\epsilon$ by lem:c07_A_B_bounds. For $y^{-p}\chi_R(y)$: by Leibniz, $\p^i(y^{-p}\chi_R)=\sum_{l\le i}\binom il\p^{i-l}(y^{-p})\chi_R^{(l)}$; $\chi_R^{(l)}$ for $l\ge1$ is supported in $[R,2R]$ and bounded by $C_lR^{-l}\le C_l2^ly^{-l}$ there, so $|\p^i(y^{-p}\chi_R)|\le Cy^{-p-i}\le C\ang{y}^{-p-i}$ on $\operatorname{supp}\chi_R\subset[R,\infty)$, $R\ge1$. The same for $|y|^{-p}\chi_R(-y)$. Finally $\chi_R(-y)=1$, $\chi_R(y)=0$ for $y\le-2R$.

nodes.title: Residual splitting
nodes.section: Uniform properties of the approximate family
nodes.statement_html: For all $0\le\epsilon\le\epsilon_0$, $\mu\in\ov B$, with $f=\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu}$: the functions $f$, $f_{0,\mu}$, $f_{\textup{slow}}$, $f_{\textup{osc}}$ are $C^\infty$ with bounded first derivative, and for every $y\in\R$ \[ \sq{\mc E}_\epsilon(f)(y)-G_\mu(y)=\mc L_0(f_{\textup{slow}})(y)+\mc L_0(f_{\textup{osc}})(y)+\mc Q_\epsilon(f)(y). \]
nodes.proof_html: Boundedness of $f'$: lem:c07_family_uniform_bounds; of $f_{\textup{slow}}'$: lem:c07_slow_bounds; of $f_{\textup{osc}}'$: eqn:approx_fosc_bounds with $j=1$ gives $|f_{\textup{osc}}'|\lesssim\epsilon\ang{y}^{-p-\beta+1/p}$ and $-p-\beta+\frac1p=-p+\theta<0$; hence also $f_{0,\mu}'=f'-f_{\textup{slow}}'-f_{\textup{osc}}'$ is bounded. By lem:c07_divided_residual_identity, $\sq{\mc E}_\epsilon(f)=\mc L_0(f)+\mc Q_\epsilon(f)$; $\mc L_0$ is linear on $C^2$ functions with bounded derivative (each singular integral converges absolutely), so $\mc L_0(f)=\mc L_0(f_{0,\mu})+\mc L_0(f_{\textup{slow}})+\mc L_0(f_{\textup{osc}})$, and $\mc L_0(f_{0,\mu})=G_\mu$ by lem:approx_linear_seed(3). This is the first equality of eqn:approx_residual_decomposition.

nodes.title: Properties of $G_\mu$
nodes.section: Uniform properties of the approximate family
nodes.statement_html:
For $\mu\in\C$ let $G_\mu$ be as in def:G_mu: $\widehat{G_\mu}(\xi)=(1-\frac\mu{\mu_*})\frac{\chi_+'(\xi)}{\xi}e^{-i\Phi_0(\xi)}$ for $\xi>0$, $\widehat{G_\mu}(\xi)=\ov{\widehat{G_\mu}(-\xi)}$ for $\xi<0$, $\widehat{G_\mu}(0)=0$, with $\Phi_0(\xi)=\xi|\xi|^p/\alpha$. Then:
  • $\mu_*\ne0$; $\widehat{G_\mu}\in C_c^\infty(\R)$ with support in $[-2,-1]\cup[1,2]$; $G_\mu$ is a real-valued Schwartz function, independent of $\epsilon$;
  • $G_\mu=\operatorname{Re}(1-\frac\mu{\mu_*})G_++\operatorname{Im}(1-\frac\mu{\mu_*})G_-$ with $G_\pm$ of def:G_pm; in particular $G_{\mu_*}=0$;
  • for every $\gamma>0$ and $N\geq0$ there is $C=C(p,\gamma,N)$ with $\sup_y\ang{y}^{N}(|G_\mu(y)|+|G_\mu'(y)|)+\|G_\mu\|_{Y_\gamma}\le C|1-\mu/\mu_*|$ and $\|G_\mu-G_\nu\|_{Y_\gamma}+\|G_\mu-G_\nu\|_{C^1(\R)}\le C|\mu-\nu|/|\mu_*|$; in particular $\sup_{\mu\in\ov B}\|G_\mu\|_{Y_\gamma}<\infty$ and $\mu\mapsto G_\mu$ is continuous into $Y_\gamma$ and into $C^1_{\textup{loc}}$.
nodes.proof_html: (1) $\mu_*=-i/\sqrt{2\pi p}\neq0$. $\chi_+'$ is smooth and supported in $[1,2]$ (as $\chi_+=0$ on $(-\infty,1]$, $=1$ on $[2,\infty)$), and $\xi\mapsto\xi^{-1}e^{-i\Phi_0(\xi)}$ is smooth on $(0,\infty)$; the conjugate-symmetric extension is smooth and compactly supported away from $0$. The inverse Fourier transform (def:fourier_convention) of a $C_c^\infty$ function is Schwartz, and conjugate symmetry $\widehat G(-\xi)=\ov{\widehat G(\xi)}$ is equivalent to $G$ real. No $\epsilon$ appears. (2) Write $1-\mu/\mu_*=a+ib$, $a,b\in\R$. On $\xi>0$, $(a+ib)\frac{\chi_+'}{\xi}e^{-i\Phi_0}=a\widehat{G_+}+b\widehat{G_-}$ by def:G_pm; both sides are conjugate-symmetric (real coefficients), so they agree on $\R$. For $\mu=\mu_*$, $a=b=0$. (3) $G_\pm$ are fixed Schwartz functions, so (2) gives the bounds with $C=\sup_y\ang y^{N}(|G_+|+|G_+'|+|G_-|+|G_-'|)$ etc.; the $Y_\gamma$ norm (def:Y_gamma) is bounded by $\sup\ang y^{\gamma+1}(|G|+|G'|)$ since $\ang{y}^{-1/p}\le 1\le\ang y$. Linearity in $\mu$ gives the difference bounds.

nodes.title: $\mc Q_\epsilon(W)$ on the negative axis
nodes.section: Uniform properties of the approximate family
nodes.statement_html: For $0\le\epsilon\le1$ and $y<0$, the integral defining $\mc Q_\epsilon(W)(y)$ converges absolutely and \[ \mc Q_\epsilon(W)(y)=-c_\alpha|y|^{-p}\int_0^1[A_\epsilon(t)-1]t^{p-1}\,dt=-(p+1)c_-|y|^{-p}. \]
nodes.proof_html: For $y<0$: $W'(y)=-1$, and $W'(z)=-1$ for $z<0$, $W'(z)=0$ for $z>0$; so the integrand vanishes for $z<0$. For $z>0$: $W'(y)-W'(z)=-1$, $|y-z|=|y|+z$, $S_W(y,z)=\frac{-y-0}{y-z}=-\frac{|y|}{|y|+z}$, and $A_\epsilon$ is even, so $\mc Q_\epsilon(W)(y)=-c_\alpha\int_0^\infty\frac{A_\epsilon(|y|/(|y|+z))-1}{(|y|+z)^{1+p}}dz$, absolutely convergent since $|A_\epsilon-1|\le\epsilon$ on $[0,1]$. Substituting $t=|y|/(|y|+z)$ ($dz=-|y|t^{-2}dt$, $(|y|+z)^{-1-p}=t^{1+p}|y|^{-1-p}$) gives $|y|^{-p}\int_0^1(A_\epsilon(t)-1)t^{p-1}dt$. The last equality is the definition of $c_-$ in eqn:approx_correction_constants.

nodes.title: Slow part, negative side
nodes.section: Uniform properties of the approximate family
nodes.statement_html: There is an admissible $C$ such that for all $\epsilon,\mu$, $y\le-8R$ and $j\in\{0,1\}$: $\mc L_0(f_{\textup{slow}})(y)+\mc Q_\epsilon(W)(y)=|D|^pf_{\textup{slow}}'(y)$ and \[\bigl|\p_y^j\bigl(\mc L_0(f_{\textup{slow}})+\mc Q_\epsilon(W)\bigr)(y)\bigr|\le C\epsilon\ang{y}^{-2p-1-j}.\]
nodes.proof_html: On $(-\infty,-2R]$, $f_{\textup{slow}}=c_-(-y)^{-p}$ (lem:c07_slow_bounds), so $f_{\textup{slow}}'=pc_-(-y)^{-p-1}$ and $f_{\textup{slow}}-yf_{\textup{slow}}'=(1+p)c_-|y|^{-p}$, which cancels $\mc Q_\epsilon(W)$ by lem:c07_QW_negative. The identity holds on the open set $y<-2R$, so derivatives may be taken. Apply lem:c07_fractional_decay to $h=f_{\textup{slow}}$ with $K=C\epsilon$ (lem:c07_slow_bounds); note $|y|\ge8R\ge1$.

nodes.title: Oscillatory part, negative side
nodes.section: Uniform properties of the approximate family
nodes.statement_html: There is an admissible $C$ such that for all $\epsilon,\mu$, $y\le-8R$ and $j\in\{0,1\}$: \[ \mc L_0(f_{\textup{osc}})(y)=-c_\alpha\alpha\int_R^\infty\frac{f_{\textup{osc}}(z)}{(z-y)^{\alpha+1}}dz,\qquad |\p_y^j\mc L_0(f_{\textup{osc}})(y)|\le C\epsilon\ang{y}^{-p-2-j}\le C\epsilon\ang{y}^{-2p-1-j}. \]
nodes.proof_html: By lem:c07_family_smooth, $f_{\textup{osc}}=f_{\textup{osc}}'=0$ on $(-\infty,R]$, so for $y\le-8R$, $\mc L_0(f_{\textup{osc}})(y)=|D|^pf_{\textup{osc}}'(y)=-c_\alpha\int_R^\infty f_{\textup{osc}}'(z)(z-y)^{-\alpha}dz$ (non-singular, $z-y\ge|y|$). Integrate by parts on $[R,T]$ and let $T\to\infty$: $f_{\textup{osc}}(R)=0$ and $f_{\textup{osc}}(T)\to0$ by eqn:approx_fosc_bounds, giving the formula. By eqn:approx_fosc_L1_bound, $\|f_{\textup{osc}}\|_{L^1}\le C\epsilon$. Since $\p_y(z-y)^{-\alpha-1}=(\alpha+1)(z-y)^{-\alpha-2}$, differentiation under the integral is justified (majorant $|f_{\textup{osc}}(z)|(8R)^{-\alpha-2}$), and $|\p_y^j\mc L_0(f_{\textup{osc}})(y)|\le C\|f_{\textup{osc}}\|_{L^1}|y|^{-p-2-j}$. Finally $p+2>2p+1$ as $p<1$, and $|y|\ge1$.

nodes.title: Splitting of $\mc Q_\epsilon(f)-\mc Q_\epsilon(W)$
nodes.section: Uniform properties of the approximate family
nodes.statement_html: For $y<0$ let $\chi_y(z):=\chi((y-z)/|y|)$. Then \begin{equation} \mc Q_\epsilon(f)(y)-\mc Q_\epsilon(W)(y)=\mc I_1(y)+\mc I_2(y)+\mc I_3(y), \end{equation} where \begin{align*} \mc I_1&=c_\alpha\int_\R\chi_y(z)\frac{f'(y)-f'(z)}{|y-z|^\alpha}[A_\epsilon(S_f(y,z))-1]dz,\\ \mc I_2&=c_\alpha\int_\R(1-\chi_y(z))\frac{g'(y)-g'(z)}{|y-z|^\alpha}[A_\epsilon(S_f(y,z))-1]dz,\\ \mc I_3&=-c_\alpha\int_0^\infty\frac{A_\epsilon(S_f(y,z))-A_\epsilon(S_W(y,z))}{(z-y)^\alpha}dz, \end{align*} all absolutely convergent ($g'(z)$ is defined for $z\neq0$).
nodes.proof_html: Absolute convergence: near $z=y$ only $\mc I_1$ has a singular kernel, with integrand $O(|y-z|^{-p})$; elsewhere integrands are $O(\epsilon|y-z|^{-\alpha})$ with bounded numerators. On $\operatorname{supp}\chi_y$, $|y-z|\le|y|/2$, so $z\le y/2<0$ and $W'(y)-W'(z)=0$; hence $\mc Q_\epsilon(W)(y)=c_\alpha\int(1-\chi_y)\frac{W'(y)-W'(z)}{|y-z|^\alpha}[A_\epsilon(S_W)-1]dz$. Split $\mc Q_\epsilon(f)$ with $\chi_y+(1-\chi_y)$, write $f'=W'+g'$ and $A_\epsilon(S_f)-1-(A_\epsilon(S_W)-1)=A_\epsilon(S_f)-A_\epsilon(S_W)$: the far part of $\mc Q_\epsilon(f)-\mc Q_\epsilon(W)$ equals $\mc I_2+c_\alpha\int(1-\chi_y)\frac{W'(y)-W'(z)}{|y-z|^\alpha}[A_\epsilon(S_f)-A_\epsilon(S_W)]dz$. In the last integral $W'(y)-W'(z)$ is $0$ for $z<0$ and $-1$ for $z>0$, and for $z>0$, $|y-z|=|y|+z>|y|/2$ so $1-\chi_y=1$; this is $\mc I_3$.

nodes.title: Near term $\mc I_1$
nodes.section: Uniform properties of the approximate family
nodes.statement_html: There is an admissible $C$ with $|\p_y^j\mc I_1(y)|\le C\epsilon|y|^{-2p-1-j}$ for all $\epsilon,\mu$, $y\le-8R$, $j\in\{0,1\}$. Moreover $\mc I_1$ is differentiable at every $y\le-8R$.
nodes.proof_html: Substitute $z=y-s$: $\mc I_1=c_\alpha\int\chi(s/|y|)\frac{f'(y)-f'(y-s)}{|s|^\alpha}[A_\epsilon(S_f(y,y-s))-1]ds$. On the support, $|s|\le|y|/2$, so $y-s\in[\frac32y,\frac12y]\subset(-\infty,0)$ and $|y-s|\ge|y|/2$. There $f'=-1+g'$, so by lem:c07_family_uniform_bounds(3) and the mean value theorem, $|\p_y^j(f'(y)-f'(y-s))|=|g^{(1+j)}(y)-g^{(1+j)}(y-s)|\le CK_0|y|^{-p-2-j}|s|$ for $j=0,1$. By lem:c07_A_B_bounds (with $|S_f|\le K_0$), $|A_\epsilon(S_f)-1|+|A_\epsilon'(S_f)|\le C\epsilon$, and $|\p_y[S_f(y,y-s)]|=|f'(y)-f'(y-s)|/|s|\le C|y|^{-p-2}$. The $y$-derivative of $\chi(s/|y|)$ is bounded by $C|y|^{-1}$ (as $|s|\le|y|$). Differentiating under the integral (justified by these bounds, uniform for $y$ in compact subsets of $(-\infty,-8R]$), every term in $\p_y^j$ of the integrand is bounded by $C\epsilon|y|^{-p-2-j}|s|^{1-\alpha}=C\epsilon|y|^{-p-2-j}|s|^{-p}$ on $|s|\le|y|/2$. Integrating with lem:c07_tail_integrals(2) gives $C\epsilon|y|^{-p-2-j}|y|^{1-p}$.

nodes.title: Far term $\mc I_2$
nodes.section: Uniform properties of the approximate family
nodes.statement_html:
For $y\le-8R$ let $\kappa(y,z):=(1-\chi_y(z))\,[A_\epsilon(S_f(y,z))-1]\,|y-z|^{-\alpha}$. Then
  • \begin{equation}\mc I_2(y)=c_\alpha g'(y)\int_\R\kappa(y,z)\,dz+c_\alpha\int_\R g(z)\,\p_z\kappa(y,z)\,dz;\end{equation}
  • for $j,l\in\{0,1\}$: $|\p_y^j\p_z^l\kappa(y,z)|\le C\epsilon\,\mathbf 1_{\{|y-z|\ge|y|/4\}}|y-z|^{-p-1-j-l}$;
  • $|\p_y^j\mc I_2(y)|\le C\epsilon|y|^{-2p-1-j}$ for $j\in\{0,1\}$,
with $C$ admissible, uniformly in $\epsilon,\mu$. Moreover $\mc I_2$ is differentiable at every $y\le-8R$.
nodes.proof_html: (1) Split $\mc I_2=c_\alpha g'(y)\int\kappa\,dz-c_\alpha\int g'(z)\kappa\,dz$. In the second, integrate by parts separately on $(-\infty,0)$ and $(0,\infty)$ ($g$ is smooth on each closed half-line, continuous at $0$). Since $|y|\ge8R$, $z=0$ lies in $\{1-\chi_y=1\}$ and $\kappa(y,\cdot)$ is smooth near $0$, so the boundary terms $\pm g(0)\kappa(y,0)$ cancel; $\kappa(y,\cdot)$ vanishes near $z=y$; and $|g(z)\kappa(y,z)|\le CK_0\epsilon\ang z^{-p}|y-z|^{-\alpha}\to0$ as $|z|\to\infty$. (2) Use lem:c07_A_B_bounds ($|A_\epsilon-1|,|A_\epsilon'|,|A_\epsilon''|\le C\epsilon$ on $[-K_0,K_0]$), lem:c07_secant_calculus ($|\p_yS_f|,|\p_zS_f|\le2K_0|y-z|^{-1}$, $|\p_y\p_zS_f|\le4K_0|y-z|^{-2}$), and the cutoff: with $w=(y-z)/|y|=-1+z/y$ (as $y<0$), $\p_zw=-1/|y|$, $\p_yw=-z/y^2$, and on $\operatorname{supp}\chi'(w)$ one has $|y|/4\le|y-z|\le|y|/2$, $|z|\le\frac32|y|$, so every derivative of $\chi_y$ of total order $m\le2$ is bounded by $C|y|^{-m}\le C|y-z|^{-m}$; finally $|\p_y^j\p_z^l|y-z|^{-\alpha}|\le C|y-z|^{-\alpha-j-l}$. Leibniz gives (2). (3) Differentiating (1) under the integral (justified by (2)): $\p_y\mc I_2=c_\alpha g''(y)\int\kappa+c_\alpha g'(y)\int\p_y\kappa+c_\alpha\int g\,\p_y\p_z\kappa$. By lem:c07_family_uniform_bounds(3), $|g^{(1+i)}(y)|\le K_0\ang y^{-p-1-i}$; by (2) and lem:c07_tail_integrals(2), $\int|\p_y^i\kappa|dz\le C\epsilon|y|^{-p-i}$, so the local terms are $\le C\epsilon|y|^{-2p-1-j}$. By lem:c07_family_uniform_bounds(2) and lem:c07_tail_integrals(1) with $q=p+2+j$: $\int|g(z)||\p_y^j\p_z\kappa|dz\le C\epsilon\int_{|y-z|\ge|y|/4}\ang z^{-p}|y-z|^{-p-2-j}dz\le C\epsilon|y|^{-2p-1-j}$.

nodes.title: Corner term $\mc I_3$
nodes.section: Uniform properties of the approximate family
nodes.statement_html: There is an admissible $C$ with $|\p_y^j\mc I_3(y)|\le C\epsilon|y|^{-2p-1-j}$ for all $\epsilon,\mu$, $y\le-8R$, $j\in\{0,1\}$. Moreover $\mc I_3$ is differentiable at every $y\le-8R$.
nodes.proof_html: Let $y\le-8R$, $z>0$, so $z-y=|y|+z$. By lem:c07_secant_calculus, $S_f-S_W=S_g$ and $|S_g(y,z)|\le\frac{|g(y)|+|g(z)|}{|y|+z}\le K_0\frac{|y|^{-p}+\ang z^{-p}}{|y|+z}$. All secants lie in $[-K_0,K_0]$ ($K_0\ge1$), so by lem:c07_A_B_bounds and the mean value theorem $|A_\epsilon(S_f)-A_\epsilon(S_W)|\le C\epsilon\frac{|y|^{-p}+\ang z^{-p}}{|y|+z}$. Next $\p_y(A_\epsilon(S_f)-A_\epsilon(S_W))=A_\epsilon'(S_f)\p_yS_g+[A_\epsilon'(S_f)-A_\epsilon'(S_W)]\p_yS_W$, with $\p_yS_g=\frac{g'(y)-S_g}{y-z}$, $|g'(y)|\le K_0|y|^{-p-1}$, $|A_\epsilon'(S_f)-A_\epsilon'(S_W)|\le C\epsilon|S_g|$ and $|\p_yS_W|\le\frac2{|y|+z}$; hence $|\p_y(A_\epsilon(S_f)-A_\epsilon(S_W))|\le C\epsilon\bigl[\frac{|y|^{-p-1}}{|y|+z}+\frac{|y|^{-p}+\ang z^{-p}}{(|y|+z)^2}\bigr]$. Also $\p_y(z-y)^{-\alpha}=\alpha(z-y)^{-\alpha-1}$. Differentiating under the integral (majorants as below, locally uniform in $y$) and using lem:c07_tail_integrals(3) with $q=p+2$ and $q=p+3$: $|\mc I_3|\le C\epsilon\int_0^\infty\frac{|y|^{-p}+\ang z^{-p}}{(|y|+z)^{p+2}}dz\le C\epsilon|y|^{-2p-1}$ and $|\p_y\mc I_3|\le C\epsilon\int_0^\infty\bigl[\frac{|y|^{-p-1}}{(|y|+z)^{p+2}}+\frac{|y|^{-p}+\ang z^{-p}}{(|y|+z)^{p+3}}\bigr]dz\le C\epsilon|y|^{-2p-2}$.

nodes.title: Residual bound for $y\le-8R$
nodes.section: Uniform properties of the approximate family
nodes.statement_html: There is an admissible constant $C$ such that for all $0\le\epsilon\le\epsilon_0$, $\mu\in\ov B$, $y\le-8R$ and $j\in\{0,1\}$, with $f=\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu}$, \[ |\p_y^j(\sq{\mc E}_\epsilon(f)-G_\mu)(y)|\le C\epsilon\ang{y}^{-2p-1-j}. \] In particular, for every $\gamma\le2p+1$ (so for every $\gamma$ with $\beta+\frac1p<\gamma<2p+1$), $|\p_y^j(\sq{\mc E}_\epsilon(f)-G_\mu)(y)|\le C\epsilon\ang{y}^{-\gamma-j}$.
nodes.proof_html: By lem:c07_residual_split and lem:c07_negative_Q_split, $\sq{\mc E}_\epsilon(f)-G_\mu=[\mc L_0(f_{\textup{slow}})+\mc Q_\epsilon(W)]+\mc L_0(f_{\textup{osc}})+\mc I_1+\mc I_2+\mc I_3$ pointwise on $(-\infty,-8R]$ (each summand is $C^1$ there, by the lemmas cited). Sum the bounds of lem:c07_negative_slow, lem:c07_negative_osc, lem:c07_negative_I1, lem:c07_negative_I2, lem:c07_negative_I3, using $|y|^{-1}\le\sqrt2\ang y^{-1}$ for $|y|\geq1$. The last statement follows from $\ang y^{-2p-1}\le\ang y^{-\gamma}$.

nodes.title: Linear corrections on the compact region
nodes.section: Uniform properties of the approximate family
nodes.statement_html: There is an admissible $C$ such that for all $\epsilon,\mu$: \begin{equation} \|f_{\textup{osc}}\|_{L^\infty(\R)}+\|f_{\textup{osc}}\|_{C^3([-8R-1,8R+1])}\le C\epsilon, \end{equation} and $\|\mc L_0(f_{\textup{slow}})\|_{C^1([-8R,8R])}+\|\mc L_0(f_{\textup{osc}})\|_{C^1([-8R,8R])}\le C\epsilon$.
nodes.proof_html: Apply lem:c07_local_fractional with $M=8R$. For $u=f_{\textup{slow}}$: by lem:c07_slow_bounds, $u,u'$ are bounded and $\|u\|_{C^3(\R)}+\|u\|_{L^\infty}\le C\epsilon$. For $u=f_{\textup{osc}}$: it is $C^\infty$, vanishes on $(-\infty,R]$ (lem:c07_family_smooth), and by eqn:approx_fosc_bounds, $|f_{\textup{osc}}^{(i)}(y)|\le C\epsilon\ang y^{-p-\beta+i/p}$ for $y\ge R$; hence $\|u\|_{L^\infty}\le C\epsilon$, $u'$ bounded (as $-p-\beta+\frac1p<0$), and $\|u\|_{C^3([-8R-1,8R+1])}\le C\epsilon\ang{8R+1}^{3/p}$, which is eqn:approx_compact_oscillatory_norms.

nodes.title: Nonlinear remainder on the compact region
nodes.section: Uniform properties of the approximate family
nodes.statement_html: For every $M\ge1$ there is an admissible $C=C(M)$ such that for all $\epsilon,\mu$: $\|\mc Q_\epsilon(\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu})\|_{C^1([-M,M])}\le C\epsilon$.
nodes.proof_html: $\mc Q_\epsilon=\mc T_{A_\epsilon-1}$ (def:c07_kernel_operator), $\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu}\in\mc P(K_0)$, and $\|A_\epsilon-1\|_{K_0}\le CK_0^2\epsilon$ by lem:c07_A_B_bounds; apply lem:c07_kernel_C1.

nodes.title: Residual bound for $|y|\le8R$
nodes.section: Uniform properties of the approximate family
nodes.statement_html: There is an admissible $C$ (depending on $R$) such that for all $0\le\epsilon\le\epsilon_0$ and $\mu\in\ov B$, $\sq{\mc E}_\epsilon(\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu})-G_\mu\in C^1(\R)$ and \[\|\sq{\mc E}_\epsilon(\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu})-G_\mu\|_{C^1([-8R,8R])}\le C\epsilon.\]
nodes.proof_html: $C^1$ regularity: $\sq{\mc E}_\epsilon(f)=f-yf'+\mc T_{A_\epsilon}(f)$ (lem:c07_divided_residual_identity) with $\mc T_{A_\epsilon}(f)\in C^1$ (lem:c07_kernel_C1, $f\in\mc P(K_0)$), and $G_\mu$ is Schwartz. The bound: by lem:c07_residual_split, on $[-8R,8R]$ the difference is $\mc L_0(f_{\textup{slow}})+\mc L_0(f_{\textup{osc}})+\mc Q_\epsilon(f)$; apply lem:c07_compact_linear and lem:c07_compact_Q with $M=8R$.

nodes.title: $\mc E_5^Y$ is $C^1$ where the cubic term is
nodes.section: Uniform properties of the approximate family
nodes.statement_html: Let $\frac34<p<1$. For every $\delta\in(0,|\mu_*|/2]$ there are $\epsilon_0\in(0,1]$ and $R_0\ge2$ such that for all $R\ge R_0$, $\epsilon\in[0,\epsilon_0]$, $\mu\in\ov B$, $Y\ge8R$ and $y\in[Y,2Y]$: if $\mc Q_{\epsilon,3}(v_Y)$ is $C^1$ at $y$, then $\mc E_5^Y$ is $C^1$ at $y$.
nodes.proof_html: Take $\epsilon_0=\min\{1,\epsilon_0^*(\delta)\}$ with $\epsilon_0^*(\delta)$ of def:c05_standing, so that the standing assumptions of the chapter on $\mc E_5$ hold. By lem:c05_E5_split, near $y>2R$, $\mc E_5^Y=\mc R_{\textup{lin}}+\mc R_{\textup{cub}}$. $\mc R_{\textup{lin}}$ is $C^1$ near $y$ by prop:approx_E5_linear, and $\mc R_{\textup{cub}}$ is $\mc Q_{\epsilon,3}(v_Y)$ minus explicit expressions in $\lambda$ and $Z$, which are $C^\infty$ on $(R,\infty)$ (lem:c04_phase_basic).

nodes.title: Patching three regions into $Y_\gamma$
nodes.section: Uniform properties of the approximate family
nodes.statement_html: Let $\gamma>0$, $\rho\ge0$, $a,b\ge0$, and $H\in C^1(\R;\R)$ with: $|H^{(j)}(y)|\le a\ang y^{-\gamma+j/p}$ for $y\ge\rho$, $|H^{(j)}(y)|\le a\ang y^{-\gamma-j}$ for $y\le-\rho$ ($j=0,1$), and $\|H\|_{C^1([-\rho,\rho])}\le b$. Then $H\in Y_\gamma$ and $\|H\|_{Y_\gamma}\le4a+4\ang{\rho}^{\gamma+1}b$.
nodes.proof_html: $H\in C^1\subset W^{1,\infty}_{\textup{loc}}$. In the norm of def:Y_gamma, for $y\ge\rho$: $\ang y^\gamma(|H|+\ang y^{-1/p}|H'|)\le2a$; for $0\le y\le\rho$: $\le\ang\rho^\gamma\cdot2b$; for $y\le-\rho$: $\ang y^\gamma(|H|+\ang y|H'|)\le2a$; for $-\rho\le y\le0$: $\le\ang\rho^{\gamma}(1+\ang\rho)b$. Each of the two suprema is $\le2a+2\ang\rho^{\gamma+1}b$.

nodes.title: Divided residual in $Y_\gamma$
nodes.section: Uniform properties of the approximate family
nodes.statement_html: For every $\gamma$ with $\beta+\frac1p<\gamma<2p+1$ there is an admissible $C=C(\gamma)$ such that for all $0\le\epsilon\le\epsilon_0$, $\mu\in\ov B$: $\sq{\mc E}_\epsilon(\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu})-G_\mu\in Y_\gamma$ and $\|\sq{\mc E}_\epsilon(\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu})-G_\mu\|_{Y_\gamma}\le C\epsilon$.
nodes.proof_html: $H:=\sq{\mc E}_\epsilon(\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu})-G_\mu\in C^1$ by prop:approx_residual_compact. Apply lem:c07_Y_gamma_patching with $\rho=8R$, $a=C\epsilon$ from prop:approx_residual_positive (region $y\ge8R$, weight $\ang y^{-\gamma+j/p}$) and prop:approx_residual_negative (region $y\le-8R$, weight $\ang y^{-\gamma-j}$), and $b=C\epsilon$ from prop:approx_residual_compact.

nodes.title: Multiplication by $B_\epsilon(f')$ on $Y_\gamma$
nodes.section: Uniform properties of the approximate family
nodes.statement_html:
Let $\gamma>0$, $K\ge1$, $0\le\epsilon\le1$, $f\in\mc P(K)$. There is $C=C(p,K)$ such that:
  • if $H\in Y_\gamma\cap C^1$ then $B_\epsilon(f')H\in Y_\gamma\cap C^1$ and $\|B_\epsilon(f')H\|_{Y_\gamma}\le C\|H\|_{Y_\gamma}$;
  • if $G\in C^1$ with $N_\gamma(G):=\sup_y\ang y^{\gamma+1}(|G(y)|+|G'(y)|)<\infty$, then $\|(B_\epsilon(f')-1)G\|_{Y_\gamma}\le C\epsilon N_\gamma(G)$.
nodes.proof_html: By lem:c07_A_B_bounds and $|f'|\le K$: $|B_\epsilon(f')|\le1+K^2$, $|B_\epsilon(f')-1|\le K^2\epsilon$, $|\p_y B_\epsilon(f')|=|B_\epsilon'(f')f''|\le\alpha\epsilon K|f''|$, and by def:c07_profile_class(2) $|f''|\le K\ang y^{\theta}\le K\ang y^{1/p}$ for $y\ge0$, $|f''|\le K\ang y^{-1}$ for $y\le0$. (1) $(B H)'=B'(f')f''H+BH'$. For $y\ge0$: $\ang y^{\gamma-1/p}|B'(f')f''H|\le\alpha\epsilon K^2\ang y^{\gamma}|H|$; for $y\le0$: $\ang y^{\gamma+1}|B'(f')f''H|\le\alpha\epsilon K^2\ang y^\gamma|H|$. The terms $BH$, $BH'$ are bounded by $(1+K^2)$ times the corresponding terms of $H$. (2) Same computation with $H$ replaced by $G$ and $B$ by $B-1$, all terms carrying a factor $\epsilon$: for $y\geq0$, $\ang y^{\gamma}|B-1||G|+\ang y^{\gamma-1/p}(|B'f''||G|+|B-1||G'|)\le C\epsilon N_\gamma(G)$, and for $y\le0$ the weight $\ang y^{\gamma+1}$ is absorbed by $N_\gamma(G)$.

nodes.title: Residual in $Y_\gamma$
nodes.section: Uniform properties of the approximate family
nodes.statement_html: For every $\gamma$ with $\beta+\frac1p<\gamma<2p+1$ there is an admissible $C=C(\gamma)$ such that for all $0\le\epsilon\le\epsilon_0$, $\mu\in\ov B$: $\mc E_\epsilon(\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu})\in Y_\gamma\cap C^1(\R)$, \[ \|\mc E_\epsilon(\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu})-G_\mu\|_{Y_\gamma}\le C\epsilon,\qquad \|\mc E_\epsilon(\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu})\|_{Y_\gamma}\le C . \]
nodes.proof_html: By lem:c07_divided_residual_identity, $\mc E_\epsilon(f)-G_\mu=B_\epsilon(f')[\sq{\mc E}_\epsilon(f)-G_\mu]+[B_\epsilon(f')-1]G_\mu$. Apply lem:c07_B_conversion(1) with $H=\sq{\mc E}_\epsilon(f)-G_\mu$ (lem:c07_tilde_residual_Y) and lem:c07_B_conversion(2) with $G=G_\mu$, $N_\gamma(G_\mu)\le C$ uniformly in $\mu\in\ov B$ (lem:c07_G_mu_properties(3)), $K=K_0$. Then $\|\mc E_\epsilon(f)\|_{Y_\gamma}\le C\epsilon+\sup_{\ov B}\|G_\mu\|_{Y_\gamma}$. $C^1$: $B_\epsilon(f')\in C^1$ as $f\in C^2$, and $\sq{\mc E}_\epsilon(f)\in C^1$ (prop:approx_residual_compact).

nodes.title: Continuity of the residuals in $C^1_{\textup{loc}}$
nodes.section: Uniform properties of the approximate family
nodes.statement_html: Fix $0\le\epsilon\le\epsilon_0$. The maps $\mu\mapsto\sq{\mc E}_\epsilon(\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu})$ and $\mu\mapsto\mc E_\epsilon(\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu})$ are continuous from $\ov B$ into $C^1_{\textup{loc}}$.
nodes.proof_html: Let $\mu_n\to\mu$, $f_n=\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu_n}$, $f=\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu}$. By lem:c07_family_continuity, $f_n\to f$ in $C^2_{\textup{loc}}$, hence $f_n-yf_n'\to f-yf'$ in $C^1_{\textup{loc}}$ (its derivative is $-yf_n''$). All $f_n,f\in\mc P(K_0)$ (lem:c07_family_uniform_bounds), so lem:c07_kernel_continuity with $\Gamma=A_\epsilon$ gives $\mc T_{A_\epsilon}(f_n)\to\mc T_{A_\epsilon}(f)$ in $C^1_{\textup{loc}}$. By lem:c07_divided_residual_identity $\sq{\mc E}_\epsilon(f_n)\to\sq{\mc E}_\epsilon(f)$ in $C^1_{\textup{loc}}$. Next $B_\epsilon(f_n')\to B_\epsilon(f')$ in $C^1_{\textup{loc}}$ (as $f_n'\to f'$ in $C^1_{\textup{loc}}$, $B_\epsilon$ is smooth and $B_\epsilon,B_\epsilon'$ are uniformly continuous on $[-K_0,K_0]$), and products of $C^1_{\textup{loc}}$-convergent sequences converge in $C^1_{\textup{loc}}$; so $\mc E_\epsilon(f_n)=B_\epsilon(f_n')\sq{\mc E}_\epsilon(f_n)\to\mc E_\epsilon(f)$.

nodes.title: Continuity of the residual in $Y_\gamma$
nodes.section: Uniform properties of the approximate family
nodes.statement_html: Fix $0\le\epsilon\le\epsilon_0$ and $\gamma$ with $\beta+\frac1p<\gamma<2p+1$. The map $\mu\mapsto\mc E_\epsilon(\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu})$ is continuous from $\ov B$ into $Y_\gamma$.
nodes.proof_html: Let $\gamma'':=\frac12(\gamma+2p+1)\in(\gamma,2p+1)$; this uses that the admissible range of $\gamma$ is open. Let $\mu_n\to\mu$. By lem:c07_residual_Y at $\gamma''$, $\sup_n\|\mc E_\epsilon(\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu_n})\|_{Y_{\gamma''}}\le C(\gamma'')$ and the limit lies in $Y_{\gamma''}$. By lem:c07_residual_continuity_C1loc, the sequence converges in $C^1_{\textup{loc}}$, hence in $W^{1,\infty}_{\textup{loc}}$. prop:appendix_convergence (second statement, with exponents $\gamma<\gamma''$) gives convergence in $Y_\gamma$.

nodes.title: Existence of approximate solutions: assembly
nodes.section: Uniform properties of the approximate family
nodes.statement_html:
Let $\mu_*=-\frac{i}{\sqrt{2\pi p}}$ (def:mu_star), and let $\epsilon_0,\delta>0$, $\ov B=\{\mu\in\C:|\mu-\mu_*|\le\delta\}$ and the functions $\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu}$ ($0\le\epsilon\le\epsilon_0$, $\mu\in\ov B$) be as in def:approximate_solution_family. For $\mu\in\ov B$ let $G_\mu$ be as in def:G_mu. Then $\mu_*\in\C\setminus\{0\}$, every $\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu}$ is a real-valued $C^\infty$ function on $\R$, and for every $\gamma$ with $\beta+\frac1p<\gamma<2p+1$:
  • $\lim_{y\to-\infty}[\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu}(y)+y]=0$ and $\lim_{y\to\infty}\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu}(y)=0$;
  • for every $j\ge0$ there is $C_j$, independent of $\epsilon\in[0,\epsilon_0]$ and $\mu\in\ov B$, such that for $y\ge0$: $|\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu}(y)|\le C_0\ang y^{-p}$ and $|\p^j\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu}'(y)|\le C_j\ang y^{-\beta+j/p}$, and for $y\le0$: $|\p^j(\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu}(y)+y)|\le C_j\ang y^{-p-j}$;
  • $\mc E_\epsilon(\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu})\in Y_\gamma$ for all $\epsilon,\mu$; each $G_\mu$ is a real-valued Schwartz function independent of $\epsilon$, with $\widehat{G_\mu}(\xi)=(1-\frac\mu{\mu_*})\frac{\chi_+'(\xi)}{\xi}e^{-i\Phi_0(\xi)}$, $\Phi_0(\xi)=\frac1\alpha\xi|\xi|^p$, for $\xi>0$ and $\widehat{G_\mu}(\xi)=\ov{\widehat{G_\mu}(-\xi)}$ for $\xi<0$; $G_{\mu_*}=0$; and there is $C_\gamma$ independent of $\epsilon,\mu$ with eqn:fixed_point_residual_bound: $\sup_{\mu\in\ov B}\|\mc E_\epsilon(\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu})-G_\mu\|_{Y_\gamma}\le C_\gamma\epsilon$ for all $0\le\epsilon\le\epsilon_0$;
  • for each fixed $\epsilon\in[0,\epsilon_0]$, the map $\mu\mapsto\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu}$ is continuous from $\ov B$ into $C^2_{\textup{loc}}$, and $\mu\mapsto\mc E_\epsilon(\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu})$ is continuous from $\ov B$ into $C^1_{\textup{loc}}$ and into $Y_\gamma$.
This is exactly the conclusion of thm:fixed_point_approximation.
nodes.proof_html: Smoothness and reality: lem:c07_family_smooth; $\mu_*\neq0$: lem:c07_G_mu_properties(1). (2) is prop:approx_profile_bounds (with $\p^j\ov f'=\p^{j+1}\ov f$), its constants being uniform in $\epsilon,\mu$. (1) follows from (2) with $j=0$: $|\ov f(y)|\le C_0\ang y^{-p}\to0$ as $y\to\infty$ and $|\ov f(y)+y|\le C_0\ang y^{-p}\to0$ as $y\to-\infty$ (as $p>0$). (3): membership and the bound eqn:fixed_point_residual_bound are lem:c07_residual_Y; the properties of $G_\mu$ (Schwartz, real, independent of $\epsilon$, explicit form, $G_{\mu_*}=0$) are lem:c07_G_mu_properties(1)--(2). (4): continuity into $C^2_{\textup{loc}}$ is lem:c07_family_continuity with $k=2$; continuity of the residual into $C^1_{\textup{loc}}$ is lem:c07_residual_continuity_C1loc, and into $Y_\gamma$ is lem:c07_residual_continuity_Y.

nodes.title: Integrability of elements of $X_\gamma$, $Y_\gamma$
nodes.statement_html: Let $\gamma>1+\frac1p$ (in particular every admissible $\gamma$). There is $C=C(p,\gamma)$ such that for $r\in X_\gamma$ and $G\in Y_\gamma$: $\|r\|_{L^1}+\|r'\|_{L^1}+\|r\|_{L^\infty}+\|r'\|_{L^\infty}\le C\|r\|_{X_\gamma}$ and $\|G\|_{L^1}+\|G'\|_{L^1}+\|G\|_{L^\infty}\le C\|G\|_{Y_\gamma}$. Moreover $G(y)\to0$ as $|y|\to\infty$, and $\widehat{G'}(\xi)=i\xi\widehat G(\xi)$ for all $\xi$; similarly $\widehat{r'}=i\xi\widehat r$.
nodes.proof_html:
The weights $\ang{y}^{-\gamma}$ and $w_1$ are integrable since $\gamma>1$ and $\gamma-\frac1p>1$, and bounded
  since $\gamma-\frac1p>0$. For the Fourier identity integrate by parts on $[-R,R]$:
  $\int_{-R}^RG'e^{-iy\xi}dy=[Ge^{-iy\xi}]_{-R}^R+i\xi\int_{-R}^RGe^{-iy\xi}dy$ ($G$ is locally absolutely
  continuous), and let $R\to\infty$ using $G\to0$ and $G,G'\in L^1$.

nodes.title: The conjugating diffeomorphism
nodes.statement_html: Let $c\in\R$ with $|c|\le\frac12$. Define $b_c:\R\to\R$ by $b_c(y)=c\,\chi_+(y)y^{-p}$ for $y>1$ and $b_c(y)=0$ for $y\le1$ (so $b_c\in C^\infty(\R)$ since $\chi_+=0$ on $(-\infty,1]$, and $|b_c(y)|\le|c|$). Since $t-b_c(t)\ge t-\frac12>0$ for $t\ge1$, we may define \[ \phi_c(y):=y\quad(y\le1),\qquad \phi_c(y):=\Bigl[1+\frac{p+1}{p}\int_1^y\bigl(t-b_c(t)\bigr)^{1/p}dt\Bigr]^{\frac p{p+1}}\quad(y>1). \] Put $\psi_c:=\phi_c^{-1}$ (a bijection of $\R$ by lem:c08_phi_diffeo). For $\epsilon\ge0$ with $|c_\epsilon|\le\frac12$ we write $\phi_\epsilon:=\phi_{c_\epsilon}$, $\psi_\epsilon:=\psi_{c_\epsilon}$, and $b_\epsilon=b_{c_\epsilon}$ (which is the coefficient of def:L_eps).

nodes.title: The integrand
nodes.statement_html: For $|c|\le\frac12$ let $g_c(t):=(t-b_c(t))^{1/p}-t^{1/p}$ for $t\ge\frac12$. Then $g_c\in C^\infty((\frac12,\infty))$, $g_c=0$ on $(\frac12,1]$, and for every $j\ge0$ there is $C_j=C_j(p,\chi_+)$ with \[ |g_c^{(j)}(t)|\le C_j|c|\,t^{\frac1p-p-1-j},\qquad t\ge1 . \]
nodes.proof_html:
On $(\frac12,1]$, $b_c=0$ so $g_c=0$. For $t>1$ write $g_c(t)=t^{1/p}h(c\,\varrho(t))$ with
  $\varrho(t)=\chi_+(t)t^{-1-p}$ and $h(s)=(1-s)^{1/p}-1$. Since $|c\varrho|\le\frac12$ and $h$ is smooth on
  $[-\frac12,\frac12]$ with $h(0)=0$, write $h(s)=s\tilde h(s)$ with $\tilde h$ smooth. Each derivative of
  $\varrho$ obeys $|\varrho^{(i)}(t)|\le C_i t^{-1-p-i}$ for $t\ge1$ (Leibniz; $\chi_+^{(i)}$ bounded). By Faà di
  Bruno, $|\p_t^i[h(c\varrho)]|\le C_i|c|t^{-1-p-i}$; multiply by $t^{1/p}$ (with $|\p^i t^{1/p}|\le Ct^{1/p-i}$) and use
  Leibniz. Smoothness across $t=1$: $g_c$ is the composition of smooth maps on $(\frac12,\infty)$ (the
  expression $(t-b_c(t))^{1/p}-t^{1/p}$ is smooth on $(\frac12,\infty)$ since $t-b_c(t)>0$ there).

nodes.title: $\phi_c$ is a smooth increasing diffeomorphism solving the ODE
nodes.statement_html: Let $|c|\le\frac12$. Then $\phi_c\in C^\infty(\R)$, $\phi_c'>0$ on $\R$, $\phi_c(y)=y$ for $y\le1$, $\phi_c$ maps $(1,\infty)$ onto $(1,\infty)$, $\phi_c:\R\to\R$ is a bijection, $\psi_c\in C^\infty(\R)$, $\psi_c(y)=y$ for $y\le1$, and \begin{equation} \phi_c(y)\,\phi_c'(y)^p=y-b_c(y)\qquad\text{for all }y\in\R. \end{equation}
nodes.proof_html: On $(\frac12,\infty)$ let $F(y):=y^{\frac{p+1}p}+\frac{p+1}p\int_1^yg_c(t)\,dt$. Since $\int_1^yt^{1/p}dt=\frac p{p+1}(y^{\frac{p+1}p}-1)$, $F(y)$ equals the bracket in def:c08_phi for $y>1$, and $F(y)=y^{(p+1)/p}$ for $y\in(\frac12,1]$ ($g_c=0$ there). $F$ is smooth on $(\frac12,\infty)$ by lem:c08_phi_integrand, and $F\ge1$ on $[1,\infty)$ (integrand $(t-b_c)^{1/p}>0$), $F>0$ on $(\frac12,1]$. Hence $\phi_c=F^{p/(p+1)}$ on $(\frac12,\infty)$, which is smooth and coincides with $y$ on $(\frac12,1]$; so $\phi_c\in C^\infty(\R)$. For $y>1$, $F'=\frac{p+1}p(y-b_c)^{1/p}$, and $F'=\frac{p+1}{p}\phi_c^{1/p}\phi_c'$, so $\phi_c^{1/p}\phi_c'=(y-b_c)^{1/p}>0$; raising to the power $p$ (both sides positive, $\phi_c\ge1$) gives eqn:linear_phi_ode on $y>1$; on $y\le1$ it is $y\cdot1=y$. Thus $\phi_c'>0$ everywhere, $\phi_c(1)=1$, and $\phi_c(y)\ge\bigl[1+\frac{p+1}p\int_1^y(t/2)^{1/p}dt\bigr]^{p/(p+1)}\to\infty$, so $\phi_c$ is an increasing bijection with $\phi_c((1,\infty))=(1,\infty)$. By the inverse function theorem $\psi_c$ is smooth, and $\psi_c=\mathrm{id}$ on $(-\infty,1]$.

nodes.title: Bounds for $\phi_c$
nodes.statement_html: There are $c_0\in(0,\frac12]$ and constants $C_j=C_j(p,\chi_+)$, $j\ge0$, such that for all $|c|\le c_0$ and $y\in\R$: \begin{equation} |\p_y^j(\phi_c(y)-y)|\le C_j|c|\ang{y}^{-p-j}\qquad(j\ge0), \end{equation} and moreover $|\phi_c'-1|\le\frac12$, $|\phi_c(y)-y|\le\frac12$, $\frac12\ang{y}\le\ang{\phi_c(y)}\le2\ang{y}$, and \[ |(\phi_c')^{p+1}-1|+\ang{y}\,|\p_y(\phi_c')^{p+1}|\le C|c|\ang{y}^{-p-1}. \] All these quantities vanish identically on $y\le1$.
nodes.proof_html: On $y\le1$ everything is trivial ($\phi_c=\mathrm{id}$). For $y>1$ (where $\ang{y}\approx y$), let $I(y)=\int_1^yg_c$ and $E(y)=\frac{p+1}py^{-\frac{p+1}p}I(y)$, so $\phi_c(y)=y(1+E(y))^{p/(p+1)}$ (from $F=y^{(p+1)/p}(1+E)$). Since $\frac1p-p>0$, lem:c08_phi_integrand gives $|I(y)|\le C|c|\int_1^yt^{1/p-p-1}dt\le C|c|y^{1/p-p}$ and $|I^{(j)}|=|g_c^{(j-1)}|\le C|c|y^{1/p-p-j}$ for $j\ge1$. By Leibniz, $|E^{(j)}(y)|\le C_j|c|y^{-1-p-j}$. Choose $c_0$ so that $|E|\le\frac12$. Writing $(1+s)^{p/(p+1)}-1=s\,k(s)$ with $k$ smooth on $[-\frac12,\frac12]$, Faà di Bruno and Leibniz give $|\p^j[yE\,k(E)]|\le C_j|c|y^{-p-j}$, which is eqn:linear_phi_bounds. Shrinking $c_0$ so that $C_0c_0,C_1c_0\le\frac12$ gives the remaining claims ($\ang{\cdot}$ is $1$-Lipschitz and $\ang{y}\ge1$). The last estimate follows from $\phi_c'-1=O(|c|\ang{y}^{-p-1})$, $\phi_c''=O(|c|\ang{y}^{-p-2})$ and smoothness of $s\mapsto s^{p+1}$ near $1$.

nodes.title: Bounds for $\psi_c=\phi_c^{-1}$
nodes.statement_html: For $|c|\le c_0$ and all $y$: $\psi_c=\mathrm{id}$ on $(-\infty,1]$, $\psi_c((1,\infty))=(1,\infty)$, \begin{equation} \tfrac12\ang{y}\le\ang{\psi_c(y)}\le2\ang{y},\quad \psi_c'=\frac1{\phi_c'\circ\psi_c}\in[\tfrac23,2],\quad \psi_c''=-\frac{\phi_c''\circ\psi_c}{(\phi_c'\circ\psi_c)^3}, \end{equation} and $|\psi_c(y)-y|\le C|c|\ang{y}^{-p}$, $|\psi_c'(y)-1|\le C|c|\ang{y}^{-p-1}$, $|\psi_c''(y)|\le C|c|\ang{y}^{-p-2}$, $|(\psi_c')^{p+1}-1|+|(\psi'_c)^{p+2}-1|\le C|c|\ang{y}^{-p-1}$.
nodes.proof_html: Differentiate $\phi_c(\psi_c(y))=y$ twice. $\psi_c(y)-y=-(\phi_c-\mathrm{id})(\psi_c(y))$, and $\ang{\psi_c(y)}\approx\ang{y}$ because $|\psi_c(y)-y|\le\frac12$. Then insert lem:c08_phi_bounds at the point $\psi_c(y)$.

nodes.title: $\mc U_\epsilon$
nodes.statement_html: For $u\in\mathcal F(\R)$ let $\mc U_\epsilon u:=u\circ\psi_\epsilon$. This is an $\R$-linear bijection of $\mathcal F(\R)$ with inverse $\mc U_\epsilon^{-1}u=u\circ\phi_\epsilon$; it does not depend on $\gamma$. (In the paper's notation $\mc U=\mc T_{\phi}^{-1}$, $\mc T_\phi u=u\circ\phi$; this is eqn:linear_conjugating_maps.)

nodes.title: $\mc V_\epsilon$
nodes.statement_html: For $u\in\mathcal F(\R)$ let $(\mc V_\epsilon u)(y):=\phi_\epsilon'(y)^{p+1}\,u(\phi_\epsilon(y))$. This is an $\R$-linear bijection of $\mathcal F(\R)$ with inverse $(\mc V_\epsilon^{-1}u)(y)=\psi_\epsilon'(y)^{p+1}u(\psi_\epsilon(y))$ (check: $\phi_\epsilon'(y)\psi_\epsilon'(\phi_\epsilon(y))=1$). It does not depend on $\gamma$. \begin{equation} \mc V_\epsilon=(\phi_\epsilon')^{p+1}\mc T_{\phi_\epsilon},\qquad \mc U_\epsilon=\mc T_{\phi_\epsilon}^{-1}. \end{equation}

nodes.title: Remainder $\mc R_\epsilon$
nodes.statement_html: For $y\neq z$ let \[ K_\epsilon(y,z):=c_\alpha\Bigl[1-\Bigl(\frac{\phi_\epsilon'(y)}{S_{\phi_\epsilon}(y,z)}\Bigr)^{p+1}\Bigr]\frac1{|y-z|^{1+p}} . \] For $r\in C^1(\R)$ with $r'$ bounded define \begin{equation} \mc R_{1,\epsilon}r:=\bigl((\phi_\epsilon')^{p+1}-1\bigr)r, \end{equation} \begin{equation} \mc R_{2,\epsilon}r(y):=\int_\R K_\epsilon(y,z)\,r'(z)\,dz =c_\alpha\int_\R\Bigl[1-\Bigl(\frac{\phi_\epsilon'(y)}{S_{\phi_\epsilon}(y,z)}\Bigr)^{p+1}\Bigr]\frac{r'(z)}{|y-z|^{1+p}}\,dz, \end{equation} (absolutely convergent by lem:c08_R2_kernel_near, lem:c08_R2_kernel_far) and $\mc R_\epsilon:=\mc R_{1,\epsilon}+\mc R_{2,\epsilon}$. For $\epsilon=0$ ($c_0=0$, $\phi_0=\mathrm{id}$) one has $\mc R_0=0$.

nodes.title: Local part of the conjugation
nodes.statement_html: Let $r\in C^1(\R)$ and $v:=\mc U_\epsilon r$. Then for all $y\in\R$, with $x=\phi_\epsilon(y)$, \[ \phi_\epsilon'(y)^{p+1}\bigl(v(x)-x\,v'(x)\bigr)=r(y)-y\,r'(y)+b_\epsilon(y)r'(y)+\mc R_{1,\epsilon}r(y). \]
nodes.proof_html: $v(\phi_\epsilon(y))=r(y)$ and $v'(\phi_\epsilon(y))=r'(y)/\phi_\epsilon'(y)$. Hence the left side equals $(\phi'_\epsilon)^{p+1}r-\phi_\epsilon(\phi_\epsilon')^pr'=r+((\phi_\epsilon')^{p+1}-1)r-(y-b_\epsilon)r'$ by eqn:linear_phi_ode.

nodes.title: A vanishing integral
nodes.statement_html: Let $|c|\le c_0$, $\phi=\phi_c$, $y\in\R$. The function $z\mapsto\frac{\phi'(y)^p\phi'(z)}{|\phi(y)-\phi(z)|^{1+p}}-\frac1{|y-z|^{1+p}}$ is in $L^1(\R)$ and its integral is $0$.
nodes.proof_html: Write it as $|y-z|^{-1-p}B(z)$, $B(z)=\phi'(y)^p\phi'(z)S_\phi(y,z)^{-1-p}-1$. Since $S_\phi(y,z)=\int_0^1\phi'(z+s(y-z))ds\in[\frac12,\frac32]$ is smooth in $z$ (including $z=y$, value $\phi'(y)$), $B$ is $C^1$ with $B(y)=0$ and $B'$ bounded (bounds of lem:c08_phi_bounds), so $|B(z)|\le C|y-z|$; also $|B|\le C$. Hence the integrand is $O(|y-z|^{-p})$ near $y$ and $O(|y-z|^{-1-p})$ at infinity: $L^1$. For $\delta\in(0,1)$, by the substitution $x'=\phi(z)$ ($\phi$ increasing, $\phi(\pm\infty)=\pm\infty$), \[ \int_{|z-y|>\delta}\frac{\phi'(z)\,dz}{|\phi(y)-\phi(z)|^{1+p}}=\frac1p\bigl[(\phi(y)-\phi(y-\delta))^{-p}+(\phi(y+\delta)-\phi(y))^{-p}\bigr], \qquad \int_{|z-y|>\delta}\frac{dz}{|y-z|^{1+p}}=\frac2{p\delta^p}. \] So the truncated integral equals $\frac{\delta^{-p}}p\bigl[a_-^p+a_+^p-2\bigr]$ with $a_\pm=\phi'(y)/S_\phi(y,y\pm\delta)$. Since $|S_\phi(y,y\pm\delta)-\phi'(y)|\le\frac12\|\phi''\|_\infty\delta$ and $S_\phi\ge\frac12$, $|a_\pm-1|\le C\delta$, so the truncated integral is $O(\delta^{1-p})\to0$. By dominated convergence the truncated integrals converge to the full integral, which is therefore $0$.

nodes.title: Nonlocal part of the conjugation
nodes.statement_html: Let $r\in C^1(\R)$ with $r'$ bounded and locally Lipschitz, $v=\mc U_\epsilon r$ and $w:=v'=(r'\circ\psi_\epsilon)\psi_\epsilon'$. Then $w$ is bounded and locally Lipschitz, and for every $y\in\R$ \[ \phi_\epsilon'(y)^{p+1}\,(|D|^pw)(\phi_\epsilon(y))=(|D|^pr')(y)+\mc R_{2,\epsilon}r(y), \] with $|D|^p$ the absolutely convergent singular integral of def:frac_multiplier.
nodes.proof_html: Write $\phi=\phi_\epsilon$, $S=S_\phi(y,z)$. Substitute $x'=\phi(z)$ in $|D|^pw(\phi(y))=c_\alpha\int\frac{w(\phi(y))-w(x')}{|\phi(y)-x'|^{1+p}}dx'$, using $w(\phi(z))=r'(z)/\phi'(z)$, $dx'=\phi'(z)dz$, $|\phi(y)-\phi(z)|=S|y-z|$: \[ \phi'(y)^{p+1}|D|^pw(\phi(y))=c_\alpha\int_\R\frac{r'(y)\phi'(y)^p\phi'(z)S^{-1-p}-\phi'(y)^{p+1}S^{-1-p}r'(z)}{|y-z|^{1+p}}dz . \] Decompose the numerator as $r'(y)\bigl[\phi'(y)^p\phi'(z)S^{-1-p}-1\bigr]+\bigl[r'(y)-r'(z)\bigr]+\bigl[1-(\phi'(y)/S)^{p+1}\bigr]r'(z)$. Each of the three resulting integrals converges absolutely (first: lem:c08_conj_cancellation; second: lem:c01_frac_well_defined; third: $|1-(\phi'(y)/S)^{p+1}|\le C\min(1,|y-z|)$, $r'$ bounded), so splitting is legitimate. The first is $0$ by lem:c08_conj_cancellation, the second is $|D|^pr'(y)$, the third is $\mc R_{2,\epsilon}r(y)$.

nodes.title: Conjugation identity
nodes.statement_html: Let $\gamma>1+\frac1p$, $0\le\epsilon\le\epsilon_c$ and $r\in X_\gamma$. Then $\mc U_\epsilon r\in X_\gamma$ (lem:c08_U_bounded) and, pointwise on $\R$, \begin{equation} \mc V_\epsilon\bigl(\mc L_0(\mc U_\epsilon r)\bigr)=\mc L_0r+b_\epsilon r'+\mc R_\epsilon r=\mc L_\epsilon r . \end{equation}
nodes.proof_html: By lem:c08_L1_embedding $r'$ is bounded, and it is locally Lipschitz as $r\in W^{2,\infty}_{\rm loc}$. With $v=\mc U_\epsilon r$, $\mc L_0v=|D|^pv'+v-xv'$; evaluate at $x=\phi_\epsilon(y)$, multiply by $\phi_\epsilon'(y)^{p+1}$, and add lem:c08_conj_local and lem:c08_conj_nonlocal.

nodes.title: $\mc U_\epsilon$ is a uniform isomorphism of $X_\gamma$
nodes.statement_html: Let $\gamma\in\R$. There is $C=C(p,\gamma,\chi_+)$ such that for $0\le\epsilon\le\epsilon_c$ and all $r\in X_\gamma$: $\mc U_\epsilon r,\ \mc U_\epsilon^{-1}r\in X_\gamma$ and $\|\mc U_\epsilon r\|_{X_\gamma}+\|\mc U_\epsilon^{-1}r\|_{X_\gamma}\le C\|r\|_{X_\gamma}$. Hence $\mc U_\epsilon$ restricts to a linear bijection $X_\gamma\to X_\gamma$ with $\|\mc U_\epsilon\|,\|\mc U_\epsilon^{-1}\|\le C$.
nodes.proof_html: $\mc U_\epsilon r=r$ on $(-\infty,1]$, which covers $y\le0$ and $0\le y\le1$. For $y>1$, $\psi=\psi_\epsilon$ maps into $(1,\infty)$, $\mc U_\epsilon r\in W^{2,\infty}_{\rm loc}$, and $(\mc U_\epsilon r)'=(r'\circ\psi)\psi'$, $(\mc U_\epsilon r)''=(r''\circ\psi)(\psi')^2+(r'\circ\psi)\psi''$ a.e. By eqn:linear_inverse_phi_bounds, $|\p^j(\mc U_\epsilon r)(y)|\le C\|r\|_{X_\gamma}\ang{y}^{-\gamma+j/p}$, $j=0,1,2$ (the constant absorbs $2^{|\gamma|+2/p}$ from $\ang{\psi(y)}\approx\ang{y}$). Same argument for $\mc U_\epsilon^{-1}r=r\circ\phi_\epsilon$ with lem:c08_phi_bounds.

nodes.title: $\mc V_\epsilon$ is a uniform isomorphism of $Y_\gamma$
nodes.statement_html: Let $\gamma\in\R$. There is $C=C(p,\gamma,\chi_+)$ such that for $0\le\epsilon\le\epsilon_c$ and $G\in Y_\gamma$: $\mc V_\epsilon G,\mc V_\epsilon^{-1}G\in Y_\gamma$ with $\|\mc V_\epsilon G\|_{Y_\gamma}+\|\mc V_\epsilon^{-1}G\|_{Y_\gamma}\le C\|G\|_{Y_\gamma}$.
