For $j=1$: $m_{1,1}$ is real, so $\operatorname{Re}\partial_z\widecheck{m_{1,1}}(z)=-\frac1{2\pi}\int\xi m_{1,1}\sin(z\xi)d\xi$. By lem:c09_mjk_bounds, $\xi m_{1,1}=-im_{2,1}+B/(2\pi\xi)$ with $B:=b(y-\xi^p)^{-2}$; the first part is bounded by $\|m_{2,1}\|_{L^1}$. For the second, with $S(\xi):=\int_1^\xi\frac{\sin(z\eta)}{\eta}d\eta$ ($S(1)=0$, $|S|\le C_{\mathrm{Si}}$ by lem:c09_sine_integral_bounded, $B$ compactly supported), $\int_1^\infty B\frac{\sin(z\xi)}{\xi}d\xi=-\int_1^\infty B'S\,d\xi$, bounded by $C_{\mathrm{Si}}\int|B'|\lesssim\ang{y}^{-2}\int|\partial b|+\int_1^\infty\xi^{p-1}(|y|+\xi^p)^{-3}\lesssim\ang y^{-2}$. For $|z|>1$ choose an integer $N\ge\max\{L,1\}$, integrate by parts $N$ times (smooth, supported in $[1,2R]$, flat at $1$), and use $|\partial^N(\xi m_{0,1})|\lesssim\xi^{-2-N}\ang y^{-2}$, $|\partial^N(\xi m_{1,1})|+|\partial^N m_{2,1}|\lesssim\xi^{-1-N}\ang{y}^{-2}$ (lem:c09_mjk_bounds, lem:c09_cutoff_bounds(4)); all integrable on $[1,\infty)$ as $N\ge1$. Conclude as in lem:c09_m10_m00_kernel.

nodes.title: Kernels with $k\ge2$
nodes.statement_html: For $k\ge2$, $L\ge0$ there is $C_{k,L}$ such that for all $R\ge2$, $y,z\in\R$: $\sum_{j=0}^1|\partial_z\widecheck{m^R_{j,k}(y,\cdot)}(z)|+|\widecheck{m^R_{2,k}(y,\cdot)}(z)|\le C_{k,L}\ang{y}^{-k-1}\ang{z}^{-L}$.
nodes.proof_html: The symbols $i\xi m_{0,k},i\xi m_{1,k},m_{2,k}$ satisfy $|\partial^\ell(\cdot)|\lesssim_{k,\ell}\xi^{-k-\ell}(|y|+\xi^p)^{-k-1}\lesssim\xi^{-k-\ell}\ang y^{-k-1}$ on $[1,\infty)$ (lem:c09_mjk_bounds, lem:c09_cutoff_bounds(4)), integrable for $k\ge2$, $\ell\ge0$. For $|z|\le1$ use the $L^1$ norm ($\ell=0$); for $|z|>1$ integrate by parts an integer $N\ge\max\{L,1\}$ times and use $|z|^{-N}\le2^{L/2}\ang z^{-L}$.

nodes.title: Symbol bounds
nodes.statement_html:
For every $L\ge0$, $k\ge0$ there are constants $C_L$, $C_{k,L}$ (depending on $p,\chi$) such that for all $y\in\R$ and $R\ge R_0(y)$:
  • $k=0$: paper eq. eqn:linear\_nonstationary\_leading\_kernel\_j0, i.e.\ $|\operatorname{Re}\partial_z\widecheck{m^R_{0,0}(y,\cdot)}(z)|\le C_L\ang y^{-1}\ang z^{-L}$, and (paper eq. eqn:linear\_nonstationary\_leading\_kernel\_j12) for $z\neq0$, $|\operatorname{Re}\partial_z\widecheck{m^R_{1,0}(y,\cdot)}(z)|+|\operatorname{Re}\widecheck{m^R_{2,0}(y,\cdot)}(z)|$ is bounded by $2C_L$ times the three-region function of lem:c09_m20_kernel;
  • $k\ge1$ (paper eq. eqn:linear\_nonstationary\_higher\_kernels): $\sum_{j=0}^1|\operatorname{Re}\partial_z\widecheck{m^R_{j,k}(y,\cdot)}(z)|+|\operatorname{Re}\widecheck{m^R_{2,k}(y,\cdot)}(z)|\le C_{k,L}\ang y^{-k-1}\ang z^{-L}$ (this part holds for all $R\ge2$).
nodes.proof_html: Collect lem:c09_m20_kernel, lem:c09_m10_m00_kernel (using $\partial_z\widecheck{m_{1,0}}=\widecheck{m_{2,0}}$) and lem:c09_k1_kernels, lem:c09_k2_kernels.

nodes.title: Weighted $L^1$ bounds for the kernels
nodes.statement_html: Let $\gamma$ be admissible and put $h^R_{j,k}(y,z):=\operatorname{Re}\partial_z\widecheck{m^R_{j,k}(y,\cdot)}(z)$ for $j=0,1$ and $h^R_{2,k}(y,z):=\operatorname{Re}\widecheck{m^R_{2,k}(y,\cdot)}(z)$. There is $C$ such that for $0\le k\le4$, $j\in\{0,1,2\}$, $y\in\R$, $R\ge R_0(y)$ (paper eq. eqn:linear\_nonstationary\_weighted\_kernels): \[ \int_\R\ang{z}^{\gamma+1}|h^R_{j,k}(y,z)|\,dz\le C\ang{y}^{-k-1}. \]
nodes.proof_html: Take $L:=\lceil\gamma\rceil+3>\gamma+2$, so $\int\ang z^{\gamma+1}\ang z^{-L}<\infty$; this settles $k\ge1$ and $j=0$, $k=0$. For $j=1,2$, $k=0$: on $|z|>1$ as before; on $|z|\le1$ ($\ang z^{\gamma+1}\le2^{(\gamma+1)/2}$) integrate the three-region bound: $2\int_0^{\ang y^{-1/p}}s^{p-1}ds+2\ang{y}^{-2}\int_{\ang y^{-1/p}}^1s^{-p-1}ds+2\ang y^{-1}\le\frac2p\ang y^{-1}+\frac2p\ang y^{-1}+2\ang{y}^{-1}$.

nodes.title: Remainder kernel
nodes.statement_html: For $M\ge2$ there is $C_M$ (depending on $p,\chi,M$) such that for all $R\ge2$, $j\in\{0,1,2\}$, $y,z\in\R$: $|K^R_{\mc R_{j,M}}(y,z)|\le C_M\ang{y}^{-M}w_E(z)$, i.e.\ $\lesssim_M\ang y^{-M}\ang z^{-1}$ for $z\le0$ and $\lesssim_M\ang y^{-M}\ang z^{\frac{1-p}{2p}}$ for $z>0$.
nodes.proof_html: By lem:c09_mjk_bounds, $|\partial_\xi m^R_{j,M-1}|\lesssim_M\xi^{j-2-M}(|y|+\xi^p)^{-M}\le\xi^{-M}2^{M/2}\ang{y}^{-M}$ on $[1,\infty)$ (lem:c09_cutoff_bounds(4)), integrable since $M\ge2$; and $|E_z(\xi)|\le C_Ew_E(z)$ (lem:c09_tail_basic(2)).

nodes.title: Stationary contribution
nodes.statement_html: Let $\gamma$ be admissible. There is $C$ such that for all $G\in\sq Y_\gamma$, $R\ge2$, $j\in\{0,1,2\}$, $y\in\R$: $|\mc T^{\textup{s},R}_{+,j}G(y)|\le C\|G\|_{Y_\gamma}w_{\gamma,j}(y)$ (paper eq. eqn:linear\_positive\_stationary\_contribution).
nodes.proof_html: If $y<y_*$ the kernel vanishes (prop:linear_stationary); in particular for $y\le0$. Let $y\ge y_*$ (so $\ang y\approx y$, $w_{\gamma,j}(y)=\ang{y}^{-\gamma+j/p}$). On $z\ge y/4$, using $|G'(z)|\le\|G\|\ang z^{-\gamma+1/p}$: contribution $\lesssim\|G\|\ang y^{\frac jp-\frac{p+3}{2p}}\int_{y/4}^\infty\ang z^{-s}dz$ with $s:=\gamma-\frac{3-p}{2p}>1$ (admissibility), and $\int_{y/4}^\infty\ang z^{-s}\lesssim\ang y^{1-s}$, giving $\ang{y}^{\frac jp-\frac{p+3}{2p}+1-s}=\ang y^{-\gamma+\frac jp}$. On $z<y/4$: by prop:linear_stationary with $M:=3$, contribution $\le C_3\ang y^{-6}\|G'\|_{L^1}\lesssim\|G\|\ang y^{-6}\le\|G\|\ang{y}^{-\gamma+j/p}$ (as $\gamma<3<6$).

nodes.title: Nonstationary contribution
nodes.statement_html: Let $\gamma$ be admissible. There is $C$ such that for all $G\in\sq Y_\gamma$, $j\in\{0,1,2\}$, $y\in\R$ and $R\ge R_0(y)$: $|\operatorname{Re}\mc T^{\textup{ns},R}_{+,j}G(y)|\le C\|G\|_{Y_\gamma}w_{\gamma,j}(y)$.
nodes.proof_html: Use lem:linear_nonstationary_symbol_expansion(3) with $M=5$. Remainder: by lem:linear_nonstationary_remainder and lem:c09_weight_facts(3), $|\mc R^R_{j,5}G(y)|\lesssim\ang y^{-5}\int|G'|w_E\lesssim\|G\|\ang{y}^{-5}\le\|G\|w_{\gamma,j}(y)$ since $5>\gamma+2$. Convolution terms, $0\le k\le4$: since $G'$ is real, $\operatorname{Re}[\widecheck{m}*G'](y)=\int\operatorname{Re}\widecheck{m}(z)G'(y-z)dz$. For $j=0,1$ integrate by parts in $z$ ($\widecheck m$ Schwartz, $G$ bounded, $G\in W^{1,1}_{\mathrm{loc}}$; no boundary terms): (paper eq. eqn:linear\_nonstationary\_convolution\_j01) $=\int h^R_{j,k}(y,z)G(y-z)dz$, and by lem:c09_weight_facts(6) and lem:c09_weighted_kernel_L1, $|\cdot|\le2^{\gamma/2}\|G\|\ang y^{-\gamma}\int\ang z^\gamma|h^R_{j,k}|\lesssim\|G\|\ang{y}^{-\gamma-k-1}\le\|G\|w_{\gamma,j}(y)$ for $j\le1$. For $j=2$ (paper eq. eqn:linear\_nonstationary\_convolution\_j2): by lem:c09_weight_facts(5), $|\int h^R_{2,k}(y,z)G'(y-z)dz|\lesssim\|G\|w_{\gamma,1}(y)\int\ang z^{\gamma+1}|h^R_{2,k}|\lesssim\|G\|w_{\gamma,1}(y)\ang y^{-k-1}\le\|G\|w_{\gamma,2}(y)$ (for $y\ge0$: $\ang y^{-\gamma+1/p-1}\le\ang y^{-\gamma+2/p}$; for $y<0$: $\ang y^{-\gamma-2-k}\le\ang y^{-\gamma-2}$). Sum over $k\le4$.

nodes.title: Truncated high-frequency bound
nodes.statement_html: Let $\gamma$ be admissible. There is $C$ such that for all $G\in\sq Y_\gamma$, $j\in\{0,1,2\}$, $y\in\R$, $R\ge R_0(y)$: $|\partial_y^j\mc T^R_{\textup{h}}G(y)|\le C\|G\|_{Y_\gamma}w_{\gamma,j}(y)$.
nodes.proof_html: $\partial^j\mc T^R_{\textup{h}}G=2\operatorname{Re}\partial^j\mc T^R_+G=2\operatorname{Re}\mc T^{\textup{s},R}_{+,j}G+2\operatorname{Re}\mc T^{\textup{ns},R}_{+,j}G$ (def:c09_stationary_split(4)); bound $|\operatorname{Re}\mc T^{\textup{s}}|\le|\mc T^{\textup{s}}|$ and apply the two lemmas.

nodes.title: Passing to the limit $R\to\infty$
nodes.statement_html: Let $w_0,w_1,w_2:\R\to(0,\infty)$ be continuous, $A\ge0$, and let $(r_R)_{R\ge2}$ be real $C^2$ functions with $r_R\to r$ uniformly on $\R$ as $R\to\infty$. Suppose that for every $Y>0$ there is $R_1(Y)$ such that $|r_R^{(j)}(y)|\le Aw_j(y)$ for $j=0,1,2$, $|y|\le Y$, $R\ge R_1(Y)$. Then $r\in C^1(\R)$, $r'$ is locally Lipschitz (so $r\in W^{2,\infty}_{\mathrm{loc}}$), $|r|\le Aw_0$, $|r'|\le Aw_1$ everywhere and $|r''|\le Aw_2$ a.e.
nodes.proof_html:
Fix $Y$ and a sequence $R_n\to\infty$, $R_n\ge R_1(Y)$. On $[-Y,Y]$ the $r'_{R_n}$ are uniformly bounded and uniformly Lipschitz ($|r''_{R_n}|\le A\max w_2$),
  so by Arzel\`a--Ascoli a subsequence converges uniformly to some $g$. Passing to the limit in $r_{R}(y)-r_R(0)=\int_0^yr_R'$ gives $r(y)-r(0)=\int_0^yg$, so $r\in C^1$,
  $r'=g$ (the limit is thus independent of the subsequence). Pointwise limits give $|r|\le Aw_0$, $|r'|\le Aw_1$, and
  $|r'(y)-r'(x)|\le A|\int_x^yw_2|$; hence $r'$ is locally Lipschitz, differentiable a.e.\ (Rademacher/Lebesgue), and at every point of differentiability
  $|r''(x)|\le Aw_2(x)$ by continuity of $w_2$.

nodes.title: High-frequency estimate
nodes.statement_html: Let $\gamma$ be admissible ($\beta+\frac1p<\gamma<2p+1$). There is $C_{\textup{h}}(\gamma)$ such that for all $G\in\sq Y_\gamma$: $\mc T_{\textup{h}}G\in X_\gamma$ and $\|\mc T_{\textup{h}}G\|_{X_\gamma}\le C_{\textup{h}}(\gamma)\|G\|_{Y_\gamma}$.
nodes.proof_html: Apply lem:c09_truncation_limit to $r_R:=\mc T^R_{\textup{h}}G$ (real, $C^\infty$), $r:=\mc T_{\textup{h}}G$ (real, lem:c09_conjugate_symmetry), $w_j:=w_{\gamma,j}$, $A:=C\|G\|_{Y_\gamma}$ and $R_1(Y):=\max\{2,\ang Y^{1/p}\}\ge R_0(y)$ for $|y|\le Y$: uniform convergence is lem:c09_kernel_representation, the bounds are lem:c09_truncated_high_bound. Then lem:c09_weight_facts(1) gives $\|\mc T_{\textup{h}}G\|_{X_\gamma}\le6C\|G\|_{Y_\gamma}$. $\R$-linearity of $\mc T_{\textup{h}}$ is clear.

nodes.title: Boundedness of $\mc T_0$
nodes.section: Assembly: proof of the linear inverse theorem
nodes.statement_html: Let $\gamma$ be admissible. For $G\in\sq Y_\gamma$, the real function $r:=\mc T_{\textup{l}}G+\mc T_{\textup{h}}G$ lies in $X_\gamma$, satisfies $\widehat r=m_G$ (so $r$ represents $\mc T_0G$ in the sense of def:T_0) and $\|\mc T_0G\|_{X_\gamma}\le C_T(\gamma)\|G\|_{Y_\gamma}$ with $C_T(\gamma):=C_{\textup{l}}(\gamma)+C_{\textup{h}}(\gamma)$. The map $G\mapsto\mc T_0G$ is $\R$-linear and given by a formula independent of $\gamma$: if $\gamma\le\gamma'$ are admissible and $G\in\sq Y_{\gamma'}$ ($\subset\sq Y_\gamma$), $\mc T_0G$ is the same function.
nodes.proof_html: Admissible $\gamma$ satisfy $1<\gamma<p+2$ (since $2p+1<p+2$), so prop:linear_low_frequency gives $\mc T_{\textup{l}}G\in X_\gamma$ with $\|\mc T_{\textup{l}}G\|_{X_\gamma}\le C_{\textup{l}}(\gamma)\|G\|_{Y_\gamma}$, and prop:linear_high_frequency gives $\mc T_{\textup{h}}G\in X_\gamma$ with the bound $C_{\textup{h}}(\gamma)$. Both are $L^1$ functions (lem:c08_L1_embedding) whose Fourier transforms are $\chi m_G$ and $(1-\chi)m_G$ (def:c08_frequency_split, lem:c09_conjugate_symmetry), so $\widehat r=m_G$; uniqueness of $r$ is part of def:T_0 (injectivity of the Fourier transform). lem:c08_frequency_split_sum gives the norm bound. $\gamma$-independence: $m_G$, $\chi$, $\ell$ do not involve $\gamma$ (def:T_0, def:ell) and $Y_{\gamma'}\subset Y_\gamma$, $X_{\gamma'}\subset X_\gamma$.

nodes.title: Assembly of the linear inverse theorem
nodes.section: Assembly: proof of the linear inverse theorem
nodes.statement_html:
Let $\epsilon_0,\delta,\ov B$ be as in thm:fixed_point_approximation, where $\epsilon_0\le\epsilon_c$ with $\epsilon_c$ the threshold of lem:linear_conjugation. Then:
  • For every admissible $\gamma$, $\ell:Y_\gamma\to\C$ is well defined and continuous: there is $C_\ell(\gamma)$ with $|\ell(G)|\le C_\ell(\gamma)\|G\|_{Y_\gamma}$.
  • The $\R$-linear map $\mc T_0$ of def:T_0, defined on $\bigcup_{\gamma\text{ adm.}}\sq Y_\gamma$ with values in functions $\R\to\R$ and given by a formula independent of $\gamma$, satisfies for every admissible $\gamma$: $\mc T_0(\sq Y_\gamma)\subset X_\gamma$, $\|\mc T_0G\|_{X_\gamma}\le C_T(\gamma)\|G\|_{Y_\gamma}$ for $G\in\sq Y_\gamma$, and $\mc L_0(\mc T_0G)=G$ pointwise on $\R$ for $G\in\sq Y_\gamma$ (eqn:fixed_point_free_inverse).
  • For each $\epsilon\in[0,\epsilon_0]$ the maps $\mc U_\epsilon,\mc V_\epsilon$ of def:U_eps, def:V_eps ($\mc U_\epsilon r=r\circ\phi_\epsilon^{-1}$, $\mc V_\epsilon u=(\phi_\epsilon')^{p+1}\,u\circ\phi_\epsilon$; independent of $\gamma$) are $\R$-linear bijections of the space of all functions $\R\to\R$ such that for every admissible $\gamma$: $\mc U_\epsilon$ maps $X_\gamma$ bijectively onto $X_\gamma$, $\mc V_\epsilon$ maps $Y_\gamma$ bijectively onto $Y_\gamma$, there is $C_{UV}(\gamma)$ with $\|\mc U_\epsilon\|_{X_\gamma\to X_\gamma},\|\mc U^{-1}_\epsilon\|_{X_\gamma\to X_\gamma},\|\mc V_\epsilon\|_{Y_\gamma\to Y_\gamma},\|\mc V_\epsilon^{-1}\|_{Y_\gamma\to Y_\gamma}\le C_{UV}(\gamma)$ for $0\le\epsilon\le\epsilon_0$, and $\mc L_\epsilon r=\mc V_\epsilon(\mc L_0(\mc U_\epsilon r))$ for all $r\in X_\gamma$.
  • For every admissible $\gamma$ there is $C_G(\gamma)$ with $\sup_{\mu\in\ov B}\|(\mc V_\epsilon^{-1}-I)G_\mu\|_{Y_\gamma}\le C_G(\gamma)\epsilon$ for $0\le\epsilon\le\epsilon_0$ (eqn:fixed_point_residual_transport).
nodes.proof_html: This assembles the linear inverse theorem (paper lines 3295--3308) from the results above. (1) prop:linear_ell_continuity (existence of the improper limit of def:ell and $|\ell(G)|\le C\|G\|_{Y_\gamma}$), applicable as admissible $\gamma>\beta+\frac1p$. (2) Let $G\in\sq Y_\gamma$. By lem:c09_T0_bounded (which combines eqn:linear_frequency_split, prop:linear_low_frequency and prop:linear_high_frequency), $\mc T_0G$ is represented by $r\in X_\gamma$ with $\widehat r=m_G$, the bound holds, and $\mc T_0$ is $\gamma$-independent. Since admissible $\gamma>\beta+\frac1p>1+\frac1p$, lem:c08_T0_right_inverse applies and gives $\mc L_0r=G$ pointwise on $\R$. (This is the Fourier-side argument of lem:c08_T0_right_inverse.) (3) lem:linear_conjugation(1) (bijections of all functions, restriction to $X_\gamma$, $Y_\gamma$, uniform bounds with $C_{UV}(\gamma):=C(\gamma)$, $\gamma$-independence) and lem:linear_conjugation(3) (the identity $\mc V_\epsilon(\mc L_0(\mc U_\epsilon r))=\mc L_\epsilon r$ pointwise for $r\in X_\gamma$), valid for $\epsilon\le\epsilon_0\le\epsilon_c$. Here $\mc L_\epsilon$ is defined in def:L_eps with the $\mc R_\epsilon$ of def:R_eps, which is precisely the remainder produced by the conjugation. (4) lem:linear_conjugation(5) with the $\delta$ of thm:fixed_point_approximation: $C_G(\gamma):=C(\gamma)\delta/|\mu_*|$, uniformly in $\mu\in\ov B$. (The uniformity in $\mu$ comes from $G_\mu=\operatorname{Re}z\,G_++\operatorname{Im}z\,G_-$, $|z|\le\delta/|\mu_*|$.)

nodes.title: The three nonlinear pieces
nodes.section: Standing notation and the decomposition of the nonlinearity
nodes.statement_html: Let $0\le\epsilon\le1$, let $\ov f\in C^2(\R)$ with $\ov f'\in L^\infty(\R)$, and let $r\in X_\gamma$ (for some $\gamma>1/p$, so that $r'\in L^\infty$). Define the functions $\mc N_1(r)=\mc N_1^{\epsilon,\ov f}(r)$, $\mc N_2(r)$, $\mc N_3(r)$ on $\R$ by (paper eq:nonlinear\_decomposition) \begin{align*} \mc N_1(r) &= \bigl(B_\epsilon(\ov f'+r')-B_\epsilon(\ov f')\bigr)\bigl(\ov f-y\ov f'\bigr),\\ \mc N_2(r) &= \bigl(B_\epsilon(\ov f'+r')-1\bigr)\bigl(r-yr'\bigr),\\ \mc N_3(r) &= \mc I_\epsilon(\ov f+r)-\mc I_\epsilon(\ov f)-b_\epsilon r'. \end{align*} Note that $\mc N_j(0)=0$ for $j=1,2,3$.

nodes.title: Decomposition of $\mc N_{\epsilon,\ov f}$
nodes.section: Standing notation and the decomposition of the nonlinearity
nodes.statement_html: Let $\beta+\frac1p<\gamma<2p+1$, let $0\le\epsilon\le\min\{1,\epsilon_0\}$ where $\epsilon_0$ is the constant of lem:linear_conjugation (so that $\mc R_\epsilon$ of def:R_eps is defined), let $\ov f\in C^2(\R)$ with $\ov f'\in L^\infty(\R)$ and $\ov f''\in L^\infty_{\mathrm{loc}}$, and such that $|D|^p\ov f'$ is defined in the sense of def:frac_multiplier; let $r\in X_\gamma$. Then $\mc E_\epsilon(\ov f+r)$ and $\mc E_\epsilon(\ov f)$ are defined, and for every $y\in\R$ \[ \mc N_{\epsilon,\ov f}(r) =\mc E_\epsilon(\ov f+r)-\mc E_\epsilon(\ov f)-\mc L_\epsilon r =\mc N_1(r)+\mc N_2(r)+\mc N_3(r)-\mc R_\epsilon r . \] In particular $\mc N_{\epsilon,\ov f}(0)=0$.
nodes.proof_html:
Put $f=\ov f+r$; then $f\in W^{2,\infty}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ and $f'\in L^\infty$, so prop:analysis_semilinear_kernel applies to both $f$ and $\ov f$: \[ \mc E_\epsilon(g)=|D|^pg'+B_\epsilon(g')(g-yg')+\mc I_\epsilon(g),\qquad g\in\{\ov f,\ov f+r\}. \] Step 1 (fractional term). By linearity of $|D|^p$ on the class of def:frac_multiplier (which contains $\ov f'$ and $r'$; note $r'\in L^1\cap L^\infty$ since admissibility gives $\gamma>\beta+1/p>1+1/p$), $|D|^p(\ov f'+r')-|D|^p\ov f'=|D|^pr'$.

Step 2 (local term). Adding and subtracting $B_\epsilon(\ov f'+r')(\ov f-y\ov f')$, \[ B_\epsilon(\ov f'+r')(\ov f+r-y\ov f'-yr')-B_\epsilon(\ov f')(\ov f-y\ov f') =\mc N_1(r)+B_\epsilon(\ov f'+r')(r-yr') =\mc N_1(r)+\mc N_2(r)+(r-yr'). \]

Step 3 (nonlocal term). By definition, $\mc I_\epsilon(\ov f+r)-\mc I_\epsilon(\ov f)=\mc N_3(r)+b_\epsilon r'$.

Step 4 (subtracting $\mc L_\epsilon$). By def:L_eps, $\mc L_\epsilon r=|D|^pr'+r-yr'+c_\epsilon\chi_+y^{-p}r'+\mc R_\epsilon r$, and by lem:analysis_coefficient $c_\epsilon\chi_+y^{-p}=b_\epsilon$. Summing Steps 1--3 and subtracting: the terms $|D|^pr'$, $r-yr'$ and $b_\epsilon r'$ cancel exactly, leaving $\mc N_1(r)+\mc N_2(r)+\mc N_3(r)-\mc R_\epsilon r$.

Since $\mc N_j(0)=0$ and $\mc R_\epsilon0=0$, $\mc N_{\epsilon,\ov f}(0)=0$.

nodes.title: Admissible profile
nodes.statement_html: Let $M>0$. A function $\ov f\in C^2(\R;\R)$ is an admissible profile with constant $M$ if for all $y\ge0$ \[ |\ov f(y)|\le M\ang{y}^{-p},\qquad |\ov f'(y)|\le M\ang{y}^{-\beta},\qquad |\ov f''(y)|\le M\ang{y}^{-\beta+1/p}, \] and for all $y\le0$ \[ |\ov f(y)+y|\le M\ang{y}^{-p},\qquad |\ov f'(y)+1|\le M\ang{y}^{-p-1},\qquad |\ov f''(y)|\le M\ang{y}^{-p-2}. \]

nodes.title: Admissibility is closed under $C^2_{\mathrm{loc}}$ limits
nodes.statement_html: If $\ov f_k$ are admissible with constant $M$ and $\ov f_k\to\ov f$ in $C^2_{\mathrm{loc}}(\R)$, then $\ov f$ is admissible with constant $M$.
nodes.proof_html:
Each of the six defining inequalities is a pointwise inequality between $\ov f_k^{(j)}(y)$ (or
  $\ov f_k(y)+y$, $\ov f_k'(y)+1$) and a fixed function of $y$; pass to the pointwise limit $k\to\infty$.

nodes.title: Approximate profiles are admissible
nodes.statement_html: There is $M_0>0$ such that for all $0\le\epsilon\le\epsilon_0$ and $\mu\in\ov B(\mu_*,\delta)$ (the parameters of thm:fixed_point_approximation), $\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu}$ is an admissible profile with constant $M_0$.
nodes.proof_html: $\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu}$ is $C^\infty$. prop:approx_profile_bounds gives, uniformly in $\epsilon,\mu$, $|\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu}|\le C\ang{y}^{-p}$ and $|\p^j\ov f'_{\epsilon,\mu}|\le C_j\ang{y}^{-\beta+j/p}$ ($j=0,1$) for $y\ge0$, and $|\p^j(\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu}+y)|\le C_j\ang{y}^{-p-j}$ ($j=0,1,2$) for $y\le0$. Take $M_0=\max\{C,C_0,C_1,C_2\}$.

nodes.title: Consequences of admissibility and of $X_\gamma$ membership
nodes.statement_html:
Let $\beta+\frac1p<\gamma<2p+1$, $M,N>0$, $\ov f$ admissible with constant $M$, $r\in X_\gamma$ with $\|r\|_{X_\gamma}\le N$, and $f=\ov f+r$. There is $C=C(p,\gamma,M,N)$ such that:
  • $\|f'\|_{L^\infty(\R)}\le C$, $\|f\|_{L^\infty([-3,3])}+\|f''\|_{L^\infty([-3,3])}\le C$, and $|f(y)-W(y)|\le C\ang{y}^{-p}$ for all $y$; the same holds with $f$ replaced by $\ov f$.
  • For $y\ge0$: $|f'(y)|\le C\ang{y}^{-\beta}$ and $|f''(y)|\le C\ang{y}^{-\beta+1/p}$.
  • For $y\le0$: $|f'(y)+1|\le C\ang{y}^{-p-1}$ and $|f''(y)|\le C\ang{y}^{-p-2}$.
  • For every $h\in X_\gamma$: $\|h\|_{L^\infty}\le\|h\|_{X_\gamma}$, $\|h\|_{L^1}\le C_\gamma\|h\|_{X_\gamma}$ with $C_\gamma=\int_\R\ang{z}^{-\gamma}dz<\infty$, and \[ |h'(y)|\le\|h\|_{X_\gamma}\begin{cases}\ang{y}^{-\gamma+1/p},&y\ge0\\ \ang{y}^{-\gamma-1},&y\le0\end{cases}, \qquad |h''(y)|\le\|h\|_{X_\gamma}\begin{cases}\ang{y}^{-\gamma+2/p},&y\ge0\\ \ang{y}^{-\gamma-2},&y\le0.\end{cases} \] In particular $\|h'\|_{L^\infty}\le\|h\|_{X_\gamma}$ and $\|h''\|_{L^\infty([-3,3])}\le 10^{2/p}\|h\|_{X_\gamma}$.
nodes.proof_html: Item 4 is read off from the definition of $\|\cdot\|_{X_\gamma}$; $C_\gamma<\infty$ as $\gamma>1$; and $\ang{y}^{-\gamma+1/p}\le1$ as $\gamma>1/p$. For items 1--3 combine the admissible bounds with item 4 for $h=r$, using: for $y\ge0$, $\ang{y}^{-\gamma}\le\ang{y}^{-p}$ ($\gamma>p$), $\ang{y}^{-\gamma+1/p}\le\ang{y}^{-\beta}$ ($\gamma-1/p>\beta$), $\ang{y}^{-\gamma+2/p}\le\ang{y}^{-\beta+1/p}$; for $y\le0$, $\ang{y}^{-\gamma-j}\le\ang{y}^{-p-j}$. For $y\ge0$, $f-W=f$; for $y\le0$, $f-W=f+y$ and $|f'|\le 1+|f'+1|$. On $[-3,3]$ all weights are bounded by $10^{2/p}$.

nodes.title: Transport-factor bounds
nodes.statement_html: Let $\beta+\frac1p<\gamma<2p+1$ and $\ov f$ admissible with constant $M$. There is $C=C(p,M)$ such that (paper eq:N1\_profile\_factor, eq:N1\_profile\_factor\_derivative) \[ |\ov f-y\ov f'|\le C\begin{cases}\ang{y}^{1-\beta},&y\ge0\\\ang{y}^{-p},&y\le0\end{cases},\qquad |\p_y(\ov f-y\ov f')|=|y\ov f''|\le C\begin{cases}\ang{y}^{1-\beta+1/p},&y\ge0\\\ang{y}^{-p-1},&y\le0,\end{cases} \] and for every $r\in X_\gamma$ and a.e.\ $y$ (paper eq:N2\_transport\_bound, eq:N2\_transport\_derivative\_bound) \[ |r-yr'|\le 2\|r\|_{X_\gamma}\begin{cases}\ang{y}^{1-\gamma+1/p},&y\ge0\\\ang{y}^{-\gamma},&y\le0\end{cases},\qquad |\p_y(r-yr')|=|yr''|\le \|r\|_{X_\gamma}\begin{cases}\ang{y}^{1-\gamma+2/p},&y\ge0\\\ang{y}^{-\gamma-1},&y\le0.\end{cases} \]
nodes.proof_html:
Use $|y|\le\ang{y}$. For $y\ge0$: $|\ov f|\le M\ang{y}^{-p}\le M\ang{y}^{1-\beta}$ because
  $1-\beta=\frac{p-1}{2p}>-p$; $|y\ov f'|\le M\ang{y}^{1-\beta}$; $|y\ov f''|\le M\ang{y}^{1-\beta+1/p}$.
  For $y\le0$ write $\ov f-y\ov f'=(\ov f+y)-y(\ov f'+1)$, so $|\ov f-y\ov f'|\le 2M\ang{y}^{-p}$, and
  $|y\ov f''|\le M\ang{y}^{-p-1}$. For $r$: $|r|\le\|r\|\ang{y}^{-\gamma}\le\|r\|\ang{y}^{1-\gamma+1/p}$ and
  $|yr'|\le\|r\|\ang{y}^{1-\gamma+1/p}$ for $y\ge0$; $|r|+|yr'|\le 2\|r\|\ang{y}^{-\gamma}$ for $y\le0$;
  similarly for $yr''$. The identity $\p_y(g-yg')=-yg''$ holds a.e.\ for $g\in W^{2,\infty}_{\mathrm{loc}}$.

nodes.title: Elementary bounds for $B_\epsilon$
nodes.statement_html: Let $0\le\epsilon\le1$, $R>0$, and $B_\epsilon(u)=(1+\epsilon u^2)^{\alpha/2}$ with $\alpha=p+1\in(1,2)$. Then for all $|u|\le R$: \[ |B_\epsilon(u)-1|\le \tfrac{\alpha}{2}\epsilon u^2,\qquad |B_\epsilon'(u)|\le \alpha\epsilon|u|,\qquad |B_\epsilon''(u)|\le \alpha(1+R^2)\epsilon . \]
nodes.proof_html:
$B_\epsilon'(u)=\alpha\epsilon u(1+\epsilon u^2)^{\alpha/2-1}$ and, since $\alpha/2-1<0$,
  $(1+\epsilon u^2)^{\alpha/2-1}\le1$, giving the second bound. Then
  $B_\epsilon(u)-1=\int_0^1B_\epsilon'(tu)u\,dt$ gives the first. Finally
  $B_\epsilon''(u)=\alpha\epsilon(1+\epsilon u^2)^{\alpha/2-1}+\alpha(\alpha-2)\epsilon^2u^2(1+\epsilon u^2)^{\alpha/2-2}$,
  so $|B_\epsilon''|\le\alpha\epsilon+\alpha(2-\alpha)\epsilon^2R^2\le\alpha(1+R^2)\epsilon$.

nodes.title: Difference of the $B_\epsilon$ coefficients
nodes.section: The local pieces $\mc N_1$ and $\mc N_2$
nodes.statement_html: Let $0\le\epsilon\le1$, $\beta+\frac1p<\gamma<2p+1$, $\ov f$ admissible with constant $M$, and $r_1,r_2\in X_\gamma$ with $\|r_j\|_{X_\gamma}\le N$. Let $\Delta B_\epsilon=B_\epsilon(\ov f'+r_1')-B_\epsilon(\ov f'+r_2')$ (paper eq:N1\_delta\_B). Then $\Delta B_\epsilon\in W^{1,\infty}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ and there is $C=C(p,\gamma,M,N)$ such that for a.e.\ $y$ (paper eq:N1\_delta\_B\_bound, eq:N1\_delta\_B\_derivative\_bound) \[ |\Delta B_\epsilon(y)|\le C\epsilon\|r_1-r_2\|_{X_\gamma}\begin{cases}\ang{y}^{-\beta-\gamma+1/p},&y\ge0\\\ang{y}^{-\gamma-1},&y\le0\end{cases}, \quad |\p_y\Delta B_\epsilon(y)|\le C\epsilon\|r_1-r_2\|_{X_\gamma}\begin{cases}\ang{y}^{-\beta-\gamma+2/p},&y\ge0\\\ang{y}^{-\gamma-2},&y\le0.\end{cases} \]
nodes.proof_html:
Let $R=M+1+N$; by lem:c10_profile_consequences $|\ov f'+r_j'|\le R$ and $|\ov f''+r_j''|$ obeys the bounds of items 2--3 there. Set $u_j=\ov f'+r_j'$ and $\delta=r_1-r_2$.

Value: by the mean value theorem, $|\Delta B_\epsilon|\le\sup_{t\in[0,1]}|B_\epsilon'(u_2+t(u_1-u_2))|\,|\delta'| \le\alpha\epsilon(|\ov f'|+|r_1'|+|r_2'|)|\delta'|$ by lem:c10_B_bounds. For $y\ge0$, $|\ov f'|+|r_1'|+|r_2'|\le C\ang{y}^{-\beta}$ and $|\delta'|\le\|\delta\|\ang{y}^{-\gamma+1/p}$; for $y\le0$, $|\ov f'|+|r_j'|\le C$ and $|\delta'|\le\|\delta\|\ang{y}^{-\gamma-1}$.

Derivative: $B_\epsilon\circ u_j$ is the composition of a smooth function with a $W^{1,\infty}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ function, so it is in $W^{1,\infty}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ with derivative $B_\epsilon'(u_j)u_j'$ a.e.; hence \[ \p_y\Delta B_\epsilon=B_\epsilon'(u_1)\delta''+\bigl[B_\epsilon'(u_1)-B_\epsilon'(u_2)\bigr](\ov f''+r_2''). \] The first term is bounded by $\alpha\epsilon(|\ov f'|+|r_1'|)|\delta''|$; the second by $\alpha(1+R^2)\epsilon|\delta'|(|\ov f''|+|r_2''|)$. For $y\ge0$: $\ang{y}^{-\beta}\ang{y}^{-\gamma+2/p}$ and $\ang{y}^{-\gamma+1/p}\ang{y}^{-\beta+1/p}$, both $=\ang{y}^{-\beta-\gamma+2/p}$. For $y\le0$: $\ang{y}^{-\gamma-2}$ and $\ang{y}^{-\gamma-1}\ang{y}^{-p-2}\le\ang{y}^{-\gamma-2}$.

nodes.title: Lipschitz bound for $\mc N_1$
nodes.section: The local pieces $\mc N_1$ and $\mc N_2$
nodes.statement_html: Let $0\le\epsilon\le1$, $\beta+\frac1p<\gamma<2p+1$, $M,N>0$, $\ov f$ admissible with constant $M$, and $r_1,r_2\in X_\gamma$ with $\|r_1\|_{X_\gamma},\|r_2\|_{X_\gamma}\le N$. Then $\mc N_1(r_1)-\mc N_1(r_2)\in Y_\gamma$ and there is $C=C(p,\gamma,M,N)$ (independent of $\epsilon$ and $\ov f$) with \[ \|\mc N_1(r_1)-\mc N_1(r_2)\|_{Y_\gamma}\le C\epsilon\|r_1-r_2\|_{X_\gamma}. \]
nodes.proof_html: $\mc N_1(r_1)-\mc N_1(r_2)=\Delta B_\epsilon\,(\ov f-y\ov f')$, a product of $W^{1,\infty}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ functions. By the product rule and lem:c10_delta_B, lem:c10_transport_factors, using $2\beta=1+1/p$: for $y\ge0$, $|\cdot|\le C\epsilon\|\delta\|\ang{y}^{-\beta-\gamma+1/p+1-\beta}=C\epsilon\|\delta\|\ang{y}^{-\gamma}$ and $|\p_y\cdot|\le C\epsilon\|\delta\|(\ang{y}^{-\beta-\gamma+2/p+1-\beta}+\ang{y}^{-\beta-\gamma+1/p+1-\beta+1/p}) =2C\epsilon\|\delta\|\ang{y}^{-\gamma+1/p}$; for $y\le0$, $|\cdot|\le C\epsilon\|\delta\|\ang{y}^{-\gamma-1-p}$ and $|\p_y\cdot|\le 2C\epsilon\|\delta\|\ang{y}^{-\gamma-p-2}$. Multiplying by the weights of def:Y_gamma ($\ang{y}^\gamma$, resp.\ $\ang{y}^{\gamma-1/p}$ for the derivative on $y\ge0$ and $\ang{y}^{\gamma+1}$ on $y\le0$) and taking suprema gives the claim.

nodes.title: Coefficient bounds for $\mc N_2$
nodes.section: The local pieces $\mc N_1$ and $\mc N_2$
nodes.statement_html: Under the hypotheses of lem:c10_delta_B, for $j=1,2$ and a.e.\ $y$ (paper eq:N2\_coefficient\_bound, eq:N2\_coefficient\_derivative\_bound) \[ |B_\epsilon(\ov f'+r_j')-1|\le C\epsilon\begin{cases}\ang{y}^{-2\beta},&y\ge0\\1,&y\le0\end{cases},\qquad |\p_y(B_\epsilon(\ov f'+r_j')-1)|\le C\epsilon\begin{cases}\ang{y}^{-2\beta+1/p},&y\ge0\\\ang{y}^{-p-2},&y\le0,\end{cases} \] with $C=C(p,\gamma,M,N)$.
nodes.proof_html: By lem:c10_B_bounds, $|B_\epsilon(u_j)-1|\le\frac\alpha2\epsilon u_j^2$ and $|\p_yB_\epsilon(u_j)|=|B_\epsilon'(u_j)u_j'|\le\alpha\epsilon|u_j||\ov f''+r_j''|$. Insert the bounds of lem:c10_profile_consequences: for $y\ge0$, $|u_j|\le C\ang{y}^{-\beta}$, $|u_j'|\le C\ang{y}^{-\beta+1/p}$; for $y\le0$, $|u_j|\le C$, $|u_j'|\le C\ang{y}^{-p-2}$.

nodes.title: Lipschitz bound for $\mc N_2$
nodes.section: The local pieces $\mc N_1$ and $\mc N_2$
nodes.statement_html: Under the hypotheses of lem:N1, $\mc N_2(r_1)-\mc N_2(r_2)\in Y_\gamma$ and there is $C=C(p,\gamma,M,N)$ with \[ \|\mc N_2(r_1)-\mc N_2(r_2)\|_{Y_\gamma}\le C\epsilon\|r_1-r_2\|_{X_\gamma}. \]
nodes.proof_html:
With $\delta=r_1-r_2$, \[ \mc N_2(r_1)-\mc N_2(r_2)=\bigl(B_\epsilon(\ov f'+r_1')-1\bigr)(\delta-y\delta')+\Delta B_\epsilon\,(r_2-yr_2'). \] Apply the product rule and lem:c10_N2_coefficient, lem:c10_delta_B, lem:c10_transport_factors (the latter with $r=\delta$ and $r=r_2$, $\|r_2\|\le N$).

$y\ge0$, value: $\ang{y}^{-2\beta}\ang{y}^{1-\gamma+1/p}=\ang{y}^{-\gamma}$ (as $2\beta=1+1/p$), and $\ang{y}^{-\beta-\gamma+1/p}\ang{y}^{1-\gamma+1/p}=\ang{y}^{-\gamma}\ang{y}^{1-\beta-\gamma+2/p}\le\ang{y}^{-\gamma}$, since $1-\beta+2/p=\beta+1/p<\gamma$ (again by $2\beta=1+1/p$). $y\ge0$, derivative: the four terms are $\ang{y}^{-2\beta+1/p}\ang{y}^{1-\gamma+1/p}$, $\ang{y}^{-2\beta}\ang{y}^{1-\gamma+2/p}$ (both $=\ang{y}^{-\gamma+1/p}$), and $\ang{y}^{-\beta-\gamma+2/p}\ang{y}^{1-\gamma+1/p}$, $\ang{y}^{-\beta-\gamma+1/p}\ang{y}^{1-\gamma+2/p}$ (both $=\ang{y}^{-\gamma+1/p}\ang{y}^{1-\beta-\gamma+2/p}\le\ang{y}^{-\gamma+1/p}$).

$y\le0$, value: $1\cdot\ang{y}^{-\gamma}$ and $\ang{y}^{-\gamma-1}\ang{y}^{-\gamma}$, both $\le\ang{y}^{-\gamma}$. $y\le0$, derivative: $\ang{y}^{-p-2}\ang{y}^{-\gamma}$, $1\cdot\ang{y}^{-\gamma-1}$, $\ang{y}^{-\gamma-2}\ang{y}^{-\gamma}$, $\ang{y}^{-\gamma-1}\ang{y}^{-\gamma-1}$, all $\le\ang{y}^{-\gamma-1}$.

Each bound carries the factor $C\epsilon\|\delta\|_{X_\gamma}$. Multiplying by the $Y_\gamma$ weights gives the claim.

nodes.title: Linearization of $\mc N_3$
nodes.statement_html: Let $0\le\epsilon\le1$, $\ov f$ as in def:c10_N_pieces, $r,h\in X_\gamma$ ($\gamma>1/p$), and $f=\ov f+r$. For $y\ne z$ set (paper eq:N3\_integrand) \[ K_{f,h}(y,z)=\p_1\Gamma_\epsilon(f'(y),S_f(y,z))\,h'(y)+\p_2\Gamma_\epsilon(f'(y),S_f(y,z))\,S_h(y,z), \] and define (paper eq:N3\_variation) \[ D\mc N_3(r)[h](y)=\int_\R\frac{K_{f,h}(y,z)}{|y-z|^\alpha}\,dz-b_\epsilon(y)h'(y). \] The displayed formula for $K_{f,h}$ also applies to arbitrary $f,h\in W^{2,\infty}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\R)$ with bounded first derivatives; the weighted-space assumptions are only needed when estimating the resulting operator in $Y_\gamma$.

nodes.title: Secant identities
nodes.statement_html: Let $g\in W^{2,\infty}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\R)$ and $y\ne z$. Then $S_g(y,z)=\int_0^1g'(z+t(y-z))\,dt$; $y\mapsto S_g(y,z)$ is $C^1$ on $\R\setminus\{z\}$ with (paper eq:N3\_secant\_derivatives) \[ \p_yS_g(y,z)=\frac{g'(y)-S_g(y,z)}{y-z}; \] and, writing $I_{y,z}$ for the closed segment between $y$ and $z$, \[ |g'(y)-S_g(y,z)|\le|y-z|\,\|g''\|_{L^\infty(I_{y,z})},\quad |\p_yS_g(y,z)|\le\|g''\|_{L^\infty(I_{y,z})},\quad |\p_yS_g(y,z)|\le\frac{2\|g'\|_{L^\infty}}{|y-z|}, \] \[ |S_g(y,z)|\le\min\Bigl\{\|g'\|_{L^\infty},\ \frac{|g(y)|+|g(z)|}{|y-z|}\Bigr\}. \]
nodes.proof_html:
Fundamental theorem of calculus for the absolutely continuous $g$ and $g'$. For the second bound:
  $g'(y)-S_g(y,z)=\int_0^1(g'(y)-g'(z+t(y-z)))dt$ and $|g'(y)-g'(w)|\le|y-w|\|g''\|_{L^\infty(I_{y,z})}$,
  giving in fact $\frac12|y-z|\|g''\|$. The quotient rule gives $\p_yS_g$.

nodes.title: A dominated pair of value and derivative kernels
nodes.statement_html:
Let $1<\alpha<2$, let $U\subset\R$ be a nonempty open interval, and let $A\ge0$. For $s\ne0$ put \[ \omega_0(s)=\frac{\min\{|s|^2,1\}}{|s|^\alpha},\qquad \omega_1(s)=\frac{\min\{|s|,1\}}{|s|^\alpha}, \] and put $\omega_0(0)=\omega_1(0)=0$. A pair of Borel measurable functions $H,J:\R^2\to\R$ is a dominated kernel pair on $U$ with constant $A$ if:
  • $H(y,y)=J(y,y)=0$ for every $y\in U$;
  • for each fixed $z$, $H(\cdot,z)$ is locally Lipschitz on $U\setminus\{z\}$ and $\p_y H(y,z)=J(y,z)$ for a.e.\ $y\in U\setminus\{z\}$;
  • $|H(y,z)|\le A\omega_0(y-z)$ for all $y\in U$ and $z\ne y$;
  • there is a null set $E\subset U$ such that $|J(y,z)|\le A\omega_1(y-z)$ for every $y\in U\setminus E$ and every $z\ne y$.
Here local Lipschitz regularity is for the actual pointwise representative, and the null set in (4) is independent of $z$.

nodes.title: Integrability and exact integrals of the kernel envelopes
nodes.statement_html: For every $1<\alpha<2$, the functions $\omega_0,\omega_1$ of def:c10_local_kernel_pair are nonnegative, Borel measurable, and integrable on $\R$, with \[ \int_\R\omega_0(s)ds=\frac2{3-\alpha}+\frac2{\alpha-1},\qquad \int_\R\omega_1(s)ds=\frac2{2-\alpha}+\frac2{\alpha-1}. \] For every $0<r\le1$ one also has $\int_{|s|<r}\omega_0(s)ds=2r^{3-\alpha}/(3-\alpha)$ and $\int_{|s|<r}\omega_1(s)ds=2r^{2-\alpha}/(2-\alpha)$.
nodes.proof_html:
Both functions are even. On $(0,1)$ they equal respectively $s^{2-\alpha}$ and
  $s^{1-\alpha}$, whose exponents exceed $-1$; on $(1,\infty)$ both equal $s^{-\alpha}$,
  whose exponent is less than $-1$. Split at $1$, integrate the powers, and use symmetry.
  The value at $0$ does not affect the integrals. The same computation on $(0,r)$ gives the
  truncated formulas; nonnegativity and Borel measurability follow directly from the definitions.

nodes.title: Weak derivative of a fixed-$z$ truncation
nodes.statement_html: Let $(H,J)$ be a dominated kernel pair on $U$ with constant $A$ and exponent $1<\alpha<2$. Fix $\vartheta\in C^\infty(\R;[0,1])$ with $\vartheta=0$ on $[-1,1]$ and $\vartheta=1$ on $\R\setminus(-2,2)$, and put $M_\vartheta=\|\vartheta'\|_\infty$. For $0<\eta<1/2$ define \[ F_\eta(y)=\int_\R\vartheta((y-z)/\eta)H(y,z)\,dz, \quad G_\eta(y)=\int_\R\left[\vartheta((y-z)/\eta)J(y,z) +\eta^{-1}\vartheta'((y-z)/\eta)H(y,z)\right]dz. \] The value integral is absolutely convergent for every $y\in U$, and both summands defining $G_\eta$ are absolutely integrable for a.e.\ $y\in U$. The actual function $F_\eta$ is locally Lipschitz on $U$, $F_\eta'=G_\eta$ a.e.\ there, and \[ \|G_\eta\|_{L^\infty(U)}\le A\left(\frac2{2-\alpha}+\frac2{\alpha-1} +\frac{2^{4-\alpha}M_\vartheta}{3-\alpha}\eta^{2-\alpha}\right). \] In particular, for every $a<b$ with $[a,b]\subset U$, $F_\eta(b)-F_\eta(a)=\int_a^bG_\eta(y)\,dy$.
nodes.proof_html: For each $z$, multiply $H(\cdot,z)$ by the cutoff. This product vanishes near $y=z$, so it is locally Lipschitz on all of $U$. Its derivative is the displayed sum, with $z$ held fixed. Apply the one-dimensional fundamental theorem on $[a,b]$ and then Fubini. Its hypotheses follow from Tonelli applied to the translated $L^1$ envelopes and the finite length of $[a,b]$. The cutoff derivative is supported where $\eta\le|y-z|\le2\eta$ and has integral at most $2AM_\vartheta\eta^{-1}\int_0^{2\eta}s^{2-\alpha}ds$. The resulting increment identity and the displayed $L^\infty$ bound prove local Lipschitz regularity and identify the a.e.\ derivative.

nodes.title: Quantitative removal of the diagonal cutoff
nodes.statement_html: With exactly the kernel and cutoff hypotheses of lem:c10_cutoff_weak_derivative, let $F(y)=\int H(y,z)dz$ and $G(y)=\int J(y,z)dz$. The first integral converges absolutely for every $y\in U$ and the second for a.e.\ $y\in U$. For every $0<\eta<1/2$, \[ \sup_{y\in U}|F_\eta(y)-F(y)| \le\frac{2^{4-\alpha}}{3-\alpha}A\eta^{3-\alpha}, \] \[ \|G_\eta-G\|_{L^\infty(U)} \le A\left(\frac{2^{3-\alpha}}{2-\alpha} +\frac{2^{4-\alpha}M_\vartheta}{3-\alpha}\right)\eta^{2-\alpha}. \] The constants are independent of $U,A,H,J,\eta$ apart from the displayed factors.
nodes.proof_html: The omitted value and derivative kernels are supported on $|y-z|<2\eta<1$. Integrate respectively $A|y-z|^{2-\alpha}$ and $A|y-z|^{1-\alpha}$ there. Add the cutoff-derivative estimate from lem:c10_cutoff_weak_derivative for $G_\eta-G$. All estimates for $J$ are taken outside its fixed exceptional null set.

nodes.title: Local Lipschitz limit from convergence of derivatives
nodes.statement_html: Let $U\subset\R$ be an open interval. Let $F_n:U\to\R$ be locally Lipschitz, let $G_n,G\in L^\infty_{\mathrm{loc}}(U)$ be measurable representatives, and suppose $F_n'=G_n$ a.e.\ on $U$. If $F_n\to F$ locally uniformly on $U$ and $\|G_n-G\|_{L^\infty(I)}\to0$ for every compact interval $I\subset U$, then the actual function $F$ is locally Lipschitz, $F'=G$ a.e.\ on $U$, and for every $a<b$ with $[a,b]\subset U$, \[ F(b)-F(a)=\int_a^bG(y)dy,\qquad |F(b)-F(a)|\le\|G\|_{L^\infty([a,b])}|b-a|. \]
nodes.proof_html:
Pass to the limit in $F_n(b)-F_n(a)=\int_a^bG_n$; the integral error is bounded by
  $|b-a|\|G_n-G\|_{L^\infty([a,b])}$. The increment estimate proves local Lipschitz regularity.
  On each compact subinterval, $F$ differs by a constant from a primitive of $G$; the fundamental
  theorem for integrable functions gives the a.e.\ derivative. Exhaust $U$ by countably many
  compact subintervals to obtain a single null set.

nodes.title: Local domination for the linearized kernel
nodes.statement_html: Let $0<p<1$, $\alpha=1+p$, and $B,L\ge1$. There exists $C=C(p,B,L)>0$ such that for every $R\ge1$, $0\le\epsilon\le1$, $H_0\ge0$, and $f,h\in W^{2,\infty}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\R)$ satisfying \[ \|f'\|_{L^\infty(\R)}\le B,\quad \|h'\|_{L^\infty(\R)}\le H_0,\quad \|f''\|_{L^\infty([-R-2,R+2])}\le L,\quad \|h''\|_{L^\infty([-R-2,R+2])}\le H_0, \] the functions, set to zero on $y=z$, \[ H(y,z)=\frac{K_{f,h}(y,z)}{|y-z|^\alpha},\qquad J(y,z)=\frac{\p_yK_{f,h}(y,z)-\alpha K_{f,h}(y,z)/(y-z)}{|y-z|^\alpha}, \] form a dominated kernel pair on $U=(-R,R)$ with constant $C\epsilon H_0$. Here $J$ is defined by the Borel chain-rule expression using the classical $f^{\prime\prime}$ and $h^{\prime\prime}$ where they exist and zero otherwise; its values on the common exceptional null set of $y$ may be set to zero for every $z$. More explicitly, for every $y\in U,z\ne y$, $|K_{f,h}(y,z)|\le C\epsilon H_0\min\{|y-z|^2,1\}$, and for a.e.\ $y\in U$, simultaneously for all $z\ne y$, \[ |\p_yK_{f,h}(y,z)|+\alpha|K_{f,h}(y,z)|/|y-z| \le C\epsilon H_0\min\{|y-z|,1\}. \]
nodes.proof_html: Write $K=(\p_1+\p_2)\Gamma_\epsilon h'+\p_2\Gamma_\epsilon(S_h-h')$. For $|y-z|\le1$, use $|f'(y)-S_f|\le L|y-z|$ and $|h'(y)-S_h|\le H_0|y-z|$; the diagonal bounds give the quadratic vanishing of $K$. Differentiate this decomposition with $z$ fixed. The diagonal bounds on $(\p_1+\p_2)\nabla\Gamma_\epsilon$ give one factor $|y-z|$ in each derivative term. For $|y-z|\ge1$, use the global first-derivative bounds and the secant quotient rule. The common null set consists of the exceptional sets for $f''$ and $h''$ and their local bounds. Off $y=z$ the kernel is a composition of locally Lipschitz functions; its a.e.\ derivative has the stated Borel chain-rule expression. Increase $C$ once to dominate both envelopes.

nodes.title: Local domination for the profile kernel
nodes.statement_html: Let $0<p<1$, $\alpha=1+p$, and $B,L\ge1$. There exists $C=C(p,B,L)>0$ such that for every $R\ge1$, $0\le\epsilon\le1$, and $g\in W^{2,\infty}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\R)$ with $\|g'\|_{L^\infty(\R)}\le B$ and $\|g''\|_{L^\infty([-R-2,R+2])}\le L$, the pair \[ H_g(y,z)=\frac{\Gamma_\epsilon(g'(y),S_g(y,z))}{|y-z|^\alpha}, \] \[ J_g(y,z)=\frac{1}{|y-z|^\alpha}\left[ \p_1\Gamma_\epsilon(g'(y),S_g)g''(y) +\p_2\Gamma_\epsilon(g'(y),S_g)\frac{g'(y)-S_g}{y-z} -\alpha\frac{\Gamma_\epsilon(g'(y),S_g)}{y-z}\right], \] with diagonal values zero and $g^{\prime\prime}$ taken to be the classical derivative where it exists and zero otherwise, is a dominated kernel pair on $(-R,R)$ with constant $C\epsilon$. For the value numerator the bound is pointwise; for the derivative numerator it holds outside a null set of $y$ independent of $z$. These envelope inequalities hold also for $|y|\le R$, pointwise for $H_g$ and a.e.\ for $J_g$. The same conclusion on $(-R,R)$ holds with the local second-derivative hypothesis only on $[-2R,2R]$, provided $R\ge1$, by using $|y-z|\le1$ in the near region.
nodes.proof_html: Use $|g'(y)-S_g|\le L|y-z|$ near the diagonal together with $|\Gamma_\epsilon(u,v)|\le C\epsilon|u-v|^2$ and $|\nabla\Gamma_\epsilon(u,v)|\le C\epsilon|u-v|$ on $[-B,B]^2$. The three terms of $J_g$ are then bounded by $C\epsilon|y-z|^{1-\alpha}$. For $|y-z|\ge1$, bounded first derivatives and the local bound for $g''(y)$ give $C\epsilon|y-z|^{-\alpha}$. Measurability and the off-diagonal weak chain rule follow as for the preceding linearized kernel. The segment from $y$ to $z$ stays in $[-2R,2R]$ whenever $|y|<R$, $|y-z|\le1$, and $R\ge1$.

nodes.title: Differentiation in the profile parameter
nodes.statement_html: Let $0<p<1$, $\alpha=1+p$, $0\le\epsilon\le1$, and let $f,h\in W^{2,\infty}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\R)$ have bounded first derivatives. For every $y\in\R$, the function $t\mapsto\mc I_\epsilon(f+th)(y)$ is $C^1$ on $\R$, all its defining integrals are absolutely convergent, and \[ \frac{d}{dt}\mc I_\epsilon(f+th)(y) =\int_\R K_{f+th,h}(y,z)|y-z|^{-\alpha}\,dz. \] The derivative integral is absolutely convergent for every $(t,y)$. Quantitatively, for every $B,L\ge1$ and $T\ge0$ there is $C=C(p,B,L,T)>0$ such that if $R\ge1$, $\|f'\|_\infty,\|h'\|_\infty\le B$ and $\|f''\|_{L^\infty([-R-2,R+2])},\|h''\|_{L^\infty([-R-2,R+2])}\le L$, then for all $|y|<R$, $|t|\le T$, and $z\ne y$, \[ |\Gamma_\epsilon((f+th)'(y),S_{f+th}(y,z))| +|K_{f+th,h}(y,z)|\le C\epsilon\min\{|y-z|^2,1\}. \] Thus one integrable majorant in $z$ works for all $t\in[-T,T]$ at each fixed $y$.
nodes.proof_html: The bounds for $f+th$ are $B(1+T)$ and $L(1+T)$, so the two kernel lemmas give the displayed estimate. Linearity of secants and first derivatives gives the pointwise $t$ derivative $K_{f+th,h}$. At fixed $(y,z)$ it is continuous in $t$. Differentiate under the integral using the translated envelope $C\epsilon\omega_0(y-z)$, and apply dominated convergence once more for continuity of the derivative. Every $t_0$ belongs to the interior of some $[-T,T]$.

nodes.title: Variation formula for $\mc N_3$
nodes.statement_html:
Let $0\le\epsilon\le1$, $\beta+\frac1p<\gamma<2p+1$, $\ov f$ admissible with constant $M$, and $r,h\in X_\gamma$. Then:
  • for every $y$ the integral defining $D\mc N_3(r)[h](y)$ converges absolutely;
  • for every $y$, the map $t\mapsto\mc N_3(r+th)(y)$ is $C^1$ on $\R$ with derivative $D\mc N_3(r+th)[h](y)$;
  • $D\mc N_3(r)[h]\in W^{1,\infty}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ and its weak derivative is (paper eq:N3\_variation\_derivative) \[ \p_yD\mc N_3(r)[h](y)=\int_\R\frac{\p_yK_{f,h}(y,z)-\alpha K_{f,h}(y,z)/(y-z)}{|y-z|^\alpha}\,dz-\p_y(b_\epsilon h')(y), \] where $\p_yK_{f,h}$ is computed by the chain rule using lem:c10_secant_identities, and the integral converges absolutely for a.e.\ $y$.
nodes.proof_html:
Put $f=\ov f+r$. The admissible-profile and $X_\gamma$ bounds give bounded $f',h'$ and finite local bounds for $f'',h''$. For each $R\ge1$, choose $B,L,H_0$ satisfying lem:c10_variation_kernel_bounds on $[-R-2,R+2]$. Its value envelope proves (1). Apply lem:c10_parameter_differentiation to $f+th$, then subtract the $t$-independent $\mc I_\epsilon(\ov f)$ and differentiate $-b_\epsilon(r'+th')$ to obtain (2).

For (3), apply lem:c10_cutoff_weak_derivative, lem:c10_cutoff_errors to the pair supplied by lem:c10_variation_kernel_bounds. Take $\eta_n=1/(n+3)$. The truncated values converge uniformly on $(-R,R)$ and their weak derivatives converge in $L^\infty$ there. By lem:c10_local_weak_limit, the untruncated value integral is locally Lipschitz and its weak derivative is the absolutely convergent integral of the displayed fixed-$z$ derivative kernel. Subtract $b_\epsilon h'$, which is locally Lipschitz because $b_\epsilon$ is smooth and $h'$ is locally Lipschitz. Exhaust $\R$ by these intervals.

nodes.title: Mean value reduction
nodes.statement_html: Let $0\le\epsilon\le1$, $\beta+\frac1p<\gamma<2p+1$, $\ov f$ admissible with constant $M$, $N>0$ and $A\ge0$. Suppose that for every $r\in X_\gamma$ with $\|r\|_{X_\gamma}\le N$ and every $h\in X_\gamma$, $\|D\mc N_3(r)[h]\|_{Y_\gamma}\le A\|h\|_{X_\gamma}$. Then for all $r_1,r_2\in X_\gamma$ with $\|r_j\|_{X_\gamma}\le N$, \[ \|\mc N_3(r_1)-\mc N_3(r_2)\|_{Y_\gamma}\le A\|r_1-r_2\|_{X_\gamma}. \]
nodes.proof_html: Let $h=r_1-r_2$ and $\rho_t=r_2+th$, $t\in[0,1]$; $\|\rho_t\|\le N$ by convexity of the ball. By lem:c10_N3_variation(2) and the fundamental theorem of calculus, for every $y$ \[ G(y):=\mc N_3(r_1)(y)-\mc N_3(r_2)(y)=\int_0^1D\mc N_3(\rho_t)[h](y)\,dt . \] Hence $\ang{y}^\gamma|G(y)|\le\int_0^1\ang{y}^\gamma|D\mc N_3(\rho_t)[h](y)|dt\le A\|h\|$. For the derivative: the function $(t,y)\mapsto D\mc N_3(\rho_t)[h](y)$ is jointly measurable (continuous in $t$, by (2)), and its $y$-weak derivative $H_t(y)$ is bounded on $[0,1]\times[-R,R]$ (by the hypothesis, or by the local bounds in the proof of lem:c10_N3_variation). For a test function $\varphi\in C_c^\infty$, Fubini gives $\int G\varphi'\,dy=\int_0^1\int D\mc N_3(\rho_t)[h]\varphi'\,dy\,dt=-\int\bigl(\int_0^1H_t\,dt\bigr)\varphi\,dy$, so $G'=\int_0^1H_t\,dt$ a.e. For each half-line, apply the triangle inequality inside the $t$-integral to the weighted sum of the value and derivative, then use $\operatorname{ess\,sup}_y\int_0^1q(t,y)dt\le\int_0^1\operatorname{ess\,sup}_yq(t,y)dt$ for $q\ge0$. Summing the two half-line estimates inside the same $t$-integral gives \[ \|G\|_{Y_\gamma}\le\int_0^1\|D\mc N_3(\rho_t)[h]\|_{Y_\gamma}\,dt\le A\|h\|. \]

nodes.title: Elementary integrals
nodes.statement_html: Let $0<p<1$, $\alpha=1+p$. There is $C=C(p)$ such that for all $\lambda\ge1$ and $a>0$: \[ \int_\R\frac{\min\{1,\lambda|\rho|\}^2}{|\rho|^{1+p}}d\rho=C_2\lambda^p,\quad \int_\R\frac{\min\{1,\lambda|\rho|\}}{|\rho|^{1+p}}d\rho=C_1\lambda^p,\quad \int_{|\rho|\le a}|\rho|^{1-p}d\rho=\tfrac{2a^{2-p}}{2-p},\quad \int_{|\rho|\le a}|\rho|^{-p}d\rho=\tfrac{2a^{1-p}}{1-p}, \] \[ \int_{|\rho|\ge a}|\rho|^{-\alpha}d\rho=\tfrac{2}{p}a^{-p},\qquad \int_{|\rho|\ge a}|\rho|^{-\alpha-1}d\rho=\tfrac{2}{1+p}a^{-1-p},\qquad \int_{|\rho|\ge a}|\rho|^{-\alpha-2}d\rho=\tfrac{2}{2+p}a^{-2-p}, \] with $C_1,C_2\le C$. Moreover, for $\gamma>1$ and $|y|\ge2$, with $C_\gamma=\int\ang{z}^{-\gamma}dz$, \[ \int_{|y-z|\ge|y|/2}\frac{\ang{z}^{-\gamma}}{|y-z|^{\alpha+k}}dz\le 2^{\alpha+k}C_\gamma|y|^{-\alpha-k} \le 2^{2\alpha+2k}C_\gamma\ang{y}^{-\alpha-k},\qquad k=1,2. \] In applications $\lambda=\ang{y}^{1/p}$, so $\lambda^p=\ang{y}$; and $a=|y|/2$ with $|y|\ge2$, so $a\ge\ang{y}/4$.
nodes.proof_html:
Substitute $\rho=s/\lambda$: $C_k=\int\min\{1,|s|\}^k|s|^{-1-p}ds$, finite because $k-1-p>-1$ near $0$
  and $-1-p<-1$ at infinity. The power integrals are explicit. For the last bound, use
  $|y-z|^{-\alpha-k}\le(|y|/2)^{-\alpha-k}$ on the region and integrate $\ang{z}^{-\gamma}$; for $|y|\ge2$,
  $\ang{y}\le\sqrt2|y|\le 2|y|$.

nodes.title: Near-field increments
nodes.statement_html: With the standing assumptions, let $|y|\ge2$ and $|y-z|\le|y|/2$ (so $z$ has the sign of $y$ and $\frac12\ang{y}\le\ang{w}\le2\ang{y}$ for $w\in I_{y,z}$). Then, with $m(y,z)=\min\{1,\ang{y}^{1/p}|y-z|\}$, for $y\ge2$ (paper eq:N3\_profile\_increment, eq:N3\_direction\_increment): \[ |f'(y)|+|S_f(y,z)|\le C\ang{y}^{-\beta},\qquad |f'(y)-S_f(y,z)|\le C\ang{y}^{-\beta}m(y,z),\qquad |f''(y)|+|\p_yS_f(y,z)|\le C\ang{y}^{-\beta+1/p}, \] \[ |h'(y)|\le\|h\|\ang{y}^{-\gamma+1/p},\quad |h'(y)-S_h(y,z)|\le C\|h\|\ang{y}^{-\gamma+1/p}m(y,z),\quad |h''(y)|+|\p_yS_h(y,z)|\le C\|h\|\ang{y}^{-\gamma+2/p}, \] and for $y\le-2$: \[ |f'(y)|+|S_f(y,z)|\le C,\quad |f'(y)-S_f(y,z)|\le C\ang{y}^{-p-2}|y-z|,\quad |f''(y)|+|\p_yS_f(y,z)|\le C\ang{y}^{-p-2}, \] \[ |h'(y)|\le\|h\|\ang{y}^{-\gamma-1},\quad |h'(y)-S_h(y,z)|\le C\|h\|\ang{y}^{-\gamma-2}|y-z|,\quad |h''(y)|+|\p_yS_h(y,z)|\le C\|h\|\ang{y}^{-\gamma-2}. \] (Second-derivative statements hold for a.e.\ $y$.)
nodes.proof_html: On $I_{y,z}$ all weights $\ang{w}^{s}$ are within a factor $2^{|s|}$ of $\ang{y}^s$. Then: $|S_g(y,z)|\le\sup_{I_{y,z}}|g'|$; $|g'(y)-S_g(y,z)|\le\min\{2\sup_{I}|g'|,\ |y-z|\sup_I|g''|\}$; $|\p_yS_g|\le\sup_I|g''|$ (lem:c10_secant_identities), applied to $g=f$ and $g=h$ with the bounds of lem:c10_profile_consequences. For $y\ge2$ and $g=f$: $\min\{\ang{y}^{-\beta},\ang{y}^{-\beta+1/p}|y-z|\} =\ang{y}^{-\beta}m$; for $g=h$ similarly with $-\gamma+1/p$ and $-\gamma+2/p$. For $y\le-2$ and $g=f$ use $\sup_I|f''|\le C\ang{y}^{-p-2}$; for $g=h$, $\sup_I|h''|\le C\|h\|\ang{y}^{-\gamma-2}$.

nodes.title: Near-field integrand bounds
nodes.statement_html: With the standing assumptions, $|y|\ge2$ and $|y-z|\le|y|/2$, we have the decomposition (paper eq:N3\_near\_decomposition) \[ K_{f,h}=(\p_1+\p_2)\Gamma_\epsilon\,h'(y)+\p_2\Gamma_\epsilon\,(S_h(y,z)-h'(y)), \] its $y$-derivative (paper eq:N3\_near\_integrand\_derivative; all $\Gamma_\epsilon$-derivatives at $(f'(y),S_f(y,z))$) \begin{align*} \p_yK_{f,h}&=(\p_{11}+\p_{12})\Gamma_\epsilon\,f''h'+(\p_{12}+\p_{22})\Gamma_\epsilon\,\p_yS_f\,h' +(\p_1+\p_2)\Gamma_\epsilon\,h''\\ &\quad+\bigl(\p_{12}\Gamma_\epsilon f''+\p_{22}\Gamma_\epsilon\p_yS_f\bigr)(S_h-h') +\p_2\Gamma_\epsilon(\p_yS_h-h''), \end{align*} and the bounds (paper eq:N3\_near\_integrand\_bound, eq:N3\_near\_integrand\_derivative\_bound) \[ |K_{f,h}|\le C\epsilon\|h\|\begin{cases}\ang{y}^{-2\beta-\gamma+1/p}m^2,&y\ge2\\\ang{y}^{-\gamma-p-4}|y-z|^2,&y\le-2\end{cases}, \] \[ |\p_yK_{f,h}|+\frac{|K_{f,h}|}{|y-z|}\le C\epsilon\|h\|\begin{cases}\ang{y}^{-2\beta-\gamma+2/p}m,&y\ge2\\\ang{y}^{-\gamma-p-4}|y-z|,&y\le-2,\end{cases} \] with $m=m(y,z)$ as in lem:c10_near_increments.
nodes.proof_html:
The decomposition is algebra. Its derivative: product and chain rule, with $\p_y[f'(y)]=f''$, $\p_y[S_f]=\p_yS_f$, and the identity $\p_1(\p_1+\p_2)+\p_2(\p_1+\p_2)$ expanded; note that $\p_y(S_h-h')=\p_yS_h-h''$. Write $u=f'(y)$, $v=S_f(y,z)$, $|u-v|=:d$.

Value. $|(\p_1+\p_2)\Gamma_\epsilon|\le C\epsilon d^2$ and $|\p_2\Gamma_\epsilon|\le C\epsilon d(|u|+|v|)$. For $y\ge2$: $\epsilon\ang{y}^{-2\beta}m^2\cdot\ang{y}^{-\gamma+1/p}+\epsilon\ang{y}^{-\beta}m\ang{y}^{-\beta}\cdot \ang{y}^{-\gamma+1/p}m$. For $y\le-2$: $\epsilon\ang{y}^{-2p-4}|y-z|^2\ang{y}^{-\gamma-1}+\epsilon \ang{y}^{-p-2}|y-z|\cdot\ang{y}^{-\gamma-2}|y-z|$.

Derivative, term by term, using $|(\p_1+\p_2)\nabla\Gamma_\epsilon|\le C\epsilon d$, $|\nabla^2\Gamma_\epsilon|\le C\epsilon(|u|+|v|)$ and lem:c10_near_increments. For $y\ge2$ (all with factor $\epsilon\|h\|$): terms 1--2: $\ang{y}^{-\beta}m\cdot\ang{y}^{-\beta+1/p}\cdot\ang{y}^{-\gamma+1/p}$; term 3: $\ang{y}^{-2\beta}m^2\ang{y}^{-\gamma+2/p}\le\ang{y}^{-2\beta-\gamma+2/p}m$; term 4: $\ang{y}^{-\beta}\ang{y}^{-\beta+1/p}\ang{y}^{-\gamma+1/p}m$; term 5: $\ang{y}^{-2\beta}m\ang{y}^{-\gamma+2/p}$. For $y\le-2$: terms 1--2: $\ang{y}^{-p-2}|y-z|\ang{y}^{-p-2}\ang{y}^{-\gamma-1}$; term 3: $\ang{y}^{-2p-4}|y-z|^2\ang{y}^{-\gamma-2} \le\ang{y}^{-2p-\gamma-5}|y-z|$ (as $|y-z|\le\ang{y}$); term 4: $1\cdot\ang{y}^{-p-2}\ang{y}^{-\gamma-2}|y-z|$; term 5: $\ang{y}^{-p-2}|y-z|\ang{y}^{-\gamma-2}$. All are $\le\ang{y}^{-\gamma-p-4}|y-z|$.

Quotient $|K|/|y-z|$: for $y\ge2$ use $m^2/|y-z|\le m\cdot m/|y-z|\le m\ang{y}^{1/p}$; for $y\le-2$ divide directly.

nodes.title: Near-field estimates
nodes.statement_html: With the standing assumptions and $|y|\ge2$ (paper eq:N3\_near\_value, eq:N3\_near\_derivative): \[ \int_{|y-z|\le|y|/2}\frac{|K_{f,h}(y,z)|}{|y-z|^\alpha}dz\le C\epsilon\|h\|\begin{cases}\ang{y}^{-\gamma},&y\ge2\\\ang{y}^{-\gamma-2p-2},&y\le-2,\end{cases} \] \[ \int_{|y-z|\le|y|/2}\frac{|\p_yK_{f,h}-\alpha K_{f,h}/(y-z)|}{|y-z|^\alpha}dz\le C\epsilon\|h\|\begin{cases}\ang{y}^{-\gamma+1/p},&y\ge2\\\ang{y}^{-\gamma-2p-3},&y\le-2.\end{cases} \]
nodes.proof_html: Integrate the bounds of lem:c10_N3_near_integrand in $\rho=y-z$. For $y\ge2$, extend to all $\rho\in\R$ and use lem:c10_elementary_integrals with $\lambda=\ang{y}^{1/p}$: value $\ang{y}^{-2\beta-\gamma+1/p}\cdot C\ang{y}=C\ang{y}^{-\gamma}$, derivative $\ang{y}^{-2\beta-\gamma+2/p}\cdot C\ang{y}=C\ang{y}^{-\gamma+1/p}$ (using $2\beta=1+1/p$). For $y\le-2$: $\ang{y}^{-\gamma-p-4}\int_{|\rho|\le|y|/2}|\rho|^{1-p}\le C\ang{y}^{-\gamma-2p-2}$ and $\ang{y}^{-\gamma-p-4}\int_{|\rho|\le|y|/2}|\rho|^{-p}\le C\ang{y}^{-\gamma-2p-3}$, using $|y|\le\ang{y}$. The factor $\alpha$ is absorbed into $C$.

nodes.title: Model coefficient subtraction
nodes.statement_html: For $y\ge2$ and every $z<0$, $S_W(y,z)=\frac{z}{y-z}\in(-1,0)$ and $\p_yS_W(y,z)=-\frac{S_W(y,z)}{y-z}$; for $z\ge0$, $z\ne y$, $S_W(y,z)=0$. Consequently, for $y\ge2$ (paper eq:N3\_model\_coefficient) \[ b_\epsilon(y)=\int_{z<0}\frac{\p_1\Gamma_\epsilon(0,S_W(y,z))}{|y-z|^\alpha}dz =\int_{|y-z|\ge y/2}\frac{\p_1\Gamma_\epsilon(0,S_W(y,z))}{|y-z|^\alpha}dz, \] hence, writing $\widetilde K(y,z)=K_{f,h}(y,z)-\p_1\Gamma_\epsilon(0,S_W(y,z))h'(y)$, (paper eq:N3\_far\_subtraction, eq:N3\_far\_subtraction\_derivative) \[ \int_{|y-z|\ge y/2}\frac{K_{f,h}}{|y-z|^\alpha}dz-b_\epsilon(y)h'(y)=\int_{|y-z|\ge y/2}\frac{\widetilde K(y,z)}{|y-z|^\alpha}dz, \] and for a.e.\ $y>2$ \[ \int_{|y-z|\ge y/2}\frac{\p_yK_{f,h}-\alpha K_{f,h}/(y-z)}{|y-z|^\alpha}dz-\p_y(b_\epsilon h')(y) =\int_{|y-z|\ge y/2}\frac{1}{|y-z|^\alpha}\Bigl(\p_y-\frac{\alpha}{y-z}\Bigr)\widetilde K(y,z)\,dz . \] (Here $\p_y$ acts with $z$ fixed; the integration region is not differentiated.)
nodes.proof_html:
For $y>0$: $W(y)=0$, $W'(y)=0$, and $W(z)=-z$ for $z<0$, $W(z)=0$ for $z\ge0$, giving the formulas for $S_W$ and $\p_yS_W$. Since $\chi_+(y)=1$ for $y\ge2$, lem:analysis_coefficient gives $b_\epsilon(y)=\int_\R\p_1\Gamma_\epsilon(0,S_W(y,z))|y-z|^{-\alpha}dz$; on $z\ge0$ the integrand is $\p_1\Gamma_\epsilon(0,0)=0$ (as $\nabla\Gamma_\epsilon(u,u)=0$). The set $\{z<0\}$ is contained in $\{|y-z|\ge y/2\}$ (indeed $|y-z|>y$), and on $\{|y-z|\ge y/2\}\cap\{z\ge0\}$ the integrand vanishes; this gives both forms of $b_\epsilon$, and the first identity follows by linearity (both integrals converge absolutely: $|\p_1\Gamma_\epsilon|\le C\epsilon$, $\alpha>1$).

For the derivative: on $y>2$, $z<0$, the integrand $\p_1\Gamma_\epsilon(0,S_W(y,z))|y-z|^{-\alpha}$ is smooth in $y$, with $y$-derivative $\bigl(-\p_{12}\Gamma_\epsilon(0,S_W)\frac{S_W}{y-z}-\alpha\frac{\p_1\Gamma_\epsilon(0,S_W)}{y-z}\bigr)|y-z|^{-\alpha}$, dominated by $C\epsilon|y-z|^{-\alpha-1}$ uniformly for $y$ in compact subsets of $(2,\infty)$; so differentiation under the integral is legitimate (paper eq:N3\_model\_coefficient\_derivative). Multiplying by $h'(y)$ and using the product rule: $\p_y(b_\epsilon h')=\int_{z<0}|y-z|^{-\alpha}(\p_y-\frac\alpha{y-z})\bigl(\p_1\Gamma_\epsilon(0,S_W)h'(y)\bigr)dz$, and again the integrand vanishes on $z\ge0$, so the region may be replaced by $|y-z|\ge y/2$. Subtract from the far part of lem:c10_N3_variation(3), which converges absolutely.

nodes.title: Far-field integrand bounds, $y\ge2$
nodes.statement_html: With the standing assumptions, $y\ge2$, $|y-z|\ge y/2$, and $\widetilde K$ as in lem:c10_far_subtraction: \begin{align*} &|\p_1\Gamma_\epsilon(f'(y),S_f(y,z))-\p_1\Gamma_\epsilon(0,S_W(y,z))|\le C\epsilon\ang{y}^{-1},\\ &|\widetilde K(y,z)|\le C\epsilon\|h\|\Bigl(\ang{y}^{-\gamma+1/p-1}+\frac{\ang{y}^{-\gamma}+\ang{z}^{-\gamma}}{|y-z|}\Bigr),\\ &\Bigl|\p_y\widetilde K(y,z)\Bigr|+\frac{|\widetilde K(y,z)|}{|y-z|}\le C\epsilon\|h\|\Bigl(\ang{y}^{-\gamma+2/p-1}+\ang{y}^{1/p-1}\frac{\ang{y}^{-\gamma}+\ang{z}^{-\gamma}}{|y-z|}\Bigr) \end{align*} (paper eq:N3\_far\_coefficient\_bound, eq:N3\_far\_integrand\_bound, eq:N3\_far\_integrand\_derivative\_bound; the last for a.e.\ $y$).
nodes.proof_html:
Decomposition (paper eq:N3\_far\_decomposition): $\widetilde K=[\p_1\Gamma_\epsilon-\p_1\Gamma_\epsilon(0,S_W)]h'(y)+\p_2\Gamma_\epsilon\,S_h(y,z)$, unmarked derivatives at $(f'(y),S_f(y,z))$.

Coefficient: the segment joining $(0,S_W)$ and $(f'(y),S_f)$ lies in $[-C_*,C_*]^2$, so by the mean value theorem and $|\nabla^2\Gamma_\epsilon|\le C\epsilon$, the difference is $\le C\epsilon(|f'(y)|+|S_f-S_W|)$. Now $|f'(y)|\le C\ang{y}^{-\beta}\le C\ang{y}^{-1}$ ($\beta>1$) and $|S_f-S_W|=|S_{f-W}|\le(|f-W|(y)+|f-W|(z))/|y-z|\le 2C/|y-z|\le 4C/y\le C'\ang{y}^{-1}$ (lem:c10_profile_consequences(1)).

Value: $|\p_2\Gamma_\epsilon|\le C\epsilon$ and $|S_h|\le(|h(y)|+|h(z)|)/|y-z|$, with $|h(w)|\le\|h\|\ang{w}^{-\gamma}$ and $|h'(y)|\le\|h\|\ang{y}^{-\gamma+1/p}$.

Derivative: with $z$ fixed, \begin{align*} \p_y\widetilde K&=[\p_1\Gamma_\epsilon-\p_1\Gamma_\epsilon(0,S_W)]h'' +\bigl[\p_{11}\Gamma_\epsilon f''+\p_{12}\Gamma_\epsilon\p_yS_f-\p_{12}\Gamma_\epsilon(0,S_W)\p_yS_W\bigr]h'\\ &\quad+\bigl[\p_{12}\Gamma_\epsilon f''+\p_{22}\Gamma_\epsilon\p_yS_f\bigr]S_h+\p_2\Gamma_\epsilon\,\p_yS_h . \end{align*} By lem:c10_secant_identities, $|\p_yS_f|\le2\|f'\|_\infty/|y-z|\le C\ang{y}^{-1}$, $|\p_yS_W|=|S_W|/|y-z|\le C\ang{y}^{-1}$, and $|\p_yS_h|\le|h'(y)|/|y-z|+(|h(y)|+|h(z)|)/|y-z|^2$. Also $|f''(y)|+\ang{y}^{-1}\le C(\ang{y}^{-\beta+1/p}+\ang{y}^{-1})\le C\ang{y}^{1/p-1}$ (as $\beta>1$, $1/p-1>-1$). With $|\nabla^2\Gamma_\epsilon|\le C\epsilon$: the four terms are bounded by $\epsilon\ang{y}^{-1}|h''|$, $\epsilon\ang{y}^{1/p-1}|h'|$, $\epsilon\ang{y}^{1/p-1}|S_h|$, and $\epsilon(\ang{y}^{-1}|h'|+\ang{y}^{-1}|S_h|)$ (using $1/|y-z|\le 2/y\le C\ang{y}^{-1}$). Insert $|h''(y)|\le\|h\|\ang{y}^{-\gamma+2/p}$. The bound on $|\widetilde K|/|y-z|$ follows from the value bound and $1/|y-z|\le C\ang{y}^{-1}\le C\ang{y}^{1/p-1}$.

nodes.title: Far-field estimates, $y\ge2$
nodes.statement_html: With the standing assumptions and $y\ge2$ (a.e.\ for the second bound) (paper eq:N3\_far\_plus\_value, eq:N3\_far\_plus\_derivative): \[ \Bigl|\int_{|y-z|\ge y/2}\frac{K_{f,h}}{|y-z|^\alpha}dz-b_\epsilon h'(y)\Bigr|\le C\epsilon\|h\|\ang{y}^{-\gamma}, \] \[ \Bigl|\int_{|y-z|\ge y/2}\frac{\p_yK_{f,h}-\alpha K_{f,h}/(y-z)}{|y-z|^\alpha}dz-\p_y(b_\epsilon h')(y)\Bigr|\le C\epsilon\|h\|\ang{y}^{-\gamma+1/p}. \]
nodes.proof_html:
By lem:c10_far_subtraction it suffices to integrate the bounds of lem:c10_far_plus_integrand against $|y-z|^{-\alpha}$ over $|y-z|\ge y/2$, using lem:c10_elementary_integrals with $a=y/2\ge\ang{y}/4$ (all with factor $C\epsilon\|h\|$):

Value: $\ang{y}^{-\gamma+1/p-1}\cdot\ang{y}^{-p}+\ang{y}^{-\gamma}\ang{y}^{-1-p}+\ang{y}^{-\alpha-1}= \ang{y}^{-\gamma+1/p-1-p}+\ang{y}^{-\gamma-p-1}+\ang{y}^{-p-2}$. Each is $\le\ang{y}^{-\gamma}$: the first since $1/p<1+p$, the third since $\gamma<2p+1<p+2$.

Derivative: $\ang{y}^{-\gamma+2/p-1-p}+\ang{y}^{1/p-1}(\ang{y}^{-\gamma-1-p}+\ang{y}^{-p-2})$. Each is $\le\ang{y}^{-\gamma+1/p}$: the first since $1/p<1+p$, the second trivially, the third $\ang{y}^{1/p-p-3}\le\ang{y}^{-\gamma+1/p}$ since $\gamma<p+3$.

nodes.title: Far-field estimates, $y\le-2$
nodes.statement_html: With the standing assumptions and $y\le-2$ (a.e.\ for the second bound) (paper eq:N3\_far\_minus\_integrand\_bound, eq:N3\_far\_minus\_value, eq:N3\_far\_minus\_derivative): for $|y-z|\ge|y|/2$, \[ |K_{f,h}|\le C\epsilon\|h\|\Bigl(\ang{y}^{-\gamma-1}+\frac{\ang{y}^{-\gamma}+\ang{z}^{-\gamma}}{|y-z|}\Bigr),\quad |\p_yK_{f,h}|+\frac{|K_{f,h}|}{|y-z|}\le C\epsilon\|h\|\Bigl(\ang{y}^{-\gamma-2}+\ang{y}^{-1}\frac{\ang{y}^{-\gamma}+\ang{z}^{-\gamma}}{|y-z|}\Bigr), \] and \[ \int_{|y-z|\ge|y|/2}\frac{|K_{f,h}|}{|y-z|^\alpha}dz\le C\epsilon\|h\|\ang{y}^{-\gamma},\qquad \int_{|y-z|\ge|y|/2}\frac{|\p_yK_{f,h}-\alpha K_{f,h}/(y-z)|}{|y-z|^\alpha}dz\le C\epsilon\|h\|\ang{y}^{-\gamma-1}. \] Moreover $b_\epsilon(y)=0$ for $y\le1$.
nodes.proof_html: $|\nabla\Gamma_\epsilon|+|\nabla^2\Gamma_\epsilon|\le C\epsilon$ on $[-C_*,C_*]^2$. Value: $|K|\le C\epsilon(|h'(y)|+|S_h|)$ with $|h'(y)|\le\|h\|\ang{y}^{-\gamma-1}$, $|S_h|\le(|h(y)|+|h(z)|)/|y-z|$. Derivative: $\p_yK=\nabla\p_1\Gamma_\epsilon\cdot(f'',\p_yS_f)h' +\p_1\Gamma_\epsilon h''+\nabla\p_2\Gamma_\epsilon\cdot(f'',\p_yS_f)S_h+\p_2\Gamma_\epsilon\p_yS_h$, with $|f''(y)|+|\p_yS_f|\le C\ang{y}^{-p-2}+2\|f'\|_\infty/|y-z|\le C\ang{y}^{-1}$, $|\p_yS_h|\le|h'(y)|/|y-z|+(|h(y)|+|h(z)|)/|y-z|^2$, $|h''(y)|\le\|h\|\ang{y}^{-\gamma-2}$ and $1/|y-z|\le C\ang{y}^{-1}$. The quotient bound follows from the value bound and $1/|y-z|\le C\ang{y}^{-1}$. Integration (lem:c10_elementary_integrals, $a=|y|/2$): value $\ang{y}^{-\gamma-1-p}+\ang{y}^{-\gamma-1-p}+\ang{y}^{-p-2}\le3\ang{y}^{-\gamma}$ (as $\gamma<p+2$); derivative $\ang{y}^{-\gamma-2-p}+\ang{y}^{-1}(\ang{y}^{-\gamma-1-p}+\ang{y}^{-p-2})\le3\ang{y}^{-\gamma-1}$ (as $\gamma<p+2$). The last claim is $\chi_+=0$ on $(-\infty,1]$.

nodes.title: Compact region $|y|<2$
nodes.statement_html: With the standing assumptions, for $|y|<2$ (a.e.\ for derivative statements): \[ |K_{f,h}(y,z)|\le C\epsilon\|h\|\min\{|y-z|^2,1\},\qquad |\p_yK_{f,h}(y,z)|+\frac{|K_{f,h}(y,z)|}{|y-z|}\le C\epsilon\|h\|\min\{|y-z|,1\}, \] hence (paper eq:N3\_far\_compact\_value, eq:N3\_far\_compact\_derivative) \[ \int_\R\frac{|K_{f,h}|}{|y-z|^\alpha}dz+\int_\R\frac{|\p_yK_{f,h}-\alpha K_{f,h}/(y-z)|}{|y-z|^\alpha}dz\le C\epsilon\|h\|, \] and $|b_\epsilon(y)h'(y)|+|\p_y(b_\epsilon h')(y)|\le C\epsilon\|h\|$. Consequently $|D\mc N_3(r)[h](y)|\le C\epsilon\|h\|\ang{y}^{-\gamma}$ and $|\p_yD\mc N_3(r)[h](y)|\le C\epsilon\|h\|\min\{\ang{y}^{-\gamma+1/p},\ang{y}^{-\gamma-1}\}$ for $|y|<2$.
nodes.proof_html: For $|y-z|\le1$ we have $y,z\in[-3,3]$, where $\|f''\|_\infty+\|h''\|_\infty/\|h\|\le C$ (lem:c10_profile_consequences); so $|f'(y)-S_f|\le C|y-z|$, $|h'(y)-S_h|\le C\|h\||y-z|$, $|\p_yS_f|\le C$, $|\p_yS_h|\le C\|h\|$. The kernel-pair bounds of lem:c10_variation_kernel_bounds on $(-2,2)$ (equivalently, the near decomposition of the integrand together with the kernel bounds) give $|K|\le C\epsilon\|h\||y-z|^2$; the five-term derivative formula gives $|\p_yK|\le C\epsilon\|h\||y-z|$ (terms 1,2,4,5 have a factor $|y-z|$ via $d=|u-v|$ or $|S_h-h'|$; term 3 has $d^2$). For $|y-z|\ge1$: $|K|\le C\epsilon(|h'(y)|+2\|h\|_\infty)\le C\epsilon\|h\|$, and $|\p_yK|\le C\epsilon(|h''|+|h'|(|f''|+|\p_yS_f|)+(|f''|+|\p_yS_f|)|S_h|+|\p_yS_h|)\le C\epsilon\|h\|$ using $|\p_yS_f|\le2\|f'\|_\infty$, $|S_h|\le2\|h\|_\infty$, $|\p_yS_h|\le|h'(y)|+|S_h|$. Integrate with lem:c10_elementary_integrals: $\int_{|\rho|\le1}|\rho|^{2-\alpha}+\int_{|\rho|\ge1}|\rho|^{-\alpha}<\infty$ and $\int_{|\rho|\le1}|\rho|^{1-\alpha}<\infty$ (as $\alpha<2$). For $b_\epsilon$: on $[-2,2]$, $b_\epsilon=c_\epsilon\chi_+y^{-p}$ is supported in $[1,2]$ where it is smooth with $|b_\epsilon|+|b_\epsilon'|\le C|c_\epsilon|\le C\epsilon$ (lem:analysis_coefficient); and $|h'|+|h''|\le C\|h\|$ on $[-2,2]$. The consequence follows from lem:c10_N3_variation(3), since on $|y|<2$ all weights are comparable to $1$. Lean route: the kernel pair on $(-2,2)$ is controlled by lem:c10_variation_kernel_bounds and lem:c10_kernel_envelopes; the near-integrand lemma is not needed.

nodes.title: Bound on the linearization
nodes.statement_html: Let $0\le\epsilon\le1$, $\beta+\frac1p<\gamma<2p+1$, $M,N>0$, $\ov f$ admissible with constant $M$, $r\in X_\gamma$ with $\|r\|_{X_\gamma}\le N$, and $h\in X_\gamma$. Then $D\mc N_3(r)[h]\in Y_\gamma$ and \[ \|D\mc N_3(r)[h]\|_{Y_\gamma}\le C\epsilon\|h\|_{X_\gamma},\qquad C=C(p,\gamma,M,N). \]
nodes.proof_html:
If $\epsilon=0$, $D\mc N_3\equiv0$. Otherwise, by lem:c10_N3_variation the value and the a.e.\ derivative of $D\mc N_3(r)[h]$ are given by absolutely convergent integrals, which for $|y|\ge2$ we split into the near region $|y-z|\le|y|/2$ and the far region $|y-z|>|y|/2$ (the boundary $|y-z|=|y|/2$ has measure zero).
  • $y\ge2$: near part by lem:c10_N3_near, far part together with $-b_\epsilon h'$ by lem:c10_N3_far_plus: $|D\mc N_3(r)[h]|\le C\epsilon\|h\|\ang{y}^{-\gamma}$, $|\p_yD\mc N_3(r)[h]|\le C\epsilon\|h\|\ang{y}^{-\gamma+1/p}$.
  • $y\le-2$: $b_\epsilon=0$ near $y$; near part by lem:c10_N3_near ($\ang{y}^{-\gamma-2p-2}\le\ang{y}^{-\gamma}$, $\ang{y}^{-\gamma-2p-3}\le\ang{y}^{-\gamma-1}$), far part by lem:c10_N3_far_minus.
  • $|y|<2$: lem:c10_N3_compact.
Multiplying by the weights of def:Y_gamma and taking suprema over $y\ge0$ and $y\le0$ yields the claim.

nodes.title: Lipschitz bound for $\mc N_3$
nodes.statement_html: Under the hypotheses of lem:N1, $\mc N_3(r_1)-\mc N_3(r_2)\in Y_\gamma$ and there is $C=C(p,\gamma,M,N)$ with \[ \|\mc N_3(r_1)-\mc N_3(r_2)\|_{Y_\gamma}\le C\epsilon\|r_1-r_2\|_{X_\gamma}. \]
nodes.proof_html: Apply lem:c10_N3_mean_value with $A=C\epsilon$ from lem:c10_N3_linearized_bound.

nodes.title: Local $W^{1,\infty}$ structure of $\mc I_\epsilon$
nodes.statement_html: Let $0\le\epsilon\le1$, $g\in W^{2,\infty}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\R)$ with $g'\in L^\infty(\R)$, and set, for $z\ne y$, \[ K^{(1)}_g(y,z)=\p_1\Gamma_\epsilon(g'(y),S_g)g''(y)+\p_2\Gamma_\epsilon(g'(y),S_g)\frac{g'(y)-S_g}{y-z}-(1+p)\frac{\Gamma_\epsilon(g'(y),S_g)}{y-z}, \] with $S_g=S_g(y,z)$. Then $\mc I_\epsilon(g)\in W^{1,\infty}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ with weak derivative (paper eq:nonlinear\_continuity\_derivative) $\p_y\mc I_\epsilon(g)(y)=\int_\R K^{(1)}_g(y,z)|y-z|^{-\alpha}dz$ (absolutely convergent for a.e.\ $y$). Moreover, for $R\ge1$, $0<\delta<1$, with $L=\|g'\|_{L^\infty}+\|g''\|_{L^\infty([-2R,2R])}$, there is $C=C(p,R,L)$ such that (paper eq:nonlinear\_continuity\_near) \[ \sup_{|y|\le R}\int_{|y-z|<\delta}\frac{|\Gamma_\epsilon(g'(y),S_g)|}{|y-z|^\alpha}dz\le C\epsilon\delta^{3-\alpha},\qquad \mathop{\mathrm{ess\,sup}}_{|y|\le R}\int_{|y-z|<\delta}\frac{|K^{(1)}_g(y,z)|}{|y-z|^\alpha}dz\le C\epsilon\delta^{2-\alpha}, \] and for $|y|\le R$, $|y-z|>4R$: $|\Gamma_\epsilon(g'(y),S_g)|+|K^{(1)}_g(y,z)|\le C\epsilon$ and $|y-z|\ge\frac23|z|$.
nodes.proof_html: On each $(-R,R)$, lem:c10_profile_kernel_bounds supplies a dominated kernel pair whose value integral is $\mc I_\epsilon(g)$ and whose derivative integral is the one stated here. Apply lem:c10_cutoff_weak_derivative, lem:c10_cutoff_errors with $\eta_n=1/(n+3)$ and then lem:c10_local_weak_limit. The derivative convergence is in essential supremum norm; $g''$ need not be continuous. This proves the qualitative local Lipschitz assertion and formula. For the quantitative near bounds use the version of lem:c10_profile_kernel_bounds with second derivatives controlled on $[-2R,2R]$, and integrate $C\epsilon|y-z|^{2-\alpha}$ and $C\epsilon|y-z|^{1-\alpha}$ over $|y-z|<\delta$. For $|y-z|>4R$, the numerator bounds follow from its far-region estimates, and $|z|\ge|y-z|-|y|>3R$ implies $|y-z|\ge(2/3)|z|$.

nodes.title: Difference estimate away from the diagonal on a compact set
nodes.statement_html: Let $0<p<1$, $\alpha=1+p$, $R\ge1$, $S\ge5R$, $0<\delta<1$, and $B,L\ge1$. There exists $C=C(p,R,S,\delta,B,L)>0$ such that for every $0\le\epsilon\le1$ and $g_0,g_1\in W^{2,\infty}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\R)$ satisfying $\|g_j'\|_{L^\infty(\R)}\le B$ and $\|g_j''\|_{L^\infty([-S,S])}\le L$ ($j=0,1$), the following holds. Put \[ e_S=\|g_1-g_0\|_{L^\infty([-S,S])} +\|g_1'-g_0'\|_{L^\infty([-S,S])} +\|g_1''-g_0''\|_{L^\infty([-S,S])},\qquad E_y=\{z:|z|\le S,\ |y-z|\ge\delta\}. \] The value-difference integrand below is absolutely integrable on $E_y$ for every $|y|\le R$, and the derivative-difference integrand is absolutely integrable there for a.e.\ $|y|\le R$. Using $K_g^{(1)}$ from lem:c10_Ieps_local, \[ \sup_{|y|\le R}\int_{E_y} \frac{|\Gamma_\epsilon(g_1'(y),S_{g_1})-\Gamma_\epsilon(g_0'(y),S_{g_0})|}{|y-z|^\alpha}dz \le C\epsilon e_S, \] \[ \mathop{\mathrm{ess\,sup}}_{|y|\le R}\int_{E_y} \frac{|K_{g_1}^{(1)}(y,z)-K_{g_0}^{(1)}(y,z)|}{|y-z|^\alpha}dz \le C\epsilon e_S. \] The inequalities remain valid if $E_y$ is replaced by any measurable subset.
nodes.proof_html: On $E_y$, the segment between $y$ and $z$ stays in $[-S,S]$. Hence $|S_{g_1}-S_{g_0}|\le\|g_1'-g_0'\|_{L^\infty([-S,S])}$, and $|g_1'-g_0'|$, $|g_1''-g_0''|$ are bounded by $e_S$ (the second a.e.). Both arguments of $\Gamma_\epsilon$ lie in $[-B,B]$. Apply the uniform Lipschitz bounds $C(p,B)\epsilon$ for $\Gamma_\epsilon$ and its first derivatives there, expand the products in $K_g^{(1)}$, and use the common bound $L$ for $g_j''$. Every denominator is bounded by a power of $\delta^{-1}$, giving a pointwise bound $C(p,\delta,B,L)\epsilon e_S$ for each absolute integrand, outside one null set in $y$. Integrate over a set of length at most $2S$. Restriction to a measurable subset only decreases the absolute integrals.

nodes.title: Uniform tails for the value and derivative kernels
nodes.statement_html: Let $0<p<1$, $\alpha=1+p$, and $B,L\ge1$. There exists $C=C(p,B,L)>0$ such that for every $R\ge1$, $S\ge5R$, $0\le\epsilon\le1$, and $g\in W^{2,\infty}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\R)$ with $\|g'\|_{L^\infty(\R)}\le B$ and $\|g''\|_{L^\infty([-2R,2R])}\le L$, \[ \sup_{|y|\le R}\int_{|z|>S} \frac{|\Gamma_\epsilon(g'(y),S_g(y,z))|}{|y-z|^\alpha}dz +\mathop{\mathrm{ess\,sup}}_{|y|\le R}\int_{|z|>S} \frac{|K_g^{(1)}(y,z)|}{|y-z|^\alpha}dz \le C\epsilon S^{-p}. \] Both absolute integrals are finite (the derivative one for a.e.\ $y$), and the bound is independent of $R,S,g,\epsilon$ apart from the displayed factors and hypotheses.
nodes.proof_html: For $|y|\le R$, $|z|>S\ge5R$, one has $|y-z|\ge(4/5)|z|>4R$. Bounded first derivatives control all secants, and $|\p_yS_g|\le2B/|y-z|\le2B$. The formulas for the numerators therefore give the common bound $C(p,B,L)\epsilon$, with the derivative statement interpreted a.e.\ in $y$. Integrate $|z|^{-\alpha}$: $\int_{|z|>S}|z|^{-\alpha}dz=2S^{-p}/p$.

nodes.title: Local continuity of $\mc I_\epsilon$
nodes.statement_html: Let $0\le\epsilon\le1$ and let $g_k,g\in W^{2,\infty}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\R)$ satisfy (paper eq:nonlinear\_continuity\_profiles) $\sup_k\|g_k'\|_{L^\infty}+\|g'\|_{L^\infty}<\infty$ and $g_k\to g$ in $W^{2,\infty}_{\mathrm{loc}}$. Then for every $R>0$, $\mc I_\epsilon(g_k)\to\mc I_\epsilon(g)$ in $W^{1,\infty}([-R,R])$ (paper eq:nonlinear\_continuity\_local).
nodes.proof_html: It suffices to consider $R\ge1$. Choose a common bound $B$ for all $g_k',g'$ on $\R$ and a common bound $L_R$ for all $g_k'',g''$ on $[-2R,2R]$; the latter exists by local $W^{2,\infty}$ convergence. Fix $0<\delta<1$ and $S\ge5R$. Split both value and derivative integrals into \[ |y-z|<\delta,\qquad |y-z|\ge\delta\ \hbox{and}\ |z|\le S,\qquad |z|>S . \] For $|y|\le R$ this is a partition up to null boundaries: the last region has $|y-z|>4R$. The sum of the two near contributions, for $g_k$ and $g$, is bounded by $C_R\epsilon\delta^{2-\alpha}$ by lem:c10_Ieps_local. For each fixed $S$, local convergence supplies a common second-derivative bound $L_S$ on $[-S,S]$ and $e_S(k)=\|g_k-g\|_{W^{2,\infty}([-S,S])}\to0$. The compact-region integrals therefore tend to zero by lem:c10_Ieps_compact_difference. The tail integrals are bounded by $C_R\epsilon S^{-p}$, independently of $k,S$, by lem:c10_Ieps_uniform_tail. Thus \[ \limsup_k\|\mc I_\epsilon(g_k)-\mc I_\epsilon(g)\|_{W^{1,\infty}([-R,R])} \le C_R\epsilon\bigl(\delta^{2-\alpha}+S^{-p}\bigr). \] Let $S\to\infty$ and then $\delta\to0$. All derivative estimates use essential suprema. In Lean the integrability of the value and derivative integrands on each region is obtained from the kernel-pair bounds of lem:c10_profile_kernel_bounds.

nodes.title: Local convergence of the nonlinear operator
nodes.statement_html: Let $0\le\epsilon\le1$, $\beta+\frac1p<\gamma<2p+1$, $r\in X_\gamma$, and let $\ov f_k$ be admissible with a common constant $M$ with $\ov f_k\to\ov f$ in $C^2_{\mathrm{loc}}$. Then for $j=1,2,3$ and every $R>0$, $\mc N_j^{\epsilon,\ov f_k}(r)\to\mc N_j^{\epsilon,\ov f}(r)$ in $W^{1,\infty}([-R,R])$.
nodes.proof_html: $\ov f$ is admissible with constant $M$ (lem:c10_admissible_closed). $\mc N_1,\mc N_2$: on $[-R,R]$, $\ov f_k'+r'\to\ov f'+r'$ and $\ov f_k'\to\ov f'$ in $W^{1,\infty}$ with values in a fixed compact set; since $B_\epsilon$ is smooth, $B_\epsilon(\ov f_k'+r')\to B_\epsilon(\ov f'+r')$ and $B_\epsilon(\ov f_k')\to B_\epsilon(\ov f')$ in $W^{1,\infty}([-R,R])$ (the derivative is $B_\epsilon'(\cdot)(\ov f_k''+r'')$). Also $\ov f_k-y\ov f_k'\to\ov f-y\ov f'$ in $W^{1,\infty}([-R,R])$ (its derivative is $-y\ov f_k''$) and $r-yr'$ is fixed. $W^{1,\infty}([-R,R])$ is a Banach algebra, so products converge. $\mc N_3$: apply lem:c10_Ieps_local_continuity to $(g_k,g)=(\ov f_k+r,\ov f+r)$ and to $(g_k,g)=(\ov f_k,\ov f)$; the hypotheses hold by lem:c10_profile_consequences(1) with constants uniform in $k$, and $C^2_{\mathrm{loc}}$ convergence implies $W^{2,\infty}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ convergence. The term $b_\epsilon r'$ does not depend on the profile.

nodes.title: Continuity in the profile
nodes.statement_html: Let $0\le\epsilon\le\min\{1,\epsilon_0\}$ ($\epsilon_0$ of lem:linear_conjugation), $\beta+\frac1p<\gamma'<\gamma<2p+1$, $r\in X_\gamma$, $M>0$, and let $\{\ov f_k\}$ be admissible profiles with common constant $M$ such that $\ov f_k\to\ov f$ in $C^2_{\mathrm{loc}}(\R)$ and such that lem:c10_N_decomposition applies to each $\ov f_k$ and to $\ov f$. Then $\mc N_{\epsilon,\ov f_k}(r)\to\mc N_{\epsilon,\ov f}(r)$ in $Y_{\gamma'}$.
nodes.proof_html: By lem:c10_admissible_closed $\ov f$ is admissible with constant $M$. By lem:c10_N_decomposition, $\mc N_{\epsilon,\ov f_k}(r)-\mc N_{\epsilon,\ov f}(r)=\sum_{j=1}^3\bigl(\mc N_j^{\epsilon,\ov f_k}(r)-\mc N_j^{\epsilon,\ov f}(r)\bigr)$, the profile-independent term $\mc R_\epsilon r$ cancelling. By lem:N1, lem:N2, lem:N3 with $r_1=r$, $r_2=0$, $N=\|r\|_{X_\gamma}$ (and $\mc N_j(0)=0$), each $\mc N_j^{\epsilon,\ov f_k}(r)$ and $\mc N_j^{\epsilon,\ov f}(r)$ lies in $Y_\gamma$ with norm $\le C(p,\gamma,M,\|r\|)\epsilon\|r\|$; hence the differences are uniformly bounded in $Y_\gamma$ (paper eq:nonlinear\_continuity\_uniform\_bound). By lem:c10_N_local_convergence they converge to $0$ in $W^{1,\infty}_{\mathrm{loc}}$. By prop:appendix_convergence (second statement, with $G_k=\mc N_{\epsilon,\ov f_k}(r)$, $G=\mc N_{\epsilon,\ov f}(r)$) the convergence holds in $Y_{\gamma'}$.

nodes.title: Uniform estimates for admissible profiles
nodes.section: Assembly: proof of the nonlinear estimates
nodes.statement_html: Let $\beta+\frac1p<\gamma<2p+1$, $M,N>0$, $0\le\epsilon\le\min\{1,\epsilon_0\}$ ($\epsilon_0$ of lem:linear_conjugation), and $\ov f$ an admissible profile with constant $M$ to which lem:c10_N_decomposition applies. There is $C=C(p,\gamma,M,N)$, independent of $\epsilon$ and $\ov f$, such that for all $r,r_1,r_2\in X_\gamma$ with norms $\le N$, $\mc N_{\epsilon,\ov f}(r)\in Y_\gamma$ and \[ \|\mc N_{\epsilon,\ov f}(r_1)-\mc N_{\epsilon,\ov f}(r_2)\|_{Y_\gamma}\le C\epsilon\|r_1-r_2\|_{X_\gamma},\qquad \|\mc N_{\epsilon,\ov f}(r)\|_{Y_\gamma}\le C\epsilon\|r\|_{X_\gamma}. \]
nodes.proof_html: By lem:c10_N_decomposition, $\mc N_{\epsilon,\ov f}(r_1)-\mc N_{\epsilon,\ov f}(r_2)=\sum_{j=1}^3(\mc N_j(r_1)-\mc N_j(r_2))-\mc R_\epsilon(r_1-r_2)$ (linearity of $\mc R_\epsilon$). lem:N1, lem:N2, lem:N3 bound the first three differences by $C\epsilon\|r_1-r_2\|$; lem:linear_conjugation gives $\|\mc R_\epsilon\|_{X_\gamma\to Y_\gamma}\le C_\gamma\epsilon$ uniformly in $0\le\epsilon\le\epsilon_0$. The second estimate is the first with $r_2=0$, since $\mc N_{\epsilon,\ov f}(0)=0$ (lem:c10_N_decomposition).

nodes.title: Nonlinear estimates: assembly
nodes.section: Assembly: proof of the nonlinear estimates
nodes.statement_html:
Let $\epsilon_0,\delta,\mu_*$ be as in thm:fixed_point_approximation, and assume (shrinking $\epsilon_0$ if necessary) that $\epsilon_0\le1$ and $\epsilon_0$ does not exceed the constant of lem:linear_conjugation. Let $\beta+\frac1p<\gamma<2p+1$ and $N>0$. Write $\ov f=\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu}$ for $0\le\epsilon\le\epsilon_0$ and $\mu\in\ov B=\ov B(\mu_*,\delta)$. Then there is $C=C(p,\gamma,N)$, independent of $\epsilon\in[0,\epsilon_0]$ and $\mu\in\ov B$, such that for all $r,r_1,r_2\in X_\gamma$ with $\|r\|_{X_\gamma},\|r_1\|_{X_\gamma},\|r_2\|_{X_\gamma}\le N$:
  • $\mc N_{\epsilon,\ov f}(r)\in Y_\gamma$ and $\|\mc N_{\epsilon,\ov f}(r)\|_{Y_\gamma}\le C\epsilon\|r\|_{X_\gamma}$ (eqn:fixed_point_nonlinear_bound);
  • $\|\mc N_{\epsilon,\ov f}(r_1)-\mc N_{\epsilon,\ov f}(r_2)\|_{Y_\gamma}\le C\epsilon\|r_1-r_2\|_{X_\gamma}$ (eqn:fixed_point_nonlinear_lipschitz);
  • for $\gamma_1<\gamma_2$ as in def:parameters, each fixed $r\in X_{\gamma_2}$ and each fixed $\epsilon\in[0,\epsilon_0]$, the map $\ov B\ni\mu\mapsto\mc N_{\epsilon,\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu}}(r)\in Y_{\gamma_1}$ is continuous.
This is exactly the conclusion of thm:fixed_point_nonlinear_estimates.
nodes.proof_html:
By lem:c10_approx_admissible, every $\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu}$ is admissible with the uniform constant $M_0$; it is $C^\infty$ with $\ov f'_{\epsilon,\mu}\in L^\infty$, and $|D|^p\ov f'_{\epsilon,\mu}$ is defined (as required in def:residual for $\mc E_\epsilon(\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu})$ to make sense; thm:fixed_point_approximation(3)), so lem:c10_N_decomposition applies.

Items 1--2: lem:c10_N_admissible_bounds with $M=M_0$; the constant $C(p,\gamma,M_0,N)$ is independent of $\epsilon,\mu$.

Item 3: $\ov B\subset\C$ is a metric space, so it suffices to prove sequential continuity. Let $\mu_k\to\mu$ in $\ov B$. By thm:fixed_point_approximation(4), $\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu_k}\to\ov f_{\epsilon,\mu}$ in $C^2_{\mathrm{loc}}$; all are admissible with constant $M_0$. Apply prop:nonlinear_continuity with $\gamma=\gamma_2$, $\gamma'=\gamma_1$ (admissible since $\beta+\frac1p<\gamma_1<\gamma_2<2p+1$ by def:parameters).

nodes.title: Fixed cutoffs and dyadic operators
nodes.section: Fixed data and global Holder transport
nodes.statement_html: Use the even cutoff $\chi=\rho$ of def:c04_osc_integral. Set \[ \eta(x)=\operatorname{smoothTransition}((49-64x^2)/13),\quad \varphi(\xi)=\chi(\xi/2)-\chi(\xi),\quad q_p(\xi)=\begin{cases}\varphi(\xi)|\xi|^{-p},&\xi\ne0,\\0,&\xi=0.\end{cases} \] Let $K_p=\operatorname{Re}\widecheck{q_p}$ and $K_{p,j}(x)=2^{(1-p)j}K_p(2^jx)$ for $j\in\N$. For a real function $v$ put \[ S_0v=\operatorname{Re}\widecheck{\chi\widehat v},\qquad \Delta_jv=\operatorname{Re}\widecheck{\varphi(2^{-j}\,\cdot)\widehat v}. \] These use the project's $e^{-ix\xi}$ transform and $1/(2\pi)$ inverse normalization. Finally define \[ C_{\eta,p}w(x)=c_p\int_\R (\eta(x)-\eta(x-z))w(x-z)|z|^{-1-p}\,dz, \] with integrand zero at $z=0$. These are total formulas; convergence and mapping properties are the separate lemmas below. Convolution means $(a*b)(x)=\int a(z)b(x-z)dz$.

nodes.title: Cutoff and annular-symbol properties
nodes.section: Fixed data and global Holder transport
nodes.statement_html: The cutoffs $\eta,\chi$ are smooth, real, even and valued in $[0,1]$. The function $\eta$ equals one on $[-3/4,3/4]$ and has support in $[-7/8,7/8]$; $\chi$ equals one on $[-1,1]$ and has support in $[-2,2]$. For every $p\in(0,1)$, $q_p$ and $\varphi$ are smooth and supported in $\{\xi:1\le|\xi|\le4\}$. All their derivatives vanish at zero.

nodes.title: Global Holder translation and restriction
nodes.section: Fixed data and global Holder transport
nodes.statement_html: For every noninteger $a>0$, real $t$, and $u\in C^a(\R)$, the translate $\tau_tu(x)=u(x-t)$ belongs to $C^a(\R)$ and $N_a(\tau_tu)=N_a(u)$. If $I=[b,c]$ with $b<c$, then $u|_I\in C^a(I)$ and $N_a(u;I)\le N_a(u)$.
nodes.proof_html:
Translate each global derivative and the two-point Holder quotient.
  Restriction uses equality of within derivatives and ordinary derivatives on a nondegenerate
  interval. Work first with the extended norms, then transfer the finite inequalities to reals.

nodes.title: Global Holder product bound
nodes.section: Fixed data and global Holder transport
nodes.statement_html: For every noninteger $a>0$ there is $C_a>0$ such that for all real $u,v\in C^a(\R)$, $uv\in C^a(\R)$ and $N_a(uv)\le C_aN_a(u)N_a(v)$.
nodes.proof_html: Apply the interval product bound on all intervals $[-R,R]$, $R\ge1$, using a constant independent of $R$. The local derivatives agree with the global derivatives. Exhaust the line for the derivative suprema and the two-point Holder seminorm.

nodes.title: Integration with a global Holder majorant
nodes.section: Fixed data and global Holder transport
nodes.statement_html: Let $a=k+\theta>0$, $k\in\N$, $0<\theta<1$. Let $F:\R^2\to\R$ and $B:\R\to[0,\infty)$ be such that $B\in L^1$, every section $F(\cdot,t)$ belongs to $C^a(\R)$, and $N_a(F(\cdot,t))\le B(t)$ for every $t$. Suppose $(x,t)\mapsto\partial_x^rF(x,t)$ is measurable for $0\le r\le k$. Then $U(x)=\int F(x,t)dt$ is absolutely defined for every $x$, lies in $C^a(\R)$, and $N_a(U)\le(k+2)\int B(t)dt$. For every $r\le k$, $\partial^rU(x)=\int\partial_x^rF(x,t)dt$ with absolute convergence.
nodes.proof_html: Restrict to compact intervals, applying the parameter-integral theorem with the real-to-complex bridge if needed. Its derivative-interchange proof gives the identities. Bounds independent of the interval give global $C^k$ regularity and bound each of the $k+1$ derivative suprema and the Holder seminorm by $\int B$. This suffices for the displayed constant.

nodes.title: Translation differences of the fixed cutoff
nodes.section: Fixed data and global Holder transport
